# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [Unreleased]

### Security

- **Scan multipart upload bodies as raw bytes instead of UTF-8 (closes #1498).** Both data-package upload paths (`rustgate-missions::multipart` and the identical copy in `rustgate-enrollment::datapackage`) decoded the *entire* multipart body as UTF-8 before scanning it, so every genuine (binary) ZIP upload was rejected with "multipart body missing `file` field" — only ASCII test fixtures passed. `extract_multipart_field` / `extract_multipart_filename` now split on the `--{boundary}` delimiter as bytes, locate each part's `\r\n\r\n` header/content split by byte index, decode **only** the header block as UTF-8 to match `name="…"` / `filename="…"`, and return the content as a raw byte range. The missions hardenings are preserved (O(n) offset tracking, #1618; CR/LF/NUL filename rejection, #1608), and the filename control-character check is now ported into the enrollment copy as well.

- **Clock-backwards fail-open closed at two retention/staleness sites (SEC-23, refs #1561).** Two wall-clock `duration_since(...).unwrap_or_default()` checks mapped an NTP step-back (or a future-dated timestamp) to a zero elapsed time, flipping the decision the wrong way. **(1) Archive rotation** (`crates/rustgate-archive/src/archive_rotation.rs`) treated a file whose mtime is in the future as age `0`, so it was **never** age-evicted — blowing retention/disk. The age sweep now treats a future mtime as fully aged and evicts it (`duration_since(mtime).map(|age| age > max_age).unwrap_or(true)`). **(2) Emergency repeater** (`crates/rustgate-router/src/repeater.rs`) treated a future `received_at` as fresh, so a stale (clock-skewed) emergency passed the staleness filter indefinitely in both `active_events()` replay and `sweep()`. A shared `is_fresh` helper now treats a future `received_at` as stale (drop). The throttle u32-ms-wrap half of SEC-23 and the correlation temporal score are intentionally out of scope here. Unit tests cover a future mtime / `received_at` at both sites.

- **`--prefer-post-quantum` is no longer a silent no-op on a `--features post-quantum` build; PQ wiring/wording corrected (closes #1512).** Previously the flag was only consulted on the non-PQ build path (where it warns the feature is missing), so on a PQ build it logged nothing — operators had no confirmation the toggle was honored. The PQ provider-install site now emits an `info!` confirming X25519MLKEM768 key exchange is preferred when the flag is set (and notes when an explicit `--kx-groups` order supersedes it). `--cnsa2`'s help text now states it is compile-time scaffolding only with no runtime effect yet (it does not switch to ML-KEM-1024 or enforce ML-DSA certs). The `rustgate-mavlink` rekey module docs and ADR 0020 corrected the overstated "forward-secret" framing to "post-quantum confidential (harvest-now-decrypt-later resistant)" and document that decap-key rotation — not the static decap key — is the forward-secrecy lever.

### Added

- **Live CRL refresh — revocation lists apply without a restart (refs #1496, Piece 1 of ADR 0025).** Certificate Revocation Lists were parsed once at boot and frozen for the process lifetime, so a freshly-published CRL only took effect after a restart. New `rustgate_tls::CrlStore` is a hot-swappable, generation-counted CRL holder (SHA-256 change-detection, fail-safe snapshot, health tracking for all-stale lists), and the client-cert verifier gains a `CrlProvider` seam so it rebuilds when the CRL generation changes. A new `--crl-refresh-interval` flag (env `RUSTGATE_CRL_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `0` = disabled, the default) starts a background watcher that reloads the CRL file on change; with no interval the static boot-frozen behavior is preserved byte-for-byte. This is Piece 1 of the revocation-lifecycle work — fail-closed staleness handling and active-session disconnect are follow-up pieces and this does **not** yet close #1496. so **DIS / ASTERIX / VMF** can be received on an exercise-LAN multicast address (sensors flooding tracks onto a group rather than addressing the router directly) with the **same** admission + validate-and-drop controls. Inbound only — no multicast egress. **(1) Shared bind helper.** New `rustgate_transport::udp_common::bind_multicast_socket_v4(group, port, interface)` — the single source of truth for the multicast receive-socket setup (`SO_REUSEADDR` + wildcard `0.0.0.0:port` bind + `join_multicast_v4`), extracted from the CoT multicast listener so the sequence is written/reviewed/corrected once. The CoT-specific `udp_multicast::bind_multicast_socket` now delegates to it (its rebroadcast/egress half is byte-for-byte unchanged); the generic `codec_ingress` listener calls it too (decision D4, same D1 single-path argument as `UdpAdmission`). The wildcard bind (not the group address) keeps it portable to Windows. **(2) Config seam.** `CodecIngressConfig` gains `multicast_group: Option<Ipv4Addr>` (default `None` = plain unicast bind, existing deployments unaffected) and `multicast_interface: Ipv4Addr` (default `0.0.0.0`, kernel default routed NIC), plus a `bind_socket(addr)` method that joins the group when set and does a plain `UdpSocket::bind` otherwise. A non-multicast group is a **fail-closed** bind error (`InvalidInput`), never a silent unicast fallback. Admission, rate limit, identity cap, size cap, and the validating decode all apply identically regardless of how the socket was bound. **(3) Server wiring.** New `--dis-multicast-group` / `--asterix-multicast-group` / `--vmf-multicast-group` flags (+ `RUSTGATE_{DIS,ASTERIX,VMF}_MULTICAST_GROUP` env + TOML keys), threaded `cli.ingress.<proto>_multicast_group → ProtocolIngress → CodecIngressConfig`; `spawn` now binds via `config.bind_socket(addr)`. A `parse_multicast_group` helper rejects a non-`224.0.0.0/4` value as a hard **startup** error too (validated at both the config and bind layers). The port comes from the existing `--<proto>-bind`; there is no separate multicast-port flag. STANAG 4586 (also UDP) deliberately has **no** multicast flag in this wave. **(4) Docs/tests.** `docs/tactical-ingress.md` gains a "Multicast ingress (UDP only)" section + a per-protocol flag-table row; unit tests cover the default-unicast config, a unicast `bind_socket` round-trip, and the non-multicast-group rejection. Live UDP ingress can now run unicast **or** multicast: CoT, DIS, ASTERIX, VMF.

- **STANAG 4586 live UDP ingress (#1473)** — wires **STANAG 4586 (UCS/UAV)** onto the existing generic UDP datagram listener, so UCS vehicle-position / status messages can be received and routed off the wire. Pure server wiring — no new mechanism: `Stanag4586EntityCodec` is already registered in the `EntityCodecRegistry` and `rustgate-stanag4586` is already a server dep, so this adds only `--stanag4586-bind` / `-group` / `-rate-limit-pps` / `-allowed-cidrs` / `-max-identities` (+ `RUSTGATE_STANAG4586_*` env + TOML) and a `start_stanag4586` calling the shared `CodecUdpInput` (one STANAG message per datagram, validate-and-drop, synthetic identity, secure-default rate limit — all inherited from the datagram listener). Default port 8586; off by default; trusted-network-only. **TCP-stream STANAG is deliberately deferred:** STANAG 4586's frame size is message-type-dependent (no self-delimiting length prefix), so a TCP stream needs a per-deployment framing decision (documented in `docs/tactical-ingress.md`). Live ingress now: CoT, MAVLink, DIS, ASTERIX, VMF, SAPIENT, Link 16, **STANAG 4586** (8 of 9 codecs). Meshtastic (LoRa) remains the last follow-up.
- **NFFI / STANAG 5527 live TCP ingress (#1473)** — wires **NFFI (NATO Friendly Force Information, STANAG 5527)** onto the generic stream-ingress listener, so friendly-force tracks can be received and routed off the wire. **(1) Wiring only — no new transport mechanism.** NFFI is an XML format, so its frames are delimited at the XML document boundary that `rustgate_transport::XmlStreamCodec` already locates (the same stream framing CoT-over-TCP uses); the leg reuses the existing `CodecTcpInput` listener + shared `UdpAdmission` gate unchanged. The only per-protocol glue is a `start_nffi` that differs from `start_sapient` solely in its framing (`FramedCodec::XmlStream`), codec (`NffiCodec`), `source_protocol` tag, and CN prefix. **(2) Server wiring.** `--nffi-bind` / `-group` / `-rate-limit-pps` / `-allowed-cidrs` / `-max-identities` / `-max-connections` (+ `RUSTGATE_NFFI_*` env + TOML), `start_nffi` on the shared `CodecTcpInput` with `XmlStreamCodec` framing + `NffiCodec` validate-and-drop, `NffiCodec` registered in the router's `EntityCodecRegistry` (`rustgate-nffi` now a server dependency), and a `SubsystemHandle` in the graceful-shutdown set. Default NFFI port 8500. Off by default; same unauthenticated / trusted-network-only posture as the other stream legs. **(3) Decode scope.** An NFFI document decodes to a canonical entity from its first `<track>` record; documents carrying several tracks surface only their first for now (same first-record limitation as ASTERIX). **(4) Docs.** `docs/tactical-ingress.md` extended with the NFFI leg. Live ingress now: CoT, MAVLink, DIS, ASTERIX, VMF, SAPIENT, Link 16, **NFFI**. STANAG 4586 (stream) + Meshtastic (LoRa) remain follow-ups.

- **TAK data-package REST API mounted on the admin server (`/api/packages`, refs #860)** — wires the already-implemented `rustgate_missions::PackageStore` and the `rustgate-admin` `missions_api` handler into the running server so operators can manage lightweight TAK data packages over HTTP. **(1) Feature + flag.** New off-by-default `missions` cargo feature on `rustgate-server` (`missions = ["dep:rustgate-missions", "rustgate-admin/missions"]`) plus `--packages-dir` / `RUSTGATE_PACKAGES_DIR` and `--packages-integrity-key-file` / `RUSTGATE_PACKAGES_INTEGRITY_KEY_FILE` (both accepted in the TOML config file). **(2) Surface.** When built with `--features missions,metrics` **and** `--packages-dir` is set, the admin HTTP server mounts `POST/GET /api/packages` (upload via multipart/form-data or raw ZIP, list) and `GET/DELETE /api/packages/{hash}` (download by SHA-256 hash, delete), each returning the shared `{"data": …}` / `{"error": …}` envelope (the download path streams the raw body with `Content-Type` from the stored metadata). **(3) Store construction.** The server reads the 32-byte HMAC integrity key from `--packages-integrity-key-file` into `Zeroizing` memory (same 64-hex-char / perm / size discipline as the client-queue key reader, via `rustgate_core::read_secret_file`), builds the on-disk `PackageStore` with default `StoreLimits` (1 GiB total / 50 MiB per package), and registers the handler into an `Arc<OnceLock<MissionsApiHandler>>` slot threaded through `setup::start_metrics` into `rustgate_admin::serve`; the dispatcher 404s `/api/packages` while the slot is empty, so non-`missions` builds and unconfigured servers pay nothing. **(4) Auth.** The REST surface is bearer-token authenticated and **reuses the `--metrics-token-file` credential** (the route lives on the metrics listener); `Cli::validate` requires both `--packages-integrity-key-file` and `--metrics-token-file` whenever `--packages-dir` is set, so the mutating upload/delete surface is never exposed unauthenticated and packages stay readable across restarts. The token is length-validated and compared in constant time inside the handler. **(5) Off-by-default + fail-loud.** When `--packages-dir` is unset the slot stays empty and a `warn!` notes the API is dark; a missing integrity key or metrics token is a hard startup error. **(6) Docs.** `docs/feature-flags.md` and the README feature table gain a `missions` row.
- **Edge ML inference pipeline wired into the router — mock backend (#858)** — turns the fully-implemented `rustgate-inference` crate (a hot-reloadable `Pipeline` behind `ArcSwap`, the `InferenceModel` trait, the `wiring::router_callback` back-annotation seam with its `source_protocol = "inference"` loop guard, and the deterministic `inference-mock` backend) into a live subsystem on the `rustgate` server. Previously `setup::start_inference` was an explicit no-op that only warned the feature was compiled in. **(1) Server wiring.** `setup::start_inference(cli, router, registry)` now reads the `--inference-config` TOML, parses + validates its `[inference]` block into `rustgate_inference::InferenceConfig`, builds a `Pipeline`, and returns the router's `OnRouted` back-annotation callback. The callback decodes each admitted message via the shared `EntityCodecRegistry`, runs the resulting entity through the registered models, and re-injects one annotated `RoutableMessage` per `InferenceResult` through `Router::route` — so the synthesized events traverse the normal **ACL / authz / dedup / egress** path exactly as the source message did, and the crate's loop guard stops them from being re-inferred. The re-injection sink dispatches on `spawn_background` to keep the `OnRouted` critical path non-blocking. **(2) Callback composition.** The inference callback is composed into the router's single `OnRouted` slot alongside the existing video-catalog (#862) and correlation-engine (#848) callbacks — `main.rs` extends the `match (video_callback, correlation_callback)` tuple to `(video_callback, correlation_callback, inference_callback)` covering all eight arms; inference chains last. **(3) Mock backend only.** This wave activates the in-tree, deterministic backend behind the new `inference-mock` passthrough feature on `rustgate-server` (forwards to `rustgate-inference/inference-mock`): one `MockInferenceModel` is registered per `[[inference.pipeline]]` entry, keyed by `model-name` and labelled by `target`. The ONNX/`ort` real backend remains separate deferred work behind a future `inference-onnx` feature and joins the same backend-selection cascade without churning the call site. With only the umbrella `inference` feature and no backend, `start_inference` warns and installs nothing. **(4) Flag.** New `--inference-config` / `RUSTGATE_INFERENCE_CONFIG` flag (also accepted in the TOML config file under `inference-config-file`); off by default, so a default build is unaffected and the pipeline is opt-in. **(5) Docs.** New `docs/inference.md` operator guide (what it does, build + enable, config reference, the re-injection / loop-guard model, mock-vs-real scope), surfaced in the doc site under Architecture → Inference Pipeline.

- **Link 16 / JREAP-C live TCP ingress (#1473)** — wires **Link 16 (JREAP-C, STANAG 5518)** onto the generic stream-ingress listener, so J-series air tracks can be received and routed off the wire. **(1) New framing codec.** `rustgate_transport::HeaderLengthCodec` — a generic "length-inside-a-fixed-header, frame-includes-header" `Decoder` (parameterized by header length, length-field offset, and width). For Link 16 this is `(16, 12, u32)`: the JREAP-C body length is a `u32` BE at offset 12 of the 16-byte header, and the delimited frame includes the header so `Link16Codec` can parse it. Length is bounded by `MAX_FRAME_SIZE` **before** any reservation; decode-only (the header is protocol-owned, so `Encoder` returns `Unsupported`). Exposed as a `FramedCodec::HeaderLength` variant. **(2) Server wiring.** `--link16-bind` / `-group` / `-rate-limit-pps` / `-allowed-cidrs` / `-max-identities` / `-max-connections` (+ `RUSTGATE_LINK16_*` env + TOML), `start_link16` on the shared `CodecTcpInput` with the `HeaderLength(16,12,u32)` framing + `Link16Codec` validation, `Link16Codec` registered in the `EntityCodecRegistry` (`rustgate-link16` now a server dependency). Default JREAP-C port 4444. Off by default; same unauthenticated / trusted-network-only posture as the other stream legs. **(3) Decode scope.** A JREAP-C frame carrying a J2.2 Air Track decodes to a canonical entity; other JREAP message types / J-series labels are dropped at the validating decode until the codec maps them. **(4) Docs/tests.** `docs/tactical-ingress.md` extended; `HeaderLengthCodec` unit tests (full-frame-includes-header, wait-for-header-then-body across reads, oversized-body rejection before allocation, encode-unsupported). Live ingress now: CoT, MAVLink, DIS, ASTERIX, VMF, SAPIENT, **Link 16**. STANAG 4586 (stream) + Meshtastic (LoRa) remain follow-ups.

- **Generic TCP codec ingress + live SAPIENT ingress (stream wave of #1473)** — extends tactical-codec ingress from datagram (UDP) to **stream-framed (TCP)** protocols, and wires **SAPIENT (BSI Flex 335)** end-to-end so counter-UAS / autonomous-sensor detection reports can be received and routed off the wire. **(1) New framing codec.** `rustgate_transport::VarintDelimitedCodec` — protobuf varint length-delimited framing (no magic prefix), with the decoded length bounded **before** any buffer reservation (a length over `MAX_FRAME_SIZE`, or a varint that does not terminate within 10 bytes, is rejected rather than allocated). Exposed as a `FramedCodec::VarintDelimited` variant so it plugs into the existing unified `Decoder`. **(2) New listener.** `rustgate_transport::codec_tcp_ingress::{CodecTcpInput, CodecTcpIngressConfig}` — the connection-oriented sibling of the UDP `CodecUdpInput`. Per connection: admission (CIDR allowlist → per-IP **connection-accept** rate → synthetic-identity cap, via the shared `UdpAdmission`, applied once at accept), a concurrent-connection cap, a per-connection framed read loop with a slow-loris read timeout, and per-frame validate-and-drop using the *same* `DynEntityCodec` the router re-decodes with (no edge/router parser-differential). A single malformed frame is dropped + audited without killing the connection; a framing-level error closes it. Wire identifiers never enter the CN or any authz input. **(3) Server wiring.** New `--sapient-bind` / `--sapient-group` / `--sapient-rate-limit-pps` / `--sapient-allowed-cidrs` / `--sapient-max-identities` / `--sapient-max-connections` flags (+ `RUSTGATE_SAPIENT_*` env + TOML), a `start_sapient` that binds the TCP listener with `VarintDelimitedCodec` framing + `SapientCodec` validation, registration of `SapientCodec` in the router's `EntityCodecRegistry`, and a `SubsystemHandle` in the graceful-shutdown set (`rustgate-sapient` is now an actually-used server dependency, removed from the cargo-machete ignore list). Off by default; unauthenticated / trusted-network-only, same posture as the UDP legs. **(4) Docs/tests.** `docs/tactical-ingress.md` extended with the SAPIENT/TCP section; `VarintDelimitedCodec` unit tests (single/back-to-back frames, split-across-reads reassembly, oversized-length and non-terminating-prefix rejection, encode/decode round-trip) and a mock-codec TCP integration test (valid frames routed, split frame reassembled, malformed frame dropped while the connection survives). Live-ingress protocols now: CoT, MAVLink, DIS, ASTERIX, VMF, **SAPIENT**. Link 16 / STANAG 4586 (stream) and Meshtastic (LoRa) remain follow-ups.

- **ASTERIX + VMF live UDP ingress on the generic codec listener (second wave of #1473)** — extends the codec-ingress seam from DIS to two more datagram protocols, so rustgate can now receive and route **ASTERIX CAT-062 system tracks** and **VMF (MIL-STD-6017) K05.1 position reports** off the wire. **(1) Wiring only — no new mechanism.** Both reuse the `CodecUdpInput` listener and shared `UdpAdmission` gate from the first wave; the per-protocol server glue (`dis.rs`) was consolidated into a single `tactical_ingress.rs` with a shared `spawn` helper + `parse_cidrs`, so the three `start_{dis,asterix,vmf}` functions differ only in their codec, `source_protocol` tag, and CN prefix (the D1 single-source principle applied to the server wiring too). **(2) Flags.** New `--asterix-bind` / `--vmf-bind` (+ `-group` / `-rate-limit-pps` / `-allowed-cidrs` / `-max-identities` each, with `RUSTGATE_ASTERIX_*` / `RUSTGATE_VMF_*` env + TOML), identical in shape to the DIS flags; off by default. **(3) Registry.** `rustgate-vmf` is now a server dependency and `VmfCodec` is registered in the router's `EntityCodecRegistry` (`AsterixEntityCodec` already was), so accepted datagrams dedup/correlate/egress end-to-end. **(4) Same security posture.** Validate-and-drop at the edge with each protocol's own codec (the same instance the router re-decodes with), synthetic transport-derived identity, wire identifiers never in the CN/authz, secure-default rate limit, size cap, audit-by-class — all inherited from the shared listener. Unauthenticated/trusted-network-only. **(5) Decode scope.** One canonical message per datagram: ASTERIX surfaces the first CAT-062 track of a datablock, VMF decodes K05.1 (other categories/message types drop at the validating decode). **(6) Docs/tests.** `docs/tactical-ingress.md` generalized to all three protocols; `parse_cidrs` unit tests cover the per-protocol diagnostic. Link 16 / STANAG 4586 / SAPIENT (stream-framed) and Meshtastic (LoRa) remain follow-ups under #1473.

- **Generic UDP codec ingress + live DIS ingress (first wave of #1473)** — closes the "codec breadth ≫ ingress depth" gap for the first datagram protocol: rustgate can now actually **receive and route DIS (IEEE 1278.1) Entity State PDUs** off the wire, not just decode them in tests. **(1) Shared admission gate.** New `rustgate_transport::udp_common::UdpAdmission` — the single source of truth for connectionless-UDP admission control (source CIDR allowlist → per-IP sliding-window rate limit → bounded synthetic-identity LRU), so the security controls are written/reviewed/fuzzed once rather than copied per protocol (design note #1473, decision D1). Returns a typed `AdmitDecision` so each rejection is audited by class. **(2) Generic listener.** New `rustgate_transport::codec_ingress::{CodecUdpInput, CodecIngressConfig}` — a codec-pluggable UDP listener that validates each datagram with the *same* `DynEntityCodec` the router uses (decision D2/Q3: no parser-differential between edge admission and router decode), drops + audits malformed/over-cap/rate-limited/CIDR-blocked datagrams at the boundary, and routes accepted ones carrying the raw bytes under a synthetic transport-derived identity tagged with the protocol's `source_protocol`. Wire identifiers (DIS entity/site IDs) are **never** folded into the identity CN or any authz input (decision D3) — they survive only in the decoded entity for correlation/dedup. **(3) Secure defaults.** The rate limit is never truly off (an unset/`0` value applies a built-in 10000 pps/IP default — these are unauthenticated amplification surfaces); a missing CIDR allowlist starts the listener but logs a prominent warning; datagrams are size-capped to the UDP and `MAX_FRAME_SIZE` maxima before any decode. **(4) Server wiring.** New `--dis-bind` / `--dis-group` / `--dis-rate-limit-pps` / `--dis-allowed-cidrs` / `--dis-max-identities` flags (+ `RUSTGATE_DIS_*` env + TOML), a `start_dis` that binds the socket and spawns the listener with `rustgate_dis::DisCodec` (already registered in the router's `EntityCodecRegistry`, so accepted PDUs dedup/correlate/egress end-to-end), and a `SubsystemHandle` in the graceful-shutdown set. Off by default (default-deny); unauthenticated/unencrypted and trusted-network-only, same posture as the plaintext CoT-UDP listener. **(5) Docs.** New `docs/tactical-ingress.md` operator guide (threat model, flag reference, drop-class audit, limitations). **(6) Tests.** Unit tests for the admission gate (CIDR-before-cap ordering, rate-limit burst, identity-cap reject-not-evict, zero-cap clamp), the config secure defaults + size clamp, and the server CIDR-list parsing. ASTERIX and VMF layer onto the same listener as the next increment; this PR proves the seam end-to-end with DIS.

- **Cross-domain egress guard server wiring (PR-C2 of #1457, closes #1457)** — turns the router hook from PR-C1 into an operator-configurable boundary in the `rustgate` server binary. **(1) Feature + flag.** New off-by-default `guard` cargo feature on `rustgate-server` (pulls in the optional `rustgate-guard` dep) and a `--guard-config` / `RUSTGATE_GUARD_CONFIG` flag (also accepted in the TOML config file). **(2) Wiring.** New `crates/rustgate-server/src/guard.rs` with `start_guard(cli, router)`: a no-op when `--guard-config` is unset; otherwise it reads the file into `Zeroizing` memory, parses the `[guard]` block into `rustgate_guard::GuardConfig` (`deny_unknown_fields`, the single source of truth for the config shape — the server does not shadow it), validates it, builds a `GuardGate`, and installs an `OnEgressGuard` closure via `Router::set_on_egress_guard`. The closure maps `GuardGate::evaluate` → `EgressGuardVerdict::{Allow, Deny { reason }}`, where the deny reason is a stable token from the new `GuardError::reason_token()` (`rate_limit` / `missing_marking` / `unauthorized_classification` / `audit_error` / `io_error`) so the reason vocabulary lives in one place in `rustgate-guard`. **(3) Direction (v1: global).** A single global direction from `GuardConfig.direction`; a `bidirectional` deployment resolves to the least-restrictive `low-to-high` for the per-call check (per-sink direction is a planned follow-up that layers on without a config break). **(4) Fail-loud + audited.** A malformed/invalid config is a hard startup error; activation emits `audit::guard_activated` plus a prominent `warn!` line; denials emit `audit::guard_rejected` (from PR-C1's router hook). **(5) Docs.** New `docs/cross-domain-guard.md` operator guide (threat model/scope, build + enable, full config reference, denial-reason table, ACL/authz interaction, v1 limitations). **(6) Tests.** Unit tests for the bidirectional→low-to-high resolution and the `[guard]` wrapper parse + unknown-field rejection. Completes the C-series guard arc and closes #1457.

- **Cross-domain egress guard hook in the router (PR-C1 of #1457)** — adds the central seam that lets the `rustgate-guard` cross-domain inspection boundary gate outbound traffic, per the [guard server-wiring design note](docs/design/guard-server-wiring.md). **(1) Core callback.** New `EgressGuardVerdict` (`Allow` / `Deny { reason }`) and `OnEgressGuard = Arc<dyn Fn(&RoutableMessage) -> EgressGuardVerdict + Send + Sync>` in `rustgate-core::egress`, alongside the existing `OnNatsPublish` / `OnFederationForward` / `OnHttpForward` aliases — a hand-written alias (not the fire-and-forget `on_callback!` macro) because a guard is a *gate* that returns a verdict, not an observer. **(2) Router hook.** `Router` gains an `ArcSwap<Option<OnEgressGuard>>` slot (hot-reloadable, same pattern as `on_routed`) and `set_on_egress_guard`. The gate is consulted inside `route_for_egress` **after** the local same-domain session fan-out (`route_inner`) and **before** the routed `Arc<RoutableMessage>` is handed to any external sink; a `Deny` verdict drops the message from external egress (returns `None`) and emits `audit::guard_rejected` with the full source CN. **(3) Single chokepoint = complete by construction.** Every ingress→egress path (UDP/NATS/MQTT/plaintext/federation) flows through `route_for_egress`, so one installed guard covers every external sink — present and future — without per-sink edits. The design is **fail-closed** (a guard that denies drops the message) and **router stays free of any `rustgate-guard` dependency** (the server installs the closure built from its `GuardGate`). **(4) Scope.** The gate guards the network-to-network cross-domain hop (external egress), not local same-domain session delivery; the un-installed default is one `ArcSwap::load` + `is_none()` check, so zero hot-path cost when no guard is configured. **(5) Tests.** Router tests for Deny→`None`, Allow→`Some`, and no-guard→unchanged; core tests for the verdict type. The server `--guard-config` flag + `start_guard` that installs the closure lands next (PR-C2).

- **MAVLink server wiring + operator docs (PR 6 of #731, closes #731)** — turns the MAVLink building blocks from PRs 1–5 into a running, operator-configurable transport in the `rustgate` server binary. **(1) CLI flags.** New `--mavlink-bind` (UDP, the canonical MAVLink transport), `--mavlink-tcp-bind` (tethered ground-control stations), `--mavlink-group` (destination; broadcast when unset), `--mavlink-signing-key-file` (TOML link manifest), `--mavlink-v1-fallback-cn`, and `--mavlink-pq-bootstrap-file`; the pre-existing `--mavlink-require-signing` / `--mavlink-allow-v1` policy flags are now actually consumed. All are accepted in the TOML config file under their kebab-case names. **(2) Link manifest (ADR 0020 §1).** New `crates/rustgate-server/src/mavlink.rs` parses a TOML manifest mapping each v2 signing `link_id` (decimal or `0x`-hex) to a rustgate identity (`cn`, `groups`) and its 32-byte `signing-key-hex`; the file is read into `Zeroizing` memory and the hex strings are wiped after decoding. The manifest populates both the `SigningKeyStore` (keys) and the `LinkRegistry` (identities). A verified `link_id` absent from the manifest is dropped — no anonymous-MAVLink path. **(3) Identity over UDP.** Since MAVLink has no TLS, the verified `link_id` *is* the identity; ingested frames become `RoutableMessage`s (`source_protocol = "mavlink"`, `MessageType::Mavlink`) routed to the configured group/broadcast destination, so ACL and authz apply exactly as for other transports. **(4) v1 fallback.** v1 is rejected by default; `--mavlink-allow-v1` requires `--mavlink-v1-fallback-cn` (v1 has no signing identity), routes all v1 traffic under that shared CN, and emits a startup warning. **(5) Lifecycle.** `start_mavlink` spawns the UDP/TCP listeners via `rustgate_mavlink::spawn_{udp,tcp}_listener`, wires an `OnMavlinkMessage` sink that dispatches `Router::route` off the read loop via `spawn_background`, and registers the `SubsystemHandle`s in the server's graceful-shutdown set. **(6) Docs.** New `docs/mavlink.md` operator guide (quick start, flag reference, identity/signing/replay model, obligations, the `mavlink-pq` PQ rekey channel, security notes), surfaced in the doc site under Architecture → MAVLink Integration. **(7) Scope.** Manifest hot-reload on SIGHUP and the live PQ-rekey receive socket are deliberate follow-ups (the rekey cryptography itself shipped in PR 4). **(8) Tests.** Unit tests for link-id parsing (decimal/hex/range), hex key decode + zeroize-on-decode, and manifest TOML round-trip + unknown-field rejection. Completes the six-PR #731 epic.

- **MAVLink obligation actuators + `Obligation::MaskCommand` (PR 5 of #731)** — wires the authz obligation chain to MAVLink's binary wire form (ADR 0020 §7), so a policy can redact or refuse MAVLink traffic the same way it already does CoT. **(1) New obligation.** Adds `Obligation::MaskCommand` to `rustgate-authz` (Group 1 redactor, serde `mask_command`): refuse to forward actuation frames while still allowing telemetry — gating *command* without gating *observation*. **(2) Actuators in `rustgate-mavlink::obligations`** (pure functions on frame bytes): `mask_position` zeroes the `lat`/`lon`/`alt`/`relative_alt` fields of a `GLOBAL_POSITION_INT` (MSG_ID 33) frame and **recomputes the CRC-16/MCRF4XX** so the masked frame stays well-formed; `mask_as_heartbeat` replaces a stripped frame with a benign zeroed v1 `HEARTBEAT` (preserving system/component IDs) instead of an empty body; `is_command_frame` classifies `COMMAND_LONG` (76) / `COMMAND_INT` (75) / `MANUAL_CONTROL` (69). A CRC accumulator matching the MAVLink spec is included (no compute helper existed before — only the `crc_extra` lookup). **(3) Router PEP dispatch.** `rustgate-router` gains a direct `rustgate-mavlink` dependency (mirroring the existing `rustgate-cot` precedent for `strip_coordinates`); `apply_mask_point` / `apply_mask_payload` branch on `source_protocol == "mavlink"` to call the binary actuators (the CoT/XML paths are byte-for-byte unchanged), and a new `apply_mask_command` arm neutralises command frames with a `mask_command` / `command_refused` audit event. **(4) CRC/signature discipline.** Masking recomputes the CRC; any v2 signature trailer is left stale for the egress re-signing path (`SigningKeyStore::resign`, PR 4) to refresh before delivery to another MAVLink sink, and is irrelevant when the masked frame rides opaquely to a non-MAVLink session. **(5) Tests.** 7 new unit tests in `rustgate-mavlink::obligations` (coordinate zeroing + CRC re-validation, non-position passthrough, command-id classification, valid-HEARTBEAT construction with preserved/defaulted IDs, CRC determinism); the new `MaskCommand` variant threads through every in-workspace exhaustive `Obligation` match (`compile.rs` tag, `as_policy_str`, `cdi.rs`). The router-level end-to-end assertion (a GLOBAL_POSITION_INT flight masked through the live PEP) lands with PR 6's mandated `mavlogdump`-style flight test. mavlink 132/132 lib tests pass; authz/router/guard suites stay green.

- **`rustgate-mavlink` ML-KEM-768 signing-key rekey channel (PR 4 of #731)** — adds the `rekey` module behind the new off-by-default `mavlink-pq` crate feature: a post-quantum, forward-secret channel for distributing MAVLink v2 signing keys (ADR 0020 §4–§6). **(1) Why.** MAVLink v2 signing keys are symmetric 32-byte values distributed out-of-band today; an adversary recording the distribution channel can recover today's traffic once classical ECDH falls. The new key now travels inside an **ML-KEM-768** (FIPS 203, via `aws-lc-rs::kem::ML_KEM_768`) encapsulation, so a recorded envelope cannot be opened even by a future quantum adversary holding the long-term bootstrap secret. **(2) Wire format.** `algorithm_id(1) ‖ mlkem_ct(1088) ‖ nonce(12) ‖ aead_ct‖tag` — the algorithm-id prefix (`0x01` = ML-KEM-768) is the crypto-agility hook so a future ML-KEM-1024 migration (`0x02`) never cross-decodes. **(3) Key schedule.** `wrap_key = HKDF-SHA256(salt = bootstrap_secret, ikm = ML-KEM-768 shared_secret, info = "rustgate-mavlink-rekey-v1")`; the 32-byte bootstrap secret is used **only** as the HKDF salt (it authenticates the wrap but is never the session key), so forward secrecy comes entirely from the ephemeral KEM. The payload is sealed with ChaCha20-Poly1305 under AAD `algorithm_id ‖ SHA-256(mlkem_ct)[..8]`, binding it to the algorithm slot and the specific KEM output. **(4) Payload.** `MavlinkRekeyPayload { timestamp, link_id, new_key, key_epoch }`, CBOR-encoded (`ciborium`) inside the AEAD; `new_key` is `Zeroize`/`ZeroizeOnDrop` with a redacting `Debug`. **(5) Replay.** `key_epoch` must strictly advance per `link_id`; `RekeyReceiver` tracks the last accepted epoch and updates it only *after* the payload authenticates, so a forged envelope cannot perturb a legitimate link's high-water mark. **(6) API.** `RekeyReceiver::{new, from_decap_bytes, open}`, `seal`, `generate_keypair`, and the `MavlinkRekeyPayload` / `RekeyError` / `ALG_ML_KEM_768` exports — all gated on `mavlink-pq`. The ML-KEM decapsulation key is the receiver's long-term PQ identity; its on-disk provisioning lands in PR 6. **(7) Dependencies & CI.** Adds `aws-lc-rs` (first *direct* workspace use; builds aws-lc from source via cmake + Go) and `ciborium` to the workspace; `cargo deny` passes (advisories/bans/licenses/sources). The feature is excluded from the `cargo-hack` feature-powerset job and instead clippy-checked + tested in the `post-quantum` CI lane (which already has the aws-lc-rs build deps). **(8) Tests.** 12 unit tests: seal/open round-trip (asserting the signing key never appears on the wire), wrong-PSK and wrong-decap-key failures, ciphertext tamper, unsupported-algorithm + too-short rejections, per-link epoch monotonicity + independence, decap-key byte round-trip, and `Debug` redaction. Default-feature build unchanged (125/125 lib tests still pass).

- **`rustgate-mavlink` UDP/TCP listeners (PR 2 of #731)** — adds the `listener` module: the ingress path that turns MAVLink wire traffic into routed, identity-bearing messages. **(1) Identity over UDP.** MAVLink over UDP has no TLS, so per ADR 0020 §1 the v2 signing `link_id` *is* the identity primitive. A new `LinkRegistry` maps each `link_id` → a rustgate `Identity` (cn + groups); a verified v2 frame whose `link_id` is absent from the registry is dropped with an audit event — there is no anonymous-MAVLink path. The registry is the identity half of the ADR 0020 link manifest; the signing-key half stays in the PR 3 `SigningKeyStore`, and the server crate (PR 6) populates both from one TOML file. **(2) Per-frame pipeline.** Both listeners decode through `MavlinkFrameCodec` (which enforces the framing-layer signing policy), verify v2 frames against the `SigningKeyStore` (signature + replay), resolve identity from the registry, and build a `RoutableMessage` with `source_protocol = "mavlink"`, `MessageType::Mavlink`, and a per-listener `Destination`. **(3) Destination is type-constrained.** `MavlinkDestination` is `Group | Broadcast` only — ADR 0020 §2's "no `direct`/`multicast` for telemetry" rule is enforced by making those variants unrepresentable rather than rejected at runtime. **(4) v1 fallback.** v1 frames are rejected by default; when an operator opts in (`allow_v1` + a configured `LinkRegistry::with_v1_fallback`), v1 frames route under the shared fallback identity with a `mavlink.v1_admitted` audit event documenting the degraded posture. **(5) Decoupled handoff.** The listener emits via an `OnMavlinkMessage` sink (`Arc<dyn Fn(RoutableMessage) + Send + Sync>`) instead of depending on `rustgate-router`, keeping the dependency graph acyclic (`rustgate-transport` already depends on `rustgate-mavlink`) — the server wires the sink to `Router::route_for_egress` so ACL/authz apply automatically. **(6) Transport details.** UDP decodes each datagram with a fresh codec (no cross-datagram/cross-peer state); TCP runs a per-connection read loop with `configure_tactical_socket`, a `READ_TIMEOUT` guard, and graceful `SubsystemHandle` drain. **(7) Audit events.** Three new `rustgate_core::audit` functions: `mavlink_signature_rejected`, `mavlink_replay_rejected`, `mavlink_v1_admitted`. **(8) Tests.** 8 new unit tests (verified-frame delivery with link identity, unknown-link-id drop, bad-signature drop, replay drop, v1 fallback admit/drop, destination projection, registry resolve/fallback); 125/125 lib tests pass. No CLI/TOML wiring yet — that lands in PR 6.

- **`rustgate-mavlink` v2 signing: `SigningKeyStore` (PR 3 of #731)** — adds the `signing` module to `rustgate-mavlink`, the trust boundary the frame codec deferred. **(1) Algorithm.** Implements the real MAVLink v2 signing algorithm — `SHA-256(secret_key ‖ frame_without_signature)[..6]`, where the signed prefix is every byte from `STX` through the 6-byte `TIMESTAMP` — **not** RFC 2104 HMAC, despite the umbrella issue's loose "HMAC-SHA256" label. This matches MAVProxy / pymavlink so frames round-trip against reference captures. **(2) `SigningKeyStore`.** Holds per-`LINK_ID` 32-byte keys wrapped in `Zeroizing<[u8; 32]>` (custom `Debug` redacts key material, prints only the non-secret link IDs). `verify(&[u8]) -> Result<VerifiedFrame, SigningError>` parses a signed v2 frame, looks up the key for its trailer `LINK_ID`, compares the computed signature in constant time via `subtle::ConstantTimeEq`, then enforces replay. `resign(frame, link_id, timestamp)` rebuilds the 13-byte trailer under a different key for cross-link forwarding — it copies the header (including the `SIGNED` INCOMPAT bit) and CRC verbatim so the CRC stays valid without re-running the per-`MSG_ID` CRC-EXTRA computation; turning an unsigned frame into a signed one (which would invalidate the CRC) is deliberately out of scope. **(3) Replay defence.** The 48-bit timestamp (10-µs ticks since 2015-01-01T00:00:00Z) must advance strictly past the last accepted value for its `(system_id, component_id, link_id)` stream; the seen-timestamp table is a bounded LRU (`DEFAULT_REPLAY_CAPACITY = 1024`, per ADR 0020) so a hostile sender spraying synthetic tuples cannot grow memory unbounded. The replay table is updated only *after* the signature verifies, so a forged frame can never poison a legitimate stream's high-water mark. **(4) Public API.** New exports: `SigningKeyStore`, `SigningKey`, `SigningError`, `VerifiedFrame`, `compute_signature`, `signing_timestamp`, plus the `SIGNING_KEY_LEN` / `SIGNATURE_LEN` / `DEFAULT_REPLAY_CAPACITY` constants. **(5) Tests.** 20 unit tests cover happy-path verify; wrong-key / flipped-payload / unknown-link / unsigned / v1 / too-short rejections; replay (non-advancing rejected, advancing accepted, per-stream isolation, no-update-on-failure); re-sign round-trip + header/payload preservation + unknown-target rejection; a known-answer signature vector; the timestamp epoch math; `Debug` redaction; and a 48-bit little-endian timestamp round-trip. No new wire behavior is enabled until the PR 2 listener and PR 6 server wiring land — the module is library surface exercised by unit tests only.

- **`rustgate-ogc-sensorthings` MQTT push subscriber (closes #1380)** — closes the deferred half of the SensorThings v1.0 adapter shipped in v0.9.0. The polling path remains the default; the new push path is gated behind `--features mqtt-push` on the `rustgate-ogc-sensorthings` crate and pulls in `rumqttc` (`default-features = false`, no TLS feature flags enabled — the MVP rejects `mqtts://` at startup, so the unmaintained `rustls-pemfile` transitive dep RUSTSEC-2025-0134 does not enter the dep tree). **(1) Wire format.** SensorThings v1.0 §10 defines an MQTT publish/subscribe transport publishing one JSON `Observation` document per measurement on the topic `v1.0/Datastreams(<id>)/Observations`. The payload shape is byte-for-byte identical to the REST-polled form, so the existing `observation_to_entity` mapper handles the projection unchanged. **(2) Configuration.** New `[sensorthings.mqtt-push]` block on `SensorThingsConfig` (`broker-uri`, `client-id`, `keepalive-secs`); enabling it requires at least one `[[sensorthings.subscriptions]]` entry because the subscriber binds its topic list from the same `datastream-id` values the polling path uses. **(3) Public API.** New `mqtt_push` module exporting `spawn_mqtt_push_task(config, router) -> Result<SubsystemHandle, SensorThingsError>` mirroring `spawn_polling_task`, plus `observation_topic_for(&Subscription) -> String` and `datastream_id_from_topic(&str) -> Option<u64>` topic helpers, plus the `MqttPushConfig` struct and `DEFAULT_MQTT_KEEPALIVE_SECS = 60` constant. **(4) MVP scope.** The push subscriber accepts only `mqtt://host[:port][/path]` broker URIs — `mqtts://` is rejected at startup with the new typed `SensorThingsError::MqttsNotSupported` variant; TLS for the push transport lands in a follow-up alongside the CA-pin / mTLS / SNI override knobs. No authentication (SensorThings does not pin an auth scheme) and a fixed QoS 1 per subscription (the SensorThings community default) — both are also follow-up extensions to `MqttPushConfig`. The subscriber lets `rumqttc` own the reconnect loop and a `tokio::select!` waits on either an event-loop tick or the `SubsystemHandle` shutdown notification, mirroring the polling task's structure. **(5) Cross-path semantics.** Operators may run polling and push side-by-side against the same `Datastream` — every observation reaches the router as a `RoutableMessage` with the same `source_protocol = "ogc-sensorthings"`, `MessageType::Status`, and synthetic `Identity::plaintext("ogc-sensorthings", …)` source, and the cross-path dedup cache (`rustgate_router::dedup`) collapses any observation that arrives via both routes. **(6) Tests.** 20 new unit tests in `src/mqtt_push.rs` cover topic composition (canonical shape), topic parsing (spec shape, unknown version, trailing segments, non-numeric id, empty / unrelated topics), broker-URI parsing (default port, explicit port, path stripping, bracketed IPv6 with and without port, `mqtts://` rejection mapping to `MqttsNotSupported`, other-scheme rejection, empty input, missing host, malformed port, unbracketed IPv6 ambiguity rejection), `MqttPushConfig` TOML round-trip + default keepalive + unknown-field rejection. 71/71 sensorthings tests pass with `--features mqtt-push`, 51/51 with the default-feature build (existing test struct literals updated to include `mqtt_push: None` behind the same feature gate). **(7) Documentation.** Crate-level `README.md` reorganised under per-transport sections; lib.rs module-level docs updated to reflect the now-available push path; the deprecated "MQTT push is deferred" prose in both `README.md` and `src/lib.rs` removed. Server-side wiring (`setup.rs` calling `spawn_mqtt_push_task` when an operator enables push) is intentionally out of MVP scope per the issue — a future follow-up PR adds the corresponding server-level feature flag that propagates `mqtt-push` to the subcrate.

- **`--cnsa2` CLI flag scaffolding + ADR 0019 (Batch K1+K2, closes #504)** — adds a `--cnsa2` / `RUSTGATE_CNSA2` flag in `rustgate-server` that today acts as a scaffolding switch: when set, the server validates that the `post-quantum` feature is compiled in (errors otherwise with a clear pointer to the required build profile) and logs the phased-readiness state at startup so operators understand the gap between "I asked for CNSA 2.0" and "what the build actually delivers." The full convergence work (ML-KEM-1024 KEX, ML-DSA-87 signatures, TLS 1.3 minimum) blocks on [aws-lc-rs #964](https://github.com/aws/aws-lc-rs/issues/964) resolving its FIPS / ML-DSA mutual exclusion — operators wanting CNSA 2.0 today get a partial answer (NIST L3 hybrid KEX + classical certs) and the diagnostic makes that honest. New `docs/adr/0019-cnsa2-hybrid-mldsa.md` documents the architectural direction: rustgate will implement CNSA 2.0 via the IETF LAMPS Composite ML-DSA hybrid certificate path (Composite ML-DSA-87 + ECDSA-P384 for Level 5; Composite ML-DSA-65 + ECDSA-P256 for Level 3), in phases tracked by sub-issues #500 (offline package signatures via the `fips204` pure-Rust crate, lands next in K3), #501 (ML-DSA TLS verification, rustls-blocked), #502 (ML-DSA cert + CRL issuance, blocked), #503 (hybrid cert support, partial-blocked). The flag's runtime behavior is intentionally limited until #501/#502/#503 land — `--cnsa2` does NOT yet override `--kx-groups` or `--tls-min-version`; those still come from their dedicated flags. ADR 0019 sets the architectural commitment; future PRs reference it as the north star for CNSA 2.0 work.

### Changed

- **Server `Cli` flattened into `#[command(flatten)]` arg groups — removes the `RUST_MIN_STACK` CI workaround (root-cause hygiene)** — the clap-derived top-level `Cli` in `rustgate-server` had grown to ~194 `#[arg(...)]` fields in a single struct, so the generated `augment_args` / `from_arg_matches` functions built one enormous stack frame. `Cli::try_parse_from` in the `cli::tests` overflowed libtest's ~2 MiB default per-test-thread stack and SIGABRTed; CI had been masking it by exporting `RUST_MIN_STACK: 16777216` on the `test` and `coverage` jobs. The flags are now grouped into eighteen `#[derive(clap::Args)]` sub-structs (`TlsArgs`, `NatsArgs`, `EnrollmentArgs`, `WebsocketArgs`, `MqttArgs`, `MavlinkArgs`, `TacticalIngressArgs`, `FederationArgs`, `AuthzArgs`, `ArchiveArgs`, `ObservabilityArgs`, …) that are `#[command(flatten)]`-ed into `Cli`, so clap emits each group's `augment_args` as its own small frame. **No operator-facing surface change**: `#[serde(flatten)]` keeps the `print-config` / config-file output flat, every CLI flag name, `RUSTGATE_*` env var, TOML key, default, and `generate-config` template/section ordering is unchanged (the flat `ConfigFile` mirror is preserved; only its merge routine routes each key to the right sub-struct). The measured parse-path stack frame dropped ~5–6× (well under 2 MiB), and the `RUST_MIN_STACK` override has been removed from CI. New server flags should be added to the relevant arg-group sub-struct, not the top-level `Cli`.

- **Clean-room interoperability policy + per-file provenance headers for TAK protocol schemas (ADR 0021)** — documents and hardens the IP posture for interoperating with copyleft-licensed protocol ecosystems (the TAK reference implementations — ATAK-CIV and TAK Server — are GPLv3; FreeTAKServer/taky are GPL/EPL) while rustgate ships proprietary. **(1) ADR 0021 (Accepted).** Records the rule: build interop only from public protocol facts (specs, schema/IDL files, published developer docs, self-observed wire behavior) and original expression; never copy a reference implementation's source. Documents the multi-ground defensibility reasoning (schema interface as uncopyrightable method-of-operation under 17 U.S.C. §102(b) / *Lotus v. Borland*; merger doctrine; independent creation; the FSF/SFLC industry norm that an independent protocol implementation is not a derivative of the reference; and the §105 U.S.-Government-works angle as a secondary factor). **(2) Provenance headers.** A 2026-audit compared the already-vendored TAK protobuf schemas (`rustgate-proto/proto/*`, `rustgate-federation/proto/*`, packages `atakmap.commoncommo.protobuf.v1` / `com.atakmap` / `gov.tak.cop.proto.v1`) field-by-field against upstream and found them to be **independent re-expressions, not copies** — they carry none of upstream's comments/headers and diverge in field types and ordering, sharing only the wire-format-required `(name, type, number)` tuples. All 22 vendored `.proto` files now carry a header asserting independent clean-room authorship for interoperability (deliberately **not** a GPL attribution NOTICE, which would wrongly concede derivative status). **(3) Contributor rule.** New mandatory "Clean-room rule for third-party protocols" section in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. No code/runtime change — protobuf codegen is unaffected (the headers are leading `//` comments). A `TakControl` `string`-vs-`uint32` wire-compatibility divergence noted during the audit is tracked separately as a correctness follow-up.

- **Dormant integration subsystems now fail loud at startup (closes #1456)** — the scaffold-only integrations that are compiled in but not yet wired to live traffic (`foundry`, `dds`) now emit their "compiled in but NOT active — no-op in this build" diagnostic at **`warn!`** instead of `info!`, with consistent wording that names the gap and points at the tracking issue. Previously an operator who built e.g. `--features foundry` expecting a live bridge got only an info-level line easily lost in startup noise; the warning makes the no-op unmistakable. No behaviour change beyond log severity/wording — these subsystems remain scaffold-only pending their respective follow-ups (#851 foundry, #870 dds). (`inference` was in this set when #1456 landed but is now wired with a mock backend — see the #858 entry above.) The `lattice` path already warned correctly when a `[lattice]` config block is present without a backend feature and is unchanged. Real backend wiring for each is tracked separately.

- **`rustgate-vmf` K05.1 production codec decode migrated to SchemaCodec (refs #1396 / closes I2)** — `K051PositionReport::decode` now delegates the bit-stream parse to the `SchemaCodec` built from `schemas/k05_1.yaml` (which landed in #1409) instead of the hand-rolled `BitReader` field-by-field reads. The wrapper layer retains the value-projection concerns: range guards (lat ∈ `[-90, 90]`, lon ∈ `[-180, 180]`), calibration math (raw → degrees / m·s⁻¹ / degrees-of-course), and `unit_identifier` sanitization (non-printable ASCII → `?`, trailing padding trimmed). **Encode stays hand-rolled** per the #1393 lesson learned — the bit-stream encode path is the high-risk surface and the production hand-rolled implementation has 26 inline unit tests + a fuzz target protecting it. **Mechanism**: the decode reads the BitReader's current bit position, takes the remaining payload bytes from `BitReader::payload()`, uses `rustgate_codec_schema::bitstream::shift_left` (added in I1, #1426) to byte-align the body, then calls `SchemaCodec::to_entity` on the byte-aligned slice. After the schema decodes, the wrapper computes the bits actually consumed (24 URN + 25 lat + 26 lon + 4 FPI bits + conditional 16/12/9/56 bits for altitude/speed/course/unit_id) and `advance_bits` on the BitReader so downstream code sees the cursor at the correct position. New BitReader API surface: `payload()` accessor and `advance_bits(n)`. Schema attributes are projected back to typed fields via `read_u32_attr` / `read_i32_attr` / `read_u8_attr` / `read_u64_attr` helpers; the 56-bit `unit_identifier` is carried by the schema as a u64 (bit-packing grammar is integer-only) and decomposed MSB-first into 7 bytes before sanitization. All 40 VMF tests pass (26 inline K05.1 tests + 4 schema-parity proptests + 6 roundtrip + 4 misc) plus the existing fuzz target. Backward-compatible at the public API level — `K051PositionReport::decode(reader)` signature and `decode_message(payload)` semantics are unchanged. Closes the loop the multi-day codec-schema arc set out to achieve: schemas are no longer just declarative pins, they drive the production decode path.

- **`rustgate-codec-schema::bitstream` module — bit-shift utilities for cross-schema composition (refs #1411)** — provides `shift_left(input, bit_shift)` and `splice_at(header, header_end_bit, body, body_bit_count)` so a wrapper layer can compose two SchemaCodecs across a non-byte-aligned boundary WITHOUT modifying the schema runtime. Targets the use case where a fixed-shape body schema follows a variable-length bit-packed header (VMF K05.1 being the canonical example: 38–94-bit header → 22-byte body that starts at whatever bit position the header ended on). The runtime keeps its existing "first declared field starts at byte 0 bit 0" contract — wrappers hand-roll the header decode (already required because it's variable-length), use `shift_left` to byte-align the remaining payload, and feed it to the body SchemaCodec. Reverse direction on encode: SchemaCodec produces byte-aligned body bytes; `splice_at` merges them back into the wire at the header's bit-cursor end. Eight new unit tests cover `shift_left` (zero / one / four / seven bit shifts, single-byte input, empty input) and `splice_at` (byte-aligned header, mid-byte header at 12 / 1 / 8 bit positions, round-trip through `shift_left`). 117/117 codec-schema tests pass (8 new + 109 existing). Cost: one allocation per encode/decode of the body slice (~22 bytes for VMF K05.1, irrelevant in any tactical workload). The full v6 grammar arc (`schema-ref` field type + cross-schema dispatch by discriminator) tracked in #1411 stays deferred — this lightweight utility delivers the same end result (VMF migration unblocked) with much smaller surface area.

- **ASTERIX datablock + FSPEC chain schema-parity test** — sixth tactical protocol to get a schema-parity test (after STANAG 4586, DIS, MAVLink v1+v2, VMF K05.1, and Link 16 JREAP), and the **second protocol to exercise v5 variable-shift `present-if`** after VMF K05.1 (#1396). Adds `crates/rustgate-asterix/schemas/datablock_fspec.yaml` declaring the 3-byte datablock header (CAT byte + length u16 BE) plus a 1–3 octet FSPEC chain where each octet packs 7 data bits in positions 7..1 with the FX continuation flag at position 0 (LSB). Each FSPEC octet after the first is gated by the previous octet's FX bit via `present-if shift-mode: collapse-when-absent` — when FX=0, the rest of the chain is absent from the wire and the schema runtime shrinks the encoded output accordingly. Three tests in `crates/rustgate-asterix/tests/schema_parity_fspec.rs`: a proptest asserting byte-identical SchemaCodec round-trip against the inline reference encoder for every (cat, length, 1..=3-octet FSPEC chain) combination, a 1-octet golden fixture (4-byte payload), and a 3-octet golden fixture (6-byte all-present maximum). The schema exercises BOTH paths v5 was designed for: VMF demonstrated "absent scalar payload" (16-bit altitude collapses); ASTERIX demonstrates "absent flag byte that itself gates more flag bytes" (octet 2's FX gates octet 3). Per-category record bodies (CAT-021 / CAT-048 / CAT-062 data items) remain out of scope — they need per-category body schemas dispatched at the call site by the `cat` byte.

- **Link 16 JREAP-C frame header schema-parity test** — adds `crates/rustgate-link16/schemas/jreap_header.yaml` and `crates/rustgate-link16/tests/schema_parity_jreap_header.rs`, extending the schema-parity coverage to the 5th tactical protocol after STANAG 4586, DIS, MAVLink (v1+v2), and VMF (K05.1). The schema declares the fixed 16-byte big-endian header (version, message_type, exercise_id, reserved at offsets 0-3 as u8; sequence, timestamp, body_length at offsets 4/8/12 as u32 big-endian). Three tests: a proptest asserting byte-identical SchemaCodec round-trip against the inline reference encoder (the #1397 pattern), a public-API round-trip proptest constrained to JREAP-C version `0x03` (the wrapper rejects any other version at decode), and a golden fixture pinning the byte layout for a canonical header (`version=0x03, message_type=JseriesData, exercise=0x11, sequence=0x12345678, timestamp=0x65535300, body_length=0x100`). Per-message-type body schemas (J2.2 PPLI, J3.x track data, J7.x indirect coordinate, J12.x mission management) remain follow-up work — dispatched at the call site by the header's `message_type` field, same pattern STANAG 4586 / DIS / MAVLink use. The schema carries `version` and `message_type` as raw bytes; the wrapper layer at `src/header.rs` enforces the `version == 0x03` JREAP-C constraint and projects `message_type` bytes to the typed `JreapMessageType` enum, preserving the forward-compat `Other(byte)` arm for unknown bytes.

- **VMF K05.1 Position Report body schema-parity test (closes #1396)** — load-bearing close of the multi-day codec-schema grammar arc. The K05.1 wire format (the Army/USMC PLI message — every Blue Force Tracker position update on a SINCGARS-ASIP or EPLRS radio is a K05.1) was the original blocker that surfaced every gap each grammar revision filled: 25-bit signed latitude and 26-bit signed longitude crossing byte boundaries (v4 cross-byte spans + v4.1 signed types) and the four-level FPI cascade gating altitude → speed → course → unit_identifier (v5 variable-shift `present-if`). This PR adds `crates/rustgate-vmf/schemas/k05_1.yaml` declaring the full 172-bit body layout end-to-end and `crates/rustgate-vmf/tests/schema_parity_k05_1.rs` with a proptest asserting byte-identical SchemaCodec round-trip against an inline reference bit-stream encoder, plus three golden fixtures (all-fields-present pins byte layout, all-FPIs-zero collapses to 11 bytes from a 22-byte all-present allocation via v5 variable-shift, negative latitude / longitude exercise v4.1 sign-extension). Also fixes a load-bearing **validator bug surfaced by this work**: the `present-if` predicate's "must precede" check compared byte offsets, which rejected bit-packed sibling fields at the same byte (`altitude_fpi` at byte 9 bit-offset 3 gating `altitude` at byte 9 bit-offset 4). Updated to compare bit positions (`offset * 8 + bit_offset`), which correctly accepts FPI siblings while still rejecting same-bit-position references. Public API does not change — the production codec at `rustgate-vmf::k05_1::K051PositionReport` stays hand-rolled (the schema-parity test is a declarative pin of the wire layout, not a drop-in replacement); a future PR can migrate the production codec to a SchemaCodec-driven path the parity test will continue to protect. **Grammar features exercised end-to-end for the first time**: v3 (bit-packing, #1389) + v4 (cross-byte spans, #1402) + v4.1 (signed bit-packed, #1404) + v5 (variable-shift `present-if`, #1407). 147/147 tests pass across `rustgate-codec-schema` (103/103) and `rustgate-vmf` (4 new parity tests + 40 existing). With this PR the codec-schema grammar can drive every bit-level tactical protocol layout the workspace ships codecs for; ASTERIX FSPEC chains and Link 16 J-series messages remain follow-up work (their multi-byte continuation patterns map to the same v5 variable-shift mechanism this PR validates).

- **`rustgate-codec-schema` v5 grammar: variable-shift `present-if` (closes #1407)** — extends `PresentIfSpec` with a new `shift-mode` knob that distinguishes two semantic interpretations of "predicate misses". The default `ShiftMode::Reserve` preserves the v3 sparse-projection behaviour: gated bytes/bits stay reserved on the wire whether the predicate matches or not, only the entity projection is gated. The new `ShiftMode::CollapseWhenAbsent` (v5) makes the gated field genuinely disappear from the wire when the predicate misses, with subsequent fields' positions sliding toward the start by the absent field's natural bit-width. **(1) Grammar.** Added `ShiftMode` enum (`Reserve` default, `CollapseWhenAbsent` new) on `PresentIfSpec.shift_mode`; defaults via `#[serde(default)]` so every existing v3 schema continues to parse and validate unchanged. **(2) Validator.** New constraint: `CollapseWhenAbsent` is only supported on bit-packed fields in this revision — byte-aligned collapse (e.g. MAVLink v2's optional 13-byte signature trailer) is a v5.1 follow-up since it requires byte-alignment bookkeeping the bit-packed path doesn't need. **(3) Runtime.** Both `decode_field` and `encode_field` grew a `bit_shift: usize` parameter (the accumulated cursor offset from earlier collapsed fields). The decode and encode loops thread a `bit_shift` accumulator: each `CollapseWhenAbsent`-predicate-misses field contributes its `bit_width` to the accumulator and skips the read/write entirely. For bit-packed fields, the declared `offset * 8 + bit_offset` becomes the position assuming all earlier collapses are present; the actual wire position is that minus `bit_shift`. A new `SchemaCodecError::BitCursorMisalignment` variant surfaces the runtime invariant that byte-aligned fields cannot follow a non-byte-aligned bit-cursor offset. **(4) Wire-size handling.** The decode-side initial bounds check (`payload.len() < size_bytes`) is bypassed for schemas containing any `CollapseWhenAbsent` fields — the wire size becomes variable, and per-field bounds checks fire on too-short input. The encode-side truncates the trailing zero bytes from the pre-zeroed buffer based on accumulated `bit_shift / 8` full bytes. **(5) Tests.** Five new unit tests: predicate-match keeps full-size wire layout, predicate-miss drops field and shifts subsequent fields (3-byte payload from a 4-byte schema), round-trip in both predicate states, validator rejection on non-bit-packed fields, and a two-field cascade (the load-bearing VMF K05.1 pattern) demonstrating both flags set / both flags cleared / mixed combinations. 107/107 codec-schema tests pass (5 new + 102 existing) plus 376/376 downstream tests across `rustgate-stanag4586`, `rustgate-dis`, and `rustgate-mavlink`. **Backward-compatibility**: every previously-valid schema continues to validate and produce byte-identical wire output — the default `ShiftMode::Reserve` matches the v3 behaviour exactly, and the `bit_shift` accumulator stays 0 for schemas without any `CollapseWhenAbsent` fields. Unblocks #1396 (VMF K05.1 body schema-parity test).

- **MAVLink v2 frame header schema-parity test** — adds `crates/rustgate-mavlink/schemas/v2_header.yaml` and `crates/rustgate-mavlink/tests/schema_parity_v2_header.rs`, completing MAVLink wire-format coverage from v1 (6-byte header) to v2 (10-byte header with `incompat_flags` / `compat_flags` and 24-bit msgid). The schema declares ten u8 fields at fixed offsets — `magic` (`0xFD`), `len`, `incompat_flags`, `compat_flags`, `seq`, `sysid`, `compid`, and three msgid bytes (`msgid_lo` / `msgid_mid` / `msgid_hi`) carrying the little-endian 24-bit message id. The msgid stays three independent u8 fields rather than collapsing into one v4-bit-packed 24-bit field because the v4 bit-packing grammar is MSB-first big-endian whereas MAVLink stores the msgid little-endian; using three byte fields matches the wire's actual byte ordering and keeps the byte-identical round-trip cheap. Wrappers recombine via `(msgid_hi as u32) << 16 | (msgid_mid as u32) << 8 | msgid_lo`. Tests include a proptest asserting byte-identical SchemaCodec round-trip against the inline reference encoder (the #1397 pattern), plus three smoke fixtures: a canonical HEARTBEAT header decoding to each named attribute, IFLAG_SIGNED bit (`incompat_flags = 0x01`) round-trip preservation, and 24-bit msgid little-endian decomposition (`0x12_3456` → `lo=0x56, mid=0x34, hi=0x12`). The optional 13-byte signature trailer gated by `IFLAG_SIGNED` is out of scope — it sits after the CRC and needs a variable-presence schema feature (the v5 grammar tracked in #1396 is the natural target). All 4 v2 tests pass alongside the existing v1 parity tests; clippy clean.

- **`rustgate-codec-schema` v4.1 grammar: signed bit-packed types (closes #1403)** — extends v4's bit-packed field types from unsigned-only (`u8/u16/u32/u64`) to also include signed (`i8/i16/i32/i64`). Closes the gap #1402 explicitly punted as the v4.1 follow-up, and is the final grammar piece blocking #1396 (VMF K05.1's signed 25-bit latitude and 26-bit longitude). **(1) Grammar.** No YAML grammar changes — just extends the validator's `max_bits_for_type` table to recognise i8 ≤ 8 bits, i16 ≤ 16 bits, i32 ≤ 32 bits, i64 ≤ 64 bits (same caps as the unsigned counterparts). **(2) Decode.** A new `sign_extend_bit_span` helper sign-extends the raw u64 returned by `read_bit_span` to a 64-bit signed value using the standard two's-complement formula: if the MSB at position `bit_width - 1` is set, OR in `!((1 << bit_width) - 1)` to fill the high bits above the field. The `bit_width = 64` case bitcasts directly (no extension needed). The decode path projects signed-typed bit-packed fields as `DecodedValue::I64` (variant already exists, no plumbing changes) and unsigned types continue to project as `DecodedValue::U64`. **(3) Encode.** Reads `value.as_i64(field)?`, range-checks against the two's-complement domain `[-2^(N-1), 2^(N-1) - 1]` (special-cased for `bit_width = 64` where the full i64 range fits trivially), bitcasts to u64, and masks to `bit_width` bits before feeding the shared `write_bit_span` path so negative values' sign-extended high bits don't leak past the field. **(4) Tests.** Five new unit tests: `sign_extend_bit_span_handles_positive_negative_and_zero` (4-bit / 25-bit / 64-bit edge cases including `i64::MIN/MAX`), `signed_bit_packed_round_trips_through_schema_codec` (25-bit i32 representative of VMF latitude, both -1 and -16,777,216 round-trip byte-identical), `signed_bit_packed_rejects_value_outside_two_s_complement_range` (i8 with bit_width = 8 rejects 128 and -129 with `i8 (bit-packed)` error type), `signed_bit_packed_full_width_i64_round_trips_i64_min_max` (every i64 edge value round-trips on a `bit_width = 64` field), `signed_bit_packed_one_bit_carries_zero_and_minus_one` (1-bit signed domain is `{-1, 0}`, value 1 rejects). Updated the validator's signed-type rejection test to only reject floats and bytes (signed is now accepted), with a new `accepts_bit_packed_on_signed_integer_types_v4_1` covering all four signed types at max width. All 102 codec-schema tests pass (6 new + 96 existing) plus 372 downstream tests across `rustgate-stanag4586`, `rustgate-dis`, and `rustgate-mavlink`. Backward-compatible — every previously-valid v4 schema continues to validate and produce byte-identical wire output.

- **`rustgate-codec-schema` v4 grammar: cross-byte bit spans (closes #1399)** — lifts the v3 single-byte `bit_offset + bit_width <= 8` constraint and extends bit-packed field types from `u8`-only to `u8 / u16 / u32 / u64`. Unblocks #1396 (VMF K05.1 body with its 24-bit URN, 25-bit latitude, 26-bit longitude, …) and the analogous ASTERIX FSPEC chain port. **(1) Grammar.** `bit_width` extends from `[1, 8]` to `[1, 64]`; `bit_offset` stays `[0, 7]` (still the byte-relative starting position). Each field type pairs with a natural max width: `u8` ≤ 8 bits, `u16` ≤ 16 bits, `u32` ≤ 32 bits, `u64` ≤ 64 bits. Signed types (`i8 / i16 / i32 / i64`) remain unsupported for bit-packing — sign-extension on decode is a v4.1 follow-up. **(2) Runtime.** Two new helpers in `codec.rs` (`read_bit_span` and `write_bit_span`) replace the v3 single-byte `(byte >> shift) & mask` formulation with an MSB-first big-endian bit stream walker that threads a bit cursor across as many bytes as `bit_offset + bit_width` consumes. Each affected byte is read-modify-written via mask-and-OR so sibling bit-packed fields at touched bytes stay intact — the v3 sibling-preservation invariant extends naturally to cross-byte spans. v3 single-byte fields (`bit_offset + bit_width ≤ 8`) take the same code path with the inner loop iterating exactly once, producing byte-identical output. **(3) Validator.** Overlap detection extends from a per-byte `HashMap<usize, u8>` lookup (single-byte check) to walking every byte a bit-packed field touches via a new `bit_packed_byte_masks` iterator. The byte-range overlap check now allows a bit-packed field whose touched bytes share ANY byte with a prior bit-packed field (canonical packed-flag-byte pattern at one byte; cross-byte FPI chains at multiple). The `prev_end` size calculation overrides typed `fixed_size()` with the actual touched-byte count for bit-packed fields, so a 12-bit `u16` at `bit_offset = 4` advances `prev_end` by 2 bytes (not the u16's natural 2-byte size, which would coincide here but diverges for a 16-bit u16 at `bit_offset = 4` that touches 3 bytes). **(4) Tests.** Twelve new unit tests pin (a) `read_bit_span` matches the v3 single-byte formula bit-for-bit, (b) 12-bit / 25-bit / 32-bit cross-byte reads work, (c) `write_bit_span` round-trips through `read_bit_span` for representative `(bit_offset, bit_width, value)` combinations, (d) sibling bits outside the field's claimed range are preserved at the head, middle, and tail of multi-byte spans, (e) end-to-end through `SchemaCodec::to_entity / from_entity` for a 12-bit `u16` field, (f) two bit-packed fields sharing a byte boundary both round-trip (1-bit flag + 15-bit cross-byte u16), (g) `bit_width = 64` on a `u64` field round-trips `u64::MAX`. Validator gains tests for the new acceptance paths (cross-byte u16, max-width u16/u32/u64) and the new rejection paths (`bit_width 12 exceeds u8 capacity`, `bit_width 65 must be in [1, 64]`, signed/float field types). All 96 codec-schema tests pass (12 new + 84 existing) plus 372 downstream tests across `rustgate-stanag4586`, `rustgate-dis`, and `rustgate-mavlink`. The v3 grammar surface is fully backward-compatible — every previously-valid v3 schema continues to validate and produce byte-identical wire output.

- **DIS Entity Appearance bitfield schema-parity test (closes #1400)** — first cross-protocol confidence test exercising the v3 bit-packing grammar from #1389 on a real wire-format bit layout. The 4-byte Entity Appearance field at body offset 72..76 of an Entity State PDU is carried as an opaque `u32` by the production codec today; this PR adds `crates/rustgate-dis/schemas/entity_appearance.yaml` decomposing the bits per IEEE 1278.1-2012 § 5.3.3.1.6 Land Platform layout (`paint_scheme` 1 bit, `mobility_kill` 1 bit, `firepower_kill` 1 bit, `damage` 2 bits, `smoke` 2 bits, `trailing_effects` 1 bit packed into byte 3; `hatch` 3 bits, `head_lights` / `tail_lights` / `brake_lights` / `flaming` / `launcher` 1 bit each packed into byte 2; `camouflage_type` 2 bits, `concealed` / `frozen` / `power_plant` / `state` / `tent` / `ramp` 1 bit each packed into byte 1; byte 0 opaque for IEEE-spec-revision extension) and `crates/rustgate-dis/tests/schema_parity_entity_appearance.rs` asserting byte-identical round-trip via the inline-reference-encoder pattern from #1397. Multi-field-per-byte packing is exercised end-to-end — byte 3 alone carries six declared bit-packed fields composed by the schema runtime's mask-and-OR path without clobbering siblings. Every field in the IEEE 1278.1 Land Platform layout fits within a single byte (the v3 grammar's `bit_offset + bit_width <= 8` validator passes uniformly); #1399 tracks the v4 grammar extension (cross-byte bit spans) that would unblock VMF K05.1 (#1396) and ASTERIX FSPEC chains. Public API does not change — `EntityStatePdu::appearance` stays a raw `u32`; the schema-parity test is a declarative pin of what those bits mean, ready for a future PR that introduces a typed `LandPlatformAppearance` Rust struct. Two tests: a proptest with each bit-field constrained to its declared bit-width range (paint_scheme `0..=1`, damage `0..=3`, hatch `0..=7`, …) and a golden fixture pinning every bit at maximum value to `[0xCC, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF]` against off-by-one bit-offset regressions.

- **DIS Entity State PDU body schema-parity test (closes #1395)** — first confidence test exercising the v3 schema grammar's variable-length repeat (`count-from`) on a real protocol body. `pdu_header.yaml` previously only covered the fixed-12-byte common header (#1373); this PR adds `crates/rustgate-dis/schemas/entity_state.yaml` (132-byte fixed prefix + `N×16-byte` articulation parameters tail) and `crates/rustgate-dis/tests/schema_parity_entity_state.rs` asserting byte-identical round-trip via the inline-reference-encoder pattern from #1397. Composite sub-structs (`entity_id`, `entity_type`, `dead_reckoning`, `linear_velocity` / `location_ecef` / `orientation`) are carried as opaque `bytes` blobs at their documented offsets — the parity contract is byte-equivalence and the schema runtime's f32/f64 encoder rejects non-finite inputs per #1362, so typed primitive splits would need NaN filtering at the strategy level just to make the round-trip well-defined. Two proptests: **path (a)** `reference_encode → SchemaCodec::to_entity → SchemaCodec::from_entity` round-trips byte-equal for arbitrary `(entity_id, force_id, entity_type, …, articulation_parameters: Vec<[u8; 16]>)` inputs with articulation counts 0..=8; **path (c)** `EntityStatePdu::encode → EntityStatePdu::decode` round-trips every typed field of the wrapper struct (constrained to finite floats and NUL-free ASCII marking per the production codec's documented round-trip domain). This proves the v3 schema runtime can drive a non-trivial protocol body, not just headers — the load-bearing claim behind the schema-first refactor. Body schema cross-checked against `crates/rustgate-dis/src/entity_state.rs::EntityStatePdu::{decode,encode}`. The 144-byte total PDU still rides on per-call-site header+body composition (`schema chaining` lands in a future v4 schema feature).

### Fixed

- **Federation V2 inbound group allowlist is now enforced from config (closes #1508).** The per-peer inbound group allowlist the V2 federation service checks on every inbound RPC path was only ever populated in tests — the `FederationManager` built the service with `.with_max_hops(…)` but never called `.with_allowed_peer_groups(…)`, leaving it `None` and running every enforcement gate in open mode, so any mTLS-authenticated peer could claim arbitrary groups. The manager now projects each configured peer's `inbound_groups` (falling back to `groups`) into the allowlist, activating the already-shipped enforcement.

- **Foundry inbound honors `change_type=Deleted` instead of resurrecting the object (closes #1499).** The inbound projection (`change_to_message`) built a live `Broadcast` entity from a change's property bag regardless of its `change_type`, so a `Deleted` ontology change re-injected the last-seen object downstream as if it were live — deleted objects resurrected. A `Deleted` change is now dropped (not re-projected); `Created`/`Updated` are unaffected. A typed cross-protocol delete/tombstone is a follow-up — the `Entity` shape carries no delete marker yet.

- **`rustgate-server`'s `marti-compat` feature now enables `missions` (build fix).** Building the server with `--features marti-compat` (e.g. the `marti-compat,metrics` feature-powerset combo exercised by CI's `check-features` job) failed to compile: `rustgate-admin`'s `marti-compat` turns on admin's `missions` API — which adds the `missions_api` parameter to the metrics server's `serve()` — but the server crate's `marti-compat` did not enable its own `missions` feature, so the `setup.rs` call site supplied one fewer argument than `serve()` declared (E0061). The server's `marti-compat` feature now also enables `missions`, aligning the two sides.

- **Position-cache eviction ranks by a monotonic sequence, not wall-clock `received_at` (F-191, closes #1542).** At capacity, the position cache evicted the entry with the oldest `received_at`. An NTP step-back can give a freshly-stored entry an *earlier* wall-clock timestamp than entries already cached, so the brand-new entry would be picked as "oldest" and evicted on arrival — losing the most current position for that client. Eviction now ranks by a monotonic per-store sequence number (immune to clock changes); the least-recently-stored entry is evicted as intended.

- **XML stream codec rejects a stray close tag instead of wedging the connection (closes #1507).** `XmlStreamCodec`'s framer returned "need more bytes" when it hit a close tag with no matching open element (depth 0), so a stray/unbalanced `</tag>` was never consumed and never errored — the connection buffered forever (until the 16 MiB frame cap) and any valid documents queued behind it were stuck. `find_element_end` now distinguishes *incomplete* (`Ok(None)`, wait for more bytes) from *malformed* (a depth-0 close tag → fatal `io::ErrorKind::InvalidData`), and the stream listener drops + audits the connection.

- **Non-CoT dedup key now binds `source_protocol` (F-189, closes #1531).** The router's deduplication cache keyed non-CoT (binary) payloads on `(tenant, cn, time-window, payload-hash)` but not the protocol, so two *different* protocols whose raw bytes coincide (e.g. a DIS PDU and an ASTERIX datablock from the same sender at the same instant) could cross-dedupe — one legitimately-distinct message silently dropped. `metadata.source_protocol` is now folded into the non-CoT key preimage (`SHA-256(b"non-cot" || … || cn || 0x00 || source_protocol || 0x00 || time || 0x00 || sha256(payload))`). The CoT path is unchanged — it correctly dedups the same event arriving across transports.

- **Correlation keys a source by `(source_id, source_protocol)`, not `source_id` alone (closes #1501).** The engine's same-source check compared only `source_id == uid`, so the same wire UID arriving over two different protocols (a DIS entity 1234 and a VMF entity 1234) was wrongly treated as an in-place update of a single source rather than two independent sensors to fuse — silently overwriting one feed's track and corrupting provenance. `find_same_source` and `update_source` now match on the `(source_id, source_protocol)` tuple the module already documents.

- **Operator clean shutdown no longer hangs on a non-signal exit (closes #1505).** The signal-handler task only completed on `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`, but `main` also flips the shutdown watch when the controller returns for a non-signal reason (error or natural completion) and then `await`s that task — which blocked forever waiting for a signal that would never arrive, so the process never exited. The signal task now also selects on the shutdown watch and exits when shutdown is triggered elsewhere.

- **Admin/metrics HTTP server survives a transient `accept()` error (closes #1503).** The accept loop propagated the first `accept()` error with `?`, permanently killing `/metrics`, `/healthz`, `/readyz`, and the admin APIs.
