A single transient `EMFILE`/`ENFILE` (fd exhaustion) would take down the liveness probe and could cascade into the orchestrator killing an otherwise-healthy pod. The loop now logs the error, backs off briefly (so a persistent condition doesn't hot-spin), and keeps serving — matching the continue-on-error behaviour of the data-plane listeners.

- **Reject MQTT topic prefixes in the reserved `$` namespace (F-192, closes #1532).** `validate_topic_prefix` only checked that a non-empty prefix ends with `/`; it accepted prefixes beginning with `$` (e.g. `$SYS/`, `$share/`). MQTT reserves topics whose first level starts with `$` for the broker, so such a prefix would route every topic into broker-reserved names (collision / silent drop). The validator now rejects a leading `$` with `InvalidTopic`. An empty prefix remains "no prefix" per the documented, tested contract.

- **Register the Meshtastic codec in the server's `EntityCodecRegistry` (F-186, closes #1530).** `rustgate-meshtastic`'s `MeshtasticCodec` existed but was never registered in the server's startup registry (which wired cot/mavlink/asterix/stanag4586/dis/vmf/sapient/link16/nffi), so Meshtastic traffic silently lost `entity_kind` classification, by-kind metrics, and cross-protocol type info. Registered it, and extracted the registry build into `build_entity_codec_registry()` with a unit test that pins the full protocol set so a future codec cannot be silently left unregistered. This is the registry wiring of the existing codec only — the LoRa ingress path remains #1491.

- **Config JSON schema regenerated + its drift guard wired into CI (closes #1565)** — `schemas/rustgate-v0.8.json` (the JSON Schema operators point TOML editors at for `rustgate.toml` autocomplete / validation) had silently drifted ~25% stale: 168 of the 224 current config keys. Entire operator-facing surfaces were missing — every tactical-ingress flag (`dis-*`/`asterix-*`/`vmf-*`/`stanag4586-*`/`sapient-*`/`link16-*`/`nffi-*` + `*-multicast-group`), all `mavlink-*`, `air-gap`, `cnsa2`, `packages-*`, `inference-config-file`, and the `lattice`/`ogc-sensorthings`/`guard` config-file keys. The protective regression test (`rustgate-server/tests/schema_export.rs`, which re-emits the schema and asserts a byte-for-byte match) already existed but was **dead** — gated behind a `schema` cargo feature present in **no** CI feature list, so the file rotted unnoticed. Regenerated deterministically via `rustgate emit-schema` (now 224 properties) and added `schema` to the `nextest` job's feature set so the drift guard runs on every PR.

- **`mask_cert_serial` / `mask_credential` no longer panic on multi-byte UTF-8 (remote DoS fix, closes #1534)** — both maskers in `rustgate-core::masking` sliced strings by **byte** index (`&serial[..4]`, `&serial[serial.len()-4..]`, `&s[..2]`). A multi-byte UTF-8 cert serial or credential made those slices land mid-codepoint and panic; because the maskers run on the audit/log emission path, a single unusual value flowing through any masked audit event was a remote denial-of-service. Both now count and slice by `char`. Regression tests feed multi-byte (`€`) inputs that panicked under the old byte-slicing.

- **`TakControl` protocol-version fields are now `uint32`, matching the public TAK wire format (closes #1463)** — surfaced during the ADR 0021 clean-room provenance audit. The vendored `rustgate-proto` `TakControl` message declared `minProtoVersion` / `maxProtoVersion` as `string`, but the public TAK protocol encodes them as `uint32`. On the same field numbers this is **not wire-compatible**: protobuf encodes `string` as length-delimited (wire type 2) and `uint32` as varint (wire type 0), so a real TAK peer negotiating protocol versions via `TakControl` would fail to decode our fields (or we theirs). **(1) Proto.** `crates/rustgate-proto/proto/takcontrol.proto` now declares both version fields as `uint32` (`contactUid` stays `string`); the `rustgate-federation` copy already used `uint32`, so no change there. **(2) Negotiation code.** `negotiate.rs` `build_tak_response` writes the version as a `u32`, and `parse_tak_request` validates a typed `u32` directly. The F-64 forced-upgrade hardening is preserved across the type change: proto3 decodes an unset scalar to its `0` default, so `require_version` rejects `0` (the lowest real version is `1`) exactly as the old parser rejected an empty/blank string — a client that omits either field is still refused rather than silently mapped to the server's full supported range. **(3) Error type.** `ProtoError::BlankVersion` doc updated to describe the zero/unset semantics (variant and wire behavior unchanged). **(4) Tests.** All `TakControl` construction sites updated to the `u32` fields; the whitespace-string rejection test (meaningless for `uint32`) is replaced by min- and max-side zero-rejection tests; a new wire-type pin asserts `TakControl { min: 1, max: 2 }` encodes to exactly `[0x08, 0x01, 0x10, 0x02]` (varint tags `0x08` / `0x10`, not the `0x0A` / `0x12` a `string` would emit), so a future regression back to `string` fails at compile-time. This is a wire-correctness fix, not an IP change — the divergence was one of the things that made our schemas demonstrably non-verbatim (ADR 0021), but it becomes a real interop bug the moment the TAK-compat work (#1455) speaks the stream/mesh protocol to live TAK clients.

- **Schema-parity proptests hardened against the SchemaCodec-against-itself tautology (closes #1394)** — three `tests/schema_parity.rs` files (`rustgate-stanag4586`, `rustgate-dis`, `rustgate-mavlink`) previously used the protocol's public `encode` / `decode` for one half of the round-trip and `SchemaCodec` for the other. After PR #1390 made the STANAG production `encode` / `decode` itself a thin wrapper over `SchemaCodec`, that parity test was silently round-tripping `SchemaCodec` against `SchemaCodec` — encoder bugs that lose data symmetrically (e.g. buffer zeroing on a finite-float rejection, the #1393 STANAG `vehicle_id → 0` regression that the weekly-fuzz harness caught) passed trivially. Fix has two parts. **(1) Inline reference encoders.** Each `tests/schema_parity.rs` now defines a hand-coded `reference_encode` (STANAG / DIS) or `v1_reference_encode` (MAVLink) directly in the test file, byte-coded against the schema YAML's documented offsets. The parity assertion is `reference_encode → SchemaCodec::to_entity → SchemaCodec::from_entity == reference_encode`, a genuine cross-implementation comparison the production codec cannot accidentally make tautological even if it migrates to a SchemaCodec-driven path in the future. **(2) Public-API round-trip proptests.** STANAG and DIS gained a `public_api_round_trip_preserves_typed_fields` proptest that exercises the production `encode → decode` path and asserts every typed field of the wrapper struct survives the round-trip — the exact invariant the weekly-fuzz target asserts, now at compile-time. STANAG's variant additionally tolerates NaN on `altitude_msl_m` / `ground_speed_mps` / `heading_deg` per the codec's documented contract (in-flight calibration ships signed / unwrapped values). MAVLink does not gain a (c)-variant because the production `MavlinkFrameCodec` operates on raw `BytesMut` and exposes no typed v1-header struct — if a future refactor introduces a typed `V1Header` wrapper with its own `encode_into` / `decode`, mirror the STANAG / DIS proptest then. All three parity tests still pass and now defend against the next #1390-class regression at proptest time.

- **`rustgate-codec-schema` hardening pass (XTCE v1 rough edges)** — three correctness fixes the post-merge review surfaced before any real codec port lands on the schema runtime:
  - **Multi-message schemas now fail at `Schema::validate`** instead of silently picking the first message type at decode. v1 has no discriminator-byte dispatch, so a 2-message schema was producing systematically-wrong decodes for payloads matching the non-first variant. The `discriminator_offset` field stays in the grammar (v2 schemas will not need a wire-format change), and the validator's error message points operators at the splitting workaround.
  - **`f32` / `f64` encode rejects non-finite values with a typed `OutOfRange`.** The `f64 as f32` cast in `encode_field` was silently saturating to `±f32::INFINITY` for out-of-range inputs and propagating `NaN` for `NaN` inputs — both almost always indicate a calibration bug, not a real measurement. Surface the failure on encode, not on the wire.
  - **`u64` round-trip is byte-exact for values with the high bit set.** Decode projects `u64` wire values through `AttributeValue::Int(i64)` (the only integer variant `Entity::attributes` carries), so a `u64` with its high bit set arrived at encode time as a "negative" `i64` and tripped the `as_u64` rejection. Bit-cast `i64 → u64` in the encoder; per-type bounds checks on `U8` / `U16` / `U32` still catch values that genuinely overflow the field width. Caught by the new proptest harness.

- **proptest harness on the schema codec** (`tests/proptest_codec.rs`). Two properties: (1) `decode_does_not_panic` exercises every primitive kind × endian × arbitrary payload bytes (including float NaN / subnormal / inf bit patterns) and asserts the codec never crashes the process; (2) `integer_payload_round_trips_byte_exact` generates arbitrary integer payloads, decodes through the attribute fallback, re-encodes, and asserts byte-equality with the original. This is the property that surfaced the `u64` high-bit bug above and now pins the fix.

- **`cargo check --workspace --all-targets` now passes on the default feature set.** Two targets in `rustgate-federation` referenced `v2`-gated symbols (`v2::proto::*`, `FederationManager::create_v2_event_handler`) without their own `#[cfg(feature = "v2")]` gate:
  - `benches/convert.rs` — added `required-features = ["v2"]` to the matching `[[bench]]` block in `Cargo.toml`. Cleaner than a source-level cfg, which would empty the file and break criterion's `main` symbol expectation under `harness = false`.
  - `manager.rs::tests::v2_handler_forwards_when_peer_groups_trusted` — added `#[cfg(feature = "v2")]` (the adjacent `v2_handler_forwards_even_with_untrusted_wire_groups` test already had the gate; this one was missed when the pair was originally added).

  Pre-existing defect; closes a CI-only red flag that would have surfaced as soon as any contributor ran the canonical workspace check locally.

### Changed

- **`rustgate-stanag4586` `vehicle_position` codec ported to `SchemaCodec`** — `crates/rustgate-stanag4586/src/vehicle_position.rs` now drives `encode` / `decode` / `encode_into` through `rustgate_codec_schema::SchemaCodec` over the embedded `schemas/vehicle_position.yaml` instead of the previous hand-rolled big-endian field-by-field implementation. Public API is unchanged (`VehiclePosition`, `FlightState`, the three free functions); the byte-identical round-trip is pinned by the existing `tests/schema_parity.rs` proptest (256 random inputs, including every `FlightState::Other(byte)` byte value). Schema changes: added `range: { min: -90.0, max: 90.0 }` on `latitude_deg` and `range: { min: -180.0, max: 180.0 }` on `longitude_deg` so the WGS-84 rejects fire at the schema layer; `flight_state` deliberately stays a raw `u8` with no value-mapping because the v2 typed value-mapping is lossy for `FlightState::Other(byte)` — every unknown byte would collapse to a single default label and re-encode to the same byte, breaking the parity contract. The enum mapping (`0x01` ↔ `LaunchPreparation`, …) lives in the Rust wrapper rather than the schema; the wrapper also keeps the explicit `is_nan()` reject on lat / lon decode because the schema's range guard accepts NaN by construction (`NaN < min || NaN > max` is false in both halves). New error variant `Stanag4586Error::Schema(String)` carries the long tail of schema-runtime errors without growing the public API for the per-error case (`FrameTooShort` and `FieldOutOfRange` retain their dedicated variants and load-bearing field names). `rustgate-codec-schema` moves from a dev-dep to a regular dep on this crate.

- **`Entity` `Tasking` / `FileRef` review polish (closes #1376)** — three follow-up fixes from the review of #1358:
  - `TaskingState` and `TaskingRole` switched from `rename_all = "kebab-case"` to `rename_all = "snake_case"` to match the sibling closed-vocabulary enums on `Entity` (`EntityKind`, `AttributeValue`). Every variant in the current vocabulary is single-word so the wire bytes are identical today, but a future `InProgress`-style addition would have silently split the wire form across sibling enums.
  - Added byte-length cap constants (`MAX_TASK_ID_LEN = 256`, `MAX_TASKING_NAME_LEN = 256`, `MAX_FILE_REF_URI_LEN = 4 KiB`, `MAX_FILE_REF_LABEL_LEN = 256`, `MAX_FILE_REF_MIME_LEN = 256`, `MAX_FILE_HASH_ALGORITHM_LEN = 32`, `MAX_FILE_HASH_HEX_LEN = 512`) and `Tasking::validate` / `FileRef::validate` / `FileHash::validate` defensive checks operators can call on inbound values before storing them. Mirrors the `MAX_CN_LENGTH = 256` / `MAX_ATTR_BAG_BYTES = 4 KiB` precedent.
  - Field docstrings now point operators at `crate::sanitize::sanitize_for_log` for the operator-facing strings (`Tasking::task_id`, `Tasking::name`, `FileRef::uri`, `FileRef::label`) — those carry caller-supplied bytes that can include CR/LF and need scrubbing before structured-tracing inclusion.
  - 6 new tests: wire-form pinning (`"acknowledged"` / `"subject"` JSON regression), unknown-variant rejection for both enums (`"bogus"` → `unknown variant` error), and oversize-string rejection for `Tasking` / `FileRef` / `FileHash`.

### Added

- **`rustgate-router` Prometheus metrics for `MessageInterceptor` verdicts** — operationalises the SPI shipped in #1379. Adds `rustgate_router_interceptor_verdict_total{verdict}` counter with `verdict ∈ {"allow", "drop", "modify"}`, fires once per interceptor invocation. Wired via a new `OnInterceptorVerdict` callback slot on `Router` (matches the existing `On*` ArcSwap pattern); `rustgate-server` installs the counter behind its `metrics` feature. Operators can now observe whether interceptors are firing and what verdicts they're returning at the per-verdict cardinality.

- **`rustgate-codec-schema` v3 bit-packed sub-byte fields (closes #1388)** — third v3 grammar feature, after conditional fields (#1385) and variable-length repeats (#1387). `FieldDef` gains optional `bit_offset` (in `[0, 7]`) and `bit_width` (in `[1, 8]`) attributes declaring a sub-byte integer subrange within ONE byte at the field's `offset`. The MSB of the byte is bit-position 0 (big-endian bit ordering), and the field must fit entirely within the single byte (`bit_offset + bit_width <= 8`) — cross-byte packing (Link 16 word-level fields spanning multiple bytes) is a separate v4 feature. The canonical use cases this unlocks are 1-bit flags and small packed enums: VMF FPI / FRI / GPI indicators, ASTERIX FSPEC bitmaps, Link 16 J-series sub-words. On decode the runtime reads the byte at `field.offset`, applies `(byte >> (8 - bit_offset - bit_width)) & ((1 << bit_width) - 1)`, and projects the extracted integer as a `DecodedValue::U64`. On encode the symmetric path reads the integer from the entity, shifts it into position, and OR-merges into the byte at `field.offset` **without clobbering** other bit-packed fields sharing the byte (the output buffer is pre-zeroed; subsequent sibling bit-fields read the in-progress byte and preserve already-written bits). `Schema::validate` rejects: `bit_offset` set without `bit_width` (or vice versa), `bit_offset >= 8`, `bit_width == 0` or `> 8`, `bit_offset + bit_width > 8`, bit-packing combined with `length_bytes` / `repeat` / `value_mapping` (incoherent in v3 — pick one), bit-packing on non-`u8` field types, two bit-packed fields at the same byte offset whose bit ranges intersect, and `range.max` exceeding the bit-width's raw capacity (only when no `calibration` reshapes the physical scale). Eight new tests (seven validator, four codec): positive case for packed flag byte, plus rejections for missing `bit_width`, `bit_offset` ≥ 8, `bit_offset + bit_width > 8`, `length_bytes` / `value_mapping` combinations, intersecting bit-range overlap, non-`u8` field type, and codec coverage for 1-bit MSB decode, 3-bit low-nibble decode, byte-identical round-trip across a packed-flag-byte schema, and same-byte encode-without-clobber proving the OR-merge correctness.

- **`rustgate-codec-schema` v3 variable-length repeats via `count-from` (closes #1386)** — second v3 grammar feature, after conditional fields (#1385). `FieldDef` gains an optional `repeat: { count_from, record_size_bytes }` spec that makes a `Bytes`-typed field's wire span a function of an earlier-decoded integer count field. The canonical "preceding count byte then N records" pattern that every variable-length tactical protocol uses — DIS articulation parameters (u8 count + 16-byte records), ASTERIX repetitive items (REP prefix + sub-record array), MAVLink v2 payloads (`len` byte driving 0..=255 payload bytes), Link 16 word-3 extensions. On decode the runtime reads `record_size_bytes × count` bytes starting at `field.offset` and surfaces them as a single `DecodedValue::Bytes` slice the consumer parses themselves (nested typed-record schemas — each element with its own field list — are a separate v4 feature). On encode the symmetric path reads the same count from the entity attribute (hex-string fallback included), writes the bytes back, and **grows the output buffer** when the dynamic end exceeds `mt.size_bytes` so operators can set `size_bytes` to the header length and emit wire-truthful variable payloads. `Schema::validate` rejects: `repeat` on a non-`Bytes` field type, `count_from` referencing an unknown field, `count_from` of a non-integer type, forward-referenced `count_from` (must precede the repeat field), `record_size_bytes == 0`, and `length_bytes` + `repeat` declared on the same field. The per-field overlap check uses `record_size_bytes × max_count_for_field_type` (capped at `size_bytes`) so subsequent fields cannot alias the repeat region for any in-range count; the dynamic bound (`record_size_bytes × actual_count ≤ remaining_bytes`) fires on every decode. Seven new validator tests (positive case + the six rejection rules) and seven new codec tests (decode reads the right span, decode with count=0 produces empty bytes, byte-identical round-trip, truncated payload surfaces `PayloadTooShort`, encode grows output to fit variable payload, encode with count=0 produces header-only output, `u16` count drives arrays > 255 records).

- **`rustgate-router` `MessageInterceptor` SPI (closes #1378)** — third-party plugins / integration adapters / on-prem policy shims can now hook the router's forward path to **inspect**, **modify**, or **drop** messages without forking `Router` itself. Interceptors fire inside `Router::route_for_egress` AFTER tenant-stamping and BEFORE ACL / dedup / PEP / fanout — the canonical pre-routing point where modifications still flow through every downstream policy check.
  - **Type alias** `MessageInterceptor = Arc<dyn Fn(InterceptorContext<'_>) -> InterceptorVerdict + Send + Sync>` matches the workspace's existing `On*` callback pattern (object-safe `Fn`, not `AsyncFn`; async work uses `spawn_background` in the closure body).
  - **Verdict enum** `InterceptorVerdict` with `Allow` (pass through), `Drop(&'static str)` (terminate immediately, fires the per-tenant `on_dropped_by_tenant` callback with the synthetic `interceptor` reason), and `Modify(Box<RoutableMessage>)` (replace the in-flight message — subsequent interceptors and downstream policy see the modified form).
  - **Builder** `Router::with_interceptor(MessageInterceptor) -> Self` appends in declaration order; **hot-swap** `Router::replace_interceptors(Vec<…>)` atomically replaces the whole chain via `ArcSwap`. Hot path on the uninstalled (default) build is a single `ArcSwap::load` + `is_empty()` check.
  - **Tests** — 5 new in `router::tests::interceptor_*` cover Allow / Drop (with audit-metric verification) / Modify (payload replacement visible to subscribers) / chain ordering with first-Drop-wins / hot-swap.

- **MAVLink v1 header schema-parity test** — third cross-protocol confidence test for the declarative XTCE-style schema vocabulary (after STANAG 4586 in #1365 and DIS in #1373). Ships `crates/rustgate-mavlink/schemas/v1_header.yaml` describing the 6-byte v1 frame header (magic `0xFE` + len + seq + sysid + compid + msgid, all `u8`) and a `tests/schema_parity.rs` proptest asserting byte-identical round-trip for every arbitrary input, plus a companion smoke test demonstrating v2 `value-mapping` projection on `msgid = 0` → `"HEARTBEAT"`. Hand-rolled v1/v2 frame codec stays in place; v2 (10-byte header + signature trailer) and per-msgid payload schemas remain follow-ups.

- **DIS PDU-header schema-parity test** — second cross-protocol confidence test for the declarative XTCE-style schema vocabulary (the first is STANAG 4586 in #1365). Ships `crates/rustgate-dis/schemas/pdu_header.yaml` describing the 12-byte IEEE 1278.1-2012 common header (clause 5.2.32) — `u8` protocol_version / exercise_id / pdu_type / protocol_family + `u32` timestamp + two `u16` length / padding — and a `tests/schema_parity.rs` proptest that asserts byte-identical round-trip against the hand-rolled `PduHeader::encode_into` for every arbitrary input. A companion non-parity test demonstrates v2 typed `value-mapping` projection on the `pdu_type` byte (raw `1` → `"EntityState"` label on `Entity::attributes`). The hand-rolled codec stays in place; per-PDU body schemas remain out of scope until the schema grammar grows variable-length record support (v3).

- **`rustgate-codec-schema` v3 conditional fields via `present-if`** — first v3 grammar feature. `FieldDef` gains an optional `present-if: { field, value }` predicate gating the field's projection onto another field's raw integer value at a strictly lower offset. The runtime uses the **sparse-projection** interpretation: the bytes at the conditional field's offset stay reserved on the wire whether or not the predicate matches (subsequent offsets never shift), only the `Entity` projection is gated. When the predicate matches, the field projects exactly like an unconditional one; when it misses, decode skips the projection (no attribute, no `entity_path` target update) and encode leaves the bytes at their pre-filled zero. Real protocols use this for fields gated on a preceding flag — DIS articulation params (gated on `articulation_params_count > 0`), MAVLink v2 signatures (gated on `incompat_flags & IFLAG_SIGNED`), ASTERIX FRNs (gated on FSPEC bits). `Schema::validate` rejects predicates that reference unknown fields, fields at the same-or-later offset, non-integer field types, and `present-if` combined with `value-mapping` on the same field. Variable-shift semantics (where the field actually disappears from the wire) are a separate v4 feature. Five new validator tests (positive case, unknown reference, forward reference, float predicate, present-if + value-mapping rejection) and five new codec tests (decode projects on match, decode skips on miss, encode writes on match, encode leaves zero on miss, round-trip in both predicate states).

- **`rustgate-codec-schema` v2 typed value-mapping projection** — the `ValueMapping { entries, default_raw }` grammar that v1 parsed-but-ignored now drives the runtime. On decode, a field with `value-mapping` projects the wire integer to the matching `AttributeValue::Str` label (e.g. raw byte `0x01` → `"friend"` for a NATO affiliation field); unknown raw values fall back to the `default_raw` entry if configured, otherwise surface `SchemaCodecError::UnmappedValue`. On encode, the reverse lookup converts the label back to the raw integer; unknown labels fall back to `default_raw` if set, else `UnmappedValue`. `Schema::validate` rejects schemas that combine `value-mapping` with `calibration` or `range` (incoherent semantics — the integer is replaced by a string), value-mapping on non-integer field types, and `default_raw` values that don't have a matching entry. Closes the v1 "ValueMapping parses but is ignored" gap noted in the codec-module docs. Four new schema-validator tests and six new codec tests (label projection, default-raw fallback on unmapped byte, UnmappedValue surfaces when no default, label → raw reverse lookup, byte-identical round-trip across the full mapping, default-raw fallback on unmapped label).

- **`rustgate-codec-schema` v2 multi-message dispatch** — schemas with more than one `message-types` entry now decode + encode through a single `SchemaCodec`. The schema declares a 1-byte `discriminator-offset`; on decode, the runtime reads the byte at that offset and selects the message-type whose `id` matches. The discriminator byte round-trips through `Entity::attributes` under `schema.<protocol>.__discriminator__` so a subsequent encode emits the same variant without the call site needing to track it externally. Five new schema tests (positive multi-message validate, missing discriminator_offset, duplicate ids, `id > 255`, plus the prior single-message tests still pass) and five new codec tests (dispatch picks the right variant by byte, unknown discriminator surfaces `SchemaCodecError::UnknownDiscriminator`, decode writes the byte to attributes, round-trip stays byte-identical for both variants, encode without the discriminator attribute fails with `MissingRequiredEntityField`). Closes the v1 hardening item that previously rejected multi-message schemas outright.

- **`rustgate-codec-schema` v2 range constraints** — `FieldDef` gains an optional `range: { min, max }` constraint applied to the *physical* value (post-calibration on decode, pre-reverse-calibration on encode). Decode and encode both reject out-of-range values with `SchemaCodecError::OutOfRange` so the error vocabulary is symmetric on both sides of the wire. `Schema::validate` rejects ranges whose bounds are non-finite or whose `max` < `min`, so operator typos surface at schema-load time. Composes with `Calibration`: an `i32 microdegrees` lat field with `calibration: { scale: 1e-6 }` + `range: { min: -90, max: 90 }` correctly rejects wire value `95_000_000` (= 95° physical) at decode. Unlocks the lat/lon WGS-84 guards in the STANAG 4586 schema (currently carried in the hand-rolled decoder) — to be wired into `schemas/vehicle_position.yaml` in a follow-up. Five new tests cover validator rejection of `.nan` / `.inf` / `-.inf` bounds, `max < min`, decode-side range error, encode-side range error, and the calibration-composes-with-range case.

- **STANAG 4586 vehicle-position schema-parity test** — first cross-protocol confidence test for the declarative XTCE-style schema vocabulary. Ships a `crates/rustgate-stanag4586/schemas/vehicle_position.yaml` schema that describes the 48-byte big-endian wire frame (`u32 vehicle_id` + `u8 flight_state` + `f64` lat/lon + `f32` alt/speed/heading + `u64` timestamp, with two reserved zero-padding regions left undeclared), plus a `tests/schema_parity.rs` proptest that asserts `SchemaCodec::from_entity(SchemaCodec::to_entity(hand_rolled_bytes))` is byte-identical to the hand-rolled `vehicle_position::encode` output for every arbitrary in-range input. The hand-rolled codec stays in place; this PR is the proof that the schema runtime is sufficient to drive a real protocol without per-codec Rust, not a rewrite. The `FlightState` enum byte → typed-variant projection and the lat / lon range guards remain v2 schema features.

- **Per-tenant federation topology (Active / Standby roles) — completes the multi-tenancy story from #859.** v0.9.0 isolated `tenant_id` at rest (per-tenant archive subdirectories, store-and-forward keying, optional NATS subject prefix), but federation fan-out was still all-peers-every-tenant. PR adds two additive `PeerConfig` fields and a topology selection layer:
  - **`PeerConfig.tenants: Vec<String>`** — empty / `["*"]` keeps legacy shared-fleet semantics; `["alpha", "bravo"]` pins the peer to specific tenant IDs. The `serves_tenant(tenant_id)` predicate filters the candidate peer set during forward — pinned peers never receive traffic outside their tenant list, and untagged messages (`tenant_id = None`) reach only shared peers.
  - **`PeerConfig.topology_role: TopologyRole`** — `Active` (default, legacy fan-out) or `Standby` (held back from forward unless every Active peer in the same tenant is unavailable, then promoted automatically for that forwarding pass).
  - **`crates/rustgate-federation/src/topology.rs`** — the selection layer with 10 unit tests covering the tenant + role matrix (shared/wildcard/pinned × tagged/untagged × all-active/standby-promoted/no-candidates). The hot path in `manager::forward_inner` applies the same rule inline; the spec module is the test surface.
  - **No persistent state** — promotion is recomputed per message from the current connection state. Operators wanting hysteresis configure circuit-breaker trip / recovery cadence rather than asking this layer to debounce.

  Back-compat: deployments with no `tenants` field on any peer behave identically to pre-PR. The wire format is unchanged.

  **Out of scope** (deferred to follow-up): Hub / Spoke topology (the local-node-role question is non-trivial; we want concrete deployment pressure first); weighted active sets; time-windowed activation policies.

- **Entity extensions — `Tasking` + `FileRef` first-class fields on `rustgate_core::entity::Entity`.** Two new always-on, `#[serde(default)]` vector fields plus their associated types:
  - **`Tasking`** with `task_id`, `state` (`TaskingState`: `Assigned` / `Acknowledged` / `Executing` / `Complete` / `Failed` / `Cancelled`), `role` (`TaskingRole`: `Subject` / `Assignee` / `Target` / `Observer`), and optional `name`. Routing-graph artifact only — rustgate does not own task state, it just carries references through the routing pipeline so consumers can correlate.
  - **`FileRef`** with `uri`, optional `size_bytes` / `mime` / `hash` (`FileHash` = `{algorithm, hex}`) / `label`. rustgate stores only the URI + metadata; the bytes live wherever the URI points at (HTTPS, S3, `content://`). Mission-file storage proper remains off-mission.
  - Both fields are `Vec<T>` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]` so pre-extension wire payloads round-trip unchanged.

  11 new unit tests in `rustgate-core::entity::tests` covering: empty-default construction, JSON back-compat round-trip on pre-extension payloads, full `Tasking` and `FileRef` round-trips, vocabulary stability for `TaskingState::as_str` / `TaskingRole::as_str`, `Default` impls, optional-field skipping on `FileRef` wire shape, and a multi-tasking-different-roles round-trip.

  Compatibility: every `Entity { ... }` struct literal in the workspace (codecs, correlation engine, mappers, tests — ~40+ sites across 19 files) updated to set the new fields to `Default::default()`. Each `EntityCodec::to_entity` implementation continues to leave the new fields empty; future per-codec work to populate them from native wire fields (CoT `<__chat>` for taskings, CoT `<fileshare>` for file refs) ships incrementally without further breakage.

- **Declarative XTCE-style codec authoring via `rustgate-codec-schema`** — a new workspace crate that adds a `SchemaCodec` implementing `EntityCodec` driven by a YAML / JSON wire-format description, so binary protocols can be onboarded by editing a schema file instead of writing Rust per protocol. Inspired by the OMG XTCE spec used by Yamcs / Open MCT and the CCSDS Space Packet Protocol descriptors, with v1 deliberately scoped to the 80% of practical wire formats that fit a fixed-offset / fixed-length model.
  - **What's in** — fixed-offset binary fields with little- and big-endian primitive types (`u8`/`u16`/`u32`/`u64`, `i8`/`i16`/`i32`/`i64`, `f32`/`f64`), fixed-length byte slices and fixed-length UTF-8 strings, linear calibration (`physical = raw * scale + offset`) applied during decode and reversed on encode, field-to-`Entity` projection via dotted-path mapping (`uid`, `callsign`, `mil_std_2525_sidc`, `position.{lat,lon,hae_meters}`, `velocity.{speed_m_s,course_deg}`, `attributes.<key>`), round-trip discipline — fields without an `entity_path` land on `Entity::attributes` under `schema.<protocol>.<field>` so a `decode → encode` cycle preserves payload bytes the `Entity` shape doesn't carry.
  - **Schema validation** — overlapping field ranges, fields extending past `message-size-bytes`, non-finite calibration coefficients, missing `length-bytes` on variable-length fields, and multi-message schemas without `discriminator-offset` all fail at parse time so operator typos surface at startup, not on the first payload.
  - **Typed errors** — `SchemaError` (Parse / Validation) for schema-load failures and `SchemaCodecError` (PayloadTooShort / Utf8 / UnmappedValue / MissingRequiredEntityField / OutOfRange) for runtime codec failures, each carrying the field name + offending value so an operator can map a runtime miss back to the schema line that's wrong.
  - **What's deferred to v2** — XML wire formats (NFFI, raw CoT XML, OGC SensorThings responses) need an XML extension to the grammar; polynomial / spline calibration; conditional / context-sensitive fields (`field A is present only when field B == 0x42`); bit-packed fields (the existing hand-rolled `rustgate-vmf` and `rustgate-link16` codecs use bit-level FPI / FRI / GPI indicators that don't fit a fixed-offset / fixed-length model). Value-mapping (enum-style raw → label) parses today but the runtime treats the raw integer as the value pending real codec ports that need it.
  - **Follow-up port** — the next PR ports the first binary codec (likely `rustgate-meshtastic`, whose protobuf-like fixed-offset layout fits the v1 schema surface) to validate the declarative path end-to-end.

- **DDS / ROS 2 real bindings for `rustgate-dds` (closes the deferred half of #870)** — the `rustgate-dds` crate gains a `dds-real` Cargo feature that turns the trait + mock scaffold into a production wire bridge:
  - **`RealDdsBridge`** (`src/real.rs`) — pure-Rust DDS-RTPS via the `rustdds` crate. CDR-encoded `DdsPayloadWire` wrapping the property-bag bytes preserves the source GUID, source timestamp, and payload across the wire. `QosProfile` (Reliability / Durability / History) maps onto rustdds's `QosPolicies` bag at participant + publisher + subscriber + topic creation time. Topics are lazily created on first publish or subscribe and cached for the bridge's lifetime.
  - **`Ros2Bridge`** (`src/ros2.rs`) — ROS 2 graph compatibility on top of the same rustdds `DomainParticipant` via `ros2-client`. Published messages appear on `rt/<topic>` per the ROS 2 name-mangling convention and are visible to `ros2 topic echo`, `ros2 bag record`, and `ros2 node list`. `from_real()` constructor wires the ROS 2 bridge to share its participant with the raw-DDS bridge so a single rustgate process serves both DDS-native peers (NGVA, VICTORY, Cyclone DDS, RTI Connext, FastDDS) and ROS 2 graph tools without running two parallel RTPS stacks.
  - **Workspace deps** — `rustdds = "0.11"` and `ros2-client = "0.8"` added under the `dds-real` feature gate. Both are pure Rust (no native library install) and `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` compatible. Default-features build of `rustgate-dds` is unchanged — the `dds-real` feature is opt-in.
  - **Tests** — 35 unit + integration tests pass (10 new in `real` / `ros2` modules + 1 new in `tests/real_loopback.rs` covering construction + publish without subscribers + 2 `#[ignore]`-gated end-to-end loopback tests that exercise the full publish → discovery → subscribe → delivery chain on a host with UDP multicast on the loopback interface).
  - **What's deferred** — DDS Security plugin configuration (rustdds's Security plugin is pre-1.0 and in-vehicle deployments today rely on link-layer security); content-filtered topics (handled on the rustgate side via the property mapper); keyed instance lifecycle on keyed topics (every topic this bridge creates is `TopicKind::NoKey`).

- **Live K8s controller apply-loop for `rustgate-operator` (closes the deferred half of #874)** — the operator now ships a `controller` Cargo feature that turns the binary into a full kube-runtime reconciler. The pure-render path stays the default (no `kube` / `k8s-openapi` in the dep tree), and the controller feature layers on top:
  - **`controller.rs`** — `kube_runtime::Controller` wired to the existing pure `reconcile()` function. Watches `RustgateCluster` cluster-wide (or in a single namespace) and `.owns(...)` the rendered children (StatefulSet, Service, ConfigMap) so drift on any child re-queues the parent.
  - **`apply.rs`** — server-side apply via `kube::api::DynamicObject` with a stable field manager (`rustgate-operator`) and `force: true`. Kind-agnostic so future renderer outputs (NetworkPolicy, PDB, …) land without code changes.
  - **`leader.rs`** — `coordination.k8s.io/v1` Lease-based leader election with the standard `leaseDuration / renewDeadline / retryPeriod` knobs (30s / 20s / 5s defaults). Followers keep watches warm and re-queue cheaply via a shared `LeaderGate`; on SIGTERM the leader clears `holderIdentity` so a peer can take over without waiting the full leaseDuration.
  - **`events.rs`** — Kubernetes Event emission via `kube::runtime::events::Recorder`. Every reconcile emits `Normal/Reconciled` (apply summary), `Warning/InvalidSpec`, `Warning/ApplyFailed`, etc., visible in `kubectl describe rustgatecluster`.
  - **`health.rs`** — `axum`-based HTTP server exposing `/healthz`, `/readyz` (probes the API server reachability), and `/metrics` (Prometheus text exposition).
  - **`metrics.rs`** — Prometheus instrumentation under the `rustgate_operator_*` namespace: `reconcile_total{result}`, `reconcile_duration_seconds`, `apply_total{kind,result}`, `clusters_total`, `leader`, `last_reconcile_timestamp_seconds`.
  - **`main.rs run` subcommand** — wires the kube client (`Client::try_default`, picks up in-cluster ServiceAccount tokens or `~/.kube/config`), spawns the elector / HTTP / signal tasks, drains in-flight reconciles on SIGTERM, and releases the lease on shutdown.
  - **Helm chart updates** — `operator-rbac.yaml` adds `coordination.k8s.io/leases` and `events.k8s.io/events` permissions; `operator-deployment.yaml` sets `replicas: 2` for hot-standby, wires `/healthz` and `/readyz` probes, exposes `:8080`, adds Prometheus scrape annotations and topology spread constraints, and increases `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` to give the drain + lease-release sequence headroom. `values.yaml` exposes `operator.leaderElection.enabled`, `operator.replicas`, `operator.watchNamespace`, `operator.httpPort`, `operator.prometheus.scrape`.
  - **`kube_types.rs`** — `#[derive(CustomResource)]` view of `RustgateCluster` so `kube_runtime::Controller` can watch it; round-trips losslessly to the existing hand-rolled `crd::RustgateCluster` via JSON so the renderer-side golden snapshots stay valid.

### Security

- **Validate the SensorThings poll cursor as RFC 3339 and track the true max (closes #1502).** The OGC SensorThings polling task (`rustgate-ogc-sensorthings`) advanced its cursor to the *last* observation in each page — trusting the server's `phenomenonTime asc` ordering — and interpolated that raw server-supplied value into the next request's OData `$filter` clause. A server returning observations out of order could drive the cursor backwards (re-delivery loop) or skip ahead (M-5), and an unvalidated `phenomenonTime` was an OData-injection sink (M-4). The task now advances to the maximum **parseable** RFC 3339 timestamp across the page (order-independent), so only a validated timestamp literal can ever reach the filter; an all-unparseable page holds the prior cursor (fail-safe — the `gt` filter re-delivers rather than skips).

- **Audit connection-reject and event-drop paths (closes #1500).** The WebSocket and MQTT listeners' per-IP rate-limit, TLS-accept, identity-extraction, and WebSocket-upgrade/timeout reject branches — plus the WebSocket per-connection sustained-rate-limit disconnect and the federation V2 `ServerEventStream` unauthorized-group drop — previously only logged via `tracing` (or fired a reject callback), leaving no entry in the structured audit trail; each now also emits the matching `rustgate_core::audit` event (`connection_rejected` / `rate_limit_triggered` / `tls_handshake_failed` / `federation_event_rejected`).

- **Harden two latent low-severity gaps (refs #1510).** *(L-3)* The OGC SensorThings bearer token (`rustgate-server`) was read with `tokio::fs::read_to_string` — no permission or size gating and no zeroization. It now reads through `rustgate_core::read_secret_file`, which rejects a group/world-readable (mode `0o077`) or oversized token file and wipes the cleartext intermediate on drop. *(L-8)* `hash_identity_into` (`rustgate-authz`) omitted the `tenant` field, so two identities differing only by tenant produced the same 128-bit `SubjectHash` — the authz decision cache could serve one tenant's verdict to another. Tenant is now folded into the hash with the same discriminant-byte scheme as the SPIFFE ID. *(L-5 federation peer-id, L-9 OCSP enum match are tracked separately.)*

- **`MaskPoint` fails closed for unmaskable position protocols (closes #1545, SEC-18).** `apply_mask_point` (`rustgate-router`) masked only CoT XML and MAVLink; every other position-bearing protocol — DIS, Link 16, ASTERIX, VMF, SAPIENT, NFFI, STANAG 4586, Meshtastic, TAK protobuf — fell through to the non-XML branch and was forwarded with coordinates *intact*, so a `MaskPoint` obligation meant to strip location did nothing and the original position egressed to NATS / HTTP / federation peers (the most serious finding of the June 2026 semantic audit). The non-XML branch now **fails closed**: the body is erased (`recovery = "dropped"`, message type `other:masked`) rather than forwarded, with `source_protocol` retained so an operator can prioritise a per-codec masker (the proper, non-interim fix). This is default-deny — a payload that cannot be proven position-free is treated as if it carries one. MAVLink is unchanged (registered masker; a point-less frame still forwards). See [ADR 0027](docs/adr/0027-maskpoint-fail-closed.md).

- **Reject multi-marking messages at the HighToLow guard boundary (closes #1604).** The cross-domain guard's marking extractor (`rustgate-guard`) returned only the *first* `<marking>` element, so a release-boundary (`HighToLow`) message could carry a benign first marking (e.g. UNCLASSIFIED) followed by a second, higher one (e.g. TOP SECRET) that crossed unexamined while the audit record named only the first — the governing classification is ambiguous. The guard now counts marking elements and rejects (deny + audit, reason `multiple_markings`) any `HighToLow` message carrying more than one. `LowToHigh` / `Bidirectional` remain permissive (elevation tolerance), matching the existing classification-dominance check.

- **Audit archive-retention rotation passes (closes #1516, F-69).** The archive rotation task (`rustgate-archive`) deleted expired/over-cap segments with only a `tracing` line — the retention enforcement left no compliance trail. A rotation pass that purges ≥1 segment now emits an `archive.rotation_completed` audit event (`bytes_after`, `files_deleted`), so the audit chain proves retention ran and a SIEM can alert on the heartbeat's absence if rotation silently stalls. Zero-delete passes stay on the tracing path. The rotation-cadence floor was already enforced in CLI validation.

- **Bound and linearize the admin mission-package upload (closes #1618).** The admin `/api/packages` upload handler (`rustgate-admin`, feature `missions`) collected the entire request body into memory with no size cap, and `extract_multipart_field` (`rustgate-missions`) re-searched the whole body for each split part with `str::find` — O(n·m) per part, super-linear overall, a CPU-amplification DoS on a periodic body. The upload body is now wrapped in `http_body_util::Limited` (`MAX_MISSIONS_API_BODY_BYTES`, 52 MiB) and returns 413 on excess, and the multipart parser tracks each part's byte offset directly instead of re-searching, making it linear.

- **Bound peer-discovery responses (closes #1619).** The Consul backend (`rustgate-federation`, feature `peer-discovery-consul`) buffered the catalog HTTP response with `reqwest`'s `.json()`, which has no size limit and trusts no `Content-Length` — a hostile or misbehaving Consul endpoint could stream an unbounded body and exhaust memory. The body is now read chunk-by-chunk and rejected once it crosses `MAX_DISCOVERY_RESPONSE_SIZE` (50 MiB), and both the Consul and etcd backends reject a discovery response carrying more than `MAX_DISCOVERY_PEERS` (10,000) entries before reconciling it into the federation peer set.

- **Hash federation peer ids in metric labels (closes #1558).** The federation peer-lag updater (`rustgate-server`), the per-peer queue-bytes gauge (`rustgate-federation`), and the per-RPC metric vectors (`rpc_total` / `rpc_duration` / `rpc_in_flight`) used the raw configured peer id as a Prometheus label value, disclosing the federation topology in plaintext on the unauthenticated-by-default `/metrics` scrape (SEC-20). All peer-id label values are now hashed with `hash_cn` before use (the central `sanitize_peer_label` helper now hashes, which also subsumes its prior CR/LF log-forging guard). This is OPSEC redaction — peer ids are configured, not user PII. SEC-19 (raw CN in access logs) was already addressed.

- **Prune idle tenants from the quota tracker (closes #1617).** The per-tenant connection-counter and throughput-bucket maps in `TenantQuotaTracker` (`rustgate-router`, active when a tenant-quota file is configured) were never pruned — they grew with every distinct certificate Organization (`O`) ever seen, so an attacker with CA control could issue certs with unbounded distinct `O` values and grow the maps without limit toward OOM. `record_disconnect` now removes a tenant's entries once it returns to zero active connections (re-checking under the write lock against a concurrent reconnect), bounding the maps by the set of *actively connected* tenants.

- **EST sign rate-limit is consumed only by well-formed, authenticated requests (closes #1611).** In `validate_and_read_body` (`rustgate-enrollment`, feature `est`), the per-IP CSR-signing rate-limit slot was recorded on the allowed path *before* auth and Content-Type validation, so an authenticated client could exhaust a legitimate peer's signing budget by sending requests with a bad Content-Type — each consumed a 60 s slot and then returned 415 without ever attempting a signature. The check order is now auth → Content-Type → rate-limit → body, so a slot is consumed only by a request that actually reaches the signing path.

- **Bound concurrent inference re-injection tasks (closes #1614).** The inference pipeline can emit up to one result per configured model (up to `MAX_PIPELINE_ENTRIES`) per inbound message, and the re-injection sink spawned a `router.route` task per result with no ceiling — so a single decodable message fanned out into hundreds of tasks, and at high message rates an authenticated client could exhaust the tokio task pool and starve routing. A semaphore now caps in-flight re-injection tasks at `INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENT_REINJECTS` (256); excess re-injections are shed (inference is best-effort enrichment) rather than spawned unboundedly.

- **Cap per-entity source tracks in the correlation engine (closes #1613).** Each merge into a fused entity appended a `SourceTrack` (cloning the full original entity) with no cap, so an authenticated client flooding the engine with reports that all fuse into one entity (identical position and kind, distinct attacker-chosen UIDs) grew the per-entity `sources` list without bound — memory plus an O(n) fuse cost on the routing hot path, which also made the un-indexed `find_same_source` scan effectively quadratic. The list is now capped at `MAX_SOURCES_PER_ENTITY` (32), evicting the stalest track before appending; this bounds both memory and the per-submit fuse/scan cost (an evicted real sensor simply re-registers on its next report).

- **Cap the per-session MQTT subscription tracker (closes #1615).** The per-session tracker dedups subscriptions on `(filter, subscription_identifier)`, so an MQTT 5.0 client could re-SUBSCRIBE the same authorized filter with a fresh Subscription Identifier on every packet — defeating the dedup, growing the tracker without bound (the idempotent `join_group` and the per-CN group cap do not bound it), and slowing the O(n) write-path scan run on every delivered PUBLISH. The tracker is now capped at `MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS_PER_SESSION` (1000, far above any legitimate client); a subscription beyond the cap is refused — `ImplementationSpecific` (0x83) in the v5 SUBACK, `Failure` (0x80) in v4 — while an already-tracked `(filter, identifier)` pair is still accepted since it does not grow the tracker.

- **Reject unbalanced tags in CoT delta `<detail>` reconstruction (closes #1610).** `parse_snapshot` (`rustgate-cot`, feature `full-detail`) captured `<detail>` children by depth counting alone, so an unmatched or mismatched closing tag (e.g. `<detail><content></unmatched></detail>`) was blindly appended or silently dropped and reconstructed as malformed XML that downstream parsers reject — message loss on position-heavy traffic. The parser now tracks a tag-name stack and rejects the snapshot (returns `None`, so the delta encoder falls back to a full verbatim event emit) on any closing-tag mismatch or stack underflow. Investigated alongside #1609 (a related report in the same sink): that one is a **false positive** — quick_xml emits a text entity reference (`&lt;`, `&amp;`) as a separate event that the detail capture drops, so the reconstruction is lossy but always well-formed (no stray unescaped `<` / `&`), never the malformed XML #1609 claimed; the suggested re-escape there would instead have double-escaped the reconstructed structural tags. A regression test pins the well-formed reconstruction.

- **Reject control characters in the multipart upload filename (closes #1608).** `extract_multipart_filename` (`rustgate-missions`) pulled the filename between quotes with no validation; it becomes the package display name and is later interpolated into a `Content-Disposition` response header on download, so a CR / LF / NUL in the filename was a header / response-splitting vector (today only blocked incidentally by hyper's header validation, not by application code). The extractor now drops a filename containing `\r`, `\n`, or `\0` (returning `None`, so the caller falls back to a generated name) rather than storing an injection vector.

- **V2 federation client `shutdown()` aborts its task instead of blocking on a stalled peer (closes #1607).** Unlike the V1 client, the V2 gRPC client's `shutdown()` awaited its background task without first calling `handle.abort()`. A peer that keeps ACKing keepalives but stops draining application data parks the task in `send_tx.send().await`, so `shutdown()` blocked until the gRPC request timeout (up to 300 s). Both callers that drive shutdown — the graceful-drain path and the peer-discovery reconciler — hold the federation manager `RwLock` across this await, so a single stalled peer wedged every `fed_forward` reader (a `/api/drain`-reachable availability outage). `shutdown()` now aborts the task before awaiting (matching V1), still sending the watch signal first so an un-wedged task exits cleanly on its own.

- **Global concurrent-session cap bounds router memory by default (closes #1606).** `Router::register` allocated a `SessionHandle` per distinct client CN with no ceiling unless a per-tenant quota file was configured (`quota_tracker` is `None` by default). An attacker holding valid CA-issued certs could reconnect with many distinct CNs and grow the session map without bound, driving the process toward OOM. `register` now rejects a *new* CN once the session count reaches `DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS` (100k, overridable via `Router::with_max_sessions`); re-registering an existing CN is a replacement (net-zero on map size) and is always allowed. Independent of, and complementary to, the per-tenant quota.

- **MQTT session resume re-validates restored subscriptions against the current certificate (closes #1605).** On a `clean_start=0` reconnect within the session-expiry window, the broker replayed every saved subscription through `router.join_group` **without** re-checking group membership — the saved set was trusted as "already authorized at SUBSCRIBE time". If the client's certificate was re-issued with fewer groups in the interim, the resume silently re-granted access to a group the present cert no longer authorizes (privilege narrowing undone on reconnect). The restore loop now performs the same `identity.is_member_of` check the live SUBSCRIBE path does, dropping (and logging) any restored subscription the current cert does not grant.

- **OCSP `Good` answers are re-validated after a TTL instead of trusted for the process lifetime (closes #1625).** The client-cert OCSP cache (`rustgate-tls`, feature `ocsp`) cached a `Good` status with no expiry, and a `get` on the verify hot path bumped LRU recency — so a frequently-reconnecting certificate's `Good` entry was never evicted and never re-queried. When the CA later revoked that cert, the OCSP layer never observed it for the rest of the process lifetime. A cached `Good` is now stamped with the wall-clock second it was recorded and treated as stale after `DEFAULT_OCSP_GOOD_TTL_SECS` (1 h): a stale entry is handled exactly like a cache miss (schedule a background re-fetch, fail open for that one handshake), so a later revocation is observed within the window. `Revoked` entries are unaffected (revocation is monotonic). The staleness check uses the rustls-provided handshake time and is clock-backwards-safe (a rewound clock keeps the entry fresh rather than forcing a re-fetch storm).

- **Gate DLQ replay on the circuit breaker (closes #1626).** The webhook DLQ replay path (`rustgate-http` `replay_entry`) issued one HTTP request per queued entry without consulting `target.circuit.allow_request()`, unlike the live dispatch path. If a target degraded again partway through a drain the circuit re-opened, yet the loop kept firing at the unhealthy endpoint — and with `rate_limit_per_sec` unset (the default) the circuit is the only outbound guard. `replay_entry` now checks the circuit first and re-DLQs the entry (returns `Failed`) when it is open, so a flapping target is retried on the next recovery cycle instead of hammered mid-drain.

- **Cap the OGC SensorThings poll response body (closes #1623).** `SensorThingsClient::poll` read the upstream response with `response.bytes()` and no size limit, so a hostile, misconfigured, or MITM'd (plaintext) SensorThings endpoint returning a chunked, Content-Length-less, multi-gigabyte body could be buffered into heap — the client already disables redirects for the same untrusted-endpoint reason. The body is now read by streaming chunks with a hard `MAX_FRAME_SIZE` (16 MiB) ceiling plus a Content-Length pre-check, rejecting with the new `SensorThingsError::ResponseTooLarge` rather than buffering an unbounded body.

- **Cap schema-codec encode allocation against `MAX_FRAME_SIZE` (closes #1624).** `SchemaCodec::from_entity` grew its output buffer with `out.resize(needed, 0)`, where `needed` derived from a `repeat` field's `count_from` value — taken from the source `Entity`, ultimately an attacker-influenced wire field in cross-protocol transcoding. A forged count (e.g. `u32::MAX` × a non-trivial record size) drove a multi-gigabyte allocation — a single-message remote DoS. Encode now rejects with the new `SchemaCodecError::PayloadTooLarge` once the grown buffer would exceed `MAX_FRAME_SIZE` (16 MiB, the single-source-of-truth cap); the decode side was already bounded by the real input length.

- **Bound the webhook error-response capture by streaming, not Content-Length (closes #1622).** `capture_response_body` (`rustgate-http`) guarded only on the server-advertised `Content-Length` before calling `response.bytes()`, so a hostile or MITM'd upstream replying with a chunked, Content-Length-less, multi-gigabyte body bypassed the 1 MiB ceiling and buffered the whole body into heap (re-buffered per retry) — a memory-exhaustion DoS. The body is now read chunk-by-chunk with a hard ceiling on total bytes consumed: at most `MAX_ERROR_RESPONSE_BYTES` are ever read regardless of (or absent) Content-Length, only the per-target cap is retained, and reads stop and drop the connection once the ceiling is hit.

- **Authenticate the federation REST API on the admin/metrics server (closes #1621).** The `/api/federation/*` dispatch branch ran its handler — which adds, modifies, and deletes federation peers including `trust_cert_cn` and inbound-group allowlists — without ever checking the `Authorization` header, while the sibling ACL/management/packages branches all require a bearer token. On a metrics server bound to a non-loopback address (a common Kubernetes scrape setup) any network-reachable peer could mutate federation trust. The branch now requires a valid bearer token *before* the body is read or the handler runs, and is **fail-closed** — it denies outright when no token is configured (stricter than the read-only `/metrics` scrape, which is open when unset). The request body is additionally capped (`http_body_util::Limited`, 256 KiB → `413`) to remove the secondary unbounded-buffering DoS.

- **Enforce the `ClientAuth` EKU on the WebSocket and MQTT transports (closes #1620).** The primary TLS listener rejects a client certificate that lacks the `id-kp-clientAuth` Extended Key Usage, but the WebSocket (`extract_client_identity` in `rustgate-websocket`) and MQTT (`extract_client_identity` in `rustgate-mqtt`) listeners called `extract_identity` without the matching `validate_key_usage` check. Because the underlying webpki client verifier treats EKU as `RequiredIfPresent` — it accepts a CA-signed certificate carrying the wrong EKU or none at all — a server-auth-only certificate signed by the trusted client CA was rejected over plain TLS but **accepted as a client identity over WebSocket and MQTT**, a cross-transport certificate-confusion gap. Both functions now call `validate_key_usage(cert, ExpectedKeyUsage::ClientAuth)` before identity extraction, with a per-listener regression test confirming a server-auth-only cert is rejected.

- **Archive encryption widens the AEAD nonce to eliminate base-nonce reuse (closes #1506).** Encrypted archives (`rustgate-archive`: CoT archive, audit log, DLQ spools) used ChaCha20-Poly1305 with only a 64-bit random per-file base nonce. By the birthday bound, at ~2³² files under one key two files could draw the same base and reuse an identical nonce sequence — catastrophic for ChaCha20-Poly1305 (keystream XOR leaks plaintext; the Poly1305 key is exposed). The writer now produces a **version-3** format using **XChaCha20-Poly1305** (192-bit nonce; 160 random base bits → ~2⁸⁰ birthday bound), retiring a false module-doc claim that key reuse across many files was safe. The fix follows [ADR 0026](docs/adr/0026-archive-xchacha-v3.md). Existing version-2 archives remain fully decryptable — `decrypt_file` dispatches on the on-disk version byte.

- **Validate the client `server_name` at config build time (closes #1517).** `ClientConfigBuilder::build()` accepted any `server_name` string and only rejected a malformed value later, at the TLS handshake. The SNI name is now validated up front with rustls's own `ServerName` parser (the same check the dial path applies) — control characters, spaces, path separators, and other injection-shaped input are rejected at build time with `ClientError::InvalidServerName`, while valid DNS names and IP literals continue to build.

- **Webhook delivery IDs use the OS CSPRNG, not `fastrand` (closes #1520).** Per-request delivery / idempotency IDs (`publisher.rs`, `dlq.rs`) were drawn from the non-cryptographic `fastrand` PRNG, making them predictable from observed outputs. A receiver may fence replays on the delivery ID, so a guessable value let an attacker forge or suppress deliveries. They now come from `rand::rngs::OsRng` (128 bits, identical 32-char-hex format). A `clippy.toml` `disallowed-methods` rule bans `fastrand::fill` so a security identifier cannot silently regress to a non-CSPRNG.

- **Cap inference pipeline length to bound task/memory fan-out (closes #1528).** `InferenceConfig::validate()` enforced no limit on the pipeline list, so a hostile or fat-fingered config could declare an unbounded number of models. The pipeline spawns one async task per model per entity and the wiring spawns one task per routed message, turning a single message into an arbitrary fan-out (task / memory DoS). `validate()` now rejects pipelines longer than `rustgate_core::constants::MAX_PIPELINE_ENTRIES` (256) — before allocating anything sized to the list — with a clear config error. Legitimate pipelines (1–10 models) are unaffected.

- **Marti-compat endpoints check the bearer token before running the handler (closes #1504).** The three bearer-gated `/Marti/api/*` routes were dispatched as `require_bearer(auth, state, handle(state).await)` — and Rust evaluates call arguments eagerly, so each handler's side effects (mission/package store reads, the contacts provider callback, the video catalog snapshot) executed for *unauthenticated* requests before the token was ever checked; the 401 only replaced the already-computed response. The auth gate now short-circuits to 401 *before* the handler runs (`deny_unless_authorized`), closing a pre-auth execution / DoS-amplification surface. Authenticated requests are unaffected.

- **Bump `quinn-proto` 0.11.14 → 0.11.15 to fix RUSTSEC-2026-0185 (closes #1580).** A remote-memory-exhaustion DoS in quinn-proto's out-of-order QUIC stream reassembler: a peer that sends many gapped stream fragments (leaving early bytes missing) forces unbounded reassembly-buffer growth on an in-order reader, enabling memory exhaustion. `quinn-proto` enters the tree transitively via `reqwest`'s HTTP/3 support (used by the HTTP egress client). Lockfile-only bump to the patched `0.11.15`; no manifest or API change. (`cargo deny check advisories` → ok)

- **Ignore RUSTSEC-2026-0173 (`proc-macro-error2` unmaintained) in `deny.toml`.** The `cargo deny` advisory gate flags `proc-macro-error2` 2.0.1 — an informational "unmaintained" advisory (the crate is itself a now-unmaintained fork of `proc-macro-error`), not a vulnerability. It is a compile-time-only proc-macro pulled purely transitively on Linux targets under the `dds` feature (`rustgate-dds` → `ros2-client`/`rustdds` → `local-ip-address` → `neli` → `getset` → `proc-macro-error2`); rustgate has no direct dependency or use site, and the chain can only be cleared upstream. Added as a documented, removal-triggered ignore matching the existing `paste`/`net2` entries so the `audit` CI gate stays green; `audit-soft` still surfaces it as a warning.

- **Codec UDP ingress rejects the reserved `224.0.0.0/24` multicast control block (SEC-12).** `--<proto>-multicast-group` (DIS/ASTERIX/VMF) and `CodecIngressConfig::bind_socket` previously accepted any `224.0.0.0/4` address. Joining the reserved link-local control block `224.0.0.0/24` (`224.0.0.1` all-hosts, `224.0.0.2` all-routers, `224.0.0.251` mDNS, …) subscribes the listener to local control-plane chatter that floods it and is never a valid tactical-data group. Both the startup config parse (`parse_multicast_group`) and the bind path now reject `224.0.0.0/24` fail-closed (`InvalidInput`). The CoT multicast listener (`udp_multicast.rs`) is unchanged. Also documents (SEC-11) that the synthetic ingress CN embeds a spoofable UDP source address that must not be used for ACLs or forensic attribution. (refs #1554)

- **Router hashes client CNs in operational log fields (SEC-19).** Several `tracing` fields in `rustgate-router` — session, group-join, offline-persist, quota, and dedup warning/debug lines — logged the raw client certificate CN, leaking PII into structured logs. All such fields now route through `rustgate_core::masking::hash_cn`, matching the ~40 existing hashed sites in the same file. The access log's `src_cn` is deliberately left raw — it is the authenticated source-identity field whose purpose is forensic attribution, and the destination CN there is already hashed (asserted by `tests/access_log.rs`). (refs #1558)

- **TCP codec ingress closes slow-drip connections with an incomplete-frame dwell cap (SEC-10).** The stream-framed tactical ingress (`codec_tcp_ingress.rs`) wrapped each read in the per-read `READ_TIMEOUT`, which resets on every byte received. A peer dribbling one byte at a time never tripped that timeout yet never completed a frame, holding a connection — and a `max_connections` concurrency slot — open indefinitely (slow-drip / slow-loris). Added a per-connection `INCOMPLETE_FRAME_TIMEOUT` (60s) that bounds how long a *partial* frame may sit buffered without completing: dribbling more bytes does not reset it (the anchor is the partial frame's start, not the last byte), so a byte-at-a-time attacker cannot defeat it, while a connection on a clean frame boundary (empty buffer) is not subject to it and may idle up to `READ_TIMEOUT` between frames — so a legitimate low-rate sensor is never disconnected. Closes with audit reason `incomplete_frame_timeout`; the shared `READ_TIMEOUT` constant is untouched. (closes #1553)

- **`HeaderLengthCodec` rejects an out-of-bounds length field instead of panicking (SEC-8).** The codec reads a big-endian length field at a configured `length_offset`/`length_size` within a fixed `header_len`, but `new()` never validated that the field fits inside the header — a misconfigured codec (`length_offset + width > header_len`) indexed past the header slice in `read_body_length` and panicked the connection task on the first frame. `decode` now checks the field lies within the header and returns `io::ErrorKind::InvalidData` otherwise; `new()` stays infallible (it is built inside a non-fallible ingress closure). (closes #1552)

- **Client-OCSP response cache is now a bounded LRU (SEC-6).** `rustgate-tls`'s client-certificate OCSP verifier (`client_ocsp.rs`) cached per-cert statuses in an unbounded `HashMap<Vec<u8>, CachedStatus>` — one entry per distinct presented client certificate, never evicted, so an adversary rotating many CA-issued certs could grow it without limit across the process lifetime (entries are tiny, hence Low severity). Replaced with an `lru::LruCache` capped at `OCSP_CACHE_CAPACITY` (4096); a cache read on the verify hot path bumps recency, so actively-connecting peers stay cached and only idle entries are evicted under pressure. (closes #1550)

- **HTTP-egress and TLS cert-reloader private keys now go through the secrets gate (SEC-5).** `rustgate-http`'s per-target mTLS client keys (`publisher.rs`) and `rustgate-tls`'s server key on initial load *and* on rotation (`cert_reloader.rs`) were read with raw `std::fs::read` — wrapped in `Zeroizing` but bypassing `rustgate_core::secrets::read_secret_file`'s mode-`0o077` permission check and size cap that the client path already enforced. A mis-pointed key path could slurp an arbitrary-size file into RAM before PEM parsing, and on a shared host a co-tenant could symlink an over-readable artifact into the configured directory. All private-key reads now route through `read_secret_file` with a 16 KiB cap; public certificates stay on plain `std::fs::read`. **Operator note:** private-key files must now be owner-only (mode `0o600`/`0o400`) — a group/other-readable key is refused at startup and on reload. (closes #1549)

- **HA federate-store KV writes are retried and failures surfaced (SEC-4).** The NATS-KV-backed federate store updated its in-memory cache optimistically but wrote through to KV fire-and-forget (`put_kv` spawned the write and returned `Ok` immediately; failures only `warn!`'d). On a KV outage/quota the local cache and the distributed KV store diverged silently, and the local change was lost on pod restart. KV writes (and deletes) are now retried with bounded exponential backoff via a unit-testable `write_with_retry` helper, recovering the common transient-NATS case; a permanent give-up increments a new `rustgate_federation_kv_write_failures_total` counter (and logs loudly) so operators can alert and reconcile (the watch loop + load-on-restart re-sync the cache from KV). The sync `FederateStore` trait precludes awaiting the write inline, so retry + observability is the chosen mitigation. (closes #1548)

- **MQTT QoS 2 inflight map is now bounded by Receive Maximum (SEC-3).** Inbound QoS 2 PUBLISHes were stored in a per-session map keyed by packet id with no admission limit: one authenticated client could send QoS 2 PUBLISHes across the full 65 535-pkid keyspace and never send PUBREL, retaining up to 65 535 × max-packet-size bytes of unacknowledged state per session → memory exhaustion. `receive_max` existed as a session field but only governed outbound flow control / CONNACK advertising, never inbound admission. The shared `qos2_admit` helper now enforces the server's Receive Maximum on inbound QoS 2: a **new** packet id past the cap is refused — **V5** with PUBREC `0x97 Quota Exceeded`, **V4 (3.1.1, which has no PUBREC reason code)** by disconnecting the client — while a DUP retransmit of a tracked id is still acknowledged idempotently. A lazy per-entry timeout sweep (`QOS2_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT`, 300 s) reclaims slots held by abandoned four-step handshakes, and `receive_max` is floored at 1 so a degenerate 0 cannot wedge QoS 2 entirely. (closes #1547)

- **Federation replay buffer now honours TTL across restarts (SEC-2).** The disk-backed replay buffer (`replay_buffer.rs`) restored persisted messages on rehydrate checking only sequence/capacity — never expiry — so messages whose TTL had lapsed while the process was down were replayed to reconnecting peers (stale tactical positions/orders and TTL-bounded classified traffic resurfacing past their intended lifetime). The persisted `enqueued_at_unix_ms` + `ttl_ms` snapshot existed precisely to re-evaluate TTL but was never consulted. Added `BufferedMessage::is_expired_at` (mirrors `Metadata::is_expired` — strict `>`, no-TTL never expires, clock-backwards tolerated) and applied it (1) in `hydrate_from_records`, which now drops expired entries and deletes them from the store on rehydrate (preserving `next_seq` continuity for reconnecting peers), and (2) on every drain/read path (`messages_since`, `all_messages`, `all_messages_deduped`) so a message that lapses while sitting in the buffer is never replayed either. (closes #1546)

- **Federation peer-certificate CN pinning (SEC-1).** Outbound federation connections validated the peer certificate *chain* against the federation CA but never bound a connection to a specific peer *identity* — any holder of a valid CA-issued certificate could impersonate any peer (and `PeerConfig::trust_cert_cn` existed for exactly this purpose but was wired nowhere). Outbound clients now pin the peer's presented leaf-certificate CN and **fail closed** on mismatch (an `audit::federation_peer_rejected` event is emitted with CNs hashed via `hash_cn`, and the peer follows the normal reconnect/backoff path). Both transports are covered: **V1** compares the CN post-handshake in `connection_loop`, before the connection joins the active pool; **V2 (gRPC)** installs a CN-pinning rustls `ServerCertVerifier` on the tonic channel via `Endpoint::tls_config_with_verifier` — tonic never surfaces the server leaf certificate to application code, so the pin (full chain validation + CN check) must run inside the TLS layer, and the gRPC channel never opens on mismatch. Expected-CN resolution per peer: an explicit `trust_cert_cn` is **always** enforced (per-peer opt-in, non-breaking); the new global `--federation-require-peer-cn-match` (`RUSTGATE_FEDERATION_REQUIRE_PEER_CN_MATCH`, off by default) additionally pins every remaining peer to its configured `id`. CN comparison is case-insensitive. Design note: `docs/design/federation-peer-pinning.md`. (closes #1544)

## [0.9.0] - 2026-05-09

### Added

- **DevSecOps packaging scaffold (closes #871)** — air-gap-ready packaging for Platform One / Iron Bank / Zarf / cATO deployments. **(1) `--air-gap` CLI flag (and `RUSTGATE_AIR_GAP` env var)** disables every internet-reaching code path: HTTP egress targets, OTEL exporter endpoints, Consul / etcd peer discovery, and OCSP fetching. Each external endpoint is checked at startup against a new `rustgate_core::air_gap::is_private_host` classifier covering RFC 1918 (`10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`), IPv4 loopback / link-local / multicast / broadcast, IPv6 loopback / ULA (`fc00::/7`) / link-local (`fe80::/10`) / IPv4-mapped, plus the `localhost`, `*.localhost` (RFC 6761), `local`, and `*.local` (RFC 6762 mDNS) DNS labels. Violations refuse to start the affected subsystem and emit the new `air_gap.violation` audit event with the offending URL recorded for the compliance trail. The mTLS data plane is unaffected — peers may still connect from any address. **(2) Iron Bank-compatible Dockerfile structure** with non-root `USER 10001:10001`, SUID/SGID stripping (`find / -xdev -type f -perm /6000 -delete`), and a clearly-marked `TODO(operator)` block for swapping the builder and runtime base images to `registry1.dso.mil/ironbank/redhat/ubi/ubi9-minimal:9.x` once Platform One credentials are available; the default `rust:1.95-alpine` and `alpine:3.23` bases continue to ship today. **(3) Zarf bundle manifest (`zarf.yaml`)** plus a development-mode CA prebuild hook (`scripts/zarf-prebuild-mtls-ca.sh`) so the Helm chart can be packaged for one-command deployment into disconnected Kubernetes clusters; the prebuild script generates a self-signed P-384 CA into `./.ca/` for staging deployments and carries inline `TODO(operator)` notes for Vault-PKI / External Secrets / pre-issued-CA replacements. **(4) CycloneDX SBOM CI step** alongside the existing SPDX flow in `.github/workflows/release.yml` — the new step installs `cargo-cyclonedx`, produces JSON + XML CycloneDX SBOMs, signs them with `cosign sign-blob` when the `COSIGN_KEY` repository secret is present, and uploads the result (with the optional `.sig` companion file) to the GitHub release. Forks / mirrors without the secret silently skip the signing step instead of failing. **(5) STIG compliance mapping** (`docs/security/stig-mapping.md`) — Application Security and Development, RHEL 8, Container Image and Deployment, and TLS controls mapped to rustgate config flags, audit events, and CI artifacts; STIGs that do not apply to a headless TLS service are marked **N/A** with a one-line reason so an auditor does not have to re-derive the conclusion. **(6) cATO evidence template** (`docs/security/cato-evidence-template.md`) — NIST 800-53 control families (AC, AU, CA, CM, CP, IA, IR, RA, SA, SC, SI) mapped to the rustgate-emitted artifacts (audit events, metrics, CI artifacts, GitHub release assets) that satisfy them, plus an audit-event inventory enumerating all 90+ events the running binary can emit. **(7) Three explicit `TODO(operator)` callouts** that need credentials we do not have: the Iron Bank base image swap (Platform One robot account credentials), the cosign signing step (`COSIGN_KEY` repo secret or OIDC issuer configuration), and the Zarf publish target (registry URL plus auth in CI). All three are marked inline so a follow-up "go-live" PR is mechanical. Closes #871.

- **`rustgate-operator` crate + `RustgateCluster` CRD + Helm chart enhancements (closes #874)** — new workspace crate `rustgate-operator` ships the Kubernetes operator for the `rustgate.io/v1alpha1/RustgateCluster` CRD, plus the supporting Helm chart additions for one-command deployment. **(1) CRD schema** — `helm/crds/rustgatecluster.yaml` declares the namespace-scoped `RustgateCluster` resource with `spec` fields for `replicas`, `image`, `imagePullPolicy`, `servicePort`, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, optional `certManager` (issuer + issuerKind + commonName), `federation` (autoDiscover + port), and `storage` (per-PVC size + storageClass for store-and-forward and audit-log volumes). The schema enforces `replicas ∈ [1, 100]`, `*Port ∈ [1, 65535]`, and a closed-vocabulary `imagePullPolicy`. **(2) Hand-rolled CRD types** — `crates/rustgate-operator/src/crd.rs` projects the CRD shape into Rust via plain serde derive macros rather than the `kube::CustomResource` proc-macro so the build does not depend on the heavier `kube` + `k8s-openapi` toolchain. The `RustgateCluster::validate()` method enforces every CRD invariant before the operator hands the spec to the renderer. **(3) Manifest renderer** — `render::render_all()` is a pure function that translates a validated `RustgateCluster` into the deterministic resource set the operator owns: a headless `Service` (stable pod DNS + `publishNotReadyAddresses: true` for federation startup), a client-facing `ClusterIP` `Service`, a `ConfigMap` carrying the rendered `rustgate.toml`, an optional `cert-manager.io/v1/Certificate` (per-cluster issuance with SANs covering every replica's pod DNS), and a `StatefulSet` with rustgate's standard security context (`runAsNonRoot`, `readOnlyRootFilesystem`, `seccompProfile=RuntimeDefault`, all capabilities dropped). Owner-references are stamped on every child object so deletion of the parent cascade-deletes the entire fleet. **(4) Federation auto-discovery** — when `spec.federation.autoDiscover: true`, the renderer emits a federation peer list keyed off the StatefulSet's stable pod DNS records (`<name>-N.<headless-svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local`); pods skip themselves at runtime via the federation manager's existing self-id filter so listing every replica unconditionally is safe. **(5) Reconcile contract** — `reconcile::reconcile()` is the deterministic validate → render → status-patch loop a live controller would call. The function takes the wall-clock timestamp as a parameter so the reconcile path is fully snapshot-testable. The terminal `Ready=True` and rejected-spec `Ready=False` conditions are produced by `ready_condition` / `failure_condition` helpers. **(6) Operator binary CLI** — `rustgate-operator render -i my-cluster.yaml | kubectl apply -f -` produces the full multi-document YAML stream from a CRD instance, suitable for one-shot deployments and CI smoke tests; `rustgate-operator validate -i …` exits 0 on success and non-zero with a diagnostic on validation failure. The live cluster controller (`run` subcommand) is documented as a deferred follow-up — the renderer is the source of truth for *what* gets created and the apply-loop is mechanical glue. **(7) Helm chart enhancements** — extended `helm/values.yaml` with `operator.{enabled, image, args, logLevel, resources, …}` and a parallel `cluster.{create, replicas, certManager, federation, storage}` block mirroring the CRD; added `helm/templates/operator-deployment.yaml`, `helm/templates/operator-rbac.yaml` (ServiceAccount + ClusterRole + ClusterRoleBinding scoped to RustgateCluster + StatefulSet/Service/ConfigMap/Certificate + Pod read + Event create), and `helm/templates/rustgatecluster.yaml` so a chart install with `operator.enabled=true` provisions the operator and creates one `RustgateCluster` resource.
