The bare StatefulSet path stays unchanged for deployments that prefer to manage rustgate directly. **(8) One-command smoke test** — `scripts/smoke/k8s/install-and-verify.sh` is a developer-facing script that installs the chart against the active kubeconfig (kind / minikube / k3d / EKS), waits for the operator deployment to become Available, and verifies the StatefulSet reconciles to Ready within 60s. **(9) Workspace plumbing** — added to `Cargo.toml` workspace members and `[workspace.dependencies]`, the main `Dockerfile` cache layer, the new `Dockerfile.operator` for the operator image, `deny.toml` proprietary-license exception, and the workspace `README.md` crate table. **(10) Test coverage** — 18 unit tests in `src/crd.rs`, `src/render.rs`, and `src/reconcile.rs` covering CRD validation (empty name, zero replicas, excess replicas, empty image, invalid service / federation port, empty cert-manager issuer, default-spec round-trip), forward / reverse YAML round-trip, conditional certificate emission, conditional volume-claim emission, owner-reference attachment, federation peer list generation, validation propagation through the reconcile path, and the `Ready` / `Progressing` / failure-condition shapes. 13 integration tests in `tests/reconcile.rs` exercise the full public API plus 5 golden-render snapshot tests that pin the rendered YAML for the full-spec, minimal-spec, no-cert-manager, no-auto-discover, and no-audit-log-PVC permutations. **(11) Out of scope (deferred to follow-up issues).** **HorizontalPodAutoscaler integration** — separate follow-up; the StatefulSet already exposes the standard scaling surface, but the operator does not yet reconcile a paired `autoscaling/v2/HorizontalPodAutoscaler`. **Backup / restore controllers** — separate follow-up; the operator owns the StatefulSet lifecycle but does not yet drive snapshotting of the store-and-forward redb queue or the encrypted audit-log archive. **Multi-cluster federation across Kubernetes clusters** — separate follow-up; the auto-discovery path generates an in-cluster peer list, but cross-cluster mesh routing requires the federation gRPC service to be exposed as a `LoadBalancer` or via a service mesh, and is a separate concern. **Live cluster controller** — the MVP ships the renderer plus the reconcile contract that a live controller would call; the apply-loop (using `kube::Api` server-side apply, watch streams, and status patches) is mechanical glue and lands in a follow-up that does not change the renderer or CRD contract. Closes #874.

- **`rustgate-inference` crate — edge ML inference pipeline (closes #858)** — scaffolds the model-execution surface that lets a rustgate node attach ML-derived attributes (classification, anomaly score, predicted intent) to entities as they flow through the router. The router stays vendor- and framework-agnostic; only this crate knows about model formats and tensor shapes. **(1) Public trait — `InferenceModel`.** Async `Send + Sync + Debug` trait with `name()`, `metadata() -> &ModelMetadata`, and `infer(&Entity) -> Result<InferenceResult, InferenceError>`. Stateless from the pipeline's perspective; backends with mutable state encapsulate it behind interior mutability. The trait surface is the public extension point — third-party backend crates (ONNX, TensorRT, cloud-served models) implement the trait, register the resulting `Arc<dyn InferenceModel>` with a `Pipeline`, and the pipeline drives every registered model uniformly. **(2) `Pipeline` — hot-reloadable model list.** Holds the registered models behind an `arc_swap::ArcSwap<Vec<Arc<dyn InferenceModel>>>` so the model set can be swapped at runtime without restarting the back-annotation task or the router. `Pipeline::run(&Entity) -> Vec<InferenceResult>` walks every model in registration order, downgrades per-model `Err` to a `tracing::debug!` log (one model failing does not poison the rest), and injects a `low_confidence = true` AttrValue::Bool flag into the result's attribute bag when the per-model or pipeline-wide confidence threshold is not met. The `LOW_CONFIDENCE_KEY` constant is exported so downstream consumers can filter on it. Cloning a `Pipeline` is cheap — clones share the underlying `ArcSwap`. **(3) Configuration — `InferenceConfig` + `PipelineEntry`.** Top-level config block intended to be deserialized from a TOML `[inference]` section. Fields use `kebab-case` at the wire level (`models-dir`, `reload-interval-secs`, `confidence-threshold`) and `deny_unknown_fields` so typos fail at parse time. `ModelTarget` is a closed-vocabulary `Classify | Anomaly | Predict` enum that drives the namespacing convention for the back-annotated metadata bag. `InferenceConfig::validate()` rejects duplicate model names, out-of-range thresholds (must be `[0.0, 1.0]`), and an empty `models-dir`. **(4) Mock backend — `MockInferenceModel` (feature `inference-mock`).** Deterministic in-memory backend used in tests and local development. Returns a fixed label and confidence on every call and synthesises a `mock.entity_uid` attribute so test assertions can distinguish results across multiple entities. Never fails — error-path testing is the responsibility of the per-module unit tests. **(5) Router back-annotation — `wiring::router_callback`.** Builds an `OnRouted` callback that the server binary plugs into `Router::set_on_routed`. The callback decodes the routed message's payload via the supplied `EntityCodecRegistry`, runs the entity through the pipeline, and emits one annotated `RoutableMessage` per produced `InferenceResult` via a configured `InferenceSink` closure. The annotated message preserves the original source identity and destination so authorization and ACL still apply to the re-injected event; only the payload (a JSON envelope with `model` / `label` / `confidence` / `attributes` keys) and `metadata.source_protocol` are rewritten. **(6) Provenance loop avoidance.** The annotated messages carry `metadata.source_protocol = "inference"` (exported as `SOURCE_INFERENCE`). The callback's first action on every invocation is to short-circuit when the inbound message already carries that source — without this guard, every annotated event would itself be routed and re-inferred, producing an infinite loop on the local node. The guard is structurally identical to the federation crate's `SOURCE_FEDERATION` discipline. **(7) Failure surface — `InferenceError`.** Typed `thiserror` enum with `ModelLoadFailed { name, path, reason }`, `InferenceFailed { name, reason }`, `MissingAttribute { name, attribute, uid }`, `OutputDecode { name, reason }`, and `ConfigInvalid { reason }`. Each variant carries enough context to debug a misconfigured pipeline without enabling trace logging. **(8) Test coverage.** 4 unit tests in `config.rs::tests` (duplicate-name rejection, out-of-range threshold rejection, empty-pipeline acceptance, `ModelTarget` round-trip) plus 5 integration tests in `tests/integration.rs` (one result per registered model, low-confidence flagging, empty-pipeline no-op, hot-reload observation, threshold clamping). All integration tests run under the `inference-mock` feature. **(9) Out of scope (deferred to follow-up).** **ONNX runtime backend (`inference-onnx` feature)** — the `ort`-backed `OnnxModel` implementor lands in a follow-up so this PR can ship without taking a dependency on `ort`'s C++ build chain (which would block the CI matrix until a separate dependency-shape decision lands). The trait surface in this MVP is intentionally designed so the ONNX backend slots in without API churn. **GPU / TensorRT backends.** **On-device training and federated learning.** **Result aggregation** (majority vote, per-class score fusion) — the current pipeline returns every model's result; the consumer aggregates as it sees fit. **Server wiring** — the `[inference]` config block, the `inference` feature flag on `rustgate-server`, the `setup::start_inference` helper, and the back-annotation supervisor are scaffolded as per-crate API but not wired into the `rustgate-server` binary in this PR; the wiring lands as a separate small PR once an operator picks a deployment shape (single-server vs federation-of-inference-nodes).

- **`rustgate-correlation` crate — multi-sensor track correlation engine (closes #848)** — when the same physical object is reported by multiple sensors (CoT from ATAK, J-series from Link 16, MAVLink position from a drone, a DIS PDU, a SAPIENT detection), the engine fuses the per-sensor reports into a single `FusedEntity` instead of letting an operator (especially an IVAS / AR-headset user) see N duplicate icons in their field of view. **(1) Algorithm** — submission flow runs spatial gating against an `rstar::RTree` keyed on `(longitude, latitude)`, then temporal / kinematic / type-compatibility gates, then a weighted-sum score with the match threshold pinned at `0.5`. Defaults: 100 m ground / 500 m air / 250 m marine / 200 m default spatial threshold; 30 s temporal window; 25 m/s kinematic tolerance; 100 000 fused-entity LRU cap. **(2) Type compatibility table** — `Aircraft × Ground = incompatible`, `Aircraft × Marine = incompatible`, etc., across the four specific platform kinds (`Aircraft`, `Ground`, `Marine`, `Munition`); permissive variants (`Track`, `Sensor`, `Unknown(_)`) fuse with any specific kind because they represent operator uncertainty rather than a positive identification — a SAPIENT "blob detected" report MUST be allowed to fuse with a CoT "friendly aircraft at coords" report. **(3) Position fusion** — inverse-variance weighted mean across contributing sources, weight derived from `correlation.ce90` (CE90 → 1-σ via the 1.645 scalar), `correlation.position_uncertainty_m`, or `cot.ce` attributes when published, falling back to a unit weight (newest-wins-bias) when neither is published. The fused altitude only averages sources that all carry an `hae_meters` value; mixing has-altitude and no-altitude sources is intentionally suppressed to avoid a systematic downward bias. **(4) Public API** — `CorrelationEngine::new` / `with_config` / `submit` / `submit_at` / `query_at` / `snapshot` / `expire_stale`; `CorrelationConfig` with per-kind thresholds and renormalisable fusion weights; typed `CorrelationOutcome` enum with `Created` / `Merged` / `Updated` / `Rejected{reason}` variants so router callbacks can drive metrics off the verdict shape; scoring primitives (`spatial_score`, `temporal_score`, `kinematic_score`, `type_score`, `types_compatible`) and fusion primitives (`fuse_position`, `fuse_classification`, `haversine_distance_m`) re-exported from `lib.rs` for callers that want to score against an external candidate set. **(5) Same-source fast path** — a flood of position updates from one sensor (e.g. a 1 Hz CoT publisher) returns `CorrelationOutcome::Updated(id)` after refreshing the source's `last_seen` and recomputing the fused position, without re-running the gate ladder. **(6) Hard temporal gate** — fused entities older than `time_window` are skipped during candidate scoring even when the spatial / kinematic / type components combine above the threshold. Mirrors the `expire_stale` policy so a long-stale entity cannot accidentally absorb a fresh report on a single high-confidence-spatial match. **(7) LRU eviction** — at `max_entities` capacity, the least-recently-updated fused entity is dropped before a new one is inserted; eviction tracks `last_update` (LRU read on submit) rather than insertion time so an old-but-active entity stays warm. **(8) Server wiring (`--features correlation`)** — gated behind the new `correlation` feature on `rustgate-server`. The setup path constructs a `CorrelationEngine`, builds an `OnRouted` callback via `rustgate_correlation::router_callback` (which decodes payloads through the existing `EntityCodecRegistry` so codec failures fall through silently), composes it with the existing video-stream catalog callback when `--features video` is also set, and exposes a `GET /api/correlation/fused-entities` snapshot endpoint via the admin HTTP server. **(9) Test surface** — 35 unit tests in `src/` covering scoring primitives, fusion math, the type-compatibility table, `EntityKind` symmetry pinning, and `CorrelationConfig` round-tripping; 14 integration tests in `tests/integration.rs` covering two-sensor target fusion, type-incompatible separation, spatial gating, temporal gating, LRU eviction at cap, three-sensor CE90-weighted bias, the same-source fast path, kinematic gating with disagreeing speeds, the `Unknown` permissive-kind path, and the spatial-query result ordering. Deferred to follow-ups: track-history retention (foundation for after-action review), multi-hypothesis tracking when two candidates both score above threshold, full Kalman-filter covariance update at the position-fusion boundary, and per-tenant engine isolation.

- **Marti API compatibility shim for drop-in TAK Server replacement (closes #863)** — added the `marti-compat` feature on `rustgate-admin` (and the matching umbrella feature on `rustgate-server`) that mounts `/Marti/api/*` on the admin HTTP server, mapping each Marti URL to the existing rustgate subsystem rather than re-implementing functionality. **(1) `POST /Marti/api/tls/signClient[/]`** — Basic-auth-gated CSR signing path that calls into the shared `rustgate_enrollment::CsrSigner` and returns a TAK-compatible PKCS#12 (`.p12`) bundle (`Content-Type: application/x-pkcs12`); the authenticated username overrides the CSR subject (subject-injection-proof) and the bundle is signed using the workspace `rustgate_enrollment::pkcs12::build_p12_bundle` so the signing path is one codebase, not two. **(2) `GET /Marti/api/tls/config`** — unauthenticated preflight returning the CA certificate (base64 DER) plus the static accepted-cipher / protocol-version list (`TLSv1.3`, `TLSv1.2`); ATAK is tolerant about extra fields, so we ship a stable JSON shape rather than reproducing TAK Server's exact XML envelope. **(3) `GET /Marti/api/missions`** — package inventory drawn from the lightweight `rustgate_missions::PackageStore` (#1329) wrapped in the Marti `Mission` envelope (`type`, `data`, `nodeId`). **(4) `GET /Marti/api/contacts/all`** — connected-client list translated into the field-stable ATAK shape (`uid`, `callsign`, `team`, `role`, `takv`, `endpoint`, `lastStatus`, `filterGroups`); the source is the same `ContactsProvider` callback the enrollment-server Marti endpoints already use, so a deployment running both servers gets coherent data. **(5) `GET /Marti/api/video`** — video stream catalog (#1328) projected into the Marti `Feed` envelope with the per-stream `protocol` field inferred from the URL scheme (`rtsp` / `rtmp` / `https` / etc.). **(6) Auth model** — `signClient` requires HTTP Basic auth (the standard TAK enrollment flow); the read-only endpoints accept the standard admin bearer token (same shape as the `missions_api` / `acl_api` modules) so an operator who already provisioned the admin token does not have to mint a second one — `tls/config` stays open because TAK clients hit it before they have a truststore. Each subsystem slot on `MartiCompatState` is independently optional: a deployment that has wired up only one or two subsystems still gets those endpoints working and the others surface as silent-success empty envelopes (or `503` for `signClient`) so an ATAK client polling for missions does not spin in retry loops. **Test coverage:** 11 unit tests in `marti_compat::tests` (auth gating with bearer token, prefix case-sensitivity, ATAK-shape contact translation, video metadata projection, scheme inference, sign-client round-trip with a real `rcgen` CSR producing a PKCS#12 SEQUENCE) plus 5 integration tests in `tests/marti_compat.rs` (full state round-trip across all five endpoints, empty-state behaviour, trailing-slash on `signClient`, bearer gate with multi-endpoint coverage, and the constant-pinning test for `MARTI_PREFIX`). **Out of scope (deferred):** `Marti/api/sync/*` mission sync (lands with the rest of #860), `Marti/api/cot/xml` live CoT push (would need a WebSocket tap into the router — separate concern), and the deprecated XML response variants (we ship JSON only — ATAK is tolerant about format). Closes #863.

- **Multi-tenant data isolation at rest (closes #859)** — coalition / multi-customer deployments now partition historical data per tenant so a compromised archive or store-and-forward queue cannot leak across tenant boundaries. The runtime tenant identifier — already populated on `Identity.tenant` from the certificate Organization (`O=`) field and used by `TenantQuotaTracker` for connection / rate limits — now flows through to data-at-rest surfaces. **(1) `Metadata::tenant_id`** — additive optional field on `rustgate_core::message::Metadata`, populated at the `Router::route_for_egress` accept path from `Identity.tenant`. Idempotent: a federated peer that already populated the field upstream is preserved verbatim. The new `with_tenant_id()` builder + `tenant_id()` accessor follow the `#[non_exhaustive]` + `with_*` pattern (refs #1303 / #1306) so existing call sites compile unchanged. **(2) Tenant-partitioned archive directories** — `rustgate-archive` writes to `<archive-dir>/<tenant>/cot-<date>.jsonl[.enc]` instead of the legacy flat layout. Path components are sanitised (path-traversal characters → `_`, leading dots collapsed) so a hostile cert Organization field cannot escape `<archive-dir>`. Messages with no tenant land under the reserved `_default` bucket so single-tenant deployments observe one extra path component and nothing else. The rotation task recurses one level deep (deliberately shallow — sub-sub-directories stay opaque) so `max_bytes` / `max_age` apply across every tenant subdirectory, with each tenant's active segment excluded from deletion sweeps via the new `active_paths()` accessor. The JSONL line embeds a `"tenant":"…"` field so a forensic analyst can re-bucket records that have been merged out of their original directory. **(3) Tenant-partitioned store-and-forward queues** — envelope bumped to v3 carrying an optional `tenant_id`; v1 / v2 records still decode (with `tenant = None`) so on-disk queues written by pre-PR binaries replay cleanly. The new `ClientQueue::drain_for_tenant(cn, Option<&str>)` filters drains by stored tenant: a connecting client whose tenant differs from a queued entry's tenant cannot drain that entry — it stays in the queue for the rightful owner's reconnect. Legacy entries (no tenant) drain to any caller, preserving backward compat. The router accept path now invokes the new `Router::drain_offline_messages_for_identity()` which threads `Identity.tenant` through. **(4) NATS subject tenant prefix (opt-in)** — new `tenant_subject_prefix: bool` on `NatsConfig` (default `false` for wire-compat). When enabled and the message carries a tenant tag, the live + JetStream history subjects are prefixed with `tenant.<sanitized-tenant>.` — same NFC + ASCII sanitisation as the existing group/UID tokens, so subject-injection attempts (`evil.>`) collapse to safe single tokens. Tenant-blind subscribers must extend their wildcards (`tenant.*.<subject_prefix>.>`) to keep observing once enabled. **(5) Per-tenant Prometheus metrics with cardinality cap** — new `rustgate_router_fanout_by_tenant_total{destination, tenant}` and `rustgate_router_dropped_by_tenant_total{reason, tenant}` counters as siblings of the existing tenant-blind family. The `tenant` label is filtered through `tenant_label_for(metric, tenant)` which caps distinct-label admissions per metric at `MAX_TENANT_LABELS = 256`; once exceeded, every subsequent tenant collapses to the reserved `_overflow` bucket and a single `audit::tenant_isolation_label_overflow(metric, count)` event fires per metric per process so a tenant-id flood cannot exhaust Prometheus memory. New `OnFanoutByTenant` / `OnDroppedByTenant` callback type aliases let the metrics layer feed without coupling `rustgate-router` to Prometheus. **(6) Cedar policy hook** — the existing `Identity.tenant` already flows into the `AuthzContext`, so Cedar policies can match on `principal.tenant == "acme"` without further plumbing. **(7) New shared constants in `rustgate-core::constants`** — `DEFAULT_TENANT_ARCHIVE_KEY = "_default"`, `TENANT_OVERFLOW_LABEL = "_overflow"`, `MAX_TENANT_LABELS = 256`. **(8) New audit event** — `tenant_isolation_label_overflow(metric: &str, distinct_tenants: usize)` records the cardinality-cap trip in the compliance audit trail. **(9) Out of scope (deferred).** **Position cache tenant key** — low risk in practice; deferred until cross-tenant cache leaks are observed in operator deployments. **Federation peer-state partitioning** — federation already keys per-peer state, and tenant slicing across peers is a separate refactor that touches the gRPC service contract. Both deferrals are noted in the PR body so operators with sensitive coalition deployments can request the follow-up explicitly. **(10) Test coverage** — 8 new unit tests on `Metadata` builder + serde round-trip + backward-compat shapes, 4 archive tests covering default-bucket fallback / per-tenant directory split / path-traversal sanitisation / `active_paths` enumeration, 3 store-and-forward tests covering cross-tenant drain isolation / legacy-entry compatibility / v3 envelope round-trip plus a new v2 backward-compat test, 3 NATS publisher tests covering off-by-default / sanitised-prefix / no-tenant-fallback, 2 metrics tests covering the 256-cap overflow + default-bucket handling, and 2 audit-emit tests. The cross-tenant SF test queues messages under tenant A then attempts a drain under tenant B and asserts the messages remain in storage; the metrics overflow test pumps 257 distinct tenants and asserts the 257th lands under `_overflow` with the audit event firing exactly once.

- **Expanded management REST API + MOSA OSMP document (closes #875)** — adds eight new endpoints on the admin HTTP server behind a new `management-api` feature flag and ships the formal Open Systems Management Plan as `docs/mosa-osmp.md`. **(1) New endpoints.** `GET /api/config` dumps the running CLI as JSON with secret fields redacted via the existing `#[serde(skip_serializing)]` and `#[serde(serialize_with = "redact_…")]` attributes on the CLI struct (so the same redaction surface that governs `--print-config-toml` controls this endpoint — there is no second redaction surface that can drift). `POST /api/config/reload` fires the same shared `Notify` SIGHUP and the legacy `/api/reload` endpoint observe and returns `202 Accepted`. `GET /api/clients` snapshots the connected-client list from the router's session registry; `GET /api/clients/{cn}` returns the same shape plus per-session `queue_depth` and `rate_limit_per_sec` (both `null` until per-session telemetry plumbing lands), with `404` when no live session matches. `GET /api/metrics/summary` returns a JSON summary of the most-relevant Prometheus counters (router fanout/dropped totals, store-forward depth, federation peer count) so operators reading the HTTP API don't have to parse Prometheus text format. `GET /api/store-forward` returns the per-CN store-and-forward queue snapshot with `enabled: false` when no queue is configured. `GET /api/audit/verify` runs `rustgate_archive::audit_chain::verify_audit_log` over the configured `--audit-log` path and returns a typed report (`verified: true/false`, `records`, `tip`, `tip_seq`); a corrupt chain returns `verified: false` with the diagnostic on `error` (still HTTP 200 — operators distinguish via `verified`). `GET /api/version` returns build identity: package version, git hash from `RUSTGATE_GIT_HASH`, the list of compiled-in feature flags, and a `fips_active` flag derived from `cfg!(feature = "fips")`. **(2) Auth model.** All endpoints reuse the existing `--mgmt-api-token-file` bearer-token discipline (constant-time `subtle::ConstantTimeEq`, `zeroize::Zeroizing` wrapping, 32–256 byte length validation), so a single operator-managed token controls every mutating REST surface on the admin port. The MOSA OSMP calls for an "admin cert OU group" gate on write endpoints; the metrics HTTP server fronting this API uses bearer tokens (not mTLS), so the bearer token itself is the admin credential — a future PR can layer mTLS in front by capturing the peer cert and checking its OU membership without changing the per-endpoint contract. **(3) Wiring.** The new `rustgate_admin::management_api` module ships the handlers, response shapes (`ClientSnapshot`, `ClientDetail`, `MetricsSummary`, `StoreForwardSnapshot`, `VersionInfo`, `AuditVerifyReport`), and a `Providers` callback bag the wiring layer fills with `Arc`-shared closures over the running router/CLI. The bag is held as `Option<…>` so a partially-wired deployment (no federation, no store-and-forward) registers the handler with missing providers and the affected endpoints degrade to structured `503`s rather than misreporting data. The dispatcher in `rustgate-admin::server::serve` gains a `ManagementApiHandler` slot and routes the new prefixes to it before falling through to the legacy `mgmt_api` handler — `/api/clients/{cn}/disconnect` continues to be served by the legacy slot unchanged. **(4) MOSA OSMP document.** New `docs/mosa-osmp.md` documents how rustgate satisfies the four DoD MOSA pillars (Modular Design, Major Interfaces, Open Standards, Certified Conformance), enumerates the 39-crate workspace, the seven load-bearing extension traits (`Codec`, `EntityCodec`, `PolicyEngine`, `PeerDiscovery`, `LatticeBridge`, `FoundryBridge`, `DdsBridge`), the 23 open standards rustgate implements (CoT, MAVLink v1/v2, MQTT 5.0/3.1.1, NATS, gRPC + Protobuf, mTLS RFC 8446, X.509 RFC 5280, EST RFC 7030, SPIFFE, Cedar, JREAP-C/Link 16, VMF MIL-STD-6017, DIS IEEE 1278.1, STANAG 4586, ASTERIX, SAPIENT BSI Flex 335, STANAG 5527 NFFI, OGC SensorThings v1.0, NGVA/VICTORY DDS, FIPS 140-3, CNSA 2.0 planned, GeoJSON RFC 7946, TAK Data-Packages), the 11-job CI conformance ladder, the 18+ load-bearing ADRs, the configuration-management surface (CLI struct as the schema source of truth, hot reload via SIGHUP and `POST /api/config/reload`), and the lifecycle policy (semantic versioning, one-minor-release deprecation window, coordinated security-advisory disclosure). **(5) Documentation.** `docs/rest-api.md` is extended with the new endpoint table, request/response shapes, and `curl` examples — no duplication, the section sits alongside the legacy management-API docs. **(6) Tests.** 17 new unit tests in `crates/rustgate-admin/src/management_api.rs::tests` cover handler dispatch, auth (missing / wrong / malformed token), each endpoint's success path, the legacy-disconnect-subroute fall-through behaviour, the `POST /api/config/reload` notify contract, and the synthetic-chain `audit/verify` path. 13 integration tests in `crates/rustgate-admin/tests/management_api.rs` exercise the same surface end-to-end with the typed JSON envelope assertions the spec required (200 with admin token, 401/403 without, JSON shape pinning, the synthetic-chain `VerifyReport` cross-check, the version-endpoint `version`/`git_hash`/`features`/`fips_active` field-presence assertions). **(7) MVP scope and deferred work.** The MVP wires the directly-available client fields (cn, fingerprint, groups, tenant) and reports the others (`connected_at`, `bytes_rx`, `bytes_tx`, `source_protocol`, `queue_depth`, `rate_limit_per_sec`) as JSON `null` so dashboards can scrape unconditionally; per-session telemetry plumbing lands as a follow-up. SSE / WebSocket live-streaming variants of `/api/clients` and the `metrics/summary` are out of scope for the MVP. mTLS-fronted admin (admin cert OU group enforcement on write endpoints) is captured in the OSMP as the natural next step but does not change the per-endpoint contract. Closes #875.
- **`rustgate-ogc-sensorthings` crate — OGC SensorThings v1.0 client integration (closes #869 alongside the parallel NFFI follow-up)** — third deliverable of the autonomous-sensor / counter-UAS umbrella tracked under #869. Issue covers SAPIENT (BSI Flex 335, shipped in #1327), NFFI (STANAG 5527, parallel PR), and OGC SensorThings (this PR — REST + JSON + MQTT for IoT sensor data); with this PR plus the NFFI PR both merged, #869 closes. **(1) HTTP polling client** — `SensorThingsClient` is a thin wrapper around a configured `reqwest::Client` plus per-subscription URL composition. For every subscription `S` with `datastream-id = N` the client issues a `GET <endpoint>/Datastreams(<N>)/Observations?$top=<page>&$orderby=phenomenonTime+asc[&$expand=Datastream/Thing/Locations][&$filter=phenomenonTime gt <iso8601>]`. The `?$expand=Datastream/Thing/Locations` clause is the standard SensorThings idiom for fetching the sensor station's lat/lon in a single round trip; the `?$filter=phenomenonTime gt …` clause is added once the polling task has seen at least one `phenomenonTime`, so subsequent polls request only newer observations. `reqwest` is configured with `rustls-tls` + `json` features, redirects disabled (defense against SSRF redirects to internal endpoints), connect-timeout 5 s, and the `Rustgate` user-agent string. **(2) Strict-subset wire types** — `Observation` / `Datastream` / `Thing` / `Location` / `ObservationsPage` typed structs cover the slice of SensorThings v1.0 the polling MVP consumes. Optional fields are `Option<…>` with `#[serde(default)]` so a server that omits `@iot.selfLink` or `@iot.count` decodes cleanly. The polymorphic `Observation.result` rides as `serde_json::Value` and the polymorphic `Location.location` (GeoJSON document) rides the same way. **(3) `Observation` → `Entity` projection** — `mapper::observation_to_entity` is a pure function that projects the `@iot.id`, `Datastream.name`, the first `Locations[0].location` (when GeoJSON `Point`), and the full `attributes.sensorthings.*` namespace onto the canonical `rustgate_core::entity::Entity`. The `Datastream.@iot.id`, `Thing.@iot.id`, `unitOfMeasurement.symbol`, `phenomenonTime`, `resultTime`, and `result` (typed by JSON shape — scalars ride as `AttributeValue::{Int, Float, Str, Bool}`, structured shapes ride as a stringified `result_json`) are all preserved on the attribute bag so a downstream consumer can recover the upstream document. The mapper rejects out-of-range coordinates (`lat ∉ [-90, 90]` or `lon ∉ [-180, 180]`) by leaving `Entity::position = None` and preserving the raw GeoJSON under `attributes.sensorthings.location_geojson`; non-`Point` GeoJSON shapes (`LineString`, `Polygon`, `MultiPoint`) ride opaque the same way. **(4) TOML config** — `[sensorthings]` block with `kebab-case` field names and `deny_unknown_fields`. Top-level fields: `endpoint` (validated for `http(s)://` scheme at runtime), optional `auth-token-path` (bearer token loaded by the wiring layer at startup), `poll-interval-secs` (default 30), `request-timeout-secs` (default 10), `expand-location` (default `true`). Repeated `[[sensorthings.subscriptions]]` tables: `datastream-id` (validated `> 0`, no duplicates), `entity-kind` (closed-vocabulary tag mapping to `EntityKind::{Sensor, Track, Aircraft, Ground, Marine, Munition}` — defaults to `Sensor`), optional `group` (`Destination::Group(<group>)` when set, `Broadcast` otherwise), optional `poll-interval-secs` and `page-size` overrides. **(5) Background polling task** — `wiring::spawn_polling_task` returns a single `SubsystemHandle` that drives graceful shutdown for the entire SensorThings subsystem. One per-subscription tokio task per configured `[[subscriptions]]` entry polls on the effective interval, advances the cursor to the maximum `phenomenonTime` seen on each successful page, and routes each emitted observation through `Router::route` as a `RoutableMessage` carrying a synthetic `Identity::plaintext("ogc-sensorthings", …)` source, `MessageType::Status`, and `metadata.source_protocol = "ogc-sensorthings"`. The synthetic-identity convention mirrors the federation inbound, NATS bridge, and Foundry inbound paths; the `source_protocol` constant is exported as `wiring::SOURCE_OGC_SENSORTHINGS` so audit and per-protocol metrics stay greppable. **(6) Typed failure surface** — `SensorThingsError` covers `Transport` (DNS / TCP / TLS / hung-up sockets), `HttpStatus { status, message }` (server-side non-success — the body is preserved as the message), `Decode` (JSON shape mismatch — the polling task logs and skips so a single malformed observation cannot wedge the loop), `Timeout`, and `Config`. `is_transient()` classifies which variants benefit from backoff + retry — used by the polling task's backoff decision. **(7) Server wiring** — feature-gated `ogc-sensorthings` flag on `rustgate-server` plus the `--ogc-sensorthings-config` CLI flag. `setup::start_ogc_sensorthings` reads the TOML, validates the block, optionally loads the bearer token from `auth-token-path`, builds the polling client, and spawns the supervisor. Failure cases log via `tracing::warn!` and the rest of the server continues unchanged — SensorThings is opt-in and a misconfigured block must not block startup. **(8) Workspace plumbing** — added to `Cargo.toml` workspace members and `[workspace.dependencies]`, `Dockerfile` cache layer, `deny.toml` proprietary-license exception, the workspace `README.md` crate table, the new `--ogc-sensorthings-config` CLI option, and the `ogc-sensorthings` feature on `rustgate-server`. **(9) Test coverage** — 6 integration tests in `tests/polling.rs` (full polling cycle through wiremock with `$expand=Datastream/Thing/Locations` round-tripping `Entity::position`, since-cursor `?$filter=` clause, HTTP 500 → typed `HttpStatus` + transient classification, HTTP 404 → non-transient classification, malformed JSON → typed `Decode`, bearer token attached to request, request timeout) plus 35 unit tests across `client.rs::tests` (URL composition, expand/filter/page-size clauses, debug redaction of bearer token, normalisation of trailing slash, transient-status classifier), `config.rs::tests` (full TOML round-trip, default fallthrough, kebab-case rejection of underscore form, zero-id rejection, duplicate-id rejection, non-http endpoint rejection, zero-interval rejection, EntityKindTag closed-vocabulary projection, override resolution, `[sensorthings]` wrapper-table parsing), `mapper.rs::tests` (full deep-expand projection with all attribute keys, no-expand → `position = None`, scalar / array / null / boolean result projection, non-Point GeoJSON kept opaque, out-of-range coordinates dropped, `EntityKind` taken from caller, missing `unitOfMeasurement.symbol` skipped cleanly, empty Locations array → `position = None`, 2-D vs 3-D Point projection, `location_to_position` direct-call coverage), `types.rs::tests` (round-trip across deep-expand and missing-optional shapes, scalar / string / array result decode), and `wiring.rs::tests` (group destination resolution, empty-group → broadcast, payload is serialised `Entity`, source-protocol tag pinning). **(10) Out of scope (deferred to follow-up issues).** **MQTT push subscription** — the SensorThings v1.0 spec defines a parallel MQTT transport (`v1.0/Datastreams(N)/Observations`) with the byte-identical `Observation` payload. The MVP exposes the polling path only; the MQTT half lands in a follow-up and reuses `rustgate-mqtt`'s client capability + the `mapper` module verbatim. **HistoricalLocations / FeaturesOfInterest enumeration** — the MVP polls `Datastreams(N)/Observations` and resolves Location via `$expand`. The full hypermedia surface is not exposed. **Server-side filter authoring** — operators configure `$filter` strings via TOML, but the crate does not compose filters from rustgate-side ACL/authz state. **Submitting observations back** — this is a one-way client (server → rustgate). Bidirectional support (`POST /Observations`) is out of scope. **Token rotation** — the bearer token is loaded once at startup; rotation lands alongside the future SIGHUP-driven config-reload umbrella. **(11) Companion protocols.** Issue #869 covers SAPIENT (BSI Flex 335) + NFFI (STANAG 5527) + OGC SensorThings (this crate). SAPIENT shipped in #1327; NFFI ships alongside this PR. With this PR plus the NFFI PR both merged, #869 closes.

### Security

- **`air_gap.violation` audit event (refs #871)** — fires whenever a configured external endpoint (HTTP egress target URL, OTEL exporter endpoint, OCSP responder, peer-discovery service) resolves to a non-private host while `--air-gap` (or `RUSTGATE_AIR_GAP=1`) is set. The masked endpoint and the offending subsystem are captured on the audit record so the compliance trail records exactly what the operator misconfigured. The mTLS data plane is unaffected — air-gap only governs outbound configuration.

- **Resolved RUSTSEC-2024-0436 (`paste` unmaintained, closes #1315)** — refreshed the `deny.toml` advisory-ignore justification to reference the latest auto-regenerated tracking issue. `paste` is purely transitive — `cargo tree --workspace --features jemalloc -e normal -i paste` confirms the only entry point is `rustgate-server -> tikv-jemalloc-ctl 0.6.1 -> paste 1.0.15`. No workspace crate imports `paste::*` or invokes the `paste!` macro, so a swap to `pastey` would require forking `tikv-jemalloc-ctl` itself. Upstream tikv/jemallocator#130 (migrating to `preinterpret`) is still open at the time of writing; the existing `deny.toml` ignore tracks that PR as the removal trigger. The advisory is informational ("unmaintained"), `paste` is a compile-time proc-macro with no runtime surface, and the `cargo deny check` pipeline continues to gate every `Cargo.lock` change through the `sources` policy. The justification now references #714 (original observation), #1249 (re-investigation), and #1315 (current github-actions auto-regenerated tracking issue) so the next regeneration finds a single growing dashboard rather than a fresh entry. No code, dependency, or `Cargo.lock` change — `cargo deny check` continues to report `advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`. Closes #1315.

### Added

- **`rustgate-dds` crate — DDS Pub/Sub bridge for NGVA / VICTORY in-vehicle data buses (closes #870; DDS half — GeoJSON output landed in #1326)** — new workspace crate `rustgate-dds` ships the integration scaffold for the DDS (Data Distribution Service) bridge mandated by NATO Generic Vehicle Architecture (NGVA, STANAG 4754) and US Army VICTORY. The crate delivers: **(1) the `DdsBridge` async trait** with three methods (`subscribe_topic` returning a `BoxStream<DdsSample>`, `publish_sample`, `shutdown`); **(2) the wire types** `DdsSample { topic, source_guid, timestamp, payload }` plus the canonical DDS QoS shape `QosProfile { reliability, durability, history }` with `Reliability::{BestEffort, Reliable}`, `Durability::{Volatile, TransientLocal, Transient, Persistent}`, and `History::{KeepLast { depth }, KeepAll }` — exposed alongside two convenience constants (`QosProfile::TELEMETRY` for high-rate Navigation / Video topics, `QosProfile::COMMAND` for Weapons / Alarms where no sample may be lost); **(3) `MockDdsBridge`** under the `dds-mock` feature flag — in-memory broadcast-channel-per-topic implementation with `set_unavailable(true)` transient kill-switch + permanent `shutdown()` lifecycle, append-only per-topic publish log for test inspection, and `inject_sample()` helper for inbound test paths; **(4) `DdsConfig`** TOML schema (`kebab-case`, `deny_unknown_fields`) with `domain-id`, `participant-name`, and a `[[subscriptions]]` array carrying `topic`, `entity-kind`, optional `qos` (defaults to `QosProfile::TELEMETRY`), and a `property-map` table; **(5) `PropertyMapper`** dotted-path projection machinery (supported entity-side paths: `uid`, `callsign`, `mil_std_2525_sidc`, `position.lat|lon|hae_meters`, `velocity.speed_m_s|course_deg`, `attributes.<key>`); **(6) inbound / outbound wiring tasks** — `spawn_outbound` returns an `OutboundHandle` with a bounded `mpsc` channel + `SubsystemHandle`; `spawn_inbound` opens one DataReader per configured topic and routes inbound samples into the `Router` as `RoutableMessage` envelopes carrying a synthesised `Identity::plaintext("dds", …)` source and `Destination::Broadcast`. **NGVA Land Data Model topic mapping** — the trait is generic, with the README and module docs documenting the MVP target schema (`rustgate.ngva.Navigation` → `ground`, `rustgate.ngva.Video` → `sensor`, `rustgate.ngva.Alarms` → `track`, `rustgate.ngva.Weapons` → `munition`). **Offline replay** — when the bridge returns `DdsError::ParticipantUnavailable` the outbound task queues the sample in an in-memory FIFO capped at `OFFLINE_QUEUE_CAPACITY = 4096` entries; on the next successful publish the queue drains in FIFO order with last-writer-wins collapse so duplicate `(topic, uid)` entries are merged to the most-recent projection, and on overflow the oldest entry is evicted. Inbound payloads are JSON-encoded property bags so the property-map machinery is portable across SDKs; a real adapter can translate CDR ↔ JSON inside the implementation. Outbound samples carry a 16-byte `source_guid`; when no `uid` rule is bound the inbound path falls back to a 32-char lowercase-hex GUID rendering for the resulting `Entity::uid`. **Real DDS SDK integration is partner / SDK-gated** so `dds-real` ships as a placeholder feature today; `cyclonedds-rs` is unmaintained as of 2026 and `dust-dds` is pre-1.0, so pinning a specific impl is a contained follow-up behind that flag once a production-grade Rust binding is ready. **Workspace plumbing** — added to `Cargo.toml` workspace members and `[workspace.dependencies]`, `Dockerfile` cache layer, `deny.toml` proprietary-license exception, the workspace `README.md` crate table, the new `dds` / `dds-mock` features on `rustgate-server`, the `cargo-machete` ignored-deps list (always-linked but dispatched via runtime registration), and a feature-gated `init_dds_scaffold` startup hook in `rustgate-server::setup` that emits an operator-visible `tracing::info!` confirmation under `--features dds`. Test coverage: 4 unit tests in `config.rs` (full-config parse, defaults, unknown-field rejection at root, kebab-case enforcement, QoS subscription default), 5 unit tests in `mapper.rs` (forward projection covers every supported path, optional-field skipping, typo surfaces as `PathNotFound`, reverse-overlay layering, round-trip preserves listed fields), 7 unit tests in `mock.rs` (subscribe-then-publish, log records each call, transient-unavailable kill-switch, shutdown blocks subsequent publishes, topic-overwrite invariant, `inject_sample` drives subscribers, idempotent shutdown), 4 unit tests in `wiring.rs` (LWW collapse on same uid, eviction on overflow, GUID hex rendering, build-bindings first-wins on duplicate kind), and 7 integration tests in `tests/wiring.rs` covering the full outbound mock round-trip, unmapped-entity-kind typed error, offline-replay drain on reconnect, last-writer-wins collapse across multiple offline dispatches, post-shutdown publish absorbed by the offline queue, inbound subscription observes published samples, and canonical GUID hex rendering. **Out of scope (deferred):** real DDS SDK calls (`dds-real` placeholder); DDS Security plugin configuration (authentication / access-control / cryptographic plugins are the SDK adapter's responsibility); CDR (Common Data Representation) wire format (the MVP carries JSON-encoded property bags; a real adapter MAY widen this by translating CDR ↔ JSON inside the implementation); DDSI-RTPS discovery tuning; per-mapping configurable inbound `Destination` (today's inbound is `Broadcast`); on-disk persistent offline queue (in-memory MVP; the existing `rustgate-router::store_forward` redb-backed queue is the natural sink for a follow-up). Closes #870 — this PR ships the DDS half alongside the GeoJSON output that landed in #1326.

- **`rustgate-nffi` crate — NFFI (NATO Friendly Force Information, STANAG 5527) Blue Force Tracking XML codec (refs #869)** — second of three deliverables under the autonomous-sensor / coalition-BFT umbrella tracked by #869 (SAPIENT shipped in #1327; OGC SensorThings ships in a parallel PR that closes the issue). New workspace crate `rustgate-nffi` decodes the canonical NFFI v2.0 XML wire form into typed `NffiDocument` / `NffiTrack` records and re-encodes them losslessly. The MVP scope covers (1) the `<nffi xmlns="urn:nato:stanag:5527:nffi:2.0:1">` root with verbatim namespace preservation; (2) one or more `<track>` children per document; (3) the `<positionalData>` block — `<wgs84Position lat lon alt>` with WGS-84 envelope range checking, `<kinematics speed course accuracy>` with `[0, 360)` course validation, and `<datetime>` with verbatim source-string preservation alongside a parsed `SystemTime`; (4) the `<identificationData>` block — typed `<sidc>` (15-char APP-6A), `<unitName>`, `<nationality>`; (5) the 15-character APP-6A SIDC parser in `sidc.rs` decoding positions 1-4 (coding scheme, affiliation, battle dimension, status) into typed enums plus an `entity_kind()` dispatch from battle dimension to canonical `EntityKind` (`A` → `Aircraft`, `G` → `Ground`, `S`/`U` → `Marine`, everything else → `Track`); and (6) a `NffiCodec` implementation of `rustgate_core::entity::EntityCodec` that participates in the cross-protocol fan-out path established by #847 — the codec surfaces the first `<track>` per document on `to_entity()` and emits a single-track document on `from_entity()`. **Forward compatibility.** Unrecognised sibling elements under `<track>` (typically `<operStatusData>`, but also any future STANAG 5527 revision extension) ride opaque through `UnknownElement` with their attributes and text body intact, so a downstream consumer expecting them is not surprised on round-trip. Same-codec round-trip preserves position to IEEE-754 double precision, kinematics, identification, the verbatim datetime body, and every unknown-element attribute and body. **Wire-format-layer failures** surface through `NffiError`: `Xml(quick_xml::Error)` for malformed XML, `MissingAttribute { element, attribute }` for required attributes (e.g. `lat` on `<wgs84Position>`), `InvalidFloat { element, attribute }` for non-numeric attribute values, `OutOfRange { field, value }` for lat/lon/course outside the WGS-84 / APP-6A envelopes, `InvalidSidcLength { actual }` for SIDC strings whose length is not exactly 15 characters, `NoTracks` for documents whose `<nffi>` root carries zero `<track>` children (rejected at the `EntityCodec::to_entity` boundary so the caller decides between "skip silently" and "log and continue"), `PayloadTooLarge { bytes }` for inputs exceeding the 16 MiB defense-in-depth cap, and `UnsupportedEntity(String)` on the encode path for entities that carry neither a position nor a velocity. **Workspace plumbing.** Added to `Cargo.toml` workspace members and `[workspace.dependencies]`, `Dockerfile` cache layer, `deny.toml` proprietary-license exception, and the workspace `README.md` crate table. Dependency footprint: `bytes`, `quick-xml`, `thiserror`, `rustgate-core` — no new deps introduced. **Test coverage.** Unit tests across `sidc.rs` and `codec.rs` cover 15-char SIDC length validation, the full APP-6A affiliation vocabulary, vendor-specific affiliation byte tolerance, unknown-battle-dimension dispatch fallback, `<wgs84Position>` lat/lon range checks, missing-attribute rejection, malformed-float rejection, kinematics course-out-of-range rejection, malformed-XML rejection, no-tracks rejection at the EntityCodec boundary, `<operStatusData>` opaque passthrough, namespace-omitted document round trip, ISO-8601 round trip through `format_iso8601`/`parse_iso8601`, unit-name → callsign promotion, and SIDC-driven `EntityKind` classification. Integration tests in `tests/roundtrip.rs` cover the full public-API surface plus a programmatic-entity → encode → decode round trip exercising the `from_entity` reconstruction path. **Out of scope (deferred to follow-up issues).** Transport binding (DDS topic adapter, SOAP-over-HTTP listener, REST endpoint wiring); typed `<operStatusData>` decode (operational-status sub-fields ride opaque on `UnknownElement` for the MVP); STANAG 5527 XSD validation (the parser accepts well-formed XML but does not check against the upstream XSD); router-side multi-track entity fan-out (the `EntityCodec` surfaces only the first track per document — typed `decode_document` already returns the full `Vec<NffiTrack>` for callers that want fan-out); `register(NffiCodec)` wiring on the runtime `EntityCodecRegistry`. **Companion protocols.** Issue #869 covers SAPIENT (BSI Flex 335, shipped in #1327) + NFFI (STANAG 5527, this PR) + OGC SensorThings (REST + JSON + MQTT for IoT sensor data). #869 stays open until the OGC SensorThings half also lands. Refs #869.

- **Mesh-native peer-to-peer multi-hop routing for `rustgate-federation` (closes #855)** — the federation layer ships a foundation for mesh routing behind a new `mesh-routing` feature flag. The new `rustgate_federation::mesh` module adds a distance-vector `MeshRoutingTable` keyed by destination `PeerId`, a `MeshRouter` that reuses the existing `provenance::FederationMetadata` chain for hop-count and loop detection, and `add_direct_neighbor` / `withdraw_neighbor` hooks wired into the `FederationManager` lifecycle so mesh state mirrors the live peer set. Forwarding decisions are exposed through `MeshRouter::should_forward(destination, provenance)` returning `ForwardDecision::{Local, Forward, DropLoop, DropTtl, DropNoRoute}`; route advertisements are exchanged as `RouteAdvertisement` payloads and serialize as JSON in the MVP so the federation gRPC schema does not have to change to ship the foundation (a typed proto field is tracked as a follow-up). New audit events `mesh.route_added`, `mesh.route_removed`, `mesh.route_updated`, `mesh.forwarded`, `mesh.loop_detected`, `mesh.ttl_expired`, and `mesh.no_route_to_destination` are emitted on the `audit` target through `rustgate_core::audit::mesh_*` helpers. **Out of scope:** Bluetooth LE peer discovery (separate `peer-discovery-bluetooth` follow-up), link-state (OSPF-like) routing (distance-vector is the MVP; documented as the upgrade path in the module docs), priority-based queuing (already provided by `BackpressureGate`), and split-brain reconciliation. Closes #855.

- **CJADC2 multi-domain routing policy with per-destination obligations (closes #853)** — extended the optional Cedar policy backend to lift a `@route("…")` policy annotation into a new `RoutingDecision` shape that names destination adapters (e.g. `lattice`, `link16`, `foundry`, `dis`) and per-destination [`RouteObligation`] envelopes (`SetClassification`, `DropFields`, `DegradePosition`, `Tag`). The PEP surface adds (1) a new `Action::Route` variant on the existing `Action` enum, (2) a `route` module under `rustgate-authz` with the `RoutingDecision` / `RouteObligation` types and the merge contract (destination set unioned, per-destination obligation vectors concatenated in policy-iteration order), (3) a `PolicyEngine::evaluate_route(subject, resource, context)` trait method with a default implementation returning `RoutingDecision::none()` so non-CJADC2 backends pay nothing and the trait extension is fully backward-compatible, (4) a Cedar-backend override that issues an `Action::"Route"` request, walks `Response::diagnostics().reason()`, and parses each contributing policy's `@route` JSON annotation into a single merged `RoutingDecision` (malformed annotations are skipped with a warning rather than failing the whole evaluation), and (5) a router-side `cjadc2::plan_routing_fanout` planner plus a `Router::plan_cjadc2_routing` entrypoint that produces one `DestinationEnvelope` per known destination so the CJADC2 dispatch loop can fan a single inbound entity out to N adapters with per-destination obligations attached. The feature ladder is `rustgate-router/cjadc2 -> rustgate-authz/cjadc2`; the obligation actuation lives on each destination adapter (Lattice / Link 16 / Foundry / DIS), which is intentionally **out of scope** here — those adapters land independently under #850, #866 (already merged), #851, etc. **Out of scope:** the destination adapters themselves, sink-registry wiring, `evaluate_route` audit emission (allow/deny per-policy correlation tokens are a follow-up), and per-destination metric counters. Tests cover the Cedar round-trip, multi-policy aggregation, malformed annotation handling, principal mismatch, and the `Action::"Route"` does-not-grant-`Action::"send"` boundary. Closes #853.

- **`rustgate-lattice` crate — Anduril Lattice bidirectional adapter (bridge trait + `MockLatticeBridge` + router wiring, closes #850)** — new workspace crate `rustgate-lattice` that lets rustgate present itself as a native Anduril Lattice sensor feed (publishing tactical entities outbound) and as a Lattice command consumer (draining entities inbound and re-injecting them into the router for fan-out across CoT, MAVLink, NATS, and the other registered protocols). The Lattice gRPC SDK ships behind Anduril partnership / NDA, so the actual proto bindings cannot land in this PR. The MVP therefore ships the **integration shape** so a partner-side PR that drops in the actual `tonic` client behind the `lattice-real` feature is a small, contained change that does not have to touch the router, the server binary, or the wiring helpers. Concretely the MVP delivers: **(1) the `LatticeBridge` async trait** — `publish_entity` / `subscribe_entities` / `report_health`, three methods that cover the publish-out / subscribe-in / report-health paths Lattice asks of a third-party data source; **(2) the shared types `Entity` / `EntityFilter` / `EntityKind` / `GeoBbox` / `GeoPosition` / `HealthStatus`** — designed to map cleanly to Lattice's `Entity` / `EntityFilter` proto when those bindings land; **(3) `MockLatticeBridge`** (feature `lattice-mock`) — an in-memory, channel-backed implementation that is sufficient for integration testing the router → bridge → router round trip without an actual Lattice endpoint, and is also a useful blueprint for the real-SDK `LatticeBridge` implementation; **(4) `LatticeConfig`** — TOML deserialisation for the `[lattice]` block in `rustgate.toml` with `kebab-case` field names, `deny_unknown_fields` so operator typos fail fast, and an `auth` sub-block declaring mTLS cert / key paths plus a JWT secret path — no actual SDK call yet, but the schema is wired so the real-SDK PR can consume it without churn; **(5) `spawn_outbound_task` / `spawn_inbound_task`** — background tasks that the server binary uses to plug the bridge into a `rustgate_router::Router`. The outbound task drains a `tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver<RoutableMessage>` (filled from a router callback hook), filters for `MessageType::Position`, maps each message to an `Entity`, and calls `bridge.publish_entity`; it also emits periodic `report_health` ticks on a `cfg.health_interval_secs` cadence. The inbound task calls `bridge.subscribe_entities` once at startup and pumps every yielded entity into `Router::route` as a `RoutableMessage`. Both tasks are parameterised over `Arc<dyn LatticeBridge>` so the partner real-SDK impl plugs in unchanged. **Auth surface.** `LatticeAuth { mtls_cert_path, mtls_key_path, jwt_secret_path }` is declared in the config schema today; the actual TLS / JWT load happens in the real-SDK PR, with the wiring helpers loading paths into `Zeroizing<...>` buffers at the bridge construction site (matching the workspace zeroize discipline). **Test coverage.** 5 integration tests in `tests/wiring.rs` covering outbound publish (position messages reach the bridge), outbound filtering (chat messages do not reach the bridge), inbound routing (an injected entity reaches the router), and health-report cadence (periodic `report_health` calls fire on schedule); 11 unit tests across `bridge`, `config`, `mock`, and `wiring` exercising the type-level surface (filter matching, geo-bbox `contains`, config validation, kind → MessageType mapping, geo-position range guards, double-subscribe rejection on the mock). **Workspace plumbing.** Added to `Cargo.toml` workspace members and `[workspace.dependencies]`, `Dockerfile` cache layer, `deny.toml` proprietary-license exception, the workspace `README.md` crate table, and feature-gated under `lattice` (the trait + config + wiring) and `lattice-mock` (the in-memory mock impl). The server-side wiring lives in `rustgate-server` setup behind `cfg!(feature = "lattice")` startup wiring (the wiring is a no-op if no `[lattice]` config block is present). **Out of scope (deferred to follow-up).** Real Lattice gRPC SDK integration (the actual proto bindings, the `tonic` client, JWT-over-mTLS auth) is partner-NDA-gated and lands behind the `lattice-real` feature flag (currently empty stub) so a no-feature build of the workspace is unaffected and the partner PR has a stable landing spot. Lattice `Task` / `Order` consumer side uses a separate proto + RPC; carrying it in this PR would force a placeholder shape that the real SDK would have to reshape. Backend selection by config (`backend = "mock" | "real"`) adds a config-driven dispatch when both backends actually exist; for now the only available impl is the mock and it is selected by the `lattice-mock` feature flag. Closes #850.

- **`rustgate-foundry` crate — Palantir Foundry / Gotham bidirectional bridge scaffold (closes #851)** — new workspace crate `rustgate-foundry` ships the integration scaffold for the Foundry / Gotham ontology bridge: the `FoundryBridge` async trait (`upsert_object`, `subscribe_changes`, `invoke_action`), the TOML config schema (`FoundryConfig` + repeated `[[foundry.object-types]]` mappings + per-mapping `property-map` table, all `kebab-case` with `deny_unknown_fields`), the `PropertyMapper` dotted-path projection machinery (supported entity-side paths: `uid`, `callsign`, `mil_std_2525_sidc`, `position.lat|lon|hae_meters`, `velocity.speed_m_s|course_deg`, `attributes.<key>`), the `MockFoundryBridge` reference implementation under the `foundry-mock` feature flag (in-memory keyed-by-`(type_id, uid)` store + per-type `tokio::sync::broadcast` change channel + `set_offline(true)` kill-switch), and the inbound / outbound wiring tasks (`spawn_outbound` returns an `OutboundHandle` with a bounded `mpsc` channel + `SubsystemHandle`; `spawn_inbound` opens one subscription per configured object-type and routes change-stream events into the `Router` as `RoutableMessage` envelopes carrying a synthesised `Identity::plaintext("foundry", ...)` source and `Destination::Broadcast`). **Offline replay** — when the bridge returns `FoundryError::Offline` the outbound task queues the upsert in an in-memory FIFO capped at `OFFLINE_QUEUE_CAPACITY = 4096` entries; on the next successful upsert the queue drains in FIFO order with last-writer-wins collapse so duplicate `(type_id, uid)` entries are merged to the most-recent projection, and on overflow the oldest entry is evicted. **Foundry SDK integration is partner-gated** so `foundry-real` ships as a placeholder feature today; plugging the real REST/WebSocket adapter in is a contained change behind that flag once the SDK drops. **Workspace plumbing** — added to `Cargo.toml` workspace members and `[workspace.dependencies]`, `Dockerfile` cache layer, `deny.toml` proprietary-license exception, and the workspace `README.md` crate table. Test coverage: unit + integration tests through the mock bridge covering forward / reverse property projection, `PathNotFound` typo detection, offline-queue admission + drain on reconnect, last-writer-wins UID collapse, the change-stream subscription path, and the queue overflow eviction policy. **Out of scope (deferred):** real REST / WebSocket SDK calls (`foundry-real` placeholder); operator-fired Action stream that injects RoutableMessages on Foundry button-presses (the trait method is final but the wiring lands alongside the SDK); OAuth2 / Bearer / JWT auth (handled by the SDK adapter); per-mapping configurable inbound `Destination` (today's inbound is `Broadcast`); on-disk persistent offline queue (in-memory MVP; the existing `rustgate-router::store_forward` redb-backed queue is the natural sink for a follow-up). Closes #851.

- **`rustgate-link16` crate — Link 16 / JREAP-C (STANAG 5518) tactical-data-link codec for the J2.2 Air Track message (closes #866)** — new workspace crate `rustgate-link16` that decodes and encodes the JREAP-C frame header plus the J2.2 Air Track J-series message, the workhorse "where is the fighter / how fast is it going" payload of every Link 16 net. The MVP scope covers (1) the 16-byte big-endian JREAP-C frame header (`JreapFrame` — version, message_type, exercise_id, sequence, timestamp, body_length); (2) the `JseriesMessage` enum carrying typed `J2_2AirTrack(...)` plus opaque `Other { label, body }` for non-MVP J-series messages so a multi-message TCP stream can still be framed past unknown labels; (3) the J2.2 Air Track body (track number, signed microdegree latitude / longitude, signed metre altitude, platform type, IFF status byte and Mode-3/A code, three-field kinematics — speed in cm/s, course in centidegrees, climb rate in dm/s); and (4) a `Link16Codec` implementation of `rustgate_core::entity::EntityCodec` that participates in the cross-protocol fan-out path established by #847. JREAP-C connection-management messages (link-connect, heartbeat, link-disconnect) and other J-series messages (J3.2 Air PPLI, J3.5 Land Point, J7.0 Track Management, J13.2 Air Platform & System Status, the broader MIL-STD-6016 catalogue) decode to placeholder variants so a follow-up PR can extend the typed coverage one message at a time, mirroring how `rustgate-asterix` grew from CAT-062 to add CAT-021 and CAT-048. Wire-format-layer failures surface through `Link16Error` (truncated buffers, body-length mismatch, unsupported version, unexpected message type, out-of-range latitude/longitude/course); EntityCodec-boundary failures surface through `Link16EntityError` (invalid frame, unsupported message type, unsupported J-series label, unsupported entity kind). The default JREAP-C TCP listener port is exported as the constant `JREAP_DEFAULT_TCP_PORT = 4444` so a future listener-wiring PR can pin it symbolically. STANAG 5518 (JREAP) and MIL-STD-6016 (J-series) are restricted-distribution documents; the wire shapes pinned in this MVP are the layered subset published in open-literature interoperability guides plus the layout pinned by issue #866, with field-width assumptions documented inline so a reviewer with access to the closed spec can correct widths without touching the codec scaffolding. The MVP keeps every J2.2 field byte-aligned for parser simplicity; a follow-up PR can layer the bit-packed MIL-STD-6016 wire form behind the same `J2_2AirTrack` struct shape if a deployment needs the on-radio bit-packed form. **Out of scope:** TLS / HAIPE-encrypted enclave handling for classified-network deployments, TCP listener wiring on port 4444, codec registration in `rustgate-server`, JREAP-A multicast and JREAP-B serial / SATCOM variants, IFF code lookup tables (raw bytes preserved; resolution against the at-issue NATO IFF table is a deployment configuration concern), other J-series messages (J3.2 / J3.5 / J7.0 / J13.2 / full catalogue). Closes #866.

- **GeoJSON ([RFC 7946]) output for HTTP egress targets (refs #870)** — new `PayloadFormat::GeoJson` variant on `rustgate-http::TargetConfig`. Single-message bodies render as a JSON `Feature` (Point geometry from the embedded CoT `<point>` lat/lon/hae); batched bodies render as a `FeatureCollection` per RFC 7946 §3.3. Content-Type is the IANA-registered `application/geo+json`. **(1) Geometry.** Lat/lon/hae from the parsed CoT `<point>` element are promoted to `geometry.coordinates = [lon, lat, alt]` (longitude first per RFC 7946 §3.1.1; altitude in metres above the WGS-84 ellipsoid, matching the CoT `hae` semantic). Non-CoT or position-less payloads emit `"geometry": null` per RFC 7946 §3.2 — Features with no spatial information remain syntactically valid. **(2) Round-trip-safe properties.** Every Feature carries `source_cn`, `source_groups`, `destination`, `message_type`, `source_protocol`, `received_at`, and `instance_id` so a downstream consumer can rebuild the original `RoutableMessage` without re-parsing the XML. CoT-derived `cot_uid`, `cot_type`, and `cot_callsign` (when a `<marti><dest callsign>` is present) ride alongside as best-effort properties. **(3) FeatureCollection batching.** When `batch-enabled = true` and `format = geo_json`, the per-target batcher buffers serialized Features and the renderer wraps them in a `{"type":"FeatureCollection","features":[…]}` envelope — the only batch shape every GIS tool (Leaflet, Mapbox, Kepler.gl, QGIS, ArcGIS) accepts as a first-class spatial dataset. The `batch-format` field (`json-array` / `ndjson`) is ignored on the GeoJSON path because neither flat-JSON shape is a valid `FeatureCollection`. **(4) Validation.** `HttpConfig::validate` now allows `format = json` or `format = geo_json` when batching is enabled; `raw-xml` and `protobuf` continue to be rejected at config-parse time (they have no portable batch wire format). **(5) Test coverage.** 9 unit tests in `crates/rustgate-http/src/geojson.rs` (Feature shape, lon-first coordinate order, properties round-trip, null-geometry contract for non-CoT payloads, FeatureCollection wrapper, content-type literal pin, byte-for-byte feature preservation in the collection envelope, CoT callsign propagation) plus 4 wiremock integration tests in `crates/rustgate-http/tests/geojson_format.rs` (per-message content-type, end-to-end Feature shape, batched FeatureCollection with three messages, non-CoT null-geometry passthrough). **Out of scope (deferred to follow-ups under #870).** DDS Pub/Sub bridge for NGVA/VICTORY (Cyclone DDS Rust bindings, `rustgate-dds` crate, NGVA Land Data Model topic mapping); the GeoJSON half of #870 lands here, the DDS half remains tracked under the umbrella issue. [RFC 7946]: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7946

- **`rustgate-sapient` crate — SAPIENT (BSI Flex 335, NATO/UK MOD) autonomous-sensor protobuf codec (refs #869; closes when NFFI and OGC SensorThings follow-ups land)** — first deliverable of the autonomous-sensor / counter-UAS umbrella tracked under #869. Issue covers three protocols (SAPIENT, NFFI, OGC SensorThings); SAPIENT lands here as the MVP and the remaining two are deferred to follow-up issues. **(1) Wire-format codec** — typed `SapientMessage` / `DetectionReport` / `Location` / `EnuVelocity` / `Classification` / `Timestamp` structs with hand-rolled protobuf encode/decode primitives in `src/proto.rs` (no `build.rs`, dependency footprint stays at `bytes` + `thiserror` + `rustgate-core`). Coordinate fields ride as IEEE-754 doubles (wire type 1, fixed64) — there is no integer scaling on the wire, so same-codec round-trip is bit-exact for every wire-format scalar. SAPIENT's `Location` puts longitude on `x` and latitude on `y` (the spec inverts the conventional ordering); the codec exposes `Location::lat()` / `Location::lon()` accessors so callers do not need to remember the convention. **(2) MVP scope** — `SapientMessage` envelope plus the `DetectionReport` arm fully decoded (location, classification list, ENU velocity, detection confidence, colour, identifier). The seven non-MVP `oneof content` arms (`Registration`, `RegistrationAck`, `StatusReport`, `Task`, `TaskAck`, `Alert`, `AlertAck`, `Error`) ride opaque through `SapientPayload::Other { field_number, bytes }` with the field-number tag preserved — the encoder honours `Other` symmetrically so a future codec revision can lift typed dispatch without breaking the wire form. Inside `DetectionReport`, the optional `track_info` / `object_info` / `behaviour` / `signal` / `prediction_location` / `associated_file` / `associated_detection` / `derived_detection` submessages skip cleanly on the read side (the canonical `Entity` shape does not surface them). **(3) `EntityCodec` implementation** — `SapientCodec` decodes a `SapientMessage` into the canonical `rustgate_core::entity::Entity` shape and re-encodes a position-bearing entity back into a `DetectionReport`-arm envelope. The `DetectionReport` classification list drives `EntityKind` lift (`UAV` / `drone` / `aircraft` / `helicopter` → `Aircraft`; `vehicle` / `person` / `pedestrian` → `Ground`; `vessel` / `boat` / `ship` → `Marine`; `missile` / `munition` / `projectile` → `Munition`; everything else → `Unknown(label)`). The attribute bag carries every wire-format field under the `sapient.*` namespace so same-codec round-trip preserves the lat/lon, classification list, ENU velocity, and metadata round-trip-clean. **(4) Forward-compat decoder** — unknown protobuf fields are skipped by wire type (varint / length-delimited / fixed32 / fixed64) so a future BSI Flex 335 revision that adds new fields stays decodable; varint overflow (>10 bytes), unknown wire types (3, 4, 6, 7), invalid UTF-8 in string fields, and length-delimited prefixes that exceed the 16 MiB defense-in-depth payload cap surface as typed `SapientError` variants rather than panicking. **(5) Workspace plumbing** — added to `Cargo.toml` workspace members and `[workspace.dependencies]`, `Dockerfile` cache layer, `deny.toml` proprietary-license exception, the workspace `README.md` crate table, the documentary `sapient` feature on `rustgate-server`, and the cargo-machete `ignored` list (the codec is dispatched via the runtime `EntityCodecRegistry` from #1304 rather than imported by name in the server source — a follow-up wire-up PR will add the explicit `register(SapientCodec)` call). **(6) Test coverage.** 15 unit tests in `src/proto.rs::tests` (varint round-trip across boundary widths, varint overflow / truncation, unknown wire-type rejection, IEEE-754 double round-trip across positive/negative/sub-normal/extremes, full `DetectionReport` round-trip, full `SapientMessage` round-trip with detection report, opaque `Other` arm byte-exact round-trip, `MissingContent` rejection, over-cap rejection, forward-compat unknown-field skip, invalid-UTF-8 rejection, ENU → speed/course conversion across cardinal directions, ENU speed/course round-trip, lat/lon accessor returns `None` on non-LAT_LNG_DEG_M coordinate systems). 6 unit tests in `src/codec.rs::tests` (entity round-trips through codec, entity-without-position rejection, classification-driven entity-kind lift across 8 cases including unknown labels, truncated payload rejection, missing-content rejection, ENU velocity round-trip via speed/course, over-cap rejection). 7 integration tests in `tests/roundtrip.rs` covering full wire round-trip, opaque-arm byte-exact preservation, full `EntityCodec` round-trip with classification preservation, malformed-input typed-error handling, over-cap rejection, field-number drift sentinel, entity-without-position rejection — plus a property-based test pinning IEEE-754 round-trip across the lat/lon/altitude envelope. **(7) Out of scope (deferred to follow-up issues).** Transport binding (TCP framing / MQTT topic envelope / gRPC body — listener wiring); typed decode of the seven non-MVP `oneof content` arms (`Registration`, `RegistrationAck`, `StatusReport`, `Task`, `TaskAck`, `Alert`, `AlertAck`, `Error`); strict validation against `proto_options` annotations (`is_mandatory`, `is_uuid`, `is_ulid` markers — currently treated as documentary); honouring `ENUVelocityUnits` overrides (the MVP assumes the SI default `m/s` for ENU velocity scalars); typed `RangeBearing` location arm (currently carried opaque on the entity attribute bag); explicit `register(SapientCodec)` wiring on the runtime `EntityCodecRegistry`. **(8) Companion protocols.** Issue #869 covers SAPIENT + NFFI (STANAG 5527, NATO Blue Force Tracking, XML over DDS / SOAP / REST) + OGC SensorThings (REST + JSON + MQTT for IoT sensor data). NFFI and OGC SensorThings are deferred to follow-up issues; #869 stays open until both land.

- **`rustgate-missions` crate — lightweight TAK Data Packages endpoint (Feature 17 of #860; full Missions API deferred) (refs #860)** — new workspace member `crates/rustgate-missions/` gated behind the `missions` feature on `rustgate-admin`. Ships the lightweight half of the TAK Mission Sync feature family tracked under #860: a content-addressed package store keyed by the SHA-256 hash of each ZIP body, with HMAC-SHA256 sidecar tags verified in constant time on every download via `rustgate_core::crypto::hmac_sha256_verify`. **(1) `PackageStore`** — async filesystem store with per-store and per-package size caps (`StoreLimits`, defaulting to 1 GiB total / 50 MiB per package), idempotent uploads (re-uploading the same content returns the existing metadata without rewriting either file), capacity arithmetic serialised through a `tokio::sync::Mutex` so concurrent uploads cannot drive the store past the configured cap, and a startup walk that rebuilds the running total from on-disk sidecars. **(2) HMAC-tagged sidecar envelope** — every `{hash}.meta.json` is a `{ meta, tag }` blob where `tag` is the lowercase-hex HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical metadata `hash || size || name || creator_uid || upload_time` joined with `0x00` separators; tampering with any field invalidates the tag, and the download path refuses to serve the body when verification fails. The HMAC construction goes through the workspace-shared `rustgate_core::crypto::hmac_sha256_*` helpers so the timing-side-channel discipline lives in one place. **(3) Manifest parser** — `manifest::parse_manifest_xml` is a streaming `quick_xml`-based parser for MissionPackageManifest v2 that pulls out the version attribute, the `<Configuration>` parameter map, and each `<Content zipEntry="..."/>` entry. Best-effort by default — unrecognised elements ride through, so a future schema revision does not require a parser change. **(4) Multipart helpers** — `multipart::{extract_boundary, extract_multipart_field, extract_multipart_filename}` host the minimal `multipart/form-data` slicing primitives used by the admin HTTP layer when forwarding TAK-client uploads. The full RFC 7578 surface is out of scope; pulling in `multer` or `axum::extract::Multipart` would add a heavy parser tree for what is fundamentally a four-line scan. **(5) HTTP handler in `rustgate-admin::missions_api`** — feature-gated module mirroring the shape of `acl_api`. Defines `MissionsApiState`, `MissionsApiHandler`, and `handle_request` for the four endpoints: `POST /api/packages` (upload, multipart or raw `application/zip`), `GET /api/packages` (list, JSON array sorted newest-first), `GET /api/packages/{hash}` (download body with `Content-Type: application/zip`), `DELETE /api/packages/{hash}` (remove). Bearer-token auth via `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` matches the discipline used by `acl_api`. Errors map to RFC-7807-style status codes (400 for malformed hash / empty upload, 404 for unknown hash, 413 for oversize package, 507 for store-capacity exceeded). The dispatcher in `admin::server::serve` will be widened to call this handler in a follow-up PR alongside the `--missions-store-path` and `--missions-token-file` CLI flags; the handler and shared state are publicly exported so the follow-up can wire it without further changes to this module. **(6) Workspace plumbing** — `Cargo.toml` workspace members + `[workspace.dependencies]`, `Dockerfile` cache layer, `deny.toml` proprietary-license exception, `README.md` crate-table row, and the new `missions` feature on `rustgate-admin` that pulls the optional `rustgate-missions` dependency. Test coverage: 13 unit tests in `rustgate-missions` (round-trip, idempotency, oversize / capacity rejection, invalid-hash rejection, missing-hash 404, delete decrement, listing order, sidecar tampering rejected with HMAC error, empty-key rejection, hex round-trip, hex decode error paths) + 4 integration tests in `crates/rustgate-missions/tests/store_integration.rs` (cross-restart persistence, foreign-key sidecars silently skipped, default-limit constants, manifest round-trip) + 9 admin-side `missions_api` tests covering auth, dispatch fall-through, raw-ZIP and multipart upload paths, listing, download, delete, invalid-hash 400, and method-not-allowed 405. **(7) Out of scope (Feature 6 of #860, deferred to follow-up).** Full Missions API: `POST /api/missions/{name}` (create), `GET /api/missions/{name}` (metadata), `POST /api/missions/{name}/packages` (upload to mission), `POST /api/missions/{name}/subscribe` (subscribe client), `GET /api/missions/{name}/changes` (Server-Sent Events stream), and the corresponding mission CoT events (`t-x-m-c` created, `t-x-m-d` deleted, `t-x-m-n` notification). Optional `KeyRing`-encrypted body storage via `rustgate_archive::encrypted::EncryptedWriter` is also deferred — the integrity-tag layer is independent and will continue to apply once encrypted bodies land. Federation replication of stored packages across rustgate peers is deferred to a federation V2 message extension. Issue #860 stays open until the Missions follow-up lands.

- **Video stream catalog with `GET /api/video/streams` (closes #862)** — new `video` feature on `rustgate-admin` and `rustgate-server` ships an in-memory catalog populated from CoT `b-i-v` events as they flow through the router. **(1) `VideoStreamCatalog`** lives in `crates/rustgate-admin/src/video.rs` as an `Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, VideoEntry>>>` keyed by event UID. The wiring path is a new `Router::set_on_routed` callback (added to `rustgate-router` alongside the existing `on_multicast_forward` slot so observers compose without colliding with the `--udp-multicast-rebroadcast` rebroadcast hook): the callback inspects every routed message, short-circuits when `metadata.message_type` is not an `Other(s)` whose `s.starts_with("b-i-v")`, and otherwise parses the CoT detail block to extract `<__video url=…>`, `<sensor fov=… azimuth=… elevation=…>`, and the `<point lat lon>` envelope into a `VideoEntry`. **(2) `GET /api/video/streams`** delegates from the existing admin HTTP dispatch ladder in `rustgate_admin::server::serve` to a feature-gated `VideoApiHandler` slot; the handler returns the live catalog snapshot as a JSON array. **(3) Lazy TTL eviction** — entries whose source CoT event carried a `start`/`stale` pair are stamped with `expires_at = received_at + ttl`; the snapshot path drops expired entries before returning, avoiding a periodic sweep task and the lifecycle it would need. **(4) MVP scope.** In-memory only — no on-disk persistence, no RTSP/RTMP proxying. Out of scope: persistence to disk; transport-level video proxy; per-tenant catalog isolation. **(5) Tests.** Five unit tests in `video.rs` (insert / overwrite / non-`b-i-v` skip / TTL eviction / handler shape) plus four integration tests in `tests/video_streams.rs` (end-to-end through `Router::route_for_egress`, JSON shape, TTL eviction, non-video filter).

- **`rustgate-meshtastic` crate — Meshtastic / LoRa TAKPacket compact-protobuf codec (closes #865)** — new `crates/rustgate-meshtastic/` crate gated behind the `meshtastic` workspace feature. **(1) Wire-format codec** — typed `TakPacket` / `Pli` / `GeoChat` / `Contact` / `Group` / `Status` structs with hand-rolled protobuf encode/decode primitives in `src/proto.rs` (no `build.rs`, dependency footprint stays at `bytes` + `thiserror` + `rustgate-core`). The 237-byte LoRa per-frame cap is a typed [`MeshtasticError::PayloadTooLarge`] error rather than a runtime panic; the encoder applies aggressive field pruning (every optional field is omitted when its source value is empty / default) so a sparse PLI-only frame fits well under the cap.
