Coordinate fields ride as `sfixed32` little-endian with the upstream firmware's `× 1e7` scale (≈ 1.1 cm precision globally); altitude uses `int32` (varint, no zig-zag) per the upstream schema; speed and course ride as `uint32` varints with the `× 100` cm/s and hundredth-degree scales documented in module-level rustdoc. **(2) `EntityCodec` implementation** — `MeshtasticCodec` decodes a TAKPacket into the canonical `rustgate_core::entity::Entity` shape and re-encodes a position- or chat-bearing entity back into a compact protobuf payload. Position-bearing entities classify as `EntityKind::Ground` (the typical Meshtastic deployment is dismounted operators and vehicles); chat-bearing entities classify as `EntityKind::Track`; the opaque `detail` arm classifies as `EntityKind::Unknown("meshtastic-detail")`. The attribute bag carries every wire-format field under the `meshtastic.*` namespace so same-codec round-trip preserves the exact wire bytes through the raw-integer carries (`meshtastic.pli.latitude_i`, `meshtastic.pli.longitude_i`, `meshtastic.pli.speed_cm_s`, `meshtastic.pli.course_centideg`). **(3) Forward-compat decoder** — unknown protobuf fields are skipped by wire type (varint / length-delimited / fixed32 / fixed64) so a future schema revision that adds new fields stays decodable; varint overflow (>10 bytes), unknown wire types (3, 4, 6, 7), invalid UTF-8 in string fields, and length-delimited prefixes that exceed the transport cap surface as typed `MeshtasticError` variants rather than panicking. **(4) Workspace plumbing** — added to `Cargo.toml` workspace members and `[workspace.dependencies]`, `Dockerfile` cache layer, `deny.toml` proprietary-license exception, and the workspace `README.md` crate table. Test coverage: 21 unit + integration tests including a property-based test for the position round-trip, a field-pruning size assertion (minimal PLI entity encodes under 50 bytes), and reject-too-large coverage for both opaque detail blobs and oversized chat bodies. **goTenna Pro X2** binding is documented as compatible (same `TAKPacket` schema) but the transport binding is deferred to a follow-up; the codec public API is stable enough for the future binding crate to consume directly. **Out of scope:** mesh-frame headers, link-layer encryption, UDP / serial listener wiring, body compression behind the `is_compressed` flag (carried opaque), goTenna SDK integration.

- **`rustgate-vmf` crate — VMF (MIL-STD-6017) bit-level codec for K05.1 Position Reports (closes #868)** — first deliverable of the VMF umbrella tracked under #868. New workspace member `crates/rustgate-vmf` ships an `EntityCodec` impl for the Army/USMC tactical messaging format used by Blue Force Tracker and every SINCGARS-ASIP / EPLRS radio. **(1) `VmfHeader`** — MIL-STD-2045-47001 application header decode/encode covering version (4-bit, pinned at `0x1`), originator URN (24-bit), optional recipient URN (24-bit, gated by FPI), optional message-id (FAD + MSG-NUM + subnumber, gated by FPI), 3-bit classification (`Unclassified` / `Confidential` / `Secret` / `TopSecret` / `Reserved(_)`), optional 64-bit POSIX-seconds + 20-bit microseconds DTG (gated by FPI). **(2) `K051PositionReport`** — bidirectional codec for the K05.1 Position Report body: 24-bit reporting URN, 25-bit signed latitude (LSB ≈ 5.4 × 10⁻⁶ deg), 26-bit signed longitude (LSB ≈ 5.4 × 10⁻⁶ deg), optional 16-bit signed altitude (metres), optional 12-bit speed (LSB 0.1 m/s), optional 9-bit course (LSB 360 / 2⁹ ≈ 0.703 deg), optional 7-byte ASCII unit identifier with control-byte sanitization. **(3) `VmfMessage`** — enum with `K05_1(K051PositionReport)` plus `Unknown { message_type, body: Bytes }` for non-MVP K-series so a follow-up PR can extend the crate without breaking call sites. **(4) `VmfCodec`** — `rustgate_core::entity::EntityCodec` impl that maps K05.1 → `Entity { uid: "vmf-{urn:08x}", position, velocity, callsign, attributes: { vmf.* } }` and back. Same-codec round-trip preserves position to the LSB envelope. **(5) `BitReader` / `BitWriter`** — minimal big-endian bit-level helpers (≈100 LOC) used as the lone parsing primitive. The asterix and stanag4586 crates established the precedent of keeping codec deps minimal; the read/write surface needed here fits in a dozen methods, so a third-party `bitstream-io` would add two compile units for no functional gain. **(6) Typed errors.** `VmfError::{Truncated, InvalidValue, Unsupported, EncodeOverflow}` for the bit-level layer; `VmfEntityError::{Decode, UnsupportedEntityKind}` at the `EntityCodec` boundary. Every error carries a symbolic field name so a session-layer log can pinpoint which UAP bit truncated. **(7) `VMF_DEFAULT_UDP_PORT = 1581`** — IANA-registered VMF UDP port exported as a constant so the future listener-wiring PR pins it symbolically. **(8) MVP scope.** Only K05.1 Position Reports decode/encode bidirectionally; K01.x (General C2), K02.x (Intelligence), K04.x (Land Combat), K06.x (Fire Support), K00.x (Free Text) decode the header but surface as `VmfMessage::Unknown` and return `VmfError::Unsupported` on encode. **(9) Tests.** Unit tests across `bitstream` (bit-walk byte boundaries, signed two's-complement, write overflow detection, byte-alignment guards, round-trip), `header` (minimal + full round-trips, version validation, classification levels, microsecond bounds), `k05_1` (minimal + full round-trips, latitude/longitude envelope rejection, URN bounds, course normalisation, control-byte sanitization, truncation), `codec` (full round-trip through `EntityCodec`, unknown message decoding header-only, unsupported-entity rejection, `EntityKind` classification, attribute-bag round-trip, truncation). 4 integration tests in `tests/roundtrip.rs` covering full wire round-trip, unknown-message-type passthrough, attribute-driven encode, and malformed-frame typed-error handling. **(10) Spec assumptions.** MIL-STD-6017 is not freely available; the wire form pinned in this MVP is the layered subset published in open-literature references (FM 6-99, NATO STANAG 5616 cross-references, JPL/Caltech VMF interop notes) plus the layout pinned by issue #868. Where the open-literature shape leaves a field ambiguous, the codec uses the most common width and documents the choice inline (search for `MVP` in `crate::header` and `crate::k05_1`). A reviewer with access to the closed spec can correct individual widths without touching the codec scaffolding. **(11) Out of scope (deferred to follow-up issues).** UDP listener wiring on port 1581; K01.x / K02.x / K04.x / K06.x / K00.x message bodies; FRI / GRI repetition (the bit helpers support the pattern but no MVP field exercises it); MIL-STD-2525 SIDC dispatch from VMF unit identifiers.- **ADR migration of `shared-infrastructure.md` prescriptive content (closes #840)** — closes the F-109 deliverable of the umbrella tracked under #840 by migrating the prescriptive content of the operator-local `.claude/rules/shared-infrastructure.md` decision table into seven new architecture decision records, completing the umbrella alongside #1261 (F-107 — `on_callback!` macro) and #1248 (F-113 — `PeerId` / `ServerName` typed-wrapper discipline). **(1) Seven new ADRs** under `docs/adr/`: [0011](docs/adr/0011-tracing-not-log-workspace-wide.md) (`tracing` for structured logging; no `log` facade), [0012](docs/adr/0012-bytes-end-to-end-no-vec-on-hot-path.md) (`bytes::Bytes` end-to-end on the routing hot path), [0013](docs/adr/0013-tactical-tcp-socket-hardening.md) (`configure_tactical_socket` for every accepted/dialed TCP stream), [0014](docs/adr/0014-hash-chained-audit-log.md) (SHA-256 hash-chained audit log with sealed terminator), [0015](docs/adr/0015-encrypted-archives-chacha20-poly1305.md) (ChaCha20-Poly1305 with per-chunk AAD for archive encryption), [0016](docs/adr/0016-on-callback-macro-for-typed-aliases.md) (`on_callback!` macro for `Arc<dyn Fn>` callback aliases), and [0017](docs/adr/0017-workspace-dependency-inheritance.md) (workspace dependency inheritance for every crate). Each ADR uses the slim Michael Nygard format seeded by #1253 (status, context, decision, alternatives, consequences) and is substantiated by either the codebase or the existing operator playbook content. **(2) `docs/decisions.md`** — a checked-in cross-reference table that maps each "I want to..." entry to the helper or pattern to reach for and the ADR that captures the rationale. Replaces the duplicated rationale formerly carried in the gitignored `.claude/rules/shared-infrastructure.md` decision table; the playbook file remains the operator-local quick-lookup, but the prescriptive standard now lives in the ADR collection. **(3) Updated `docs/adr/README.md`** index with the seven new entries. Closes #840 (umbrella close — F-107 already shipped via #1261, F-113 via #1248, F-109 lands here). Out of scope: ADRs for decisions not yet substantiated by codebase or playbook content; restructuring the existing ten seed ADRs from #1253; F-107 / F-113 (already shipped).

- **`rustgate-dis` crate — DIS (IEEE 1278.1) Entity State PDU codec (closes #867)** — new workspace crate `rustgate-dis` that decodes and encodes the IEEE 1278.1 Entity State PDU plus closed-form WGS-84 ↔ ECEF coordinate conversion. The MVP scope covers the 12-byte common header (`PduHeader`), the Entity State PDU body (entity identification, force, type tuple, linear velocity, ECEF position, Euler orientation, dead-reckoning parameters, marking, capabilities, articulation parameters), the dead-reckoning algorithm tag (parameters preserved verbatim as opaque bytes for round-trip fidelity), and a `DisCodec` implementation of `rustgate_core::entity::EntityCodec` that participates in the cross-protocol fan-out path established by #847. The remaining 71 IEEE 1278.1 PDU types (Fire, Detonation, Collision, Service Request, Resupply, Repair, Radio Communications, Simulation Management, Distributed Emission Regeneration, …) are deliberately out of scope for the MVP and will land in follow-up PRs against typed-shape sub-issues. The closed-form ECEF↔WGS-84 conversion is single-pass Bowring 1985, accurate to better than 1 mm of altitude precision and 1e-9 deg of lat / lon across the Earth-atmosphere envelope and well into the geostationary regime — the round-trip property is pinned by a 256-case proptest plus the Statue-of-Liberty fixture and a hand-picked spread of typical exercise locations. Wire-format-layer failures surface through `DisError` (truncated buffers, length-field mismatch, wrong PDU type, invalid marking); EntityCodec-boundary failures surface through `DisEntityError` (invalid PDU, unsupported PDU type, unsupported entity kind). DIS conventionally runs on UDP port 3000 and the `header::DIS_DEFAULT_UDP_PORT` constant is exported for the future listener-wiring PR; this crate ships as a pure decode / encode library matching the pattern of `rustgate-asterix` and `rustgate-stanag4586` with no transport dependencies. Closes #867.

- **`migrate-config` subcommand + upgrade matrix doc — config-validation umbrella complete (closes #815)** — finishes the third deliverable of the configuration story tracked under #815: F-136 (validation consolidation, #1244) and F-137 (JSON Schema export, #1259) shipped earlier; this PR lands F-138, the operator-facing migration tool, completing the umbrella. **(1) New `rustgate migrate-config <PATH> [--output <PATH>] [--from <VERSION>]` CLI subcommand** in `crates/rustgate-server/src/diagnostics/migrate_config.rs`. Rewrites a TOML config file from a previous schema into the schema this binary understands. Output goes to `--output` (file) or stdout. Source version is detected in priority order: `--from` flag → `# rustgate-version: <version>` comment in the file → heuristic check for known-obsolete top-level keys → fallback to current schema (no-op pass). **(2) `Version` enum** with chronological variants (`PreV08`, `V08`) and `Version::parse` that accepts canonical strings (`0.8`, `pre-0.8`) plus the aliases an operator might type (`v0.8`, `0.8.0`, `0.7`, `0.7.0`). Unrecognised values surface as the typed `MigrateError::UnrecognizedVersion { value }` so a CI wrapper can branch on the failure mode without parsing stderr. **(3) Migration chain.** `chain_for(source)` walks every step between detected source and `Version::current()`. The single shipping transition `MigratePreV08ToV08` renames the legacy three-letter TLS keys (`tls_cert` → `cert`, `tls_key` → `key`, `tls_ca` → `ca`) and drops the obsolete `legacy_xml_strict` knob with a warn-level event on stderr. The framework is the v1 deliverable: subsequent breaking schema changes append a new `Version` variant + `Migration` impl + matrix row in `docs/migrations.md`. **(4) Comment-preserving rewrites.** `toml_edit` (new direct workspace + crate dep) round-trips through a syntax tree that keeps blank lines, comments, and key ordering. The `rename_key` helper captures the *key's* leaf decor before the remove drops it and re-applies it on the destination key, so an operator's `# Operator note: this is the production cert` line above `tls_cert` lands above the renamed `cert` key. **(5) Generation banner.** Every successful run stamps `# Generated by rustgate migrate-config from <source>` at the top of the output. Idempotent across repeated runs — running the subcommand twice does not stack banners. The banner doubles as a documented `# rustgate-version` for any future migration. **(6) `docs/migrations.md`.** Operator-facing upgrade matrix with one section per transition listing every key the migration touches plus the rationale; a "How the tool decides what to do" walk-through of detection priority; and a "Adding a new transition" template for future contributors. **(7) Tests.** 14 unit tests in `migrate_config::tests` (version parsing across canonical + aliased forms, version-comment extraction, rename + drop semantics, no-op-on-current-schema, version-comment vs explicit-flag priority, heuristic detection, typed-error path, banner idempotency across repeated runs); 10 integration tests in `crates/rustgate-server/tests/migrate_config.rs` covering the operator-facing contract (round-trip on already-current config, file output, stdout fallback, version detection from comment, version detection from `--from`, typed error on bad version, key renames, warn-on-drop on stderr, end-to-end `migrate-config | validate-config` round trip, comment preservation). Closes #815 — completing the umbrella alongside #1244 (F-136) and #1259 (F-137).
- **`EntityCodecRegistry` + router-side dispatch pivot — Entity Model Abstraction Layer umbrella complete (closes #847)** — closes the umbrella tracked under #847 by landing the router pivot the four concrete codec PRs (CoT XML #1289, MAVLink #1292, ASTERIX #1295, STANAG-4586 #1300) were waiting on. The router now consults a per-protocol `EntityCodec` at message dispatch and surfaces the canonical `Entity` shape to audit and metrics without changing the wire format. **(1) `rustgate_core::entity::DynEntityCodec`** — new object-safe sibling of the per-impl `EntityCodec` trait whose blanket `impl<T: EntityCodec> DynEntityCodec for T` boxes per-codec error types into `Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync>` so a heterogeneous registry can hold every codec variant under one `Arc<dyn …>` slot without per-codec wrapping boilerplate. The blanket impl requires `T::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static`; the existing MAVLink, ASTERIX, and STANAG-4586 codec error enums already satisfy the bound (they derive `thiserror::Error`); the CoT `ParseError` did not, so this PR migrates `rustgate_cot::ParseError` to `thiserror::Error` with documented `Display` strings ("XML parse error: …", "missing required attribute: …", "invalid float for field: …", "field `{field}` out of range: {value}") that mirror the previous `Debug` shape — operators relying on `{}` format see the same human-readable output. **(2) `rustgate_core::entity::EntityCodecRegistry`** — `HashMap<String, Arc<dyn DynEntityCodec>>` mapping `metadata.source_protocol` to its codec, with `register(&mut self, protocol, codec)`, `get(&self, protocol) -> Option<Arc<dyn DynEntityCodec>>`, `is_empty(&self)`, and `len(&self)` accessors. Lookup is O(1) avg on the routing hot path; the registry is built once at startup and held behind `Arc` so the router shares ownership without allocation churn. Re-registering the same key silently replaces — the registry is expected to be built once at startup, so a panicking `expect_unique` API would be wrong for the server-binary feature-flag overlap case. The custom `Debug` impl renders only the registered protocol keys (the `dyn` codec itself is not `Debug`), which is the operationally interesting signal for an operator dump. **(3) `EntityKind::as_str(&self) -> &'static str`** — closed lowercase-ASCII vocabulary for use as a Prometheus label value. Every variant maps to one of `"aircraft" | "ground" | "marine" | "sensor" | "track" | "munition" | "unknown"`. The free-form label inside `EntityKind::Unknown(_)` is intentionally **not** surfaced here so cardinality stays bounded; operators wanting the codec-specific tag use `Entity.attributes` directly. **(4) Router pivot.** `rustgate_transport::Router` gains `entity_codec_registry: Option<Arc<EntityCodecRegistry>>` (default `None` for backward compat — unit tests that build a bare `Router::new()` continue to work unchanged), the builder method `with_entity_codec_registry(self, Arc<EntityCodecRegistry>) -> Self`, and the accessor `entity_codec_registry(&self) -> Option<&Arc<EntityCodecRegistry>>`. The new internal `classify_entity_kind(&self, &RoutableMessage) -> Option<&'static str>` helper looks up `metadata.source_protocol` in the registry and returns the canonical `EntityKind::as_str()` tag on a hit, or `None` on registry-absent / protocol-unregistered / decode-failure. Decode failures are logged at `tracing::debug!` (with the source protocol and the boxed error) and downgrade the surface to `None` — the wire payload still flows to subscribers. The entity surface is best-effort, never gating; per scope it is **not persisted** on `RoutableMessage` (that's #848 territory) but computed transiently at dispatch for cross-cutting concerns. **(5) Per-recipient delivery audit extension.** `rustgate_core::audit::message_delivered` gains a sixth parameter `entity_kind: Option<&str>` rendered through the `?` formatter as `entity_kind=Some("aircraft")` / `entity_kind=None` — SIEM rules can correlate kind to delivery without re-parsing payloads. The matching `OnMessageDelivered` callback type adds `Option<&str>` as its sixth argument so the closure-based wiring in the server binary (`--audit-delivery` flag) flows the kind through. **(6) Per-kind Prometheus counter.** New `rustgate_messages_routed_by_kind_total{kind, protocol}` (`IntCounterVec`) registered from `rustgate-server::metrics` under the existing `metrics` feature. The label cardinality is bounded by the closed `EntityKind` vocabulary on the `kind` axis and the small fixed-vocabulary set of registered protocols on the `protocol` axis. The counter fires once per **admitted message** (post-Send-PEP allow), not per recipient — broadcast to N subscribers produces a single increment, matching the existing `messages_routed_total` cardinality model. The new `OnRoutedByKind` callback type bridges the router's `emit_routed_by_kind` site to the metric vector via the wired-up `router_routed_by_kind_callback()` helper; un-installed builds keep the routing hot path at a single `ArcSwap::load` + `is_none()` check. The `UNKNOWN_ENTITY_KIND_LABEL = "unknown"` constant short-circuits the per-message cost when the registry is absent or the codec rejects the payload — no allocation. **(7) Server-binary registry construction.** `rustgate_server::main` builds the registry once at startup and registers all four shipping codecs: `CotEntityCodec` under `"cot"`, `MavlinkEntityCodec` under `SOURCE_MAVLINK = "mavlink"`, `AsterixEntityCodec` under `"asterix"`, and `Stanag4586EntityCodec` under `"stanag4586"`. The registration is always-on (no per-codec feature flag) because the codec types are zero-sized and the registry construction is zero-cost when no traffic of the corresponding protocol arrives — the per-codec "we ship this codec" signal lives at the `rustgate-mavlink` / `rustgate-asterix` / `rustgate-stanag4586` workspace-dependency declaration in the server's `Cargo.toml`. **(8) 22 new tests.** 11 in `rustgate_core::entity::tests` exercising `EntityKind::as_str` (closed-vocabulary pin), `DynEntityCodec` blanket impl (typed error round-trips through the boxed shape), `EntityCodecRegistry::{register, get, is_empty, len}` (returns Some for registered + None for unknown + replace-on-re-register + multi-protocol dispatch + Debug rendering). 11 in `rustgate_transport::router::tests` covering `classify_entity_kind` (returns canonical tag on registered+success path, returns None on unregistered protocol, returns None on codec parse failure, returns None when no registry installed), the four-protocol dispatch matrix (cot→ground, mavlink→aircraft, asterix→track, stanag4586→aircraft), end-to-end `delivery_audit` field flow (entity_kind flows through callback on success, omitted on unregistered protocol, omitted on codec failure), `routed_by_kind_callback` (fires once per admitted message with canonical kind, `unknown` label on no-registry, `unknown` label on decode failure), `router_without_registry_continues_to_dispatch_unchanged` (backward-compat — wire payload flows unchanged), and `unknown_entity_label_matches_entity_kind_unknown_as_str` (drift sentinel between the metric-hot-path constant and `EntityKind::Unknown::as_str()`). 4 in `rustgate_core::audit::tests::delivery` extending the existing `message.delivered` shape pins to cover `entity_kind=Some("aircraft")` / `entity_kind=None` rendering through the audit boundary. **(9) Wire-format compatibility.** Zero wire-format changes. The `Entity` is computed at dispatch and never serialised — federation, NATS, HTTP, MQTT egress paths continue to forward the original `RoutableMessage.payload` bytes. Operators who do not register codecs (a `Router::new()` without `with_entity_codec_registry`) see byte-identical pre-PR routing behaviour. **(10) Out of scope.** Persisting `Entity` on `RoutableMessage` (tracked in #848 — multi-source track correlation); federation outbound `Entity` shape (deferred to a follow-up issue); track correlation across multi-source entities (#848). Closes #847 — the umbrella that began with #1289 (trait + scaffold + CoT XML codec), continued through #1292 (MAVLink), #1295 (ASTERIX), and #1300 (STANAG-4586), now finishes with this router pivot.
- **`Metadata.trace_context` field + end-to-end federation propagation (closes #852; completes the umbrella alongside #1293)** — finishes the W3C Trace Context split plan tracked under #852 by persisting the parsed `rustgate_core::TraceContext` on every `RoutableMessage::metadata` so the upstream trace continues across local routing and onto further federation egress. PR-A + PR-B (#1293) shipped the type, parser, and federation gRPC inject/extract helpers; this PR (PR-C) lands the metadata carry, callback plumbing, audit surfacing, and 12 new test functions. **(1) Core `Metadata.trace_context: Option<TraceContext>`.** New optional field on `rustgate_core::message::Metadata` carrying the W3C Trace Context attached at ingress. Defaults to `None` inside `Metadata::new`; set via the builder method `Metadata::with_trace_context(ctx)` returning `Self`. The field is `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` so the wire format stays stable for messages that did not arrive with a `traceparent` header. Wire-format compatibility: pre-PR peers and on-disk store-and-forward queues continue to deserialize cleanly (the `#[serde(default)]` accepts the absent field as `None`); both the `"trace_context": null` and the omitted-field shapes are pinned in `metadata_serde_old_wire_format_without_trace_context_field_still_deserializes`. **(2) `TraceContext::trace_id_hex()`.** New helper on `rustgate_core::traceparent::TraceContext` that renders the 16-byte `trace_id` as a 32-character lowercase hex string (no version prefix, no separators, no padding) so log-shipping grep rules can join across services on a fixed-width token. Per-byte zero padding is pinned in `trace_id_hex_zero_pads_each_byte`. **(3) Federation V2 `OnEvent` callback signature gains `Option<TraceContext>`.** Both `rustgate_federation::v2::server::OnEvent` and `rustgate_federation::v2::client::OnEvent` accept the parsed inbound trace context as a third argument so the consumer can persist it on `RoutableMessage::metadata.trace_context`. The V2 server's `send_one_event` and `server_event_stream` handlers call `extract_into_current_span` (PR-B helper) and forward the returned `Option<TraceContext>` to the callback. The streaming RPC sets `traceparent` on the gRPC HTTP/2 headers at stream-open time (the per-event override is consulted on stream re-open / reconnection — per-message override on a streaming gRPC requires re-opening the stream and is out of scope). **(4) Federation manager `OnInbound` callback gains `Option<TraceContext>`.** `rustgate_federation::manager::OnInbound` now takes `(PeerId, Bytes, Option<TraceContext>)` so the federation server's wire-up surfaces the parsed context to the routing layer. V1 federation predates W3C trace context and surfaces `None`; V2 inbound forwards the parsed value from the V2 callback. **(5) Server-side wiring populates `Metadata.trace_context` on inbound federation traffic.** `rustgate_server::setup::build_federation_inbound_handler` consults the third argument and applies `metadata.with_trace_context(ctx)` when the parsed context is `Some`. Local-protocol transports (TLS, MQTT, WebSocket, NATS) leave the field `None` because their wire format has no native `traceparent` carry. The interesting case the umbrella was designed for — federation peer A → local subscriber B → federation peer C — works end-to-end because B's `route_for_egress` preserves `metadata.trace_context` through Send-PEP, then the outbound federation manager reads it back from `Metadata` and forwards. **(6) Federation outbound: explicit `Metadata.trace_context` wins over the active OTel span.** `rustgate_federation::v2::client::V2Client::send_with_trace(event, trace_context)` is the new entry point that threads an explicit context through `V2Queued.trace_context`. `rustgate_federation::v2::client::outbound_request_with_trace` plus `rustgate_federation::v2::traceparent::inject_explicit_context` together implement the explicit-wins-over-OTel contract: when the source `Metadata.trace_context` is `Some(ctx)`, the federation client renders `ctx.to_string()` directly into the gRPC `traceparent` metadata; when `None`, the existing `inject_into_request` path consults the active OTel span (PR-B behaviour). The federation manager's `forward_with_metadata` reads `Metadata.trace_context` and passes it to `V2Client::send_with_trace`. The legacy `V2Client::send(event)` is preserved as a thin shim over `send_with_trace(event, None)` so existing callers (V1-to-V2 bridge, replay) don't need updates. **(7) `audit::message_delivered` surfaces `trace_id`.** The per-recipient delivery audit (closes #854) gains a sixth `Option<&str>` argument carrying the 32-char lowercase hex `trace_id` when the routed message carried a W3C trace context. SIEM correlation joins now key on `trace_id` to link the delivery record back to the upstream producer's audit trail. The audit field is rendered via `?trace_id` (Debug formatting) so `Some("hex32")` and `None` both render cleanly in the JSON output. **(8) `OnMessageDelivered` callback signature.** `rustgate_transport::OnMessageDelivered` gains a sixth `Option<&str>` parameter — the trace_id hex string — that `Router::emit_message_delivered` derives from `msg.metadata.trace_context.as_ref().map(TraceContext::trace_id_hex)`. Callers in `rustgate-server::main.rs` and `tests/audit_delivery_wiring.rs` thread the value into `audit::message_delivered`. **(9) Tests.** 12 new test functions across 3 test surfaces. **`crates/rustgate-core/src/message.rs::tests`** (5 functions): `metadata_new_initializes_trace_context_to_none`, `metadata_with_trace_context_sets_field` (chained builder leaves other fields untouched), `metadata_with_trace_context_overwrites_previous_value` (idempotent re-application), `metadata_serde_round_trip_preserves_trace_context_some` (W3C banner string in JSON output, parsed value compares equal), `metadata_serde_round_trip_preserves_trace_context_none` (skip_serializing_if omits the field), `metadata_serde_old_wire_format_without_trace_context_field_still_deserializes` (pre-PR wire compat). **`crates/rustgate-core/src/traceparent.rs::tests`** (2 functions): `trace_id_hex_renders_32_lowercase_chars`, `trace_id_hex_zero_pads_each_byte`. **`crates/rustgate-federation/tests/v2_traceparent.rs`** (5 functions): `federation_inbound_populates_metadata_trace_context_from_traceparent_header` (the V2 `OnEvent` callback receives the parsed banner via the third argument when the inbound carries `traceparent`), `federation_inbound_without_traceparent_yields_metadata_trace_context_none` (absence-tolerant path), `federation_inbound_malformed_traceparent_yields_metadata_trace_context_none` (parser-failure path; RPC still completes), `federation_outbound_metadata_trace_context_renders_canonical_banner` (the wire-form is identical to PR-B's OTel-driven path), `federation_relay_preserves_trace_context_across_two_hops` (end-to-end relay invariant — the upstream banner round-trips through B's `Metadata.trace_context` and back to a hypothetical hop 2 outbound). **`crates/rustgate-transport/tests/delivery_audit.rs`** (2 functions): `delivery_audit_includes_trace_id_when_metadata_carries_trace_context` (router emits the 32-char hex `trace_id` to the recorder when the message carries a context), `delivery_audit_omits_trace_id_when_metadata_has_no_trace_context` (default-path messages surface `trace_id = None`). Plus 4 unit tests inside `rustgate-federation` (`inject_explicit_context_sets_traceparent_metadata`, `inject_explicit_context_carries_tracestate_when_present`, `outbound_request_with_trace_uses_explicit_context_when_some`, `outbound_request_with_trace_falls_back_to_inject_into_request_when_none`) pinning the helper-level wire-format contract. **(10) Wire-format compatibility.** No existing peer interaction breaks — every wire-level addition is additive (the new metadata field has `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`, the new gRPC header injection follows the W3C standard the receiver already tolerates absent), every test pre-PR continues to pass, and old peers without the `trace_context` carry continue to interoperate cleanly. Closes #852.
- **`Metadata.classification` field + per-recipient egress enforcement (closes #849; completes the umbrella alongside #1282 + #1297)** — third and fourth deliverables of the CAPCO classification umbrella tracked under #849: the parser + lattice shipped via #1282 and the policy-side `AuthzContext` hook shipped via #1297; this PR lands the wire-level `Metadata.classification: Option<rustgate_core::classification::ClassificationMarking>` field, threads it through every Send and Receive PEP call site in `rustgate-transport::router`, and adds the operator-facing `--require-classification-marking` and `--default-classification` CLI flags. **(1) New optional `Metadata.classification` field.** Carries `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` so pre-#849 federation peers and on-disk store-and-forward queues continue to deserialize cleanly — the field round-trips through the existing CAPCO banner-string serde wire form (e.g. `"//SECRET//NOFORN"`). New `Metadata::with_classification(marking) -> Self` builder follows the established pattern from #1303 (parallel to `with_ttl`). **(2) Router-side egress enforcement.** Every `authz_evaluate_send_with_classification` and `authz_evaluate_receive_with_classification` call site forwards the source message's marking through `PolicyEngine::evaluate_with_context` so backends (Cedar via #1297, custom engines that override the trait method) can deny release based on the marking. The dedicated `audit::classification_denied(source_cn, dest_cn, msg_uid, marking, group)` event fires whenever a per-recipient deny lines up with a present marking, so SIEM dashboards can isolate marking-driven denials from the broader `authz_denied` bucket. The Send and Receive PEP sites cover direct-recipient, group-fan-out, broadcast-fan-out, multicast-egress envelope, position-replay-on-reconnect, and offline-drain paths. **(3) Mandatory-marking opt-in.** New `--require-classification-marking` / `RUSTGATE_REQUIRE_CLASSIFICATION_MARKING` CLI flag (default `false`). When set, every inbound message that lacks a `Metadata.classification` is rejected at admission with the dedicated `audit::missing_classification_marking(source_cn, msg_uid, source_protocol)` event. The check runs after dedup + TTL but before any PEP, cache store, or fanout — a rejected message has zero observable side effects beyond the audit record. **(4) Per-listener default marking.** New `--default-classification` / `RUSTGATE_DEFAULT_CLASSIFICATION` CLI flag accepts a CAPCO banner string. Validated at startup via the existing `ClassificationMarking::from_str` parser; an invalid banner fails fast with a clear error. Every inbound message that does not already carry a marking is stamped with the configured default before reaching the router. The new `MessageBuilder::with_default_classification(marking)` builder on `rustgate-cot` plumbs the default through both the TLS and plaintext-TCP listener paths. Combine with `--require-classification-marking` for a "stamp-or-reject" pipeline; combine without it to default-tag only unmarked traffic. **(5) Plumbing.** New `Router::with_require_classification_marking(bool)` builder. New `EnvelopeEvaluator::evaluate_send` trait signature now takes `Option<&ClassificationMarking>` so the multicast egress envelope helper from #746 also folds marking-aware deny semantics across the addressed groups. New audit functions `classification_denied` and `missing_classification_marking` in `rustgate_core::audit`, both routing every user-controlled string through `sanitize_for_log` per the audit-boundary discipline (#1197 / #1220). **(6) Tests.** 4 unit tests in `rustgate-core::message::tests` (`metadata_new_initializes_classification_to_none`, `metadata_with_classification_sets_field`, `metadata_serde_round_trip_preserves_classification`, `metadata_serde_old_wire_format_without_classification_still_deserializes`); 4 unit tests in `rustgate-core::audit::tests` (`classification_denied_emits_expected_fields`, `classification_denied_sanitizes_all_string_fields`, `missing_classification_marking_emits_expected_fields`, `missing_classification_marking_sanitizes_user_fields`); 8 integration tests in `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/classification_egress.rs` covering: filter recipient when classification dominates clearance, admit recipient when clearance dominates classification, preserve legacy behaviour when `Metadata.classification` is `None`, mandatory-marking rejects unmarked inbound, mandatory-marking admits marked inbound, the listener default-classification builder hook, the `classification.denied` audit-event field set under capture, and composition with the `InjectMarking` obligation from #1286 demoting `//SECRET//NOFORN` to `//UNCLASSIFIED//FOUO` at the boundary. 3 CLI tests in `rustgate-server::cli::tests` (`cli_require_classification_marking_flag_parses`, `cli_default_classification_flag_parses_capco_banner`, `validate_rejects_invalid_default_classification_banner`). **(7) Wire-format compatibility.** Older peers without the `classification` field continue to deserialize cleanly because the field is `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; deployments that have not opted into either CLI flag observe identical pre-#849 behaviour. **(8) Out of scope.** MIL-STD-2525 SIDC carry on the `Entity` model (item 6 of the umbrella) remains for a separate future PR. Cross-domain guard hooks already shipped via #1296 and compose naturally with the new `Metadata.classification` field. Closes #849.
- **`rustgate_stanag4586::entity::Stanag4586EntityCodec` — fourth concrete `EntityCodec` impl (refs #847)** — fourth deliverable of the Entity Model Abstraction Layer tracked under #847; the trait + CoT XML scaffold shipped via #1289, the MAVLink codec shipped via #1292, and the ASTERIX codec shipped via #1295. This PR completes the planned codec set under #847; the router/federation/NATS/HTTP/MQTT integrations against the same trait remain and are blocked on the `Metadata` builder migration tracked in #1298. Adds a new `rustgate_stanag4586::entity` module with `Stanag4586EntityCodec` (stateless, `Default + Clone + Copy`, `Send + Sync` via the `EntityCodec` bound), the `Stanag4586EntityError` enum (`InvalidMessage(String)` for malformed wire bytes wrapped from the underlying `Stanag4586Error`, `UnsupportedMessage(u32)` for STANAG-4586 message IDs outside the mapped subset, `UnsupportedEntityKind(String)` for entities that lack a STANAG-4586 wire form, `MissingField(&'static str)` for forward-compatibility with future variable-length STANAG-4586 message types), the public `VEHICLE_POSITION_MSG_ID = 4001` constant pinning the conventional Edition 2 message-ID number for vehicle-state telemetry, and the `stanag4586_message_supported(u32) -> bool` predicate so call sites can pre-filter without invoking the full decode path. **Only the LOI 2-3 vehicle-position frame is supported in v1.** Other STANAG-4586 message types (sensor pointing, payload status, system state, BIT report, mission abort, route upload, GCS handover, payload control, emergency status, payload calibration, waypoint command) surface `UnsupportedMessage(N)` — their `EntityCodec` impls land in subsequent PRs as router integration demands them. Inbound mapping (`Stanag4586EntityCodec::to_entity`): `vehicle_id` (u32) folds into `Entity.uid` as `"stanag4586-{vehicle_id}"`; `latitude_deg` / `longitude_deg` become `Entity.position` with `lat` / `lon` in WGS-84 decimal degrees; `altitude_msl_m` lifts to `Entity.position.hae_meters` verbatim (best-effort — STANAG-4586 carries MSL altitude, not WGS-84 HAE; the originally transmitted MSL value rides on `stanag4586.altitude_msl_m` for codecs that need the wire-truth distinction); `ground_speed_mps` and `heading_deg` resolve into `Entity.velocity` as a polar `(speed_m_s, course_deg)` pair with `course_deg` normalised to `[0, 360)` via `rem_euclid` (non-finite headings clamp to zero rather than poisoning the rest of the stack); `flight_state` dispatches `EntityKind` (`Loiter` / `Transit` / `ReturnToBase` → `Aircraft`, `LaunchPreparation` / `Landed` → `Ground`, `Other(byte)` → `Unknown("stanag4586-flight-state-{byte:#04x}")`) and rides on `stanag4586.flight_state.byte` + `stanag4586.flight_state.label`; `timestamp_unix_ms` folds into `Entity.timestamp` via `Duration::new(secs, nanos)` (saturating at `SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH` on the rare overflow). Every numeric wire field also rides on the `stanag4586.*` attribute namespace (`stanag4586.message_id`, `stanag4586.vehicle_id`, `stanag4586.flight_state.byte` / `.label`, `stanag4586.altitude_msl_m`, `stanag4586.ground_speed_mps`, `stanag4586.heading_deg`, `stanag4586.timestamp_unix_ms`) so a same-codec round-trip recovers the wire encoding without going through the lossy float math on the canonical `Velocity` shape. Outbound mapping (`Stanag4586EntityCodec::from_entity`) is intentionally narrower: only `Position`-bearing entities encode into a 48-byte vehicle-position frame. Entities without a position surface `Stanag4586EntityError::UnsupportedEntityKind("entity has no Position")`; entities whose `uid` does not match the `"stanag4586-<vehicle_id>"` shape AND whose attribute bag carries no `stanag4586.vehicle_id` fallback surface the same variant with the offending UID in the message (silently substituting `vehicle_id = 0` would let a crafted CoT event spoof `vehicle_id = 0` on a downstream STANAG-4586 sink); entities with NaN/inf or out-of-WGS-84-envelope coordinates surface `UnsupportedEntityKind("non-finite position")` / `UnsupportedEntityKind("position out of WGS-84 envelope")`. The encoder reuses any `stanag4586.flight_state.byte` / `.altitude_msl_m` / `.ground_speed_mps` / `.heading_deg` / `.timestamp_unix_ms` carry from `to_entity` to preserve the original wire encoding; absent the carry it synthesises `flight_state` as `FlightState::Other(0)` (cross-codec entities), `altitude_msl_m` from `Entity.position.hae_meters`, ground speed / heading from `Entity.velocity`, and the timestamp from `Entity.timestamp` via `systemtime_to_unix_ms`. Round-trip discipline: same-codec round-trip is byte-exact for the position-bearing subset (the fixture round-trip test asserts `bytes1 == bytes2` rather than tolerance-based equality); cross-codec entities (e.g. a CoT event encoded through the STANAG-4586 codec) lose `flight_state` precision silently per the `EntityCodec` contract documented on `rustgate_core::entity`. 13 new tests in `rustgate_stanag4586::entity::tests` (test-runner `cargo nextest run -p rustgate-stanag4586`): `vehicle_position_round_trips_through_entity_codec` (wire bytes round-trip byte-for-byte through the codec), `vehicle_position_to_entity_extracts_position_from_lat_lon_alt` (canonical Massachusetts coordinates 42°N / -71°W / 100 m MSL round-trip cleanly), `vehicle_position_to_entity_extracts_velocity_from_speed_and_heading` (100 m/s on bearing 90° preserves both fields), `vehicle_position_to_entity_uid_format_includes_system_id` (vehicle_id 0xA1B2C3D4 → uid `"stanag4586-2712847316"`), `vehicle_position_classifies_fixed_wing_uav_as_aircraft` (Loiter / Transit / ReturnToBase → Aircraft; LaunchPreparation / Landed → Ground), `vehicle_position_classifies_unknown_kind_as_unknown_with_label` (FlightState::Other(0xEE) → `Unknown("stanag4586-flight-state-0xee")`), `invalid_message_returns_error_no_panic` (out-of-range latitude on the wire surfaces `InvalidMessage` rather than panicking), `unsupported_message_id_returns_typed_error` (empty payload → `UnsupportedMessage(0)`; arbitrary short payload → `UnsupportedMessage(u32::MAX)`), `entity_with_no_position_emits_unsupported_for_from_entity`, `entity_to_vehicle_position_emits_minimal_message_with_required_fields` (position-bearing Entity with no attribute carry produces a well-formed 48-byte frame that decodes through `vehicle_position::decode`), `entity_with_unrecognised_uid_emits_unsupported_for_from_entity`, `vehicle_position_unmapped_fields_appear_in_attributes` (every wire field rides on the `stanag4586.*` attribute namespace), plus `stanag4586_message_supported_covers_only_vehicle_position` pinning the public predicate against the future-work boundary. **Wire-format compatibility is unchanged** — the STANAG-4586 wire format is untouched and the Entity codec is a NEW abstraction layered on top of the existing `vehicle_position::encode` / `vehicle_position::decode` round-trip. **Out of scope:** `EntityCodec` impls for STANAG-4586 message types other than vehicle position (sensor pointing, payload status, system state, BIT report, mission abort, route upload, GCS handover, payload control, emergency status, payload calibration, waypoint command — those land in subsequent PRs as router integration demands them); the router-internal pivot to use `EntityCodec` at message dispatch (blocked on the `Metadata` builder migration in #1298); the federation/NATS/HTTP/MQTT egress wiring through `Entity`; STANAG-4586 over MAVLink wrapping. Refs #847.
- **Per-RPC observability metrics for the V2 federation gRPC layer (closes #1299)** — adds three Prometheus vectors that give operators per-RPC granularity over the V2 federation gRPC suite so a slow latency tail can be attributed to `SendOneBlob` (large payloads), `ServerEventStream` (steady state), `ServerROLStream` (bursty), or `ClientFederateGroupsStream` rather than blurred into the existing aggregate counters. (1) `rustgate_federation_rpc_duration_seconds{rpc, peer, result}` (HistogramVec) records wall-clock duration of every V2 RPC invocation. (2) `rustgate_federation_rpc_in_flight{rpc, peer}` (IntGaugeVec) tracks currently-open invocations via a new `rustgate_federation::metrics::InFlightGuard` RAII handle that increments on `enter()` and decrements on `Drop` — moved into the spawned drain task for streaming RPCs so the gauge reflects the actual stream lifetime, paired one-shot with the unary `SendOneBlob` handler. (3) `rustgate_federation_rpc_total{rpc, peer, result}` (IntCounterVec) classifies each invocation under one of `success` (gRPC `Ok`), `error` (any non-OK gRPC `Status` other than `DeadlineExceeded`), or `timeout` (`DeadlineExceeded` or local deadline). The `rpc` label is one of `send_one_blob`, `server_event_stream`, `server_rol_stream`, `client_federate_groups_stream`. The `peer` label is the federate-id (mTLS CN) routed through `rustgate_core::sanitize::sanitize_for_log` before reaching the metric vector so a peer that smuggled `\r\n` into its federate-id can't forge log lines downstream of a Prometheus scrape that prints labels verbatim. New helpers in `rustgate_federation::metrics`: `rpc_duration()`, `rpc_in_flight()`, `rpc_total()` accessors following the workspace `OnceLock` + `init()` + accessor + `fallback_*` pattern; the `RPC_*` and `RESULT_*` label constants; `classify_status(tonic::Code) -> &'static str`; `sanitize_peer_label(&str) -> String`; and the `InFlightGuard` RAII handle. Server-side wiring in `crates/rustgate-federation/src/v2/server.rs` instruments each handler at the boundary: `send_one_blob` (split into a `send_one_blob_handle` inner helper so the per-RPC duration / in-flight / total metrics in the trait implementation can wrap a single `Result<Response, Status>` call site) plus the three streaming RPCs (`server_event_stream`, `server_rol_stream`, `client_federate_groups_stream`) where the in-flight guard moves into the spawned drain task and duration measures handler-entry through stream-close. Client-side wiring in `crates/rustgate-federation/src/v2/client.rs` instruments the four matching outbound paths: the unary `send_one_blob` arm of the `select!` loop (full duration + in-flight + total per call), and the three open-call sites for `ServerEventStream`, `ServerROLStream`, and `ClientFederateGroupsStream` (open-call duration is the actionable signal — the stream-lifetime duration is what the server-side handler covers). All metric code is gated behind the federation crate's existing `api` feature (workspace `metrics` brings it in alongside `federation`); the no-feature build never pulls `prometheus` in. The Grafana dashboard at `dashboards/rustgate-overview.json` gains a new "Federation per-RPC" row with three panels: per-RPC p99 latency (`histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (rpc, le) (rate(rustgate_federation_rpc_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))`), per-RPC in-flight (`rustgate_federation_rpc_in_flight`), and per-RPC error rate (`sum by (rpc) (rate(rustgate_federation_rpc_total{result="error"}[5m]))`). The dashboard's existing `every_referenced_metric_exists_in_the_codebase` validation test under `crates/rustgate-server/tests/grafana_dashboard.rs` picks up the three new metric names automatically by literal scan of `crates/*/src/metrics.rs`. 8 new tests in `crates/rustgate-federation/tests/v2_rpc_metrics.rs`: `rpc_duration_metric_records_on_handler_completion` (drive a unary `SendOneBlob` end-to-end via mTLS and assert at least one observation lands in the success bucket), `rpc_in_flight_gauge_increments_during_handler_and_decrements_on_exit` (pause the server-side `OnBlob` callback on an `std::sync::mpsc::Receiver`, observe the gauge `> baseline` while the handler is parked, release, confirm drain to baseline), `rpc_total_counter_classifies_success_vs_error` (drive a successful `SendOneBlob` through an allowlist and a failing one against an allowlist that doesn't include the client CN, assert two distinct label-set increments), `rpc_metrics_label_peer_is_sanitized` (peer-id with `\r\n` is stripped at the metric-vector boundary), `rpc_metrics_init_is_idempotent` (calling `init()` twice does not panic), `rpc_metrics_accessor_works_without_init` (the `OnceLock::get_or_init` fallback path returns a usable handle even without `init()`), `rpc_metrics_classify_status_pins_three_buckets` (gRPC `Code::Ok` → `success`, `Code::DeadlineExceeded` → `timeout`, every other code → `error`), and `rpc_metrics_in_flight_guard_lifecycle_for_streaming_rpcs` (guard `Drop` decrements; same peer with different `rpc` label gets its own series). Plus 6 new unit tests in `crates/rustgate-federation/src/metrics.rs::tests` covering the same lifecycle from the metrics module's own scope. **Wire-format compatibility is unchanged** — the V2 federation gRPC wire format is untouched; the metrics are a NEW observation surface layered on top of the existing handlers. **Out of scope:** gRPC method-level distributed-tracing spans (those land via the W3C `traceparent` propagation in #852 / #1293), per-RPC rate limits (separate concern), and backward-compat shimming for the existing aggregate `messages_in` / `messages_in_by_rpc` / `errors` federation metrics (they keep their pre-#1299 semantics so existing dashboards continue to work alongside the new per-RPC panels). Closes #1299.
- **`rustgate_asterix::entity::AsterixEntityCodec` — third concrete `EntityCodec` impl (refs #847)** — third deliverable of the Entity Model Abstraction Layer tracked under #847; the trait + CoT XML scaffold shipped via #1289 and the MAVLink codec shipped via #1292; the STANAG-4586 codec impl plus the router/federation/NATS/HTTP/MQTT integrations against the same trait remain. Adds a new `rustgate_asterix::entity` module with `AsterixEntityCodec` (stateless, `Default + Clone + Copy`, `Send + Sync` via the `EntityCodec` bound), the `AsterixEntityError` enum (`InvalidDatablock(String)` for malformed wire bytes wrapped from the underlying `Cat062Error`, `UnsupportedCategory(u8)` for ASTERIX category bytes outside the mapped subset, `UnsupportedEntityKind(String)` for entities that lack a CAT-062 wire form, `MissingField(&'static str)` for tracks without a strict-subset field), and the `asterix_category_supported(u8) -> bool` predicate so call sites can pre-filter without invoking the full decode path. **Only ASTERIX CAT-062 ("System Track Data") is supported in v1.** CAT-021 (ADS-B) and CAT-048 (Monoradar Plate) are recognised by their category byte but surface `UnsupportedCategory(N)` — their `EntityCodec` impls land in subsequent PRs. Inbound mapping (`AsterixEntityCodec::to_entity`): the codec consumes one CAT-062 datablock per call and surfaces the **first** record as the canonical `Entity` (multi-record fan-out at the router is tracked separately in #847; the record count rides on `asterix.datablock.record_count`); I062/010 (Data Source SAC/SIC) plus I062/040 (Track Number) fold into `Entity.uid` as `"asterix-{sac}-{sic}-{track_num}"`; I062/105 (Calculated Track Position WGS-84) becomes `Entity.position` with `lat` / `lon` in decimal degrees; I062/135 (Calculated Track Barometric Altitude — Mode-C) becomes `Entity.position.hae_meters` via a barometric-feet → metres approximation (LSB 25 ft × 0.3048 m/ft); I062/185 (Calculated Track Velocity Cartesian) resolves `(vx, vy)` m/s into `Entity.velocity` as a polar (speed_m_s, course_deg) pair using `atan2(east, north)` normalised to `[0, 360)` — the arithmetic mirrors the MAVLink codec's `decode_global_velocity` so a track translated CAT-062 → MAVLink → CAT-062 yields the same polar representation at every hop; I062/070 (Time of Track Information, seconds since midnight UTC) anchors `Entity.timestamp` against today's UTC midnight at decode time (the codec has no calendar carry, so consumers needing absolute epoch combine `asterix.time_of_day_seconds` with their own date source). `EntityKind` dispatch: garbled or unvalidated Mode-3/A → `Unknown("asterix-mode3a-garbled")` / `Unknown("asterix-mode3a-unvalidated")`; tracks without a position → `Unknown("asterix-no-position")`; tracks with Mode-C altitude → `Aircraft`; tracks with position but no altitude → `Ground`. Every decoded scalar field rides on the `asterix.*` attribute namespace (`asterix.category`, `asterix.data_source.{sac,sic}`, `asterix.track_number`, `asterix.time_of_day_seconds`, `asterix.velocity_cartesian.{vx,vy}_mps`, `asterix.mode_3a.{octal,raw,validation_failed,garbled,from_local_track}`, `asterix.mode_c_altitude_feet` / `asterix.mode_c_altitude_raw_25ft_units` / `asterix.mode_c_flight_level`, `asterix.track_status.{monosensor,spi,geometric_altitude_more_reliable,altitude_source,confirmed}`) so a same-codec round-trip recovers integer wire encodings without lossy float math. Outbound mapping (`AsterixEntityCodec::from_entity`) is intentionally narrower: only `Position`-bearing entities encode into a one-record CAT-062 datablock carrying I062/010 (Data Source) / I062/015 (Service Identification) / I062/040 (Track Number) / I062/105 (WGS-84 Position) / I062/130 (Calculated Geometric Altitude, when HAE present) / I062/185 (Cartesian Velocity, when velocity present). Mode-3/A and Mode-C are emitted only when their `asterix.*` attribute carry is present so cross-codec entities do not gain spurious zero-valued transponder codes; some SDPS-derived fields (calculated-track-quality, predicted track, flight-plan reconciliation) cannot be reconstructed from `Entity` at all and their FSPEC bits are not set on encode. Entities without a position surface `AsterixEntityError::UnsupportedEntityKind("entity has no Position")`; entities whose UID does not match `"asterix-<sac>-<sic>-<track>"` AND whose attribute bag carries no SAC/SIC/track-number fallback surface the same variant with the offending UID in the message; entities with NaN/inf or out-of-WGS-84-envelope coordinates surface `UnsupportedEntityKind("non-finite position")` / `UnsupportedEntityKind("position out of WGS-84 envelope")`. Round-trip discipline: the encoded datablock is **not** byte-identical — Mode-3/A and Mode-C ride on the attribute bag rather than as first-class `Entity` fields; same-codec round-trip recovers them through the bag, cross-codec entities lose them silently per the `EntityCodec` contract documented on `rustgate_core::entity`. 15 new tests in `rustgate_asterix::entity::tests` (test-runner `cargo nextest run -p rustgate-asterix`): `cat062_track_round_trips_through_entity_codec` (Entity round-trip preserves uid + kind + position across the encode/decode cycle), `cat062_to_entity_extracts_track_number_into_uid` (SAC=1, SIC=2, track=0x789 → uid `"asterix-1-2-1929"`), `cat062_to_entity_extracts_position_from_i105` (canonical Massachusetts coordinates 42°N / -71°W round-trip cleanly), `cat062_to_entity_extracts_velocity_from_i185_ground_speed_and_heading` (vx=100 m/s east → 100 m/s on bearing 90°), `cat062_to_entity_classifies_civilian_aircraft_as_aircraft` (Mode-3/A 1234 + FL350 → Aircraft), `cat062_to_entity_classifies_unknown_as_unknown_with_label` (garbled Mode-3/A → `Unknown("asterix-mode3a-garbled")`), `cat062_invalid_datablock_returns_error_no_panic` (truncated datablock surfaces `InvalidDatablock` rather than panicking), `cat062_unsupported_category_returns_typed_error` (CAT-048 datablock → `UnsupportedCategory(48)`), `cat062_unsupported_cat021_returns_typed_error` (CAT-021 datablock → `UnsupportedCategory(21)` — pinned independently so the future CAT-021 EntityCodec PR has a single test to flip), `cat062_unmapped_fields_appear_in_attributes` (Mode-3/A code, validation flags, integer wire encodings, and Cartesian velocity components all ride on the `asterix.*` namespace), `entity_to_cat062_emits_minimal_datablock_with_required_items` (CAT-062 datablock encodes with the strict subset I062/010 + I062/015 + I062/040 + I062/105 + I062/130 + I062/185 and round-trips back through `decode_cat062`), `entity_to_cat062_round_trips_position` (`to_entity → from_entity → to_entity` preserves position within the I062/105 LSB envelope), `entity_with_no_position_emits_unsupported_for_from_entity`, `entity_with_unrecognised_uid_emits_unsupported_for_from_entity`, plus `asterix_category_supported_covers_only_cat_062` pinning the public predicate against the CAT-021 / CAT-048 future-work boundary. **Wire-format compatibility is unchanged** — the ASTERIX wire format is untouched and the Entity codec is a NEW abstraction layered on top of the existing `decode_cat062` decoder. **Out of scope:** `EntityCodec` impls for ASTERIX categories other than CAT-062 (CAT-021 ADS-B, CAT-048 monoradar — those land in subsequent PRs as router integration demands them); STANAG-4586 and Link 16 codec implementations against the same trait; the router-internal pivot to use `EntityCodec` at message dispatch; the federation/NATS/HTTP/MQTT egress wiring through `Entity`; multi-record-per-datablock fan-out to multiple `Entity` values (single-record-only for v1; multi-record datablocks surface only the first record with the count on `asterix.datablock.record_count`). Refs #847.
- **`rustgate-guard` crate — cross-domain content inspection guard (closes #857; completes the umbrella alongside #1286)** — finishes the cross-domain inspection guard tracked under #857 by landing the dedicated crate the obligation-engine scaffold from #1286 promised. The scaffold shipped three obligation kinds (`StripPii`, `DegradePosition`, `InjectMarking`) wired into the existing obligation engine; this PR closes the umbrella by landing the four boundary-crossing controls those obligations alone could not provide. **(1) New `rustgate-guard` crate.** Workspace member at `crates/rustgate-guard` carrying `CrossDomainGuard` (the orchestration entry point), `GuardConfig` (operator-supplied caps + audit log path + direction hint), `GuardDirection` (`LowToHigh` / `HighToLow` / `Bidirectional`), and `GuardError` (`RateLimitExceeded`, `MissingMarking`, `UnauthorizedClassification`, `Audit`, `Io`). The crate consumes `rustgate-core` (audit chain, sanitization, classification lattice), `rustgate-resilience` (the per-direction `TokenBucket`), and `rustgate-cot` (CDI helpers + quick-xml access for marking extraction). **(2) Per-direction throughput cap.** Each `evaluate` call charges one `rustgate_resilience::token_bucket::TokenBucket` token per payload byte against the direction-keyed bucket (`low_to_high_max_bps` or `high_to_low_max_bps`). Caps are independent — a saturated `LowToHigh` channel does not affect `HighToLow`. The fail-open / fail-closed contract on the bucket carries through unchanged from #883's primitive. **(3) Mandatory CAPCO marking.** When `GuardConfig::mandatory_marking = true` (the v1 default), every inbound payload MUST carry a parseable `<marking value="…"/>` child of `<detail>`. Messages without one are rejected with `GuardError::MissingMarking` and the audit record carries `reason = "missing_marking"`. The marking is parsed via `rustgate_core::classification::ClassificationMarking` (refs #1282) so unparseable bangers degrade to `null` in the audit field rather than failing closed silently. **(4) Per-direction classification gating.** A `TopSecret` payload travelling `HighToLow` is rejected with `GuardError::UnauthorizedClassification` per the documented v1 policy (CDS releases require explicit operator approval); `LowToHigh` and `Bidirectional` admit every classification level (admission-to-higher is policy-permitted at the boundary). **(5) Dedicated hash-chained audit envelope.** The guard owns a `rustgate_core::audit_chain::HashChainWriter<File>` pointed at a SEPARATE log file from the general audit chain, so cross-domain accountability survives rotation of the operational log. The chain resumes from the existing tip via `read_chain_state` on construct so consecutive guard restarts maintain a single monotonic `seq` series. Every `evaluate` call — admit or deny — emits exactly one `boundary.evaluate` record with the documented field set: `ts` (RFC 3339 UTC), `event = "boundary.evaluate"`, `direction`, `source_cn` (sanitized via `sanitize_for_log`), `msg_uid`, `marking` (nullable), `input_sha256`, `output_sha256`, `decision` (`allow` / `deny`), `reason` (`ok` / `rate_limit` / `missing_marking` / `unauthorized_classification`). The `prev_sha256` and `sha256` fields are auto-injected by the `HashChainWriter` so tamper detection against the existing `verify_audit_log` primitive is preserved unchanged. **(6) Pre-egress before/after hashes.** Each record carries `input_sha256` and `output_sha256` hex digests (computed over the raw payload bytes, not the rendered XML) so an external auditor can prove what changed at the guard. The current scaffold runs no transforms inside `evaluate` — the input and output hashes match — but the hash slot makes the audit format forwards-compatible with the chained-transform follow-up. **(7) Optional Prometheus metrics.** Behind the `metrics` feature: `rustgate_guard_evaluations_total{direction, decision}` (counter), `rustgate_guard_throughput_bps{direction}` (gauge tracking the post-decision bucket level), and `rustgate_guard_rejections_total{direction, reason}` (counter). The metrics module follows the workspace `OnceLock` + `init()` + accessor pattern with `rustgate_core::metrics_util::fallback_*` so unregistered accessors still produce a working metric instance. **(8) Composition with the obligation engine.** Guard rejection is final — even with obligations applied (e.g. `StripPii` ahead of the boundary), a rate-limit or missing-marking trip drops the message; the audit record is the only artifact that survives. An upstream obligation that mutated the payload before it reached the guard is visible in the trail because the guard hashes whatever bytes reached it. **(9) Tests.** 26 test functions across `crates/rustgate-guard/src/lib.rs::tests` (21) and `crates/rustgate-guard/tests/integration.rs` (5): admit-within-cap, reject-over-cap-with-typed-error, throughput-refill-over-paused-time, per-direction-cap-isolation, mandatory-marking-rejects-no-marking, mandatory-marking-disabled-admits, audit-log-with-input-output-hashes, audit-log-rejection-with-reason, audit-chain-tamper-evident-via-existing-`HashChainWriter`, input-hash-equals-payload-sha256, output-hash-changes-when-obligation-applied-pre-guard, unauthorized-classification-rejected-`HighToLow`, low-to-high-accepts-top-secret, default-config-sensible-v1-caps, audit-log-grows-one-record-per-evaluate-regardless-of-outcome, chain-resumes-across-construct-drop-construct, source-cn-sanitization-strips-newlines, plus marking + uid extractors and error-display pins. The metrics-feature integration tests (`evaluations_metric_increments_on_decision`, `throughput_bps_metric_reflects_consumption`, `rejections_metric_labels_by_reason`) exercise the Prometheus counter / gauge contract end-to-end. **(10) Wire-format compatibility.** The dedicated boundary audit log is a NEW file alongside the existing operational audit chain — no change to the general audit envelope, no migration step on existing deployments. Operators who do not deploy `rustgate-guard` see no change. **(11) Out of scope.** The CDI obligation kinds (already shipped via #1286), the full CAPCO parser (already shipped via #1282), hardware diode integration (separate concern), and per-rule custom XML transforms beyond the existing CDI helpers. Closes #857.
- **Policy-side `ClassificationMarking` enforcement hook (refs #849)** — second deliverable of the CAPCO classification umbrella tracked under #849. The parser, banner-format `Display`/`FromStr`, serde wire form, and `dominates`/`lub` lattice operations on `rustgate_core::classification::ClassificationMarking` shipped via #1282; this PR teaches the authorization engine to forward an optional marking to policy backends so Cedar policies can condition decisions on it without yet requiring the field on `Metadata`. **(1) New `rustgate_authz::AuthzContext` struct.** Carries `classification: Option<ClassificationMarking>` plus a fluent `with_classification(self, marking) -> Self` builder; `#[non_exhaustive]` so future request-scoped policy hints (e.g. release-marking, originator-domain) extend the surface without breaking downstream construction. The struct is constructed at the PEP call site from the message envelope and is not serialised on its own — the classification field round-trips through its existing `Display`/`FromStr` (and `serde(into="String", try_from="String")`) wire form. **(2) New `PolicyEngine::evaluate_with_context` trait method.** Takes the existing `(subject, resource, action)` plus `&AuthzContext`; the default implementation delegates to the existing `evaluate(...)` so every existing trait impl (the in-process `NativeEngine`, downstream test backends, the optional `CedarBackend`) continues to compile without modification. Backwards-compat for every existing call site: `AuthzContext::default()` carries `classification: None` and the legacy entrypoint `evaluate(...)` still funnels through the same code path. **(3) Cedar backend wiring.** `CedarBackend` overrides `evaluate_with_context` to forward the marking under `context.classification.label` carrying the canonical CAPCO banner string (e.g. `"//SECRET//NOFORN"`) so policy authors write conditions like `context.classification.label like "*SECRET*" && !(context.classification.label like "*NOFORN*")`. The intermediate record shape leaves room for future fields (parsed level, SCI / dissemination sets) without breaking the wire contract. The diagnostics-aware fail-closed override in the existing `evaluate_inner` helper still applies: a policy that references an undefined classification field errors during Cedar evaluation, the diagnostics surface the failure, and the override forces the verdict to `Decision::Deny` regardless of any other matching `permit(...)`. **(4) Tests.** 3 unit tests in `rustgate_authz::model::authz_context_tests` (`authz_context_default_has_no_classification`, `authz_context_with_classification_sets_field`, `authz_context_with_classification_is_idempotent_overrides_last_writer`); 4 backend-agnostic integration tests in `crates/rustgate-authz/tests/classification_policy.rs` (`native_engine_evaluate_with_default_context_matches_evaluate`, `native_engine_pass_through_with_classification_set`, `engine_passes_classification_through_to_decision_callback` exercising a custom recording `PolicyEngine` impl, `lub_of_two_inputs_drives_egress_decision` confirming `ClassificationMarking::lub` composes with the new context surface); 5 Cedar-gated integration tests in the same file under `mod cedar_classification` (`policy_can_condition_on_classification_label_substring` for the headline operational pattern, `policy_denies_when_classification_label_contains_noforn_for_foreign_subject`, `classification_serializes_to_canonical_banner_in_policy_input` for an exact-banner equality check pinning the wire format, `engine_rejects_policy_referencing_undefined_classification_field` exercising the diagnostics-driven deny, and `cedar_evaluate_without_context_matches_evaluate_with_default_context` pinning the legacy entrypoint round-trip). All 248 tests pass without `cedar`; all 295 tests pass with `cedar`. **(5) Wire-format compatibility.** Every existing `evaluate(...)` call site in `crates/rustgate-transport/src/router.rs` and the integration suite continues to make the same decision as before — backends that do not override `evaluate_with_context` see the contextless path; backends that do override observe `AuthzContext::default()` from any caller that has not been migrated, which is identical to "no classification". **(6) Out of scope.** `Metadata.classification: Option<ClassificationMarking>` (item 3 — deferred alongside #852 PR-C because of the same 138-site refactor cost), router enforcement at egress (item 4 — needs item 3 first), and MIL-STD-2525 SIDC carry on the Entity model (item 6) remain. Cross-domain guard hooks (item 5) are tracked under #857. Refs #849.
- **`rustgate_mavlink::entity::MavlinkEntityCodec` — second concrete `EntityCodec` impl (refs #847)** — second deliverable of the Entity Model Abstraction Layer tracked under #847; the trait + CoT XML scaffold shipped via #1289 and the ASTERIX, STANAG-4586, Link 16, and router/federation/NATS/HTTP/MQTT integrations against the same trait remain. Adds a new `rustgate_mavlink::entity` module with `MavlinkEntityCodec` (stateless, `Default + Clone + Copy`, `Send + Sync` via the `EntityCodec` bound), the `MavlinkEntityError` enum (`InvalidFrame(String)` for malformed wire bytes, `UnsupportedMessage(u32)` for `MSG_ID` outside the mapped subset, `UnsupportedEntityKind(String)` for entities that lack a MAVLink wire form, `MissingField(&'static str)` for frames whose declared payload truncates past a strict-subset field), the public `GLOBAL_POSITION_INT_MSG_ID = 33` constant, and the `mav_msg_supported(u32) -> bool` predicate so call sites can pre-filter without invoking the full decode path. Inbound mapping (`MavlinkEntityCodec::to_entity`): system + component identifiers fold into `Entity.uid` as `"mavlink-{system_id}-{component_id}"`; HEARTBEAT (`MSG_ID = 0`) dispatches `EntityKind` from `MAV_TYPE` (FIXED_WING / QUADROTOR / COAXIAL / HELICOPTER / HEXAROTOR / OCTOROTOR / TRICOPTER / VTOL_TAILSITTER_DUOROTOR / VTOL_TAILSITTER_QUADROTOR / VTOL_TILTROTOR / AIRSHIP / KITE → `Aircraft`, GROUND_ROVER → `Ground`, SURFACE_BOAT / SUBMARINE → `Marine`, ANTENNA_TRACKER / GIMBAL / CAMERA → `Sensor`, GENERIC / GCS / FREE_BALLOON / ROCKET / FLAPPING_WING / ONBOARD_CONTROLLER / unknown bytes → `Unknown("mavlink-{:?}")` with the typed label tag); GLOBAL_POSITION_INT (`MSG_ID = 33`) lifts `lat_e7` / `lon_e7` / `alt_mm` into `Entity.position` (1e-7 deg / 1e-3 m resolution) and resolves `(vx, vy)` cm/s into `Entity.velocity` as a polar (speed_m_s, course_deg) pair using `atan2(east, north)` normalised to `[0, 360)`; every numeric wire field also rides on the `mavlink.global_position_int.*` attribute namespace (lat_e7 / lon_e7 / alt_mm / relative_alt_mm / vx_cm_s / vy_cm_s / vz_cm_s / hdg_cdeg / time_boot_ms) so a same-codec round-trip recovers the integer encoding without lossy float math. Outbound mapping (`MavlinkEntityCodec::from_entity`) is intentionally narrower: only `Position`-bearing entities encode into a v2 unsigned `GLOBAL_POSITION_INT` frame (CRC bytes are zero placeholders — the framing layer in `MavlinkFrameCodec` re-runs CRC and signature generation when the frame egresses on a real link). Entities without a position surface `MavlinkEntityError::UnsupportedEntityKind("entity has no Position")`; entities whose `uid` does not match the `"mavlink-<sys>-<comp>"` shape surface the same variant with the offending uid in the message. The encoder reuses any `mavlink.global_position_int.{vx,vy,vz}_cm_s` / `hdg_cdeg` carry from `to_entity` to preserve the original integer wire encoding; absent the carry it synthesises `(vx, vy)` from `(speed, course)` via the inverse polar conversion (lossy fallback for entities that originated outside the MAVLink codec). 13 new tests in `rustgate_mavlink::entity::tests` (test-runner `cargo nextest run -p rustgate-mavlink`): `mavlink_heartbeat_round_trips_through_entity_codec` (uid + kind preserved across two decodes, `from_entity` on a HEARTBEAT-only entity surfaces the typed unsupported error), `mavlink_global_position_int_to_entity_extracts_position` (canonical Massachusetts coordinates 42°N / -71°W / 100 m HAE round-trip cleanly), `UnsupportedMessage(253)`), `entity_with_no_position_emits_unsupported_for_from_entity`, `entity_to_mavlink_emits_global_position_int` (round-trip preserves uid / kind / position / velocity and the encoded frame parses back as GLOBAL_POSITION_INT), plus `mav_msg_supported_covers_the_two_mapped_ids` and `mav_type_byte_dispatch_covers_every_documented_branch` pinning the public predicate and full MAV_TYPE table from the module docs. **Wire-format compatibility is unchanged** — the MAVLink wire format is untouched and the Entity codec is a NEW abstraction layered on top of the existing `MavlinkCodec` and `MavlinkFrameCodec`. **Out of scope:** decoding for MAVLink message IDs other than HEARTBEAT and GLOBAL_POSITION_INT (those land via subsequent PRs as router integration demands against `Entity`. - **W3C Trace Context type + V2 federation gRPC traceparent propagation (refs #852, PR-B of the 3-PR split)** — first half of the distributed-trace propagation umbrella tracked under #852. Splits the original brief into three PRs after the deferral comment on #852 noted that the `Metadata.trace_context: Option<TraceContext>` field would trigger a 138-site refactor; PR-A defines the type, PR-B (this PR — combined with PR-A) wires the type through federation gRPC headers, and PR-C will land the `RoutableMessage::metadata` field plus the corresponding migration. **(1) New module `rustgate_core::traceparent`.** Hosts `TraceContext` (`trace_id: [u8; 16]`, `parent_span_id: [u8; 8]`, `trace_flags: u8`, `tracestate: Option<String>`), the `ParseTraceparentError` typed error surface (`WrongFieldCount`, `UnsupportedVersion`, `WrongLength`, `NonHex`, `AllZeroTraceId`, `AllZeroSpanId`, `TracestateTooLarge`), the `MAX_TRACESTATE_BYTES = 512` constant pinning the W3C section-3.3.1.2 cap, and the `Display` / `FromStr` round-trip on the wire-stable banner form `00-{trace_id_hex}-{parent_span_id_hex}-{flags_hex}` (lowercase, fixed-width). Serde delegates to `Display` / `FromStr` via `#[serde(into = "String", try_from = "String")]` so JSON, TOML, bincode, and MsgPack all carry the same banner string a peer sees on the wire instead of a struct dump that would break on a future field addition. The parser strictly enforces the W3C section-3.2.2.3 invariants: an all-zero `trace_id` or `parent_span_id` is rejected, the version byte must be `00` (other versions are reserved by the W3C spec and require an explicit upgrade), and the hex fields are length-checked before per-character parsing. Twelve unit tests in `rustgate-core::traceparent::tests` pin every documented branch (round-trip; non-`00` version reject; wrong-length reject; non-hex reject; all-zero trace_id; all-zero span_id; ≤ 512-byte tracestate accept; > 512-byte tracestate reject; serde JSON banner-string round-trip; field-count mismatch; uppercase-hex normalisation on Display; `is_sampled` reads bit 0 of `trace_flags`). **(2) New module `rustgate_federation::v2::traceparent`.** Provides the `inject_into_request` (outbound) and `extract_into_current_span` / `extract_from_metadata` (inbound) helpers that move the W3C `traceparent` and `tracestate` headers across federation gRPC RPC boundaries via `tonic::metadata`. Outbound: when the `otel` feature is on, the helper reads `tracing::Span::current().context()` and (if the OTel context is valid) injects `traceparent` plus optionally `tracestate` onto the request's `metadata_mut`. When the `otel` feature is off, the helper is a no-op — the wire format is unchanged from the pre-#852 baseline. Inbound: the helper extracts the `traceparent` metadata entry, parses it via the new type, and (with the `otel` feature on) attaches the parsed parent context to the current span via `tracing-opentelemetry`'s `OpenTelemetrySpanExt::set_parent` so downstream telemetry sees the federation hop as a continuation of the upstream trace. Without the `otel` feature, the helper emits `tracing::debug!(traceparent = %ctx, "federation peer trace context received")` for log-only correlation. Every outbound V2 RPC (`SendOneBlob`, `SendOneEvent` via `ServerEventStream`, `ServerROLStream`, `ClientFederateGroupsStream`, `HealthCheck`, both `ClientEventStream` / `ServerFederateGroupsStream` subscription opens) routes through a single `outbound_request` helper in `v2/client.rs` that wraps `Request::new` with the inject call — the inject path lives at exactly one site. Every inbound V2 handler (`send_one_event`, `send_one_blob`, `health_check`, `server_event_stream`, `server_rol_stream`, `client_federate_groups_stream`, `client_rol_stream`, `server_federate_groups_stream`) calls `extract_into_current_span` after `peer_id_from_request` so trace linkage runs after mTLS authentication but before any payload processing. **(3) New audit event `federation.traceparent_invalid`.** `rustgate_core::audit::federation_traceparent_invalid(peer_cn, reason)` emits at `tracing::info` level on the `audit` target with `event_type = "federation.traceparent_invalid"`, `action = "trace_propagation"`, `result = "rejected"`, plus the documented `peer` and `reason` fields. Both `&str` arguments cross the audit boundary via `sanitize_for_log` per the workspace audit-boundary discipline (#1197 / #1220) — a rogue federation peer that forges a `traceparent` header with embedded CR/LF cannot log-forge a fake rejection record. The RPC itself still completes when a malformed header is observed; trace propagation is best-effort and a misbehaving peer cannot fail federation traffic by sending a junk header. **(4) New federation feature `otel`.** Behind `[features] otel = ["dep:opentelemetry", "dep:tracing-opentelemetry"]` so deployments without OTel infrastructure pay no compile-time cost for the OTel SDK references. The workspace `tracing-opentelemetry` and `opentelemetry` dependency entries pre-existed (`rustgate-server` already uses them under `otel`); the federation crate now opts in optionally. **(5) Tests.** Twelve unit tests in `rustgate-core::traceparent::tests` pin the type-level contract; nine unit tests in `rustgate_federation::v2::traceparent::tests` (`extract_returns_none_when_metadata_has_no_traceparent`, `extract_parses_well_formed_traceparent`, `extract_rejects_malformed_traceparent_and_returns_none`, `extract_carries_tracestate_alongside_well_formed_traceparent`, `extract_drops_oversize_tracestate_but_keeps_traceparent`, `inject_is_a_no_op_when_otel_feature_is_off` — gated `#[cfg(not(feature = "otel"))]`, `header_constants_are_lowercase`) pin every helper-level branch including the no-op contract for non-otel builds; six integration tests in `crates/rustgate-federation/tests/v2_traceparent.rs` (`federation_inbound_records_traceparent_header_when_present`, `federation_inbound_handles_missing_traceparent_gracefully`, `federation_inbound_rejects_malformed_traceparent`, `tracestate_round_trip_through_grpc_metadata`, `traceparent_audit_event_records_invalid_header`, `federation_outbound_propagates_traceparent_when_otel_active`) stand up a real `FederationService` mTLS gRPC server and drive the wire-level `FederatedChannelClient` directly to exercise the end-to-end propagation path including audit emission. One audit-shape test in `rustgate-core::audit::tests::federation::test_traceparent_invalid` pins the four documented call shapes plus the CR/LF sanitization defence on every `&str` field. **(6) Wire-format compatibility.** Federation peers running this version send the `traceparent` metadata entry only when the local server has an active span with a valid OTel context (or, on non-`otel` builds, never). Receivers tolerate the header's absence — every existing federation peer continues to interoperate cleanly with no migration step. A peer that does not understand the header simply ignores it (gRPC metadata is extension-friendly by design). **(7) Out of scope (PR-C).** Persisting `Option<TraceContext>` on `RoutableMessage::metadata` plus the 138-site migration that surfaces extracted trace context to local routing, the position cache, dedup, and downstream egress paths is explicitly deferred to PR-C.
