PR-C will let trace context flow into the local-session log pipeline; this PR (PR-B) carries it only at the federation gRPC header level, which is enough for Jaeger / Tempo to hop-link the trace via the OTel SDK's span hierarchy. Local-session trace propagation, B3 / Zipkin headers, and sampling-policy changes are also out of scope. Refs #852.
- **Per-tenant aggregate-throughput token bucket (closes #883, completes the umbrella alongside #1251 + #1268 + #1277)** — finishes the four-sub-item resilience-hardening deliverable tracked under #883: encrypted-archive KDF + key-expiration shipped via #1251, audit-chain sequence numbers shipped via #1268, NATS poison-message infinite-redelivery guard shipped via #1277; this PR rounds out the umbrella by layering a tenant-keyed token bucket on top of the existing per-session `ClientThrottle` so a noisy tenant with N sessions cannot collectively consume N× the intended aggregate throughput. **(1) Two new `TenantQuota` fields.** `max_throughput_bps` (sustained byte-per-second cap; the bucket's burst capacity) and `refill_throughput_bps` (refill rate; defaults to `max_throughput_bps` when unset for steady-state semantics) extend the existing JSON tenant-quota file with backwards-compatible defaults — existing deployments without the new keys parse cleanly and behave exactly as before because both fields default to `0` (the documented "this layer does not apply" sentinel). The new keys still flow through the F-136 `deny_unknown_fields` discipline, so a typo like `max_throuhgput_bps` produces a clear deserialization error rather than a silently-ignored unlimited cap. **(2) New `try_acquire_tenant_tokens(tenant, bytes)` method on `TenantQuotaTracker`.** Charges a per-tenant `rustgate_resilience::token_bucket::TokenBucket` keyed by certificate Organization (O) field, lazily constructed in a `DashMap<Arc<str>, Arc<TokenBucket>>` so per-tenant lookups are lock-free on the message-send hot path — a single `parking_lot::RwLock<HashMap<…>>` would serialize every tenant's send through the same shard, defeating per-tenant isolation. Returns `Ok(())` when the cap admits the request OR the tenant has no quota configured (this layer is additive on top of per-session, not a replacement); returns `Err(TenantThroughputRejection { tenant, requested, available })` when the bucket holds fewer than `bytes` after lazy refill, so audit emission attributes the drop to the actual headroom rather than a stale snapshot. **(3) New `try_acquire_n` + `current_tokens` + `capacity` API on the shared `TokenBucket`.** Adds byte-token semantics (the existing single-token `try_acquire` would force callers into an N-iteration loop) plus a non-consuming snapshot accessor for metrics-gauge code paths. The new `TokenBucketRejection { available }` error carries the post-refill bucket level so the per-tenant audit event sees exactly the headroom the rejection saw. **(4) Wire-up at the router send path.** `Router::route_inner` charges the per-tenant bucket after the Send-PEP allow but before `cache.store` and before obligation actuation — a tenant-throttled drop must not enter the SA replay cache, must not pay the obligation cost, and must not fan out to any local recipient or egress forwarder. Tenant key falls back to the existing `crate::quota::DEFAULT_TENANT_KEY` when the source identity has no tenant. The `OnDropped` callback's reason vocabulary gains a new `"tenant_throughput_exceeded"` label so SIEM dashboards and the `rustgate_router_dropped_total{reason}` Prometheus counter share a single vocabulary across the per-tenant and existing per-session drops. **(5) New audit event `quota.tenant_throughput_exceeded`.** `rustgate_core::audit::tenant_throughput_exceeded(tenant, msg_uid, requested, available)` emits at `tracing::info` level on the `audit` target with `action = "send"`, `result = "rejected"`, plus the documented `tenant` / `uid` / `requested` / `available` fields. Both string fields cross the audit boundary via `sanitize_for_log` per the workspace audit-boundary discipline — a rogue client with a CoT `uid="…"` carrying CR/LF cannot log-forge fake throughput records. **(6) Two new metrics.** `rustgate_tenant_throughput_rejections_total{tenant}` (counter, increments once per drop) and `rustgate_tenant_throughput_bps{tenant}` (gauge, post-decision bucket level updated on every admit OR reject) — both wired through hot-reloadable `OnTenantThroughputRejection` / `OnTenantThroughputConsumed` callback aliases on the tracker so the transport crate stays metric-free and the server binary owns the Prometheus registration. The accessor for the gauge returns `Option<&'static GaugeVec>` to match the workspace tier-1 fallback pattern (`unwrap_used` is denied workspace-wide). **(7) Tests.** Eight integration tests in `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/tenant_token_bucket.rs` drive the full router send path: `tenant_token_bucket_default_throughput_caps_aggregate` (5 sessions on the same tenant collectively try to send 3× the cap; only the cap's worth pass), `tenant_token_bucket_per_tenant_isolation` (acme saturates; globex unaffected), `tenant_token_bucket_override_raises_cap_for_named_tenant` ("Acme Corp" override gives 10× the default cap), `tenant_token_bucket_refills_over_time` (drain → throttled → `tokio::time::advance` → admit, paused-clock determinism), `tenant_throughput_exceeded_audit_event_fires` (custom `tracing::Layer` capturing the `target = "audit"` event for the documented field shape), `tenant_throughput_metric_increments_on_rejection` (per-rejection callback fires exactly once per dropped message), `tenant_token_bucket_handles_unknown_tenant_with_default` (default-cap path applies when no per-tenant entry exists), and `tenant_token_bucket_does_not_double_account_with_per_session_bucket` (per-session and per-tenant buckets compose: a charge on one does not affect the other; a message that passes both is delivered exactly once). 12 additional unit tests in `crates/rustgate-transport/src/quota.rs::tests` pin the tracker contract (admit-under-cap, reject-with-attribution, unknown-tenant-admit, zero-cap-admit, default-quota-applies-to-unknown, per-tenant-isolation, metrics-callback-fires-on-admit-and-reject, available-snapshot-reflects-drain-state, rejection-and-consumed-callbacks-coalesce, legacy-3-field-tenant-entry-still-parses, and unknown-throughput-typo-rejected-by-deny-unknown-fields). 9 new tests in `crates/rustgate-resilience/src/token_bucket.rs::tests` cover the new `try_acquire_n` / `current_tokens` / `capacity` API across partial-burst admit, over-cap reject, zero/negative/NaN sanitisation, refill-over-time, and rejection-display contract. 1 new test in `rustgate-core::audit::tests` (`test_tenant_throughput_exceeded`) pins the audit-record shape across small / large / control-character-laden inputs. **(8) Wire-format compatibility.** The new TOML / JSON keys are additive — existing deployments without `max_throughput_bps` continue to operate exactly as before because the default `0` is the documented "no per-tenant throughput cap" sentinel and the tracker admits unconditionally in that branch. **(9) Out of scope.** Cross-server tenant-quota coordination remains per-server only for v1; new tenant-discovery mechanisms (cert O field is the existing pattern); reworking the per-session token bucket. Closes #883.

- **`rustgate_core::entity::Entity` + `EntityCodec` trait with the CoT XML implementation (refs #847, scaffold-only deliverable)** — first concrete deliverable of the Entity Model Abstraction Layer tracked under #847. Adds a new `rustgate_core::entity` module with the canonical `Entity` value type (`uid` / `kind` / `position` / `velocity` / `timestamp` / `callsign` / `mil_std_2525_sidc` / `attributes`), the supporting enums (`EntityKind` covering Track / Sensor / Aircraft / Ground / Marine / Munition / Unknown(label), `Position` lat-lon-hae, `Velocity` speed-course, `AttributeValue` Str/Int/Float/Bool), and the `EntityCodec` trait the protocol crates implement (`type Error`, `to_entity(&[u8]) -> Result<Entity, Self::Error>`, `from_entity(&Entity) -> Result<Bytes, Self::Error>`, `Send + Sync` bound). All types derive `Serialize` / `Deserialize` so the canonical form survives JSON / MsgPack / bincode round-trips without an intermediate representation. The CoT XML implementation lives in the new `rustgate_cot::entity` module: `CotEntityCodec` decodes `<event uid type time start stale how>` into the strict-subset fields, dispatches `EntityKind` from the second segment of the SA atom (`a-*-A-*` → Aircraft, `a-*-G-*` → Ground, `a-*-S-*`/`a-*-U-*` → Marine, `a-*-P-*`/`a-*-M-*` → Munition, other SA atoms → Track, `t-*` → Sensor, anything else → Unknown carrying the raw type), pulls `<point lat lon hae ce le>` into `Position` plus `cot.point.{ce,le,hae}` carries on the attributes bag, lifts `<detail><track speed course>` to `Velocity`, lifts `<detail><contact callsign>` to `Entity.callsign`, and folds every other `<detail>` child element + attributes (and any text body) into the `cot.detail.<elem>.<attr>` / `cot.detail.<elem>.text` namespace so a same-codec round-trip preserves the unmapped extension data. `from_entity` reverses the mapping, emitting a minimal CoT envelope (`<event version uid type time start stale how>` with `<point>` and `<detail>` children only when the entity carries the matching data). 13 new tests pin the contract: 3 in `rustgate-core::entity::tests` (serde JSON round-trip with all four `AttributeValue` shapes; `EntityKind::Unknown(label)` carry; `Position` with `hae_meters: None` serialises as `"hae_meters":null`); 10 in `rustgate-cot::entity::tests` (round-trip through codec preserves uid / kind / position / velocity / callsign / attributes / timestamp; uid extraction; `EntityKind` dispatch covers all seven branches; `<point>` extraction with and without `hae`; `<track>` velocity extraction; `<contact>` callsign extraction; unmapped detail children land in the attribute bag; malformed XML returns a typed `ParseError::InvalidFloat`; round-trip preserves `<event how>` / `<event version>` plus `<remarks>` text and `<__group name>` carries through the `cot.detail.<elem>.<attr>` namespace). **This PR is the trait + CoT impl scaffold only**: the MAVLink, ASTERIX, STANAG-4586, and Link 16 codec implementations against the same trait, the optional `Entity` carry on `RoutableMessage`, the router-internal pivot from XML payloads to `Entity` values, the federation/NATS/HTTP/MQTT egress wiring against `Entity`, and the protobuf wire shape for `rustgate-proto` are all explicitly deferred to subsequent PRs. Wire-format compatibility is unchanged — `Entity` is a new abstraction, not a replacement for `RoutableMessage` or any existing type. Refs #847.
- **V2 federation client-side ROL / `BinaryBlob` / GroupSync senders (closes #864)** — completes the round-trip for the three TAK-ecosystem RPCs whose server-side handlers (with `OnRolEvent` / `OnBlob` / `OnGroupSync` callback observability + audit + metrics + hop-count + allowlist gating) shipped via #1248. Pre-this-PR `V2Client` could only push `FederatedEvent`s through the long-lived `ServerEventStream`; ROL events, binary blobs, and group-sync updates produced locally had nowhere to go on the outbound path. **(1) Three new public methods on `V2Client`.** `send_blob(BinaryBlob)` dispatches a single blob through the unary `SendOneBlob` RPC — the path the server's `OnBlob` callback observes. `send_rol(Rol)` enqueues a ROL event onto an internal mpsc that the connection loop forwards over a long-lived `ServerROLStream` client-streaming RPC opened during handshake. `send_groups(FederateGroups)` enqueues a `FederateGroups` update onto a separate mpsc that the connection loop forwards over the existing `ClientFederateGroupsStream` RPC (which previously sent only the local roster on handshake and held the stream open without further updates). Each method follows the same shape as the pre-existing `send` — channel-closed surfaces a `FederationError`, transient gRPC errors are logged inside the connection loop and trigger reconnect via the existing exponential-backoff path. **(2) Per-RPC channel isolation.** The three side channels (`blob_tx`, `rol_tx`, `groups_tx`) are held independently of the `outbound_tx` event channel so a stalled remote on one path cannot back-pressure the others. Channel capacities mirror the event path's 256 (groups: 64 — group-sync updates are low-cardinality). On reconnect the streams are reopened transparently and the local roster is re-sent automatically; callers do not replay it. **(3) `run_streams` reorganization.** The handshake now opens five client-side streams in addition to the receive-only `ClientEventStream` (`ServerFederateGroupsStream` → receive remote groups, `ClientFederateGroupsStream` → send our groups + ongoing updates, `ServerEventStream` → send events, `ClientEventStream` → receive events, `ServerROLStream` → send ROL events). Outbound `BinaryBlob` traffic goes through unary `SendOneBlob` from the `select!` arm rather than a dedicated long-lived stream — matches the server-side path that fires `OnBlob` and lets a slow remote naturally back-pressure the in-flight blob queue. **(4) Tests.** Seven round-trip integration tests in `crates/rustgate-federation/tests/v2_rpcs.rs` stand up an mTLS `FederationService` and drive the wire-level `FederatedChannelClient` to verify each RPC end-to-end: `send_one_blob_round_trip_invokes_on_blob` (43-byte payload preserves bytes, filename, timestamp, type), `send_one_blob_with_no_callback_still_succeeds` (no-op default callback path returns `Empty` cleanly), `send_one_blob_at_hop_limit_silently_drops` (hop-count gate fires before the callback), `server_rol_stream_round_trip_invokes_on_rol_event` (three ROL events arrive with correct `program` values in order), `server_rol_stream_drops_event_at_hop_limit` (per-event hop gate filters before the callback while the valid event passes), `client_federate_groups_stream_round_trip_invokes_on_group_sync` (three updates round-trip in order with full membership preservation), and `client_federate_groups_stream_drops_update_at_hop_limit` (per-update hop gate). One unit test in `v2::client::tests` (`rpc_side_channels_fail_after_shutdown`) pins that all three side channels surface a closed-channel error after the connection loop exits — without this, callers could enqueue blobs onto a dead channel forever. **(5) Wire-format compatibility.** All additions are pure client-side senders; the wire-level RPC contracts on `FederatedChannel` are unchanged. Existing V2 federation peers continue to interoperate without modification — a remote peer that does not consume any of the three RPCs will simply receive empty (or no) traffic on those streams. **(6) Out of scope.** Server-side outbound machinery for `ClientROLStream` / `ServerFederateGroupsStream` (proto: server-streaming, "we push payloads back"); these remain observable stubs that hold the stream open after the subscription audit + allowlist gate. Closes #864.
- **JWKS `kid` rotation-window state machine (closes #952, completes the umbrella alongside #1230 + #1252)** — finishes the three-sub-item JWKS deliverable tracked under #952: Ed25519 (RFC 8037 EdDSA) signing shipped via #1230 and JWKS URL fetching with periodic refresh shipped via #1252; this PR rounds out the umbrella with a four-state `Pending → Active → Retiring → Retired` lifecycle that smooths the two edges of a key rotation. Pre-this-PR, every refresh that dropped a `kid` from the upstream JWKS immediately removed the verifier; correct fail-closed behaviour but transiently brittle — a JWT minted by a peer 10 ms before our refresh dropped its `kid` would fail verification, and a typo'd JWKS push that added a `kid` and was rolled back within seconds would briefly register a verifier the operator never intended to trust. **(1) New module `rustgate_federation::jwks_rotation`.** Hosts `RotationState` (`Pending`, `Active`, `Retiring`, `Retired`), `RotationStateMachine` (per-`kid` lifecycle map behind a `parking_lot::Mutex` — no `.await` boundary, no poison panic, no `.unwrap`), `RetainedVerifiers` (cache of last-good verifier material so Retiring kids keep verifying during the grace window), `RefreshTransitions` (per-tick diff returned by `observe_refresh`), and `install_on_authority` (wires the post-validate hook into `JwtAuthority`). The four states are deterministic functions of (in-JWKS observations seen, time): a newly-observed kid enters Pending; a second consecutive observation past `pending_window` promotes to Active; an Active kid that drops from upstream demotes to Retiring with `retiring_started_at` recorded; a Retiring kid past `retiring_window` advances to Retired (verifier dropped from the install set); and a Retiring kid that reappears in upstream JWKS skips Pending and goes straight back to Active because the operator never intended to remove it. A `pending_window` of zero opts out of the smoothing — newly observed kids go straight to Active — for test scaffolding and the rare single-shot bootstrap where there is nothing to roll back from. **(2) New post-validate hook on `JwtAuthority`.** `OnKidUsed = Arc<dyn Fn(&str) + Send + Sync>` is the workspace-idiomatic `On*` callback type, hot-reloadable via `ArcSwap<Option<OnKidUsed>>` so the rotation state machine can install / replace it after construction without taking a lock on the validation hot path. The internal `decode` helper now returns `(Option<String>, FederationClaims)` so `validate` can fire the callback with the resolved kid after every successful signature check; un-installed cost is one atomic load + one nullable check per validation. **(3) Two new `JwksConfig` fields plus matching CLI flags.** `pending_window: Duration` (default `60s`, alias `--jwks-pending-window-secs` / `RUSTGATE_JWKS_PENDING_WINDOW_SECS`) and `retiring_window: Duration` (default `300s`, alias `--jwks-retiring-window-secs` / `RUSTGATE_JWKS_RETIRING_WINDOW_SECS`) are added to `JwksConfig` with `serde(default)` so existing JWKS deployments without the new flags pick up the documented defaults — same behaviour they have today plus the rotation-window smoothing. The `define_config_file!` macro in `rustgate-server::cli` mirrors the new flags as kebab-case TOML keys (`jwks-pending-window-secs`, `jwks-retiring-window-secs`) so all four input paths (CLI, env, TOML, default) merge through the same `apply_to` flow. **(4) New audit event `jwt.using_retiring_kid`.** `rustgate_core::audit::jwt_using_retiring_kid(kid, retiring_for_seconds)` emits at `tracing::info` level on the `audit` target with `event_type = "jwt.using_retiring_kid"`, `action = "verify"`, `result = "warning"`, plus the documented `kid` and numeric `retiring_for_seconds` fields. SIEM dashboards key on this event to spot peers that have not yet rotated — every emission is a hint that the issuing peer still mints JWTs against a soon-to-be-removed key, so a moving-window count of `retiring_for_seconds` reveals which peers will start failing once the grace window elapses. The `kid` field crosses the audit boundary via `sanitize_for_log` per the workspace audit-boundary discipline (#1197 / #1220) — a rogue federation peer that forges a JWT with embedded CR/LF in its `kid` header cannot log-forge a fake retiring-key record. **(5) `JwksClient::start` wiring.** Constructs a `RotationStateMachine` + `RetainedVerifiers` pair, installs the kid-used callback on the supplied `JwtAuthority`, and routes the refresh task through a new `refresh_once_with_rotation` body that calls `observe_refresh` per tick and `filter_for_install` to derive the install set (Active kids from `next` plus Retiring kids from the retained cache; Pending and Retired excluded). The pre-existing `refresh_once` is preserved for backward compatibility with the existing wiremock integration tests in `tests/jwks_client.rs` — those tests intentionally drive the raw refresh path because they cover protocol-layer invariants (refresh interval, fail-closed semantics, audit emission) and do not need the rotation gate. **(6) Tests.** Seven integration tests in `crates/rustgate-federation/tests/jwks_kid_rotation.rs` pin every state transition end-to-end using `tokio::time::pause` + `tokio::time::advance` for deterministic clock control: `kid_lifecycle_pending_then_active_after_two_consecutive_refreshes` (first observation → Pending; second after `pending_window` → Active), `kid_lifecycle_pending_disappears_before_promotion` (typo'd JWKS push pruned, never registered as Active), `kid_lifecycle_active_to_retiring_when_dropped_from_upstream`, `kid_lifecycle_retiring_still_verifies_jwts_during_grace` (drives an actual `JwtAuthority::validate` against a Retiring kid using a real Ed25519 keypair, asserts both verification success and audit emission), `kid_lifecycle_retiring_to_retired_after_grace_window`, `kid_lifecycle_retiring_returns_to_active_if_kid_reappears_in_jwks` (defends against momentary upstream JWKS hiccups), and `audit_jwt_using_retiring_kid_fires_with_retiring_seconds_field` (pins the wire shape SIEM rules key on — `event_type`, `kid`, numeric `retiring_for_seconds`, `action`, `result`). Eleven additional unit tests inside the module cover edge cases (filter-excludes-Pending, filter-installs-Retiring-from-cache, steady-state diff is empty, notify_kid_used silent for Active/unknown kids, pending_window floor blocks too-fast promotion, retained-verifiers round-trip). Three new tests in `rustgate-core::audit::tests` (`test_jwt_using_retiring_kid_smoke`, `jwt_using_retiring_kid_emits_documented_shape`, `jwt_using_retiring_kid_sanitizes_kid_field`) pin the audit-record contract. **(7) Out of scope.** Federation peer-discovery is a separate umbrella; HMAC HS256 rotation is not shipped because the JWKS path does not advertise HS256 by default; cross-server kid synchronisation remains operator-orchestrated through a shared upstream JWKS endpoint. Closes #952.

- **`rustgate_transport::hw_identity` — `HardwareIdentity` trait + reference `Pkcs11StubBackend` (closes #856, foundational deliverable)** — first concrete deliverable of the hardware-rooted identity umbrella tracked under #856. Adds the `HardwareIdentity` trait (object-safe: every method `&self`, no generics, no `Self` in return types outside `Box<dyn …>`), the `HardwareIdentityError` typed error surface (`Unavailable`, `PinRequired`, `Rejected`, `Io`), the `Pkcs11StubBackend` reference implementation that mirrors the API shape of a real PKCS#11 driver using software-backed material so the trait, the audit hooks, and the resolver adapter can be exercised end-to-end without hardware, and the `HardwareIdentityResolver` adapter that drives `rustls::server::ResolvesServerCert` so a hardware-rooted listener composes through the existing `TlsConfig::build_reloadable_server_config` entry point — no changes to `TlsListener` itself. **(1) Trait surface.** `cert_chain()` returns the X.509 chain bound to the hardware identity (leaf first, intermediates following); `sign(message, algorithm)` runs the TLS-handshake signature operation inside the hardware module (the trait carries a transport-layer `SignatureAlgorithm` enum mirroring rustls's so the trait does not leak rustls-version churn into every backend); `is_available()` is the cheap liveness probe the resolver consults on every handshake; `backend_name()` returns a stable fixed-vocabulary slug (`"pkcs11-stub"` for the reference backend; future drivers will return `"pkcs11"`, `"tpm2"`, `"yubikey"`); `certified_key()` is the rustls `CertifiedKey` factory the resolver invokes — the default implementation returns `Rejected` so a backend that has not yet wired its hardware-side signing path fails closed instead of silently substituting a software key. **(2) `Pkcs11StubBackend`.** Loads a software-backed cert chain + private key from PEM material, wraps the private key in `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` so the test harness never carries an un-zeroed copy, exposes `set_available(bool)` so tests can simulate "token unplugged" / "PIN locked" without real hardware, implements custom `Debug` that redacts the private key (`[REDACTED]`) per the workspace secret-handling discipline, and emits `audit::hw_identity_loaded("pkcs11-stub")` on successful initialization. **(3) Fail-closed contract.** When `is_available()` returns `false` at the moment a TLS handshake requests the server certificate, the `HardwareIdentityResolver` fires `audit::hw_identity_unavailable(backend, reason)` and returns `None` — rustls aborts the handshake. The listener does NOT silently fall back to a software key, and operators who require a hardware-rooted identity can alert on the audit gap between `hw_identity.loaded` and the next completed handshake. Sign-path failures emit `audit::hw_identity_sign_failed(backend, reason)` so SIEM rules can distinguish "token not present" from "token present but rejected the operation". **(4) Three new audit events** in `rustgate-core::audit`: `hw_identity.loaded` (success on backend init, fields `event_type / backend / action="load" / result="success"`), `hw_identity.unavailable` (the fail-closed event, fields `event_type / backend / reason / action="sign" / result="rejected"`), `hw_identity.sign_failed` (fields `event_type / backend / reason / action="sign" / result="failure"`). Every `&str` field is sanitized at the audit boundary via `sanitize_for_log` per the workspace audit-boundary discipline (#1197 / #1220) — even though every in-tree caller passes a static slug today, the boundary discipline is uniform across the audit module and a future configuration-driven driver name could be operator-supplied. **(5) Tests.** Ten unit tests in `crates/rustgate-transport/src/hw_identity.rs::tests` (`pkcs11_stub_loads_from_pem`, `pkcs11_stub_rejects_garbage_pem`, `pkcs11_stub_signs_tls_certificate_verify`, `pkcs11_stub_reports_unavailable_when_set_false`, `pkcs11_stub_returns_chain_on_demand`, `hw_identity_unavailable_audit_event_fires`, `hw_identity_loaded_audit_event_fires`, `hardware_identity_trait_object_is_object_safe` — pinned via `let _: Box<dyn HardwareIdentity> = Box::new(...)`, `hardware_identity_resolver_returns_none_when_unavailable`, `pkcs11_stub_debug_redacts_private_key`). Two integration tests in `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/hw_identity.rs` (`tls_listener_uses_hw_identity_when_configured` — full mTLS handshake against a `HardwareIdentityResolver`-backed `ServerConfig`, asserts bytes flow round-trip; `tls_listener_rejects_handshake_when_hw_identity_unavailable` — pins the fail-closed contract end-to-end through a real listener). Seven audit-shape tests in `rustgate-core::audit::tests` (`test_hw_identity_loaded_smoke`, `test_hw_identity_unavailable_smoke`, `test_hw_identity_sign_failed_smoke`, `hw_identity_loaded_emits_documented_shape`, `hw_identity_unavailable_emits_documented_shape`, `hw_identity_sign_failed_emits_documented_shape`, `hw_identity_events_sanitize_user_controlled_fields`) pin every documented call site, the JSON wire format SIEM rules key on, and the log-forging defence on every `&str` field crossing the audit boundary. **(6) Out of scope.** Real PKCS#11 driver loading (the `pkcs11` C-library wrap is its own dependency-graph change and lands behind a feature gate in a follow-up PR), TPM2 attestation flows, YubiKey-specific PIN entry / FIDO2 flows, hardware-backed enrollment (the EST endpoints continue to read the CA key from disk), and the `--hw-identity-backend` CLI flag (deferred so the surface area lands together with the first real driver — the trait + resolver are the load-bearing pieces of #856 and a real driver PR will wire the CLI alongside the driver-specific config knobs without breaking the trait). The trait is shaped so a real backend can land without reshaping in-tree consumers — `certified_key()` is the only hot-path entry point the resolver uses, and a backend that overrides it with a `HardwareSigningKey` adapter routes signatures through `HardwareIdentity::sign` without the resolver knowing. Closes #856.
- **`rustgate_core::classification::ClassificationMarking` — CAPCO classification banner type (refs #849, parser-only deliverable)** — first concrete deliverable of the CAPCO Classification Marking Engine umbrella tracked under #849. Adds a new `rustgate_core::classification` module with `ClassificationMarking` and four supporting enums (`Classification`, `SciControl`, `DisseminationControl`, `NonIntelControl`), a strict CAPCO banner parser, a wire-stable `Display` form, classification-lattice operations (`dominates`, `lub`), and 63 tests covering DoDM 5200.01 Vol 2 Appendix banner shapes (`//UNCLASSIFIED//`, `//UNCLASSIFIED//FOUO`, `//CONFIDENTIAL//NOFORN`, `//SECRET//SI//NOFORN`, `//TOP SECRET//SI/TK//NOFORN`, `//SECRET//REL TO USA, FVEY//`, `//SECRET//SI/TK//REL TO USA, GBR//`, and the FOUO/LES/SBU/HCS-P/HCS-O/KLONDIKE/RSV variants). Serde delegates to `Display` / `FromStr` so JSON, TOML, bincode, and MsgPack callers all carry a stable banner string instead of a struct dump that would break on a future variant addition. The lattice ordering follows the standard rules: TS dominates S dominates C dominates U on the base classification dimension; SCI compartments compose as set superset ("TS // SI/TK" dominates "TS // SI" but not "TS // TK"); NOFORN dominates any release marking at the same level; `REL TO X` dominates `REL TO Y` when `X ⊆ Y` (a narrower release set is more restrictive). The `lub` operator computes the high-water mark across two markings — base classification is `max`, SCI sets union, dissemination collapses via the rule "any NOFORN ⇒ NOFORN; otherwise intersect REL TO country lists, collapse to NOFORN if disjoint" — for use by the eventual cross-domain guard. **This PR is parser-only**: the `Metadata.classification` field (item 2 of the umbrella, a 138-site refactor), the router enforcement against destination-domain policy (item 3), the Cedar policy backend integration (item 4), the cross-domain guard hooks (item 5), and the MIL-STD-2525 SIDC carry on the Entity model (item 6) all remain and ship in subsequent PRs. Refs #849.
- **Cross-domain inspection obligation scaffold: `StripPii`, `DegradePosition`, `InjectMarking` (refs #857)** — extends the existing obligation engine with three CoT-specific transformations the deferred `rustgate-guard` crate will use to redact, coarsen, and tag events crossing a security boundary. **(1) New `Obligation` variants.** `StripPii` (unit) blanks operator-identity attributes (`callsign`, `phone`, `email`, `endpoint`, IM/chat tokens) on `<contact>` and any `<detail>` child whose attribute key matches a PII token. `DegradePosition { precision_meters: u32 }` rounds CoT `<point lat lon>` to a coarser grid sized in metres — the scaffold uses an equator-equivalent step for both axes (preserving idempotence under repeated application; the full guard will scale longitude by `cos(latitude)` once it accepts the per-application drift trade-off). `InjectMarking { marking: String }` inserts `<marking value="…"/>` as a child of `<detail>`, replacing any existing `<marking>` so a previous CDI hop's banner does not accumulate; XML special characters are escaped via quick_xml's writer so a crafted banner cannot break out of the attribute value. The `Obligation` enum's `Copy` derive is dropped (replaced with `Clone + Hash + Eq`) because `InjectMarking` carries a `String`; existing call sites that needed `.copied()` move to `.cloned()` (one site in `proptest_obligation_idempotence.rs`). **(2) New `rustgate-cot::cdi` module.** Hosts the three transformation primitives `strip_pii`, `degrade_position`, and `inject_marking` — each one returns either a transformed `Bytes` or `mask::MaskError` under the same fail-closed contract as `mask::strip_coordinates`. Non-XML payloads are echoed verbatim; XML-intent parse failures surface `MaskError::Xml` so the dispatcher can fail-closed at the boundary message rather than forward partially-redacted bytes. Element matching is namespace-prefix-tolerant and case-insensitive. **(3) Dispatcher wiring.** `rustgate-transport::obligations::apply_obligations_with_limiter` adds three new arms (`Obligation::StripPii`, `Obligation::DegradePosition { … }`, `Obligation::InjectMarking { … }`) plus a shared recovery helper that emits the new `OBLIGATION_REASON_CDI_NON_XML` / `OBLIGATION_REASON_CDI_XML_ERROR` audit tokens. The new variants join Group 1 (Redactors) and Group 2 (Classifier/Tagger) of the canonical chaining order — `StripPii` and `DegradePosition` are redactors that run before any classifier or auditor sees the bytes; `InjectMarking` is a classifier that attaches the banner to the already-redacted body. `obligations_mutate_payload` returns `true` for all three so the per-recipient clone-out-of-`Arc` path runs. **(4) Audit & metrics labels.** `obligation_kind_label` in `router.rs` and `obligation_label` in the engine metrics expose the new `"strip_pii"`, `"degrade_position"`, `"inject_marking"` strings on the `rustgate_authz_obligations_emitted_total` and `egress.obligation.applied` audit-event vocabulary. The `egress_obligation_applied` audit docstring documents the extended bounded vocabulary. **(5) Tests.** Fourteen unit tests in `crates/rustgate-cot/src/cdi.rs` pin the per-helper transformation contract, the non-XML pass-through, the XML-intent parse-failure shape, the chaining associativity property, and XML-special-character escaping. Eleven integration tests in `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/cdi_obligations.rs` pin the dispatcher-level contract end-to-end including the `authz.obligation_failed` audit event shape with `obligation = "StripPii"` / `"DegradePosition"` / `"InjectMarking"` and the new `cdi_non_xml` reason token. The `proptest_obligation_idempotence.rs` strategies are extended to include the three CDI variants so the existing four composition invariants (idempotence, order-independence, permutation-independence, composition-equivalence) now hold across the seven-variant known set. **(6) Out of scope.** The full `rustgate-guard` crate (rate limiting at the boundary, mandatory marking-injection enforcement, dedicated audit envelope, encrypted spool), the CAPCO parser (#849), and CDS hardware diode integration are explicitly deferred to a follow-up PR. Refs #857.
- **Native IPv4 UDP multicast CoT input + optional rebroadcast egress (closes #861)** — ATAK devices on tactical mesh radio networks (MPU5, Silvus) use IPv4 multicast (typically `239.2.3.1:6969` for SA, `239.2.3.1:17012` for chat) for peer-to-peer Situational Awareness sharing; pre-this-PR the existing `rustgate-transport::udp` listener handled only unicast, so rustgate could not participate in those mesh fabrics. **(1) New module `rustgate_transport::udp_multicast`.** Exposes `MulticastGroup` (validated `host:port` parser that rejects non-multicast IPv4 and any IPv6 address), `MulticastConfig` (groups list, bind interface, `IP_MULTICAST_LOOP`, `IP_MULTICAST_TTL`, `rebroadcast` flag, BPS cap), `OnMulticastForward` (router callback type), `spawn_inbound` (one `tokio::net::UdpSocket` per configured group via socket2 + `SO_REUSEADDR` + `join_multicast_v4`, kernel-side join semantics), `spawn_egress` (single shared egress socket bound to ephemeral source port, optional `set_multicast_if_v4` via socket2 `SockRef` since tokio's UDP wrapper does not surface IP_MULTICAST_IF), and `SOURCE_UDP_MULTICAST = "udp-multicast"` (source-protocol tag stamped on every routed datagram so existing federation/NATS/HTTP forwarders' echo guards filter it without re-parsing the payload). The egress task wraps a `rustgate_resilience::token_bucket::TokenBucket` keyed by datagram bytes (1 token = 1 byte) so the configured cap measures wire bandwidth rather than packets/second; a CoT-shape filter (`looks_like_cot_xml` — leading `<` after whitespace) keeps protobuf and MAVLink frames off the multicast fabric, and a source-protocol equality check on `"udp-multicast"` prevents the egress task from re-emitting a datagram it just received. **(2) New router setter `Router::set_on_multicast_forward`.** Stores an `Arc<dyn Fn(Arc<RoutableMessage>) + Send + Sync>` in an `ArcSwap` slot fired exactly once from `route_for_egress` after the per-recipient fan-out has completed; the un-installed default path costs a single `ArcSwap::load` + `is_none()` check, matching the pattern of the existing `set_on_fanout` / `set_on_message_delivered` family. The slot is hot-reloadable so an operator can flip rebroadcast at runtime without restarting the listener. **(3) New CLI flags.** `--udp-multicast-groups` (comma-separated `host:port` list; empty default disables the subsystem entirely), `--udp-multicast-interface` (defaults `0.0.0.0` = "all interfaces"; operators on multi-NIC hosts can pin), `--udp-multicast-loop` (default `false` — tactical deployments don't want loopback), `--udp-multicast-ttl` (default `1` — same subnet only, the safe default for mesh radio), `--udp-multicast-rebroadcast` (default `false` — opt-in egress), `--udp-multicast-max-bps` (default `1_048_576` = 1 MiB/s — sensible default for radio links). All six are mirrored as `RUSTGATE_UDP_MULTICAST_*` env vars and as the matching kebab-case keys in the TOML config file. **(4) New audit events.** `audit::udp_multicast_joined(group, interface)` fires once per successful `join_multicast_v4` so SIEM operators can confirm the server is participating in the mesh and alert on absence at startup; `audit::udp_multicast_publish(group, msg_uid)` fires once per outbound datagram on the rebroadcast path so a chain-of-custody trail exists for tactical exfil monitoring. Both string fields cross the audit boundary via `sanitize_for_log` per the workspace audit-boundary discipline (#1197 / #1220) — an attacker-controlled CoT `uid` or operator-supplied interface name cannot log-forge a record. **(5) Tests.** Seven integration tests in `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/udp_multicast.rs` cover the contract end-to-end: `udp_multicast_join_on_default_group` (bind + join + sibling-socket send + listener receives), `udp_multicast_dispatches_through_router` (registered subscriber actually observes the routed message), `udp_multicast_source_protocol_stamped_correctly` (`metadata.source_protocol == "udp-multicast"`), `udp_multicast_rebroadcast_emits_to_configured_group` (opt-in flag + `set_on_multicast_forward` + sibling sniffer captures egress bytes), `udp_multicast_rate_limit_caps_outbound_bps` (200 B/s cap on a 30-message burst drops at least one datagram), `udp_multicast_audit_join_event_fires` (dedicated tracing subscriber observes `udp_multicast.joined` with the correct group), and `udp_multicast_disabled_by_default` (empty groups ⇒ no listener tasks spawned). The six live-network tests are gated `#[cfg_attr(not(target_os = "linux"), ignore)]` because some CI runners disable IPv4 multicast on `lo`; `udp_multicast_disabled_by_default` is the always-on baseline that pins the no-op path. Eleven unit tests in the module cover the `MulticastGroup` parser (rejects unicast, IPv6, garbage; round-trips valid forms), config defaults (disabled by default; honours `enabled()` invariant; default TTL/BPS), `looks_like_cot_xml` shape detector, and `extract_uid` bounded-scan invariants. Four audit-shape tests in `rustgate_core::audit::tests` pin the JSON wire format SIEM rules key on (`udp_multicast_joined_emits_documented_shape`, `udp_multicast_joined_sanitizes_interface_field`, `udp_multicast_publish_emits_documented_shape`, `udp_multicast_publish_sanitizes_uid_field`). **(6) Out of scope.** IPv6 multicast (`join_multicast_v6` etc.), source-specific multicast (SSM), and multicast routing across subnets are deferred — the operator's network handles cross-subnet routing, and the v1 surface targets the IPv4 administratively-scoped (`224.0.0.0/4`) tactical fabric. Closes #861.

- **Management REST API: `GET /api/v1/cert-status` and `POST /api/v1/clients/{cn}/disconnect` (closes #902)** — completes the four-endpoint umbrella tracked under #902. The CRL passthrough (`GET /api/v1/crl`) and the operator-facing dedup counters (`GET /api/v1/dedup/stats`) shipped via #1273; this PR adds the remaining cert-status read endpoint and the v1 force-disconnect write endpoint, both bearer-token authenticated through the existing `MgmtApiState` plumbing on the metrics HTTP server. **(1) `GET /api/v1/cert-status`.** Returns the server's own leaf certificate validity snapshot — `subject_cn`, `issuer_cn`, `serial` (lowercase hex, leading zero bytes preserved, matches the format used by `rustgate_transport::extract::cert_serial` and the `rustgate-server cert-info` CLI), `not_before` / `not_after` in RFC 3339, `days_remaining` as a saturating signed integer (negative for expired certs), `fingerprint_sha256` over the full DER (lowercase hex, 64 chars, the same fingerprint rustls reports and certificate-pinning code compares against), and the `expiring_soon` / `expired` boolean flags so dashboards can alert without doing arithmetic on the date strings. The `expiring_soon` flag fires when `days_remaining < 30` (mirrors the standard `cert-manager` warning window) and is saturating: an already-expired cert satisfies `expiring_soon: true` because zero-or-negative days left is, definitionally, less than thirty — dashboards do not need to OR the two flags. Status code matrix: `200 OK` with the JSON envelope when the cert reloader has a live leaf and the DER parses cleanly; `404 Not Found` when no certificate reloader is configured (the rare plaintext-only deployment path — distinct from `503` so operators can scrape unconditionally and distinguish "off by design" from "configured-but-unhealthy"); `503 Service Unavailable` when a reloader was configured but currently has no certified key (mid-rotation race) or the leaf chain is empty; `500 Internal Server Error` if the DER fails to parse. Successful access fires `audit::mgmt_api_accessed("/api/v1/cert-status", "bearer")` so the operator trail matches every other `/api/v1/*` read endpoint. The legacy unversioned `GET /api/cert/status` (added pre-#902) keeps its existing shape — operators on the legacy contract can continue scraping it until they migrate to v1. **(2) `POST /api/v1/clients/{cn}/disconnect`.** Force-closes any active session for the given CN and emits a structured audit record. Response is `{"data": {"sessions_closed": N}}` — currently `0` or `1` because the router holds at most one `SessionHandle` per CN, but the field is a `u64` on the wire so a future per-CN multi-session model (multiple concurrent connections from the same identity) is not a breaking response-shape change. Status code matrix: `200 OK` with the count regardless of whether `N` is zero (`0` is a normal, not-exceptional state for the endpoint — the operator may have scripted a batch disconnect against a stale CN list, and the audit record still fires); `400 Bad Request` for an empty CN segment (`/api/v1/clients//disconnect`) so the handler short-circuits with a precise diagnostic instead of falling into the router with a misleading `0`; `405 Method Not Allowed` for verbs other than POST; `401 Unauthorized` is enforced by the outer `handle_request` guard before the handler runs. The legacy unversioned `POST /api/clients/{cn}/disconnect` (added pre-#902) keeps its `disconnected: bool` shape and does NOT emit the new audit event — only the v1 path is wired into `client_force_disconnected`. **(3) New audit event: `client.force_disconnected`.** New helper `rustgate_core::audit::client_force_disconnected(cn, by_operator, sessions_closed)` emits a structured audit record with `event_type = "client.force_disconnected"`, `action = "force_disconnect"`, `result = "success"`, plus the three documented fields. `cn` and `by_operator` are sanitized at the audit boundary via `sanitize_for_log` per the workspace audit-boundary discipline (#1197 / #1220) — an attacker-controlled CN with embedded CR/LF cannot log-forge a fake force-disconnect record. `by_operator` is currently the literal `"bearer"` because the metrics HTTP server fronting the management API uses bearer-token auth, not mTLS, so there is no caller CN to record; the field shape is retained as `&str` so a future mTLS-fronted variant can populate the actual peer principal without a breaking audit-shape change. The event pairs with the pre-existing `client.disconnected` for full lifecycle coverage: the session task itself emits `client.disconnected` on its exit path (driven by the writer-channel drop forced here), so a SIEM can join the operator action with the eventual session teardown via the `cn` field. **(4) Tests.** Twelve new tests across three layers pin the contract end-to-end. In `crates/rustgate-server/src/mgmt_api.rs`: `build_v1_cert_status_returns_documented_fields_for_fresh_server_cert` (parser smoke, asserts every documented field is populated and the fingerprint is exactly 64 hex chars), `build_v1_cert_status_flags_expiring_soon_at_30_day_threshold` (7-day cert satisfies `expiring_soon: true` and `expired: false`), `build_v1_cert_status_flags_expired_for_past_cert` (past-dated cert satisfies `expired: true`, `expiring_soon: true`, and non-positive `days_remaining`), `mgmt_v1_cert_status_returns_404_when_no_reloader_configured` (plaintext-only deployment 404 path), `mgmt_v1_cert_status_wrong_method_returns_405`, `mgmt_v1_cert_status_requires_auth`, `mgmt_v1_disconnect_unknown_cn_returns_zero_count`, `mgmt_v1_disconnect_wrong_method_returns_405`, `mgmt_v1_disconnect_empty_cn_returns_400`, `mgmt_v1_disconnect_requires_auth`, `mgmt_v1_endpoints_require_auth_for_new_endpoints` (extends the legacy auth-boundary test), `mgmt_v1_disconnect_terminates_active_session` (registers a real `SessionHandle` in the `Router` and confirms the v1 endpoint reports `sessions_closed: 1` AND clears the writer-channel slots — the latter is load-bearing because a regression that returned `1` without signalling the channels would slip past a body-only inspection), and `mgmt_v1_disconnect_endpoint_reaches_audit_emission` (smoke-tests that the route reaches the audit emission without panicking). In `crates/rustgate-server/tests/mgmt_api_audit.rs`: `client_force_disconnected_emits_pinned_audit_shape` pins the wire format SIEM rules key on (`event_type`, `cn`, `by_operator`, numeric `sessions_closed`, `action`, `result`). In `crates/rustgate-core/src/audit.rs`: `test_client_force_disconnected` smoke-tests every documented call shape (including the `0` count edge-case and oversize boundary), `client_force_disconnected_emits_documented_shape` pins the JSON wire format end-to-end through the audit subscriber, and `client_force_disconnected_sanitizes_cn_and_by_operator` pins the log-forging defence (CR/LF and ANSI CSI in either field replaced with U+FFFD; the captured snapshot must contain the record on exactly one logical line). **(5) Out of scope.** Restructuring the management HTTP framework, new auth schemes, per-tenant management endpoints. Closes #902.

- **`dump-state` and `crl-info` diagnostic CLI subcommands (closes #900, completes the umbrella alongside the parallel test-connection / generate-config PR)** — finishes the six-subcommand operator tooling tracked under #900: `cert-info` and `check-cert-expiry` shipped via #1271; `test-connection` and `generate-config` ship in a parallel PR; this PR lands the remaining two. **(1) `rustgate dump-state --config <PATH> [--format json|toml] [--output PATH]`** captures an offline diagnostic snapshot of a running server's locally observable state for forensics and bug reports. It runs against the same `--config` the live server consumes, never opens a listener, never connects to a remote endpoint, and never reads private key material. The snapshot embeds: `rustgate_version` (compile-time `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`), an RFC 3339 UTC `generated_at` timestamp, the merged effective `config` with secrets redacted, an explicit `redacted_fields` array surfacing exactly which fields were scrubbed (so an operator double-checking before sending the snapshot to a third party can confirm), an embedded `crl_info::CrlReport` when `--crl` is configured, and an `audit_log` section carrying up to the last 100 entries from the configured audit log (lines that fail to parse as JSON are wrapped in `{ raw: "<line>" }` so corruption is visible rather than silently dropped). Redaction is layered: the existing `enrollment_password` `serialize_with` redactor in `Cli` flows through unchanged, and a second pass scrubs any non-empty value at one of nine known-secret-path keys (`key`, `ca-key`, `nats-credentials`, `nats-tls-key`, `metrics-token-file`, `acl-api-token-file`, `mgmt-api-token-file`, `archive-key-file`, `client-queue-key-file`) — the conservative default per the F-149 / #900 review notes is "when in doubt, redact". `--format toml` round-trips the same `Snapshot` struct through `serde_json::Value` → `toml::Value` so both forms expose identical top-level keys. `--output PATH` writes the snapshot with mode `0o600` on Unix (owner-only); on Windows the permission tightener is a no-op and the file inherits the default ACL — the snapshot is redacted by construction so a slightly looser POSIX permission is treated as defense-in-depth, not a security boundary. **(2) `rustgate crl-info <FILE> [--json]` exit-code contract.** `crl-info` shipped as a viewer in #1271; this PR formalises the operator-facing exit-code ladder advertised in the issue: `0` = parsed cleanly with `nextUpdate` in the future (or absent), `1` = malformed PEM / no X.509 CRL block (surfaced via `?` in `main.rs`), `2` = `nextUpdate` already in the past (CRL stale; operator should refresh). The stale signal is in-band (`Ok(2)` from `run`) because the CRL still parses cleanly — operators reading the report fields care about the same shape regardless of staleness. **(3) Wiring.** New module `crates/rustgate-server/src/diagnostics/dump_state.rs` follows the same self-contained pattern as the other diagnostic modules: synthetic `argv = ["rustgate", "--config", PATH]` is fed to `Cli::command().try_get_matches_from(...)`, the parser succeeds because `--cert/--key/--ca` carry `required_unless_present_any = ["config", "spiffe"]`, and `ConfigFile::apply_to` overlays the file's values onto the defaults — so the snapshot reflects the same merged view the running server would consume from CLI + env + file precedence. Dispatch lives next to the existing diagnostic arms in `main.rs`; `subcommand_negates_reqs = true` already in place from #1271 keeps the dump-state UX clean (no dummy TLS paths required to invoke it). **(4) Tests.** Ten unit tests in `crates/rustgate-server/src/diagnostics/dump_state.rs` cover the structured-data shape (version + timestamp, redaction of known secret-path fields, audit-log absence handling, audit-log tail with mixed parsed/raw entries, audit-tail capacity capping at `AUDIT_TAIL_MAX_LINES = 100`, embedded CRL report for a configured `--crl`, JSON round-trip, TOML round-trip, owner-only file permissions on Unix, missing-config-file error path). Eight integration tests in `crates/rustgate-server/tests/cli_dump_state.rs` pin the binary surface end-to-end (`dump_state_emits_valid_json_with_required_keys`, `dump_state_redacts_secret_fields` — verifies literal secret values are absent from stdout AND that `redacted_fields` lists each scrubbed key, `dump_state_format_toml_emits_valid_toml`, `dump_state_to_file_writes_then_reads` plus the Unix `0o600` permission check, `crl_info_prints_issuer_and_revoked_count`, `crl_info_returns_2_for_stale_crl`, `crl_info_handles_malformed_pem_gracefully` (also asserts no `panicked at` on stderr — operators running this from cron rely on a clean error stream), `crl_info_json_format_is_valid_json`). The integration runner scrubs every `RUSTGATE_*` env var before spawning the binary so a developer machine that exports e.g. `RUSTGATE_AUDIT_LOG=/tmp/x.log` does not inject unrelated state into the snapshot. **(5) Out of scope.** A live HTTP API for dump-state — the management API (`/api/cert/status`, `/api/crl/status`, `/api/dedup/stats` shipped via #1273) already covers the on-the-wire diagnostic story for a running server; dump-state is the offline / forensic complement. Real-time streaming dump-state and per-connection snapshot detail are deferred. Closes #900.
- **Per-recipient delivery audit events with `--audit-delivery` opt-in (closes #854)** — adds two new structured audit events, `message.delivered` and `message.dropped`, that fire once per recipient on every routed message when the operator enables `--audit-delivery` / `RUSTGATE_AUDIT_DELIVERY=true` (default off because per-recipient audit is high-volume in busy deployments). The pre-existing audit family had 28+ event types covering connection lifecycle, federation, enrollment, authorization, and obligation actuation, but no per-recipient delivery confirmation — for classified-traffic chain-of-custody, operators need a forensic record of exactly which CN received exactly which `uid` exactly when, and a paired drop record when delivery fails. **(1) New audit helpers in `rustgate-core::audit`.** `message_delivered(source_cn, dest_cn, msg_uid, msg_type, group)` emits an event with `event_type = "message.delivered"`, `action = "deliver"`, `result = "success"`, and the five string fields documented above; `message_dropped(source_cn, dest_cn, msg_uid, reason)` emits `event_type = "message.dropped"`, `action = "deliver"`, `result = "dropped"` with a small fixed-vocabulary `reason` token (`"backpressure"` for channel-full / channel-closed, `"no_subscribers"` for an offline recipient with no store-and-forward queue). Every `&str` argument is sanitized at the audit boundary via `rustgate_core::sanitize::sanitize_for_log` per the workspace audit-boundary discipline (#1197 / #1220) — an attacker-controlled CN with embedded CR/LF cannot log-forge a fake delivery record. CNs are recorded **raw** (not via `hash_cn`) per #1207 / #1221: the audit log is a forensic chain of custody that must support filtering by raw CN at SIEM-query time, while the lower-cardinality access-log keeps using `hash_cn`. **(2) New router callbacks.** `OnMessageDelivered = Arc<dyn Fn(&str, &str, &str, &str, &str) + Send + Sync>` and `OnMessageDropped = Arc<dyn Fn(&str, &str, &str, &str) + Send + Sync>` (declared via `rustgate_core::on_callback!`) sit alongside the existing `OnFanout` / `OnDropped` / `OnPepDecision` slots on `Router`, hot-reloadable via `ArcSwap` so the audit layer can be installed and replaced after construction without a lock on the routing hot path. The setters `Router::set_on_message_delivered` / `Router::set_on_message_dropped` follow the same shape as the pre-existing per-fanout / per-PEP setters. **(3) Wired into every per-recipient `try_send` path in `Router`.** `send_to_session` (Direct), `send_to_group` (Group), `send_to_all` (Broadcast), and `send_to_group_excluding` (Multicast) each call the helpers `emit_message_delivered` / `emit_message_dropped` after the matching `try_send` outcome. The two helpers share an `ArcSwap::load` + `is_none()` short-circuit on the un-installed default path, so the routing hot-path cost when `--audit-delivery` is unset is exactly one atomic load + one nullable check per recipient — no allocation. When the slot is installed, each delivery pays one bounded `extract_cot_uid` scan over the payload prefix and one `MessageType::Display` allocation. **(4) New CLI flag and TOML key.** `--audit-delivery` (alias `RUSTGATE_AUDIT_DELIVERY`, default false) and `audit-delivery` in `rustgate.toml` are added under the existing `-- Observability --` block in `cli.rs`; the `define_config_file!` macro entry keeps the `Cli` ↔ `ConfigFile` 1:1 mapping. The flag is wired in `main.rs` next to the other router observability callbacks: when set, the binary installs callbacks that thread to `rustgate_core::audit::message_delivered` / `message_dropped`; when unset, the slots stay `None`. **(5) Documentation.** `docs/authorization.md` gains a new "Per-recipient delivery audit (`--audit-delivery`)" subsection under the obligation-dispatcher audit-events block, naming the two new events, their full field set, the volume implications (a broadcast to N subscribers produces N records — non-trivial on busy tactical links), the PII discipline (raw CNs for chain-of-custody; sanitization at the audit boundary), the performance contract (un-installed: one `ArcSwap::load` + `is_none` per recipient; installed: one bounded scan + one allocation), the four destination paths the events fire on, and SIEM correlation patterns ("did recipient X actually receive this classified message?" via uid join with `authz.classified_delivery`; "which recipients lost messages this hour?" filtered to `reason in [backpressure, no_subscribers]`). **(6) Tests.** Five integration tests in `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/delivery_audit.rs` pin the per-recipient contract: `message_delivered_audit_fires_when_callback_set` (single direct recipient, callback fires once with correct fields including `msg_type = "chat"` and `group = "direct"`), `message_delivered_audit_does_not_fire_when_callback_unset` (default + revoke path is silent), `message_dropped_audit_fires_on_send_failure` (saturated channel, callback fires with `reason = "backpressure"` and the dropped uid scraped from payload), `audit_callbacks_propagate_per_recipient_for_multicast` (multicast across two groups of five recipients, callback fires exactly five times with five distinct dest CNs and the per-recipient group label preserved), `audit_event_fields_are_sanitized` (CN with embedded CR/LF goes through the audit boundary; the captured JSON shows U+FFFD replacement, no raw newline, and the static `action`/`result` tokens are stable). Two integration tests in `crates/rustgate-server/tests/audit_delivery_wiring.rs` mirror the `--audit-delivery` arms: `audit_delivery_cli_flag_wires_callbacks` (server-side wiring path emits `message.delivered` end-to-end through the audit subscriber) and `audit_delivery_cli_flag_unset_leaves_callbacks_silent` (default arm produces no audit records). Two CLI parsing tests in `cli.rs::tests` (`cli_audit_delivery_defaults_false`, `cli_audit_delivery_opt_in`) pin the flag's parser contract. Boundary smoke tests and explicit sanitization tests in `rustgate-core::audit::tests` (`test_message_delivered_smoke`, `test_message_dropped_smoke`, `message_delivered_emits_documented_shape`, `message_delivered_sanitizes_cn_with_log_forging`, `message_dropped_emits_documented_shape`, `message_dropped_sanitizes_reason_field`) pin the wire shape of every documented call site so a future refactor that drops a field, reorders arguments, or skips sanitization fails the build. **(7) Out of scope.** Configurable audit-field redaction, per-tenant audit policies, real-time audit streaming, and hash-chained delivery audits to a separate file are explicitly deferred — the audit log already supports hash chaining via `rustgate_core::audit_chain::HashChainWriter` when `--audit-log` is configured, and that chain covers the new events alongside the existing 28+ types. Closes #854.
- **NATS poison-message dead-letter handling with structured audit emission (refs #883 sub-item 3)** — closes the third sub-item of the poison-message gap called out in #883: pre-this-PR the NATS subscriber silently ACKed four classes of local-drop traffic (`oversized`, `unparseable`, `unknown-position`, `invalid-identity`) with no audit record, so a SIEM operator had no way to distinguish "consumer is healthy" from "consumer is burning a poison message every redelivery interval". This PR adds the `nats.poison_dlq` structured audit event and bumps the default `max_deliver` cap so the JetStream pull consumer gives up after a bounded number of redelivery attempts on the panic edge-case (handler dies between receive and ACK). **(1)** `rustgate_core::audit::nats_poison_message_dlq(subject, msg_id, reason, attempts)` is the new event helper — `event_type = "nats.poison_dlq"`, `action = "dead_letter"`, `result = "moved"`. Every `&str` field crosses the audit boundary via `sanitize_for_log` so an attacker who can publish to the live stream cannot forge a log line through the original subject. `attempts` is numeric so SIEM rules can do numeric comparisons without parsing. **(2)** `NatsSubscriber::handle_poison_message` (renamed from `publish_dead_letter`) now fires the audit event on every drop path, regardless of whether the optional `dead_letter_subject` is wired — the audit trail is the security record; the DLQ subject is the forensic-payload sink. The DLQ publish remains opt-in, best-effort, and unchanged in wire format (`X-Rustgate-DLQ-Reason` / `X-Rustgate-DLQ-Original-Subject` / `X-Rustgate-DLQ-Timestamp` headers, original payload byte-for-byte). **(3)** `NatsSubscriber::handle_poison_message` now extracts `(msg_id, attempts)` from `async_nats::jetstream::Message::info()` — `msg_id` is the JetStream stream sequence rendered as a decimal string (the canonical correlation token a forensic operator uses to point JetStream's `nats consumer` admin tooling at the exact stuck record); `attempts` is `info.delivered` saturating-cast to `u32`. A failed `info()` call falls back to `("unknown", 0)` so the audit emission is not gated on JetStream availability. **(4)** `NatsConfig::max_deliver` default flips from `0` (JetStream "unlimited" sentinel) to `5` (the workspace poison-message handling standard). Operators who need the pre-#883 unlimited-redelivery semantics back must set the field explicitly to `0` (or any non-positive value) — the legacy-compat escape hatch is documented in the field's rustdoc, the new `--nats-max-deliver` default in `rustgate-server`, and the CLI flag's help text. This is a deliberate, documented behaviour change for upgraded deployments: a persistently-failing message will now be ACKed (and audit-emitted) after five attempts instead of redelivering forever. **(5)** New CLI flag `--nats-dead-letter-subject` / env var `RUSTGATE_NATS_DEAD_LETTER_SUBJECT` on `rustgate-server` wires the optional DLQ subject through the same `define_config_file!` TOML overlay as the existing NATS knobs. The JSON config schema (`schemas/rustgate-v0.8.json`) gains a `nats-dead-letter-subject` property. **(6) Tests.** `crates/rustgate-core/src/audit.rs` adds three tests: `test_nats_poison_message_dlq` (smoke-tests the four drop-path slugs plus boundary shapes), `audit_nats_poison_message_dlq_emits_documented_shape` (pins the JSON wire format SIEM rules key on — `event_type`, `action`, `result`, `subject`, `msg_id`, `reason`, numeric `attempts`), and `audit_nats_poison_message_dlq_sanitizes_subject_msg_id_and_reason` (pins log-forging defence on every `&str` field crossing the audit boundary). `crates/rustgate-nats/src/config.rs` adds `default_max_deliver_is_five_for_poison_handling` and `explicit_zero_max_deliver_opts_into_legacy_unlimited`; the pre-existing `default_max_deliver_is_unlimited_sentinel` is updated to reflect the new default. `crates/rustgate-nats/src/subscriber.rs` adds `build_consumer_config_default_max_deliver_is_workspace_poison_cap` and `build_consumer_config_explicit_zero_max_deliver_passes_through`. `crates/rustgate-nats/tests/integration.rs` adds five new integration tests against a live `nats-server`: `nats_subscriber_default_max_deliver_is_five_in_jetstream` (verifies the new default reaches a real JetStream consumer's config via `consumer.info()`), `nats_subscriber_explicit_zero_max_deliver_is_unlimited_in_jetstream` (verifies the legacy-compat escape hatch round-trips into JetStream), `nats_subscriber_default_5_attempts_does_not_break_happy_path` (well-formed traffic still ACKed under the new default), `nats_subscriber_acks_after_max_delivery_attempts_to_break_redelivery_loop` (drives a manual JetStream consumer with `max_deliver = 3`, never ACKs, asserts redelivery stops at three exactly — the panic-edge-case proof), `nats_poison_message_dlq_audit_event_fires` (captures the audit-target tracing output via a custom `tracing_subscriber::Layer` and asserts the event fires once per poison drop with `subject = "points.AUDIT"` / `reason = "unparseable"`), and `nats_subscriber_dead_letter_payload_includes_original_subject_and_attempts` (pins the JetStream-derived `msg_id` and `attempts` fields on the audit event). The pre-existing `dead_letter_publishes_unparseable_payload` and `no_dead_letter_when_subject_not_configured` tests are unchanged. **(7) Out of scope.** Sub-item 4 of #883 (per-tenant token bucket on the NATS publisher) ships in a separate future PR. Sub-items 1 + 2 (encrypted-archive KDF + key expiration; audit-chain sequence numbers) already shipped via #1251 and #1268 respectively. Refs #883.

- **Golden Grafana overview dashboard JSON (closes #771, completes the issue together with the metrics extension shipped via #1267)** — adds `dashboards/rustgate-overview.json`, a Grafana 10.x dashboard (`schemaVersion = 38`) that an operator imports directly into a Grafana instance pointing at the workspace's Prometheus `/metrics` endpoint. The dashboard ships 38 panels organised into six rows — `System overview` (build info, total active connections across all transports, federation peer count, server cert expiry days), `Throughput` (messages-per-second by protocol stacked from `rustgate_mqtt_publishes_total` / `rustgate_nats_publishes_total` / `rustgate_ws_messages_total` / `rustgate_federation_messages_in_total` + `_out_total` / `rustgate_http_publishes_total`, bytes-per-second from `rustgate_per_identity_bytes_received_total` and `_sent_total`, messages routed by destination, CoT parse rate by `result`), `Authorization and latency` (decisions stacked by `decision`, engine evaluations, cache hit ratio over 5m, in-flight gauge, `rustgate_authz_evaluation_seconds_bucket` p50/p95/p99 via `histogram_quantile`, obligations emitted by type), `Federation` (in/out/dropped/ttl, circuit-breaker trips and recoveries per minute, reconnects per minute, per-peer queue bytes and EWMA latency filtered by the `peer` template variable, replay-buffer bytes on disk), `Resilience and queues` (global backpressure queued bytes, top-10 store-and-forward depth per CN, enqueue/drain/drop/expired rates, dedup hit ratio over 5m, position cache size, router drops by reason, tenant quota rejections per minute filtered by the `tenant` template variable, enrollment rate-limit triggers per minute), and `TLS and cert health` (handshake failures by reason, TLS handshake duration p50/p95/p99 from `rustgate_tls_handshake_duration_seconds_bucket`, OCSP cache hit ratio, CRL age in seconds with one-day and seven-day thresholds, reload rollbacks by subsystem, SPIFFE SVID refresh by outcome, SVID notAfter, recent negotiation outcomes). Three template variables drive the per-peer and per-tenant filtering: `DS_PROMETHEUS` (Prometheus datasource picker), `peer` (multi-select with `All`, populated from `rustgate_federation_peer_queue_bytes`), and `tenant` (multi-select with `All`, populated from `rustgate_tenant_quota_rejections_total`). The dashboard uses the UID `rustgate-overview-golden` so it coexists without import conflicts with the smaller historic SRE-rotation dashboard at `ops/grafana/dashboards/rustgate-overview.json` (UID `rustgate-overview`). **Spec items dropped because the underlying metric does not exist in the workspace.** The original issue mentioned a `process_start_time_seconds` uptime stat (the Prometheus process collector is not wired into the rustgate exporter — replaced with a `rustgate_build_info` stat that pins the active version label), `rustgate_federation_peers_connected` (the actual gauge is `rustgate_federation_connections` — used directly), `rustgate_federation_circuit_state{peer}` (no per-peer state metric exists today; replaced with `rustgate_federation_circuit_breaker_trips_total` and `_recoveries_total` rates), `rustgate_jwks_refresh_*` (no JWKS refresh metric — panel dropped), `rustgate_rate_limit_rejected_total` (the only rate-limiter counter is `rustgate_enrollment_rate_limited_total` — used), `rustgate_tls_handshake_failed_total` (the actual counter is `rustgate_handshake_failures_total` — used), and a histogram-style cert expiry distribution (`rustgate_cert_expiry_seconds` is a single gauge, not a per-cert distribution — rendered as a stat with red/orange/green thresholds). Each surviving panel references at least one metric defined in `crates/*/src/metrics.rs`, and the validation test below pins that contract. **Validation.** `crates/rustgate-server/tests/grafana_dashboard.rs` ships five integration tests: `dashboard_is_valid_json_with_required_top_level_keys` (asserts the eight Grafana-required top-level keys are present and that `schemaVersion >= 30`), `dashboard_has_a_meaningful_number_of_panels` (asserts at least 12 top-level panels and 10 non-row panels — guards against accidental panel deletion), `dashboard_templating_includes_datasource_and_peer_variables` (pins `DS_PROMETHEUS` + `peer` template variables), `every_referenced_metric_exists_in_the_codebase` (walks every `targets[].expr`, extracts every `rustgate_*` token, strips the histogram suffixes `_bucket` / `_sum` / `_count`, and asserts each name is also defined as a `"rustgate_..."` string literal in some `crates/*/src/metrics.rs` — the production source-of-truth scan covers all 56 referenced names against the 139 defined names so a metric removal that forgets the dashboard fails fast), `every_panel_target_expression_has_balanced_parens_and_quotes` (a syntactic floor for PromQL expressions). The integration test depends only on `serde_json` (already a dev-dep via the main-deps inheritance) so no workspace-deps change is required. **`dashboards/README.md`** documents the import flow (Grafana UI → Dashboards → New → Import → upload JSON → pick datasource), the provisioning flow (drop into `/etc/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/`), the templating-variable contract, the layout (ASCII art of the panel grid), and the maintenance contract (re-run `python3 -m json.tool < ... > /dev/null` and the `cargo nextest run -p rustgate-server --test grafana_dashboard` validation). No production code paths touched, no metrics added, no metrics renamed. The metrics-extension half of #771 shipped via #1267 (per-crate `metrics` modules in authz / cot / mqtt / websocket / proto); this PR completes the issue. Closes #771.

### Changed

- **Extracted `rustgate-router` crate from `rustgate-transport` (closes #888)** — relocated the routing engine and its tightly coupled support modules into a dedicated workspace crate so the routing-graph hot path evolves independently from byte-level codecs and UDP I/O. Twelve files moved with `git mv` so blame is preserved: `crates/rustgate-transport/src/{router,acl,cache,dedup,store_forward,filter,replay,repeater,obligations,quota,throttle,egress}.rs` → `crates/rustgate-router/src/`. `egress.rs` moved alongside the routing engine because it is intrinsically coupled (calls `obligation_kind_label` and consumes `obligations::*` to render per-recipient envelopes); leaving it in `rustgate-transport` would have created a cyclic dep with the router. The `mod rustgate_transport_types` workaround in `udp.rs` was deleted in this PR — `udp.rs` and `udp_multicast.rs` now import `Router` / `SessionHandle` / `RoutedMessage` / `ReplayFilter` directly from `rustgate_router`. The `OnMulticastForward` callback typedef relocated to `rustgate_router::router` (transport re-exports it for source-level compatibility) so the router crate, which owns the `ArcSwap` hot-swap slot, can declare the type without a transport dep. Twenty-one routing-bound integration tests moved with `git mv`: `access_log`, `authz_evaluate_split`, `authz_reload_mid_request`, `authz_routing`, `cdi_obligations`, `classification_egress`, `delivery_audit`, `e2e_routing`, `egress_envelope`, `mask_point_recovery_audit`, `multicast_egress_pep`, `obligation_static_reason_audit`, `position_replay_rate_limit_audit`, `proptest_obligation_idempotence`, `router_auth`, `store_forward_authz`, `store_forward_drain_panic_audit`, `store_forward_dwell_audit`, `store_forward_obligation_after_offline`, `tenant_quota`, `tenant_token_bucket`. Two router-domain benches (`router_fanout`, `dedup_contention`) moved alongside; the codec bench stays in transport. Public API: `rustgate_router::{Router, SessionHandle, RoutedMessage, PendingDelivery, PendingAudit, AuthzEvent, AuthzObserver, OnFanout, OnDropped, OnPepDecision, OnObligationApplied, OnAuthzInFlightChanged, OnDuplicate, OnInsert, OnMessageDelivered, OnMessageDropped, OnMulticastForward, OnMulticastOversizeDropped, OnRoutedByKind, OnTenantThroughputConsumed, OnTenantThroughputRejection, OnDrainObservation, OnCacheSize, GroupAcl, GroupAclPolicy, PositionCache, PositionReplayLimitConfig, DedupCache, DedupStats, DEFAULT_DEDUP_MAX_ENTRIES, MessageFilter, GeoBounds, ReplayFilter, EmergencyRepeater, ClientQueue, QueueStats, StoreForwardError, DEFAULT_CLIENT_QUEUE_MAX_BYTES, TenantQuotaTracker, TenantQuota, TenantThroughputRejection, QuotaConfig, DEFAULT_TENANT_KEY, ClientThrottle, ThrottleConfig, EgressEnvelope, EgressError, RecipientClass, ACCESS_LOG_TARGET, NORMAL_CHANNEL_CAPACITY, PRIORITY_CHANNEL_CAPACITY}`. Consumer crates rewired to import the moved symbols directly from `rustgate_router::*` rather than through the legacy `rustgate_transport::*` re-exports: `rustgate-server` (main, setup, session, mgmt_api, metrics, authz_reloader), `rustgate-admin` (server, acl_api, acl_config, acl_reloader), `rustgate-federation`, `rustgate-mqtt` (config, lib, server, session), `rustgate-nats` (jetstream, subscriber), `rustgate-websocket` (server), `rustgate-client`, plus the integration test suites for each. `rustgate-transport` now declares `rustgate-router` as a prod dep (consumed by `udp.rs` / `udp_multicast.rs`) and drops `dashmap`, `smol_str`, `redb`, `serde_json`, `arc-swap`, `serde` (no longer used by what remains: codec / codecs / hw_identity / udp / udp_multicast). `rustgate-nats` / `rustgate-mqtt` / `rustgate-admin` drop their direct `rustgate-transport` dep (they only ever needed the router-bound symbols). Wire format unchanged: ACL group resolution, dedup cache hash construction, store-and-forward redb schema, position-cache TTL semantics, throttle token-bucket math, and tenant-quota CAS atomicity all behave identically. Workspace member added; `Cargo.toml`, `Dockerfile`, `deny.toml`, and the workspace `README.md` architecture table updated. Closes #888.

- **Extracted `rustgate-admin` crate from `rustgate-server` (closes #895)** — relocated the HTTP management server (Prometheus exposition, Kubernetes-style health/readiness probes, federation/mgmt/ACL REST APIs) into a dedicated workspace crate so the long-running microservice that fronts `/metrics` and the operator REST surface evolves independently from the Prometheus metric definitions themselves. Three files moved with `git mv` so blame is preserved: `crates/rustgate-server/src/acl_api.rs`, `acl_config.rs`, and `acl_reloader.rs` are now under `crates/rustgate-admin/src/`. The HTTP-server portion of `crates/rustgate-server/src/metrics.rs` (~789 LOC: `HealthState`, `ReadinessState`, `ReadinessReport`, `DependencyCheck`, `CheckStatus`, `RouterSlot`, `FedApiHandler`, `AclApiHandler`, `MgmtApiHandler`, `DEFAULT_MAX_HTTP_CONNECTIONS`, the `serve()` entrypoint, the request-routing dispatcher, the dependency-check helpers `check_tls_cert` / `check_nats` / `check_federation` / `check_http`, and the `cert_expiry_seconds` gauge that the readiness probe maintains as a side effect) moved alongside as `crates/rustgate-admin/src/server.rs`. The Prometheus metric *definitions* (≈130 metric statics, the `init()` ladder, fanout/PEP/obligation callbacks, MAVLink/SA-upgrade/jemalloc/per-identity bucketing, etc.) stay in `rustgate-server::metrics` because they are domain-specific and are wired from feature-gated call sites elsewhere in `rustgate-server`. Public API: `rustgate_admin::{HealthState, ReadinessState, ReadinessReport, DependencyCheck, CheckStatus, RouterSlot, AclApiHandler, MgmtApiHandler, DEFAULT_MAX_HTTP_CONNECTIONS, serve, init, register_metrics, cert_expiry_seconds, AclApiState, AclReloader, GroupAclFile, GroupAclEntry, validate_bearer_token_length}` plus feature-gated `FedApiHandler` (under `federation`). The optional `pre_scrape: Option<Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>>` field on `ReadinessState` lets the server orchestration wire the jemalloc stats refresh into the `/metrics` request path without expanding the `serve()` signature. The HTTP server portion of admin runs the existing `rustgate_metrics::MetricsRegistry` ladder via a new `rustgate_admin::init()` callback that registers `rustgate_cert_expiry_seconds` against the default Prometheus registry. Consumer crate `rustgate-server` rewired: `main.rs`, `setup.rs`, `mgmt_api.rs`, `authz_reloader.rs`, and `federation_reloader.rs` now reach into the moved types via `rustgate_admin::*` rather than the old `metrics::*` and `crate::acl_*::*` paths. Wire format unchanged: `/metrics` Prometheus text exposition, `/health/{live,ready,startup,authz}` and `/healthz`/`/readyz` legacy aliases, the `/api/{federation,acl,cert,crl,dedup,clients,dlq,v1,reload,drain}` REST routes, and the bearer-token auth shape are all byte-identical. Workspace member added; `Cargo.toml`, `Dockerfile`, `deny.toml`, and the workspace `README.md` architecture table updated. Closes #895.

- **Extracted `rustgate-tls` crate from `rustgate-transport` (closes #890)** — relocated TLS, certificate handling, OCSP stapling, SPIFFE workload identity, and TCP listener primitives into a dedicated workspace crate so the cross-cutting TLS feature matrix (`fips`, `post-quantum`, `ocsp`, `spiffe`) is scoped to a single crate and `rustgate-transport` can focus on routing, sessions, dedup, ACL, codecs, store-and-forward, throttling, and UDP — pure post-handshake transport. Eleven files moved with `git mv` so blame is preserved: `cert_reloader.rs`, `config.rs`, `verifier.rs`, `extract.rs`, `listener.rs`, `pem.rs`, `client_ocsp.rs`, `ocsp.rs`, `spiffe.rs`, `plaintext.rs`, and `session.rs` (post-handshake `AuthenticatedSession` / `SessionReader` / `SessionWriter`). Pure-TLS integration tests (`tls_listener`, `tls_security`, `tls_error_paths`, `crl`, `client_ocsp`, `fips`, `pq_kex`) stay in `rustgate-transport/tests/` since they exercise the `Router` + listener wiring end-to-end; they now import via `rustgate_tls::*`. Public API: `rustgate_tls::{TlsConfig, TlsMinVersion, TlsListener, OnHandshakeError, DEFAULT_MAX_HANDSHAKES, CertReloader, extract_identity, validate_key_usage, ExpectedKeyUsage, DynamicCertVerifier, RootStoreProvider, PlaintextListener, PlaintextIdentityConfig, PlaintextSession, AuthenticatedSession, SessionReader, SessionWriter, CrlFileSummary, check_crl_freshness, crl_max_age_seconds, is_fips_provider_active, is_pq_provider_active}` plus feature-gated `{ClientOcspVerifier, FetchFuture, OcspFetcher, OcspStaplerFetcher}` (under `ocsp`), `{install_fips_provider}` (under `fips`), `{install_pq_provider, install_provider_with_kx_groups}` (under `post-quantum`), and `{SpiffeConfig, SpiffeHooks, SpiffeIdentity}` (under `spiffe`). Consumer crates rewired: `rustgate-server` (acl_reloader, main, metrics, mgmt_api, session, setup), `rustgate-federation` (connector, manager, v1/server), `rustgate-mqtt` (config, listener, server), `rustgate-websocket` (lib, server), `rustgate-client` (e2e tests), and the `rustgate-transport` integration test suite (cert_rotation, chaos_cert_expiry_midflight, client_ocsp, crl, e2e_routing, fips, hw_identity, negative_expired_cert_mid_session, pq_kex, tls_error_paths, tls_listener, tls_security).
