Feature flags `fips`, `post-quantum`, `ocsp`, `spiffe` now live on `rustgate-tls`; `rustgate-transport` keeps thin passthrough features (`fips = ["rustgate-tls/fips"]` etc.) so existing transport-test gates (`#![cfg(feature = "fips")]`) compile unchanged. `rustls-pki-types`, `tokio-rustls`, `x509-parser`, `ocsp-stapler`, and `spiffe` are no longer direct deps of `rustgate-transport`. Wire format unchanged: TLS configs, certificate hot-reload semantics, OCSP cache state, SPIFFE SVID rotation, and plaintext-listener identity injection all behave identically — `rustgate-transport`'s router consumes the same `(stream, Identity)` tuple it always did. Workspace member added; `Dockerfile`, `deny.toml`, and the workspace `README.md` architecture table updated. Closes #890. Unblocks the `rustgate-router` extraction (#888).

- **Extracted `rustgate-metrics` crate for shared Prometheus scaffolding (closes #894, refs #794)** — relocated the `OnceLock` + `init()` + `fallback_*` boilerplate that the `rustgate-server`, `rustgate-federation`, and `rustgate-http` metrics modules had previously copied independently (and which #794 had partially consolidated under `rustgate_core::metrics_util`) into a dedicated `rustgate-metrics` workspace crate. The metric instances themselves stay in their domain crates — `rustgate_federation::metrics::peer_latency` is still federation-domain code; only the scaffolding moved. **(1) New crate `crates/rustgate-metrics`** depends on `prometheus` and nothing else (no `rustgate-core` dep). Public surface: `fallback_counter`, `fallback_gauge`, `fallback_counter_vec`, `fallback_gauge_vec`, `fallback_histogram`, `fallback_histogram_vec` (six `OnceLock`-fallback constructors); `standard_duration_buckets()` returning `[1ms, 5ms, 10ms, 25ms, 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2.5s, 5s, 10s]` and `standard_byte_size_buckets()` returning `[64B, 256B, 1KiB, 4KiB, 16KiB, 64KiB, 256KiB, 1MiB, 4MiB, 16MiB]`; and `MetricsRegistry`, a thin orchestration helper (`register(...).register(...).init_all()?`) that aggregates every domain crate's `init()` callback into one ordered list. Insertion order is preserved and the first error short-circuits, matching the historical hardcoded `init_a()?; init_b()?;` sequence. **(2) Consumer crates migrated.** Nine domain crates' `metrics` features previously declared `rustgate-core/metrics`; they now declare `dep:rustgate-metrics` and import from `rustgate_metrics::*`: `rustgate-server`, `rustgate-federation`, `rustgate-http`, `rustgate-authz`, `rustgate-cot`, `rustgate-mqtt`, `rustgate-websocket`, `rustgate-proto`, `rustgate-guard`. **(3) `rustgate-core` dropped its `metrics` feature.** With every consumer migrated, `rustgate_core::metrics_util` and the corresponding `prometheus` optional dep were deleted; `rustgate-core` no longer carries a `metrics` feature gate. Downstream non-metrics crates that link `rustgate-core` no longer inherit the optional `prometheus` cfg. **(4) Wire format unchanged.** Prometheus text exposition (the `/metrics` endpoint output) is byte-identical before and after — every metric name, help string, label set, and bucket boundary is preserved. The `init()` ordering inside each consumer crate's `init()` body is unchanged, so any test that depends on registration order still passes. **(5) Tests.** Thirteen new unit tests in `crates/rustgate-metrics/src` pin the helper contracts: per-helper construction without `init()`, per-label-combination independence for vec helpers, signed-write behaviour for gauges, observation count + sum for histograms, the documented bucket values for both standard-bucket helpers, and a `Registry::register` smoke test verifying a fallback-built counter shows up in `Registry::gather()`. The `MetricsRegistry` aggregator pins (a) `init_all` runs registered closures in insertion order, (b) the first error propagates and short-circuits subsequent initialisers, (c) `Default + register + len + is_empty + Debug` shape, and (d) the empty-registry path is `Ok(())`. The 5,655 existing workspace tests continue to pass without modification. **(6) Documentation.** New `crates/rustgate-metrics/README.md` (per the per-crate README pattern from #1246), workspace `README.md` architecture-table row added, `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `[Unreleased] / ### Changed` (refactor with no behaviour change). Subsumes the original #794 deliverable. Closes #894, refs #794.

- **Extracted `rustgate-archive` crate from `rustgate-core` and `rustgate-server` (closes #892)** — relocated ~6.4K LOC of crypto + audit-chain code into a dedicated workspace crate so consumers update import paths only. Four files moved with `git mv` so blame is preserved: `crates/rustgate-core/src/encrypted.rs` → `crates/rustgate-archive/src/encrypted.rs` (`KeyRing`, `EncryptedWriter`, `SharedEncryptedWriter`, `decrypt_file`, `KeyFile`, `Derivation`, Argon2/HKDF derivation paths); `crates/rustgate-core/src/audit_chain.rs` → `crates/rustgate-archive/src/audit_chain.rs` (`HashChainWriter`, `verify_audit_log`, `read_chain_tip`, `write_anchor`, `read_anchor_with_seq`, `write_anchor_with_seq`, `check_chain_continuity`); `crates/rustgate-server/src/archive.rs` → `crates/rustgate-archive/src/archive.rs` (`CotArchiver`); `crates/rustgate-server/src/archive_rotation.rs` → `crates/rustgate-archive/src/archive_rotation.rs` (`RotationConfig`, `RotationStats`). The integration-test binary `crates/rustgate-core/tests/audit_chain_ci.rs` (#772) moved alongside to `crates/rustgate-archive/tests/audit_chain_ci.rs`. `rustgate-core` no longer depends on `chacha20poly1305`, `argon2`, `hkdf`, or `arc-swap`; downstream crates that did not use the moved modules (`rustgate-cot`, `rustgate-authz`, `rustgate-transport`, `rustgate-federation`, `rustgate-mqtt`, `rustgate-websocket`, `rustgate-nats`, `rustgate-enrollment`, `rustgate-mavlink`, `rustgate-asterix`, `rustgate-stanag4586`, `rustgate-resilience`, `rustgate-client`, `rustgate-proto`, `rustgate-test-utils`) stop paying that transitive compile cost. Consumer crates updated: `rustgate-server` (main.rs, session.rs, setup.rs), `rustgate-http` (dlq.rs, dlq_reader.rs, publisher.rs, dlq_drain_integration.rs), and `rustgate-guard` (lib.rs, integration.rs) — all sites switched from `rustgate_core::{encrypted,audit_chain}::*` and `rustgate_server::{archive,archive_rotation}::*` to `rustgate_archive::*`. The `rustgate_archive_bytes` Prometheus gauge is now updated through the new `RotationConfig::on_stats: Option<OnRotationStats>` callback so the archive crate stays Prometheus-free; the server binary wires the metric in `main.rs` under `#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]`. Wire format unchanged: encrypted-archive bytes (`MAGIC = b"RGENC1\0\0"`, `FORMAT_VERSION = 2`), audit-log JSON record shape, and anchor files all read identically — files written by `rustgate-server` ≤ 0.7 remain readable. New `crates/rustgate-archive/README.md` and updated workspace `README.md` architecture table. The `rustgate-core` audit emission (`audit::archive_key_rotation_due`, `audit::chain_anchor_persist_failed`) stays in `rustgate-core` to avoid a circular dep; the encrypted module emits the rotation-due event via `rustgate_core::audit::archive_key_rotation_due(...)`. Closes #892.

- **Documented async-runtime contracts on synchronous-looking constructors (closes #833)** — pure documentation pass that surfaces the implicit "must be called from within a tokio runtime" or "performs blocking I/O" requirements on a set of `pub fn` constructors whose signature does not advertise either. Eight call sites annotated, each with a new `# Runtime requirement` and/or `# Blocking I/O` doc section: `rustgate_federation::trust_store::TrustStore::new` (synchronous and pure — clarified), `rustgate_federation::trust_store::TrustStore::load_from_directory` (blocking `std::fs` directory scan), `rustgate_transport::DynamicCertVerifier::new` (synchronous; documents the per-handshake `provider` invocation contract), `rustgate_federation::jwks_client::JwksClient::start` (calls `tokio::spawn` directly — panics outside a runtime), `rustgate_http::HttpPublisher::new` (calls `tokio::spawn` for the dispatch and DLQ-drain workers AND performs blocking `std::fs` work for the DLQ key ring + directory creation), `rustgate_federation::v1::client::V1Client::start` (calls `tokio::spawn` for the connection loop), `rustgate_federation::v2::client::V2Client::start` (calls `tokio::spawn` for the gRPC connection loop), and `rustgate_federation::v1::server::V1Server::start_with_listener` plus `rustgate_federation::v2::server::FederationService::start` (each calls `tokio::spawn` for an accept loop). Three new doc-tests pin the call-site shape: `TrustStore::new` (compile-and-run, demonstrates the no-runtime-required path), `TrustStore::load_from_directory` (compile-only `no_run`, demonstrates the path-based load with a clear `expect`), and `DynamicCertVerifier::new` (compile-only `no_run`, demonstrates a minimal `RootStoreProvider` closure with an empty store). The `JwksClient::start` doc-test compiles under the `--features jwks` build but is `no_run` because the call requires a real `Arc<rustls::ClientConfig>` and `Arc<JwtAuthority>` for which no zero-arg fixture exists in the federation crate. No public API rename was attempted: the workspace has 30+ call sites across `crates/rustgate-server/src/setup.rs` and integration tests that would all need to migrate, and the asymmetric churn against the documentation benefit (no behavioural change) is not justified per the F-122 directive in #833. Renaming `new → init` is also blocked by the `#[deprecated] pub fn new` shim trick the issue suggests as the breaking-change escape hatch — the existing constructors do not block on async work synchronously, so the shim would not be a spurious wrapper, just a name redirect, and the rename ergonomics do not pay for that. F-118 (SmolStr through `Identity`) is **obsoleted** by #784 and #1245 (the `cn: Arc<str>` and `GroupId: Arc<str>` migration), so the umbrella issue closes with documentation alone. Closes #833.
- **Property-based and integration test coverage finished — closes #789 umbrella alongside #1258** — extends the fuzz / proptest / drain coverage shipped via #1258 (proto / mavlink / federation v1↔v2 round-trips + two negative integration tests) with the remaining F-131, F-133, and F-134 work items. **(F-131 enrollment + http proptests.)** `crates/rustgate-enrollment/tests/proptest_csr.rs` adds three proptest cases against `CsrSigner::sign_csr`: random byte sequences fed in as the CSR PEM (always typed `EnrollmentError`, never panic); random ASCII Common Names up to the workspace-wide `MAX_CN_LENGTH = 256` cap, asserting the issued cert's subject round-trips the supplied username; random DNS-SAN counts up to the `MAX_SAN_ENTRIES_PER_CATEGORY = 32` cap, asserting the documented #794 invariant that a CSR-supplied SAN list is stripped from the signed cert regardless of count. `crates/rustgate-http/tests/proptest_publisher.rs` covers `HttpPublisher::publish` with two proptests (random payload bytes 0..=64 KiB never panic; arbitrary `source_protocol` strings exercise both the echo-prevention drop arm and the dispatch-channel arm) plus three boundary integration tests pinning the empty / exact-max / over-max payload sizes. **(F-133 transport drain tests.)** Four new files mirror the abstract `SubsystemHandle` drain contract pinned by `crates/rustgate-server/tests/shutdown_drains_subsystems.rs` (added by #1270) at the concrete listener boundary: `crates/rustgate-federation/tests/drain_federation.rs` pins `V1Server::shutdown` (idle drain inside the 5s budget; repeated shutdowns are idempotent and stay within budget); `crates/rustgate-http/tests/drain_http.rs` pins `HttpPublisher::shutdown` with three in-flight publishes against a wiremock target plus an idle-drain pin; `crates/rustgate-mqtt/tests/drain_mqtt.rs` pins `MqttServer::run` shutdown with three real mTLS-authenticated CONNECT/CONNACK clients in flight plus an idle-listener pin; `crates/rustgate-websocket/tests/drain_websocket.rs` pins `WebSocketServer::run` with three real wss:// clients registered with the router plus an idle-listener pin. Each test asserts the listener task joins inside the documented 5-second drain budget and that no message is silently dropped (wiremock counters / CONNACK readbacks / router `session_count` are the visibility signals). **(F-134 federation partial-write + authz reload.)** `crates/rustgate-federation/tests/proptest_partial_write.rs` exercises a custom `tokio::io::AsyncWrite` shim (`CutoffWriter`) wrapped in `Framed<LengthPrefixedCodec>`: a proptest sweeps the cutoff `N` from 1 to a full frame size and asserts every partial-write produces a typed `io::Error` (kinds: `WriteZero`, `BrokenPipe`, `UnexpectedEof`); a buffer-cleanliness test verifies a fresh duplex pair + fresh `Framed` parses a valid follow-up frame after a partial-write failure on the previous stream — pinning the documented invariant that the V1 federation reconnect path's parse buffer is local to each new session; a zero-byte-cutoff test pins the worst-case error propagation. `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/authz_reload_mid_request.rs` covers the documented #721 + #1129 hot-reload semantics: a custom `BlockingAllowEngine` that parks `evaluate` on a `std::sync::Barrier` is installed on the `Router`; `Router::route` is invoked from a tokio task, the `rustgate_authz_evaluations_in_flight` callback observes the `+1`, and a separate thread calls `Router::swap_authz` to install a `DenyAllEngine` while the original evaluation is held; the test asserts (a) the gauge stays at 1 across the swap window (in-flight evaluations are not aborted), (b) on barrier release the original allow decision was returned and the message reached the recipient, (c) the gauge drains to 0, (d) the very next `Router::route` call uses the new deny-all engine. **(Constraints honoured.)** No production-code changes — none of the proptests or drain tests exposed a real defect. No new workspace dependencies (`proptest = "1"` was already a workspace dev-dep from #1258); the only Cargo.toml edits add `proptest` to the `dev-dependencies` blocks of `rustgate-enrollment` and `rustgate-http`. The two crates that needed proptest for F-133 (`rustgate-mqtt`, `rustgate-websocket`) and F-134 partial-write (`rustgate-federation`) reuse existing dev-dep declarations. Closes #789.

- **`rustgate_core::message::Metadata` migrated to a builder pattern with `#[non_exhaustive]` (closes #1298, unblocks #847 / #849 / #852)** — refactors the construction story for `Metadata` so future fields can be added without churning the ~130 construction sites currently spread across the workspace. **(1) Type definition.** `Metadata` is now `#[non_exhaustive]`, derives `PartialEq + Eq + Serialize + Deserialize`, and the `ttl` field carries `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` so wire shapes that omit `ttl` (or send an explicit `null`) deserialize identically. `MessageType` gains the same serde derives so the parent type can derive cleanly. **(2) Constructor.** `Metadata::new(received_at, source_protocol, message_type)` takes the three required fields and zeros every optional field to its empty value. The `source_protocol: String` parameter is owned (rather than `impl Into<String>`) to keep call-site type inference simple — the workspace clippy gate flagged `<expr>.into()` callers under the `impl Into<String>` form because `&str: Into<T>` is ambiguous in the absence of the target. **(3) Builder method.** `Metadata::with_ttl(self, ttl: Duration) -> Self` is `#[must_use]` and returns `self` for chaining. Future optional fields each get their own `with_<name>` method and the constructor remains source-stable. **(4) Migration.** All 130 production and test struct-literal construction sites migrated via three sed/perl passes (`ttl: None`, `ttl: Some(<expr>)`, shorthand-field shapes) followed by six manual fixes for sites where `ttl` was bound to a runtime `Option<Duration>` (notably `rustgate-cot::Builder::build_event`, `rustgate-federation::v2::convert::routable_message::federated_event_to_routable`, `rustgate-transport::store_forward::DecodedEnvelope`, `rustgate-transport::cache::make_position_with_ttl`, `rustgate-transport::cache::make_expired_position`, `rustgate-transport::tests::chaos_clock_jump::position_with_received_at`). After migration, `grep -rn "Metadata {" crates/` returns only the type definition and `impl` blocks. **(5) Wire format.** Serde representation is byte-identical for the `ttl: None` branch (field omitted via `skip_serializing_if`) and round-trips cleanly for the `ttl: Some(d)` branch. The pre-PR JSON shape (with explicit `"ttl": null` or omitted field) deserializes unchanged. Pinned by six new tests in `crates/rustgate-core/src/message.rs::tests` (`metadata_new_initializes_optional_fields_to_none`, `metadata_with_ttl_sets_ttl_field`, `metadata_with_ttl_overwrites_previous_value`, `metadata_serde_round_trip_preserves_wire_format_for_default_ttl`, `metadata_serde_round_trip_preserves_wire_format_for_some_ttl`, `metadata_serde_existing_wire_format_still_deserializes`, `metadata_struct_is_non_exhaustive_for_external_crates`). **(6) Forward extension.** A `// Future field additions:` comment in the struct definition pins the four-step recipe future contributors must follow (declare the field as `Option<T>` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = …)]`, default it to its empty value inside `new`, add a matching `with_<name>` method). This unblocks #847 (router pivot to `EntityCodec` over `RoutableMessage`-shaped traffic, which adds protocol-classification fields to `Metadata`), #849 (`AuthzContext::classification` propagation, which adds a `classification` field), and #852 (PR-C trace-context propagation, which adds a `trace_context` field) — each of those PRs becomes purely additive on the type definition and zero call-site touches. No public behaviour, audit emission, or routing decision changes. Closes #1298.

- **Per-crate dependency hygiene: target-gated jemalloc, scoped fastrand, audited ocsp-stapler, dropped unused deps (closes #831)** — four small dependency-isolation items shipped as one PR so the workspace dep graph is leaner and platform-portable.

  **(F-A) `fastrand` already correctly scoped, verified.** `cargo tree -i fastrand` shows the crate is pulled in only by `rustgate-resilience` (jitter for `retry::backoff_with_jitter` and `token_bucket::TokenBucket` lazy refill), `rustgate-http` (test-side and DLQ ID generation in `dlq.rs` / `publisher.rs`), and `rustgate-client` (deterministic reconnect jitter in `reconnect.rs`). Each crate's `[dependencies]` list contains exactly one `fastrand = { workspace = true }` entry that maps onto an actual `fastrand::*` call site. The `rustgate-core` matches on `fastrand_u64` are a synthetic local helper function name (time-based fallback in `encrypted.rs` test scaffolding), not the crate — `rustgate-core` does not depend on `fastrand`. No change required; logged here so the audit trail covers all four sub-items.

  **(F-B) `jemalloc` deps target-gated to non-Windows.** `tikv-jemallocator` and `tikv-jemalloc-ctl` are POSIX-only — the upstream crates fail to compile on `target_os = "windows"`. Pre-this-PR they sat under `[dependencies]` with `optional = true`, so a Windows build that nonetheless enabled the `jemalloc` feature flag (or a `cargo hack --feature-powerset` run that did not exclude `jemalloc`) would attempt to compile the upstream crate and fail. They now live under `[target.'cfg(not(target_os = "windows"))'.dependencies]` in `crates/rustgate-server/Cargo.toml`, and the matching `#[cfg(feature = "jemalloc")]` gates in `src/main.rs` (the `#[global_allocator]` static), `src/metrics.rs` (the four `OnceLock<IntGauge>` statics, the `init()` registration block, the `refresh_jemalloc_stats` function, and the per-scrape `metrics` HTTP handler call) are widened to `#[cfg(all(feature = "jemalloc", not(target_os = "windows")))]`. The result: a Linux or macOS `--features jemalloc` build is unchanged; a Windows build with `--features jemalloc` compiles cleanly and falls back to the system allocator. The CI matrix is `ubuntu-latest`-only today (`cargo hack` already excludes `jemalloc` from the feature-powerset), so no CI job changes; the gate is a pure forward-compatibility hardening for the Windows build the issue called out.

  **(F-C) `ocsp-stapler` already correctly feature-gated, verified.** `cargo tree -i ocsp-stapler` against a default-feature build returns "package ID specification did not match any packages" — the dep is absent from the default workspace tree. With `--features ocsp` it appears under `rustgate-transport` only (transitively reached via `rustgate-{client,federation,mqtt,nats,server,websocket}`). The transport crate's `[features]` block has `ocsp = ["dep:ocsp-stapler"]` and the `[dependencies]` entry is `ocsp-stapler = { workspace = true, optional = true }`. The server-binary feature flag forwards correctly: `ocsp = ["rustgate-transport/ocsp"]`. No change required.

  **(F-D) Five unused per-crate deps removed; three build-script deps added to `cargo-machete` ignore lists.** `cargo machete --with-metadata` flagged eight items pre-this-PR: five genuinely unused (`tempfile` in `rustgate-authz` dev-deps, `tonic-build` in `rustgate-federation` build-deps + `v2` feature gate, `rustls-pki-types` in `rustgate-mqtt` dev-deps, `tracing-subscriber` in `rustgate-mqtt` dev-deps, `tokio` in `rustgate-mavlink` dev-deps — the test files only use `tokio_util::codec`) and three false positives (`prost-build` in `rustgate-proto`, `prost-build` and `tonic-prost-build` in `rustgate-federation` — all three are invoked from the crate's `build.rs` to compile `.proto` files, which `cargo-machete` cannot parse). The unused deps are removed from the corresponding `Cargo.toml` files; the build-script deps are listed under each crate's `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored = [...]` block with a comment explaining the build-script invocation. The `rustgate-federation` ignore list also drops `tonic-prost`, which `cargo-machete` reported as "marked as ignored, but is actually used!" — `tonic-prost` is referenced via `use tonic_prost::ProstDecoder;` inside `src/v2/server.rs` so the ignore was stale. Final state: `cargo machete --with-metadata` reports no findings. `Cargo.lock` regenerates accordingly: `tempfile`, `tonic-build`, `tokio`, `rustls-pki-types`, and `tracing-subscriber` lose one dev-dep edge each from the affected crate's lock entry; the actual lockfile-wide presence of each transitive crate is unchanged because they are still pulled in by other workspace crates that legitimately use them.

  **No public API, wire format, feature semantics, or behaviour change.** Pure dep-graph hygiene. Refs #831.

- **Workspace-wide adoption of `spawn_background` for fire-and-forget background tasks (closes #792)** — migrated 27 production-side `tokio::spawn(...)` call sites in 13 files across 8 crates (`rustgate-mqtt`, `rustgate-websocket`, `rustgate-http`, `rustgate-transport`, `rustgate-federation`, `rustgate-enrollment`, `rustgate-server`) to `rustgate_core::tasks::spawn_background("name", async move { … })`. Every migrated site is a fire-and-forget background task — long-running listener subsystems wired through `SubsystemHandle::new` are unchanged because they were already correctly tracked. The migration replaces bare `drop(tokio::spawn(...))` (which silently lost panics) with the workspace helper that logs `tracing::error!(task = name, error = %e, "background task panicked")` so any panic in a session handler, reloader, watcher, or stream-drain task is observable rather than disappearing into the ether. Cancellation discipline preserved: every migrated `loop { … }` task either already had a `select!` against a shutdown `Notify` / `tokio::sync::watch` channel (MQTT session reaper, federation V2 stream drains, claim adoption with jitter), exits when its driving channel closes (HTTP DLQ drain worker, store-and-forward writer, OCSP fetcher, KV stats flush), or terminates when the owning `Arc` is dropped (SPIFFE refresh task, client queue metrics scraper). Task bodies are byte-equivalent to the pre-migration form — the only change is the spawn boundary. **Regression test.** `crates/rustgate-server/tests/shutdown_drains_subsystems.rs` pins the `SubsystemHandle::new` + `stop_subsystem` contract every server-crate listener relies on: (a) a single subsystem drains within the documented 5s timeout, (b) draining four sequential subsystems (MQTT / WebSocket / plaintext-TCP / UDP shape) stays under the 5s budget per subsystem, (c) a stuck task that ignores its `Notify` is detached at exactly the 5s timeout, and (d) a previously-spawned panicking `spawn_background` task does not poison subsequent subsystem drains. Each migrated task receives a stable `&'static str` name (e.g. `"mqtt-session"`, `"ws-session"`, `"acl-reloader"`, `"cert-reloader"`, `"spiffe-svid-refresh"`, `"fed-v2-server-event-stream"`, `"http-dlq-drain-worker"`) so panic logs and the existing `tracing::info!(task=…, "spawned")` envelope are correlate-able with their source. No new workspace dependencies were added — `tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken` was *not* introduced; the existing `Arc<Notify>`-based shutdown plumbing already covers every long-running task and adding it would have required a workspace-feature change for zero behavioural improvement. Closes #792.
- **`prepare_egress_envelope` helper extracted for sink fan-out (refs #746, first half)** — addresses the architectural risk noted in #746 that the pre-existing `route_for_egress` returned a single `Arc<RoutableMessage>` and handed it to every sink (local fanout, NATS, federation, HTTP, MQTT) under the assumption that "one Arc fits all sinks". For multicast destinations this leaked the *unmasked* source form to external sinks because the local-fanout code applied per-group obligations recipient-side. **(1) New module `rustgate-transport::egress`** hosting `prepare_egress_envelope`, `EgressEnvelope`, `EgressError`, and the `RecipientClass` enum (`Multicast(Vec<Arc<str>>)`, `LocalSession(GroupId)`, `NatsSink(String)`, `FederationPeer(PeerId)`, `HttpSink(String)`, `MqttSink(String)`). The helper renders one `Arc<RoutableMessage>` per envelope — for an N-recipient multicast the obligation actuation runs exactly once, and each recipient's send path pays only the cost of an `Arc::clone`. **(2) Multicast call site migrated.** The multicast arm of `Router::route_for_egress` now invokes `prepare_egress_envelope` with `RecipientClass::Multicast(groups)`. The legacy `compute_multicast_egress` method and its `MulticastEgress` enum are removed. The single-recipient classes are exposed for #737 (separate follow-up PRs) but not yet wired through. **(3) Deny-first fold for multicast.** When any addressed group's Send rule denies, the entire envelope is suppressed (`route_for_egress` returns `None`) so no external sink observes a partial or unmasked copy. Per-group `authz_denied` records are still emitted by `send_to_group_excluding` on the local-fanout path so the audit trail is unchanged. The local fanout itself is unaffected — allow-side groups still receive their per-recipient delivery. **(4) `egress.obligation.applied` audit event** added in `rustgate-core::audit` with fields `{sink, obligation_type, recipient_class, action="apply_obligation", result="success"}`. Fires once per applied obligation per envelope — *not* once per recipient. The cadence change is the central forensic improvement of #746 over the pre-existing per-recipient duplicate emission. Each `&str` field is sanitized at the audit boundary via `sanitize_for_log`. **(5) Tests.** `crates/rustgate-transport/src/router.rs::tests::prepare_egress_envelope_for_multicast_uses_most_restrictive_obligations` pins (a) the union of allow-side obligations across three groups carrying different obligations and (b) the deny-first arm where one group's deny vetoes the entire envelope. `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/egress_envelope.rs` covers the externally-observable contract: a multicast where one group denies returns `None` from `route_for_egress`, and a multicast that triggers `MaskPoint` emits exactly one `egress.obligation.applied` audit record per envelope (asserted via a custom `tracing_subscriber::Layer`). **(6) Out of scope.** Wiring the NATS, federation, HTTP, and MQTT sinks through `prepare_egress_envelope` is the second half of the architecture change and ships as #737 follow-up PRs. The single-recipient `RecipientClass` variants are forward placeholders so the sink crates can compile against the same enum when those PRs land. Refs #746.
- **Chaos / fault-injection test suite added (closes #788)** — five new chaos test files cover the scenarios listed in #788 (slow consumer, network partition, disk-full, clock jump, certificate expiry mid-flight). Each test pins a behavioural invariant that fault injection must not violate, and every test uses deterministic timing so the suite is reproducible across runs. **(1) Slow consumer.** `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/chaos_slow_consumer.rs` drives the router fan-out against a session whose `mpsc::channel(1)` is held parked, deterministically forcing `try_send` rejection on every message after the first; asserts (a) the global `BackpressureGate` peak never exceeds the configured high-water cap, (b) all permits release once the resident message is consumed, (c) a single stalled consumer does not starve other live sessions. **(2) Network partition.** `crates/rustgate-federation/tests/chaos_network_partition.rs` simulates partition + heal cycles against the production reconnect helpers (`backoff_delay`, `should_stop_reconnecting`) and the V1 dedup cache; asserts (a) backoff delays are deterministic and bounded by `min(base * 2^attempt, 300s)`, (b) `should_stop_reconnecting` terminates exactly at the configured boundary, (c) replays after partition heal are suppressed by `MessageDedup` regardless of how many cycles, (d) the dedup cache size stays within its configured capacity across 100 partition cycles. **(3) Disk-full.** `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/chaos_disk_full.rs` drives the durable per-client store-and-forward queue beyond its configured byte cap and pins drop-oldest FIFO eviction (the surviving messages are a contiguous tail of the insertion order, the newest message always survives, `drops_total` increments by exactly the number of evictions); also covers oversize-message rejection and writer-channel-overflow accounting. The chaos test uses the queue's documented byte cap rather than a fault-injecting filesystem because `redb` owns its file handles internally — the byte cap is the production code's actual disk-full response. **(4) Clock jump.** `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/chaos_clock_jump.rs` simulates clock progression by manipulating `received_at` fields (the `PositionCache` TTL is `SystemTime`-based so `tokio::time::pause` does not affect it) and uses `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` to drive the `start_sweep_task` interval on virtual time. Asserts (a) forward jump past TTL filters the entry from `get_all`, (b) backwards jump (entries stamped in the future) are tolerated and not evicted, (c) the sweep task fires after one full interval but not before, (d) `Duration::ZERO` TTL with any elapsed time excludes the entry. **(5) Cert expiry mid-flight.** `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/chaos_cert_expiry_midflight.rs` drives a real mTLS handshake with a 4-second-validity client cert via `TestCa::issue_near_expiry_client_cert`, exchanges bytes, generates a CRL revoking the cert, sleeps past `not_after`, and asserts (a) the live session continues to read/write through both expiry and CRL generation (today's grandfather-on-handshake behaviour), (b) a fresh handshake with the now-expired cert does not yield a usable session — using the connection-probe pattern from `tls_security.rs` to handle TLS 1.3's deferred client-cert validation. **(6) Why no `turmoil`.** The original issue suggested `turmoil` for network partition; this PR uses the production helpers directly because the resilience invariants live in pure functions and a synchronous cache, and adding a workspace dependency for a single test crate is more cost than the in-process simulation is worth. **(7) No production code changes.** The chaos suite did not expose any defects — the production paths (backpressure permits, store-and-forward eviction, position cache TTL, federation reconnect, mTLS verifier) all behaved as documented under fault injection. Refs #788.
- **`on_callback!` macro consolidates `Arc<dyn Fn>` callback type aliases (refs #840 F-107)** — adds `rustgate_core::on_callback!` and migrates 55 hand-written `pub type On* = Arc<dyn Fn(...) + Send + Sync>;` aliases across 22 files in 10 crates (`rustgate-core/egress`, `rustgate-cot`, `rustgate-enrollment/server`, `rustgate-federation` v1/v2/ha/manager, `rustgate-mavlink/frame`, `rustgate-mqtt/config`, `rustgate-nats/subscriber`, `rustgate-resilience/circuit + backpressure`, `rustgate-server/session`, `rustgate-transport` cache/client_ocsp/dedup/listener/obligations/router/store_forward/udp, `rustgate-websocket/server`) to a single declarative form. The macro hardcodes the `Arc<dyn Fn(...) + Send + Sync>` shape so future drift (a missing `+ Send`, an accidental `Box`, a stray `'static`) becomes a parse error at definition time rather than a confusing trait-bound failure at the call site. Generated alias is byte-equivalent to the previous hand-written form — no public API surface, wire format, or runtime behaviour change. Aliases that produce a return type (`PeerStatusFn`, `JwkSetFn`, `OutboundRootStoreProvider`, `ContactsProvider`, `NatsRequestHandler`, `ReloadFn`, `FedApiHandler`, `AclApiHandler`, `MgmtApiHandler`, `ReplayDrain`, `V2ReplayDrain`) and the one `Box<dyn Fn>` alias (`RootStoreProvider`) stay hand-written by design — the macro is `Arc`-only, no-return-type, and the limitations are documented in `rustgate_core::callbacks`. F-109 (reframe `shared-infrastructure.md` as prescriptive ADRs) remains for a follow-up; F-113 (PeerId / ServerName type discipline) already shipped in #1248.

- **Property-based and negative-integration test coverage extended (refs #789, F-131 partial + F-134 partial)** — adds proptests in three previously uncovered crates and two negative integration tests that pin defects-in-waiting on the transport layer. **(1) Proptests.** `crates/rustgate-proto/tests/proptest_xml_protobuf_roundtrip.rs` generates valid CoT XML covering the structural cross-section (uid, type, lat/lon/hae/ce/le, time triple, optional contact and __group detail elements) and asserts the `xml_to_proto -> proto_to_xml` round-trip preserves every structurally-meaningful field through re-parsing — extending the existing hand-written round-trip tests in `convert/mod.rs` to a generator-driven property. `crates/rustgate-mavlink/tests/proptest_frame_resync.rs` pins the codec's three resync invariants under arbitrary input: (a) `Decoder::decode` never panics, (b) on `Ok(None)` any remaining buffer head is a magic byte (resync consumed all non-magic bytes), (c) a v1 frame preceded by an arbitrary non-magic prefix is recovered intact. `crates/rustgate-federation/tests/proptest_v1_v2_conversion.rs` exercises the V1 (length-prefixed XML) <-> V2 (gRPC `FederatedEvent`) bridge, asserting that any V1 CoT XML round-trips through the V2 protobuf representation with identical `GeoEvent` content, plus a `RoutableMessage <-> FederatedEvent` cross-conversion that pins source-CN preservation. **(2) Negative integration tests.** `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/negative_expired_cert_mid_session.rs` drives a real mTLS handshake with a client cert that expires 5 seconds in the future, sleeps 6 seconds past expiry, and asserts the live session continues to read and write — pinning today's intentional grandfathering behaviour as a regression target. The doc comment explains the deliberate baseline so a future fail-closed reload-on-expiry feature has a clear update site. `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/negative_malformed_cot_drain.rs` enqueues three deliberately-malformed CoT XML payloads (truncated `<event>`, mismatched tags, missing required `uid`) plus one valid event into the store-and-forward queue, drains them, and asserts (i) every payload survives verbatim — store-forward is opaque to CoT — and (ii) `rustgate_cot::parse` rejects each malformed payload with a typed `ParseError` rather than panicking. The test did not expose a defect: the queue and parser both handle malformed CoT cleanly, but the test pins those guarantees. **(3) Test-utils helper added.** `TestCa::issue_near_expiry_client_cert(cn, groups, seconds_remaining)` in `rustgate-test-utils` mirrors the existing `issue_near_expiry_server_cert` for the negative cert test; lives next to its sibling so future tests that need an about-to-expire client cert have a one-line entry point. **(4) Workspace dev-deps.** `proptest = "1"` added as a dev-dependency to `rustgate-proto`, `rustgate-mavlink`, and `rustgate-federation` (the workspace-level declaration was already in place from the existing `rustgate-transport/tests/proptest_codec.rs`). No production dependencies, no public APIs, no wire formats touched. **(5) Deferred to follow-up PRs.** F-131 remaining proptest targets (`rustgate-enrollment` CSR/EST parsing, `rustgate-http` payload encoding); F-133 entirely (drain tests for federation/http/mqtt/websocket — four separate test files); F-134 remaining negative tests (federation partial write, authz reload mid-request).

### Added

- **`cert-info` and `check-cert-expiry` diagnostic CLI subcommands (refs #900, F-178 + F-179)** — wires two operator-facing diagnostic subcommands into the `rustgate` binary so an on-call operator can inspect a PEM certificate or pre-flight a fleet of cert files without starting the server. **(1) `rustgate cert-info <FILE> [--json]`** parses the first `CERTIFICATE` block in the given PEM and prints subject / issuer CNs, serial, RFC 3339 validity window, SHA-256 fingerprint, organization, country, OU-derived groups, SPIFFE ID, every SAN category (DNS / URI / IP / email), key usage, extended key usage, CA flag, and signature algorithm. The JSON form is the public contract pinned by unit tests; the human form is for readability and may evolve. The command is intentionally a *viewer*: an expired cert still exits 0 with `expired=true` in the report. **(2) `rustgate check-cert-expiry <FILE>... [--warn-days N] [--json]`** is the automation half — designed for cron, systemd `ExecStartPre=`, and CI smoke tests. Each positional file may be a single cert, a chain bundle, or a cert + key file; every `CERTIFICATE` block is inspected independently. Exit codes form a monotonic severity ladder: `0` = every cert is beyond the warning window, `1` = at least one cert is within `--warn-days` (default 30) and nothing worse, `2` = at least one cert is expired / not-yet-valid / unreadable. A file-level error (missing path, unparseable PEM) elevates the overall verdict to `2` even when other certs are healthy, so a typo in `/etc/rustgate/tls/*.pem` cannot mask a real expiry next door. The JSON shape (`warn_days`, `overall_status`, `min_days_until_expiry`, `files[].{path,error,certs[]}`) is pinned by unit tests and intended to be consumed by jq pipelines / SIEMs. **(3) Wiring.** Each subcommand lives in its own module under `crates/rustgate-server/src/diagnostics/` (`cert_info.rs`, `check_cert_expiry.rs`); the existing CLI dispatch in `main.rs` calls `diagnostics::cert_info::run` / `diagnostics::check_cert_expiry::run` and propagates the expiry-check exit code via `std::process::exit`. Both commands waive the top-level `--cert/--key/--ca` requirement (they take their own path argument) so an operator can run them on a host that cannot start the server. **(4) Tests.** Unit tests in each diagnostics module cover the structured-data shape (RDN extraction, SAN parsing, status ladder, severity ordering, error-vs-cert overall escalation, JSON contract keys); seven new integration tests in `crates/rustgate-server/tests/cli_cert_diag.rs` pin the binary surface end-to-end (`cert_info_prints_subject_for_valid_pem`, `cert_info_json_format_emits_valid_json`, `cert_info_handles_expired_cert_gracefully`, `check_cert_expiry_returns_0_for_long_lived_cert`, `check_cert_expiry_returns_1_for_expiring_soon`, `check_cert_expiry_returns_2_for_already_expired`, `check_cert_expiry_respects_custom_warn_days_flag`, plus bundle and missing-file regressions). **(5) Out of scope.** The remaining four diagnostic subcommands listed in #900 — `test-connection`, `generate-config`, `dump-state`, `crl-info` — ship in a separate follow-up PR (batch 38). Refs #900.

- **Management REST API: `GET /api/v1/crl` and `GET /api/v1/dedup/stats` (refs #902)** — two read-only operator endpoints added under the new versioned `/api/v1/` prefix on the metrics HTTP server. Both routes are bearer-token-authenticated through the existing `MgmtApiState` plumbing and emit `audit::mgmt_api_accessed(endpoint, identity)` on the success path so SIEM correlation rules can attribute operator-driven reads. **(1) `GET /api/v1/crl`.** Returns the active CRL contents in PEM format with `Content-Type: application/x-pem-file`. Status code matrix: `200` with the PEM body when a CRL was configured AND the file reads cleanly at request time; `404` when no CRL was configured (server operating without revocation checking by design); `503` when a CRL was configured but the file fails to read (deleted, permission error, transient FS issue) — distinct from `404` so operators can distinguish "off by design" from "off by misconfiguration". The handler reads the file at request time so the response reflects what the next SIGHUP would load — there is no separate in-memory CRL cache to go stale. **(2) `GET /api/v1/dedup/stats`.** Returns the richer operator-facing counter set: `entries`, `capacity`, `hit_count`, `miss_count`, `evictions`, `ttl_seconds`. Status code matrix: `200` with the JSON envelope when a dedup cache is installed; `404` when dedup is disabled (server started without `--dedup-window-secs`). The legacy unversioned `GET /api/dedup/stats` remains for tooling that has not migrated; the versioned path reserves `200` for "the cache exists and counts can be reported", whereas the legacy endpoint reports `enabled: false` with null counters in the disabled case. **(3) `DedupCache` accounting extended.** Two new atomic counters (`misses`, `evictions`) and accessors (`misses()`, `evictions()`, `capacity()`, `stats() -> DedupStats`) were added to `rustgate_transport::DedupCache`. The `lookup_or_insert` hot path now uses `LruCache::push` (not `put`) so capacity-driven eviction tuples are visible — `put` filters them internally via `replaced.filter(|_| capture)` and would silently undercount. TTL refresh of an expired entry counts as a miss but **not** as an eviction (the value is overwritten in place; eviction is reserved for "the LRU tail had to be pushed out to make room"). New unit tests in `dedup.rs::tests` (`stats_track_hits_misses_and_capacity`, `stats_track_capacity_driven_evictions`, `stats_ttl_refresh_does_not_count_as_eviction`) pin the accounting boundary. **(4) `Router::dedup_full_stats() -> Option<DedupStats>`.** Added alongside the existing `dedup_stats() -> Option<(u64, usize)>` so the management endpoint can read the full snapshot through the same `ArcSwap<Option<DedupCache>>` plumbing the legacy accessor uses; the legacy method is preserved for callers that only need `(hits, len)`. **(5) `mgmt_api_accessed(endpoint, identity)` audit event.** Added to `rustgate_core::audit` with fields `{endpoint, identity, action="access", result="success"}`. Both `endpoint` and `identity` are sanitized at the audit boundary via `sanitize_for_log` per #1197 / #1220 — control characters and newlines are replaced with U+FFFD before emission, so a pathological caller cannot log-forge through the audit trail. The `identity` field is currently the literal `"bearer"` because the metrics HTTP server uses bearer-token auth (no client CN to record); the field is retained as a parameter so a future mTLS-fronted variant can populate it without a breaking change. Failures (401) deliberately do NOT emit this event — operators can distinguish "successful read" from "brute-force attempt" by absence-vs-presence in the audit trail. **(6) Tests.** Eight new mgmt-API unit tests pin the route + status code matrix (`mgmt_crl_endpoint_returns_pem_when_loaded`, `mgmt_crl_endpoint_returns_404_when_unconfigured`, `mgmt_crl_endpoint_returns_503_when_file_unreadable`, `mgmt_v1_crl_wrong_method_returns_405`, `mgmt_dedup_stats_endpoint_returns_counts`, `mgmt_v1_dedup_stats_returns_404_when_dedup_disabled`, `mgmt_v1_dedup_stats_wrong_method_returns_405`, `mgmt_v1_endpoints_require_auth`) plus `mgmt_v1_endpoint_access_emits_audit_event` for the route → audit emission smoke. Two integration tests in `crates/rustgate-server/tests/mgmt_api_audit.rs` (`mgmt_api_accessed_emits_pinned_audit_shape`, `mgmt_api_accessed_sanitizes_endpoint_at_audit_boundary`) pin the JSON wire shape of the audit record under a fresh tracing subscriber, matching the integration-boundary pattern used by `admin_drain_audit.rs` (the per-callsite `Interest` cache prevents this from being a unit test). **(7) Out of scope (#902 remaining).** The cert-status endpoint and the client-disconnect endpoint listed in #902 are NOT touched by this PR — they are tracked separately under batch 38. The unversioned `/api/cert/status` and `/api/clients/{cn}/disconnect` paths added in earlier work remain unchanged. Refs #902.
- **Audit anchor file carries `tip_seq` high-water mark (refs #883, sub-item 2)** — extends the `<path>.anchor` file format so an external auditor can prove **completeness** (no contiguous range of records was deleted between two known seq values) without re-walking the live log. The pre-existing single-line anchor (64-char hex SHA-256 of the chain tip) caught in-place tampering and tail truncation against a *known* anchor, but a verifier reading only the anchor file could not bound how many records had ever been written — so a truncation followed by anchor rewrite produced a still-verifying chain whose record count was unknowable. **(1) New on-disk format.** The anchor file is now a two-line UTF-8 file: the first line is the 64-char lowercase hex tip hash (unchanged), the second line is `tip_seq=<decimal-u64>`. Whitespace-only and missing files are still treated as "no anchor". **(2) New API.** `audit_chain::write_anchor_with_seq(path, tip, tip_seq)` is the new persist entry point; `audit_chain::read_anchor_with_seq(path) -> io::Result<Option<(String, u64)>>` is the new read entry point. **(3) Backward compatibility — both directions.** Legacy single-line anchor files still load: `read_anchor_with_seq` returns `tip_seq = 0` on a one-line file, and the writer falls back to scanning the live log via `read_chain_state` to recover the authoritative seq. The pre-existing `write_anchor` / `read_anchor` functions are retained — `write_anchor` now emits the new two-line format with `tip_seq = 0` (still parses cleanly under both APIs), and `read_anchor` discards the second line and returns just the tip hash. Callers that have no seq on hand (the encrypted-archive sink that restarts at genesis) keep using `write_anchor` unchanged. **(4) Forward compatibility.** Unknown extension lines (`key=value` syntax) are silently ignored so a future writer can add fields without breaking older readers. A non-u64 `tip_seq` value, however, is rejected as `InvalidData` — that is corruption, not a forward-compat unknown. **(5) Server shutdown wires the new path.** `rustgate-server`'s shutdown hook now resolves the seq high-water via `read_chain_state` (bounded by `REWIND_BUDGET`) and passes it to `write_anchor_with_seq`. On a `read_chain_state` failure the shutdown logs a warning and falls back to `tip_seq = 0` rather than aborting the anchor write, so a partial-recovery startup is still possible. **(6) Tests.** Eight new unit tests in `crates/rustgate-core/src/audit_chain.rs::tests` pin the contract: `seq_starts_at_one_for_new_log`, `seq_is_monotonic_across_records` (100 records), `seq_persists_across_writer_close_and_reopen` (close at 50, reopen, seq 51), `verify_audit_log_detects_seq_gap` (delete a middle record, assert `Gap` with the missing seq number), `anchor_file_with_no_tip_seq_loads_backward_compat` (legacy single-line file → `(tip, 0)`), `tip_seq_round_trips_through_anchor` (write 50 records, persist anchor, read back `tip_seq = 50`), `write_anchor_emits_legacy_format_with_zero_seq` (the legacy entry point still produces a parseable anchor), `anchor_with_unknown_extension_keys_is_tolerated` (forward-compat for unknown fields), `anchor_with_invalid_tip_seq_is_rejected` (corruption is not silently accepted). **(7) Runbook updated.** `docs/runbooks/audit-chain-corruption.md` gains a "Gap Detection (sequence numbers)" section that explains how to read `VerifyError::Gap` against the SIEM's high-water mark, the new anchor format, and the triage path on a mid-log gap (treat as a security incident; the deletion span is `expected..=found-1`). **(8) Out of scope (#883 remaining).** Sub-item 3 (NATS infinite redelivery on panic) and sub-item 4 (per-tenant token bucket) ship in separate future PRs. Sub-item 1 (encrypted-archive KDF + key expiration) shipped via #1251. Refs #883.
- **`#[tracing::instrument]` on critical request paths (closes #770)** — adds compile-time `#[tracing::instrument(...)]` attributes to twenty-one hot-path entry-point functions across the router, federation, authz, store-and-forward, TLS listener, and enrollment crates so distributed-tracing exporters (OpenTelemetry, Jaeger) see a span hierarchy instead of flat events. Pre-this-PR the workspace already used `tracing::info!` / `warn!` extensively but only seven manual `tracing::*_span!` constructions existed, so a request that passed through ingress → ACL → authz → fanout → federation forwarding produced a flat event timeline rather than nested spans, and operators wiring an OTLP exporter for cross-service correlation (issue #771) could not pivot from a peer-side span into the local enforcement chain. **Coverage**: `Router::route` / `Router::route_for_egress` / `Router::authz_evaluate_inner` / `Router::register` / `Router::unregister` / `Router::join_group` / `Router::leave_group` / `Router::replay_positions` (transport); `TlsListener::accept` (transport); `ClientQueue::drain` (store-and-forward); `FederationManager::forward_with_metadata` plus the V1 / V2 outbound `send` and the V2 gRPC service handlers `send_one_event` / `send_one_blob` / `health_check` (federation); `NativeEngine::evaluate` and `RuleSet::compile` (authz); `handle_sign_client_v1` / `handle_sign_client_v2` / `handle_revoke` (enrollment). **Level discipline**: `info` for connection-acceptance, policy compilation, and enrollment endpoints (low frequency; default-on logs are useful); `debug` for everything on the per-message hot path so production deployments at INFO level pay no observable overhead. **PII discipline**: every span field that would carry a CN passes through `rustgate_core::masking::hash_cn(...)` before recording (matching the access-log convention from #1207 / #1221), every IP passes through `mask_ip(...)`, and `skip_all` is the default with explicit per-field opt-in so a `Bytes` payload can never accidentally land in a span. The two pre-existing manual `tracing::debug_span!` constructions in `Router::route_for_egress` and `FederationManager::forward_with_metadata` are replaced by the equivalent `#[tracing::instrument]` attribute so the discipline (PII masking, `skip_all`, level) lives in one place per function instead of bracketing the call to a sibling `_inner` future. The `Instrument` trait import drops from both files because no manual `.instrument(span)` calls remain. No new log statements, no new audit events, no behaviour change on builds without a tracing subscriber installed — `#[tracing::instrument]` compiles down to ~nothing when the subscriber is filtered above the span's level. Closes #770.
- **Per-crate Prometheus metrics modules in `authz` / `cot` / `mqtt` / `websocket` / `proto` (refs #771, metrics extension — partial close)** — closes the metrics-extension half of #771 by adding a feature-gated `metrics` module to each of the five crates that previously had no in-crate Prometheus surface (only server-side counters wired through callbacks). The Grafana dashboard JSON sub-item of #771 is **deferred to a separate PR** so this change ships only the metric registration + accessor + call-site instrumentation. **(1) `rustgate-authz`** — `rustgate_authz_evaluations_total{decision, subject_class}`, `rustgate_authz_evaluation_seconds{decision}` (canonical SI sibling of the legacy `rustgate_authz_eval_nanos`), `rustgate_authz_cache_size` gauge (live decision-cache occupancy), `rustgate_authz_obligations_emitted_total{obligation_type}`. The pre-existing `rustgate_authz_cache_hits_total` / `_cache_misses_total` / `_decisions_total` / `_eval_nanos` / `_policy_rules` / `_evaluations_in_flight` stay in `rustgate-server::metrics` so existing dashboards do not break. The `record_metrics` helper on `NativeEngine::evaluate` updates all four metrics post-decision; the cache exposes a new `total_entries()` helper feature-gated to `metrics` so the gauge tracks the sharded cache occupancy without leaking the type into the no-features build. **(2) `rustgate-cot`** — `rustgate_cot_parse_total{result=ok|err}`, `rustgate_cot_parse_seconds`. Wired into `parse()` via a feature-gated wrap so the no-features build emits zero extra instructions on the parse hot path. The pre-existing `rustgate_cot_delta_*` family stays in `rustgate-server::metrics`. **(3) `rustgate-mqtt`** — `rustgate_mqtt_publish_total{qos=0|1|2}` (sibling of the pre-existing label-free `_publishes_total`), `rustgate_mqtt_publish_seconds{qos}`, `rustgate_mqtt_active_sessions` gauge, `rustgate_mqtt_will_messages_total` (counts wills *registered* on CONNECT, sibling of the pre-existing `_will_published_total` which counts wills *delivered*). Wired into `handle_publish_v5` / `handle_publish_v4` via a thin metrics-wrap split (`_inner` helpers carry the same nine-arg fan-in with an F-156 justification), session start / end for the gauge, and the will-validation site for the will counter. **(4) `rustgate-websocket`** — `rustgate_ws_active_connections` gauge, `rustgate_ws_messages_total{direction=in|out}` (data frames only — control frames are excluded since they are not application-observable), `rustgate_ws_compression_negotiated_total{result=enabled|disabled|not_offered}` (pairs with #884), `rustgate_ws_subprotocol_selected_total{subprotocol}` with a reserved `none` token for handshakes that did not negotiate a subprotocol. Wired into `handle_ws_session` (gauge inc on accept, dec on every scope-exit including the tenant-quota rejection arm), the read loop (inbound counter), the write loop (outbound counter post-flush). The pre-existing `rustgate_ws_connections_total` / `_connections_rejected_total` stay in `rustgate-server::metrics`. **(5) `rustgate-proto`** — `rustgate_proto_decode_total{kind=proto_to_xml|xml_to_proto, result=ok|err}`, `rustgate_proto_decode_seconds{kind}`. Wired into the public `proto_to_xml` / `xml_to_proto` re-exports in `convert::mod` via a feature-gated wrap (the no-features build re-exports the inner functions directly so the hot path is unchanged). **(6) Pattern.** Every module follows the workspace `OnceLock<Metric>` + `init()` + accessor pattern with fallback constructors via `rustgate_core::metrics_util` so accessors work cleanly without `init()` (e.g. unit tests). Each crate adds a `metrics` cargo feature that is off by default; `rustgate-server`'s `metrics` feature now turns on the matching feature for each crate so a single `--features metrics` build drives the full surface. **(7) `rustgate-server::setup::start_metrics`** registers each new crate's metrics next to the existing federation / HTTP init calls under the same orchestration block. **(8) Tests.** Each new module ships unit tests for the fallback path, label isolation, accessor stability, and `init()` registration plus an integration test (`crates/rustgate-{cot,proto,authz,mqtt,websocket}/tests/metrics.rs`) that exercises the externally-observable contract — a successful parse / decode / evaluation / handshake increments the matching counter, gauge inc/dec round-trips, and obligation-emitted counters fire once per emitted obligation. Refs #771; the Grafana dashboard JSON sub-item of #771 remains for a follow-up PR.

- **JSON Schema export for `rustgate.toml` (refs #815, F-137 only — partial close)** — operators can now wire their `rustgate.toml` into VS Code (Even Better TOML), Helix, IntelliJ TOML, or any other JSON-Schema-aware editor for autocomplete and inline validation. **(1) New `schema` cargo feature on `rustgate-server`.** Off by default; pulls in `schemars = "0.9"` only when the binary is built with `--features schema`. The default release image therefore does not carry the dependency — it is a development-experience tool, not a runtime dep. **(2) `JsonSchema` derive on the config types** behind `#[cfg_attr(feature = "schema", derive(schemars::JsonSchema))]`. Applied to the `define_config_file!` macro so every `ConfigFile` field gets a schema entry automatically (including the kebab-case `serde(rename_all)` so editor autocomplete suggests `tls-min-version`, not `tls_min_version`), and to the five enum types reachable from the config (`Framing`, `Encoding`, `AuthzPolicyFormat`, `MqttWildcardPolicy`, `PeerDiscoveryBackend`). The schema therefore tracks the live `Cli` surface — adding a new TOML key is a single-line edit on the `define_config_file!` invocation, no schema-side maintenance required. **(3) `rustgate emit-schema` CLI subcommand.** Feature-gated behind `schema`; calls `schemars::schema_for!(ConfigFile)` and writes a pretty-printed JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) to stdout. Operators regenerate the canonical schema with `cargo run -p rustgate-server --features schema -- emit-schema > schemas/rustgate-v0.8.json`. **(4) Canonical schema checked in at `schemas/rustgate-v0.8.json`** (~25 KB, version-tagged so referencing `main` from a VS Code settings file pins to a stable shape across point releases). **(5) Drift-detection regression test** in `crates/rustgate-server/tests/schema_export.rs` — re-runs the generator at test time and asserts byte-for-byte parity against the checked-in artifact. If a contributor adds a new `define_config_file!` field but forgets the regen step, this test fails with the exact regen command in the error message so the fix is mechanical. **(6) Documentation.** `docs/configuration.md` gains a new "Editor Autocomplete (JSON Schema)" section with the VS Code wire-up snippet, a note on Helix / IntelliJ usage, and the regen command; the workspace `README.md` "Running → Configuration file" section gains a matching subsection so the discoverability path is short for new operators. The existing F-156 rule (every `#[allow(...)]` in production code preceded by a `// justification:` comment) is unaffected — the new code introduces no allow annotations. **Backward compatibility:** every previously-valid `rustgate.toml` continues to parse and validate. Editor wire-up is opt-in: operators who do not configure the schema association see no change. **Out of scope (deferred to keep #815 open):** F-138 (config migration story) is the remaining sub-item and ships in a separate follow-up PR. F-136 (config validation discipline) shipped earlier via #1244.
- **Path-specific `.github/CODEOWNERS` for security-critical crates (closes #816, F-158 — completes #816)** — completes the #816 governance umbrella by replacing the previous mostly-flat `.github/CODEOWNERS` (a global `* @rchiofalo`, four broad CI/build rules, and seven whole-crate rules) with a structured catch-all + whole-crate + build/supply-chain + governance + security-critical layout that routes review requests automatically when a PR touches a high-risk surface. The new file groups rules into five sections in *broad-to-narrow* order so GitHub's last-match-wins resolution puts the security-specific rules last and therefore in effect: (1) the catch-all `* @rchiofalo`, (2) one whole-crate rule per crate under `crates/`, (3) build / supply-chain & CI surface (`Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `deny.toml`, `clippy.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `rustfmt.toml`, `.github/workflows/`, `.github/CODEOWNERS` itself, `Dockerfile`, `helm/`, `scripts/`), (4) documentation governance (`CHANGELOG.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `LICENSE`, `docs/adr/`), and (5) security-critical paths within the broader crates: the authz engine (`crates/rustgate-authz/`), the certificate enrollment surface (`crates/rustgate-enrollment/`), the TLS client-cert verifier and its support files (`crates/rustgate-transport/src/verifier.rs`, `cert_reloader.rs`, `spiffe.rs`, `quota.rs`), the encrypted-archive key ring + hash-chained audit log + audit event vocabulary + secret-file reader + PII masking helpers (`crates/rustgate-core/src/encrypted.rs`, `audit_chain.rs`, `audit.rs`, `secrets.rs`, `masking.rs`), and the federation JWT / JWKS authentication plane (`crates/rustgate-federation/src/jwt.rs`, `jwks_client.rs` — the JWKS client itself was added in #1252). A top-of-file comment block names the layout convention, links to GitHub's CODEOWNERS docs, and states the last-match-wins rule explicitly so a future contributor extending the file knows where to place a new rule (broad rules go in section 2, narrowest path-specific rules go in section 5, and inserting a new rule in the wrong section silently masks the rule above or below it). Every owner is `@rchiofalo` because the repo is currently single-maintainer; the file structure is what matters — once a multi-reviewer setup arrives, swapping `@rchiofalo` for `@<security-team>` on the section-5 rows is a one-line edit per row and does not require any restructuring of the file. **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** gains a one-bullet note under the "Review and merge" checklist (section 8 of the new-feature workflow) that names the security-critical surface area and explains the auto-request behaviour, so a contributor whose PR touches one of these files is not surprised when GitHub adds the maintainer as a requested reviewer the moment the diff lands. **Net rule delta: 1 catch-all + 18 whole-crate + 11 build/supply-chain + 5 governance + 13 security-critical = 48 total rules, 47 path-specific.** Pure governance change — no Rust code, no `Cargo.toml` dependency, no CI workflow, and no public API is altered. **Completes #816.** With this entry, the four sub-items of #816 are all shipped: F-139 (per-crate READMEs) via #1246, F-140 (ADR collection) via #1253, F-141 (CONTRIBUTING new-feature checklist) via #1243, and F-158 (path-specific CODEOWNERS) here. The umbrella issue closes with this PR.

- **Architecture Decision Records (ADR) collection (refs #816, F-140 only — partial close)** — seeds a new `docs/adr/` directory with the slim Michael Nygard format and ten initial records covering the workspace's most non-obvious architectural decisions: `parking_lot::Mutex` over `std::sync::Mutex` on synchronous hot paths (ADR 0001), `tokio::sync` locks for state held across `.await` (ADR 0002), `ArcSwap<Option<T>>` with the double-deref read pattern for hot-reloadable shared state — ACL, authz, CRL, dedup, peer set (ADR 0003), `rcgen` for `rustgate-test-utils` certificate generation rather than `x509-cert` (ADR 0004), `tokio-tungstenite` for the WebSocket layer recorded as **Documented** because the historical reasoning was not captured in writing at the time (ADR 0005), `redb` for the per-client store-and-forward queue rather than `sled` or a C-bound KV (ADR 0006), `thiserror` everywhere with `anyhow` permitted only at binary entry points (ADR 0007), `std::sync::OnceLock` over `once_cell::sync::Lazy` per the workspace `clippy.toml` ban (ADR 0008), the `Zeroizing<T>` + `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` discipline for every secret and credential comparison (ADR 0009), and the `spawn_background` / `SubsystemHandle` pair in `rustgate-core::tasks` for fire-and-forget tasks and drainable subsystems respectively (ADR 0010). Pre-this-PR, the only place these decisions lived was in commit messages — a new contributor opening the workspace had no discoverable answer to "why parking_lot?" or "why is `once_cell::sync::Lazy` banned?" The ADR collection is rooted at [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md), which lists every record with status (Accepted / Documented / Superseded / Deprecated / Proposed) and is linked from the workspace `README.md` documentation table. A `template.md` provides the canonical empty form for future ADRs (status: Proposed → flipped to Accepted on landing). `CONTRIBUTING.md` gains a one-paragraph subsection under the "new feature" checklist that points contributors at the directory and at the template, and instructs that the new-feature commit reference the ADR file in the body so the rationale travels with the change. The seed set deliberately does not retroactively migrate every commit-message rationale into an ADR — only decisions where the rationale was non-obvious *and* the codebase reflects the decision today qualified for inclusion. ADR 0005 (`tokio-tungstenite`) is recorded as **Documented** rather than **Accepted** because the original choice predates any written discussion; the ADR honestly says so and lists the alternative (`soketto`) as not benchmarked. **Out of scope (deferred to separate PRs that keep #816 open):** F-158 (path-specific CODEOWNERS) remains; F-139 (per-crate READMEs) shipped via #1246 and F-141 (CONTRIBUTING update for the new-feature checklist) shipped via #1243. Pure documentation change — no public APIs, dependency versions, or wire formats are altered.
- **Observable ArcSwap authz hot-reload window with in-flight gauge (closes #721)** — `Router::authz` is `arc_swap::ArcSwap<Option<Arc<dyn PolicyEngine>>>` for lock-free hot-reload, which means a `Router::swap_authz` install is atomic for *future* `.load()` calls but already-running `authz_evaluate_inner` invocations continue to run against the engine `Arc` they cloned out before the swap. The window is sub-microsecond on healthy traffic but operationally non-zero, and pre-this-PR it was invisible — operators had no way to determine when an `authz.reload_success` audit event had actually become effective on every in-flight request. **The fix is observation, not a barrier.** The issue itself flagged the alternative (a router-wide stall on `swap_authz` that waits for in-flight evaluations to retire) as the higher-invasiveness option and recommended the metric+docs path; that's what shipped here. A new `OnAuthzInFlightChanged = Arc<dyn Fn(i64) + Send + Sync>` callback type sits alongside the existing per-PEP / per-fanout / per-obligation observation callbacks (#768) and is hot-reloadable via `ArcSwap` on the same discipline. A small RAII `AuthzEvalGuard { _phantom: PhantomData }` constructed at the entry of `authz_evaluate_inner` emits `+1` to the callback on `new()` and `-1` on `Drop`, so every Send PEP, Receive PEP, early `?` return, and panic-unwind path through the inner evaluator is symmetric by construction — a future refactor that introduces a fallible step *cannot* leak the gauge because the local is bound before any fallible call. The server binary registers `rustgate_authz_evaluations_in_flight` (Prometheus `IntGauge`) under `--features metrics` with help text "In-flight authz evaluations currently holding the engine Arc cloned out of the router's ArcSwap; observe this gauge after a SIGHUP / policy reload to determine when the previous engine has fully drained", wires `metrics::router_authz_in_flight_callback()` once at startup in `main.rs` next to the other #768 router observability callbacks, and uses the `OnceLock` + `init()` + accessor + fallback-constructor pattern from `rustgate-core::metrics_util` so accessors work cleanly on a build without `init()` (e.g. unit tests). **`swap_authz` is unchanged.** The metric is purely observation — `Router::swap_authz` does not touch the gauge, the lock-free contract is preserved, and the dataplane hot path is unaffected on builds without the metrics feature because the slot stays `None` and the in-flight guard short-circuits its emit on the empty arm. **Net test delta**: +2 inline tests in `rustgate_transport::router::tests` — `authz_eval_gauge_reflects_concurrent_evaluations` spawns 4 threads each holding a guard at a `std::sync::Barrier`, asserts the gauge reads exactly 4 mid-flight, releases the barrier, and asserts the gauge drains to 0; `authz_eval_gauge_decrements_on_panic_safe_path` covers four scope-exit shapes (normal, `?`-style early return, panic unwind via `catch_unwind`, and the no-callback installed path) and asserts the gauge invariant holds in all four. **Documentation update**: `docs/authorization.md` gains a new `## Policy reload effective time` section, additive to the existing `## Reload semantics` material, written for an SRE planning a tightening rollout. The section explains the three properties operators need (the swap is atomic for future `.load()` calls; in-flight evaluations finish on the old policy; effective time is "T plus drain time"), positions the new gauge as the operator-visible drain signal, gives concrete operational uses (steady-state baseline, reload drain observation, stuck-evaluation alerting, capacity planning), and records the rationale for choosing the metric path over a barrier-stall.
- **WebSocket `permessage-deflate` (RFC 7692) negotiation surface and lenient subprotocol default (closes #884)** — closes the umbrella WebSocket-completeness issue by shipping (a) RFC 7692 `permessage-deflate` extension negotiation as a first-class operator-visible surface and (b) a default-flip on RFC 6455 §4.2.2 subprotocol enforcement from strict to lenient. **(1) `permessage-deflate` negotiation.** The new `rustgate_websocket::compression` module parses the client's `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions` request header per RFC 7692 §7.1 (multiple comma-separated extensions, each a primary token plus zero or more `key[=value]` parameters, RFC 7230 OWS tolerated around `=` and `,`, defensive cap of 8 parameters per offer to neutralise a malicious client offering pathological parameter copies), walks the offers in client order, and selects the first `permessage-deflate` offer whose parameter set fits the configured `PermessageDeflateConfig` envelope (`allow_server_no_context_takeover`, `require_client_no_context_takeover`, `max_window_bits` at the RFC 7692 §7.1.2 8..=15 range with a 15 default — every additional bit pays for itself in match length on the first long-form CoT event the session sees). The agreed parameters echo back as a `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions` response header in canonical RFC 7692 §5.1 order (server-side parameters first, then client-side) and surface on the new `WsSession::negotiated_compression()` accessor for downstream metrics / audit. The new `WsListenerConfig::compression: CompressionConfig` field defaults to `Enabled(PermessageDeflateConfig::default())`; operators worried about CRIME/BREACH-style chosen-plaintext attacks against compressed TLS payloads flip to `CompressionConfig::Disabled` (or `--ws-compression-disabled` / `RUSTGATE_WS_COMPRESSION_DISABLED`) and the negotiation surface goes silent — no `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions` response header is emitted regardless of what the client offered. CRIME-style attacks are largely killed by mandatory mTLS and short-lived session keys, but the kill-switch ships nonetheless. The on-wire per-frame compressed-payload codec is gated on a future tokio-tungstenite release exposing the upstream `deflate` feature on the `tungstenite` crate (verified absent in the workspace's currently-pinned `tokio-tungstenite = "0.29"` — tungstenite 0.29 actively rejects RSV1=1 frames as a `NonZeroReservedBits` protocol error, so wire-level interop awaits the dep upgrade); until that lands, the negotiation surface and operator config knob ship today, and the new `compression::Deflater` / `compression::Inflater` raw-DEFLATE codec helpers (RFC 7692 §7.2 trailing-empty-block strip / re-injection) are unit-tested against the same XML payload shape an operator-deployed link will see — so the wire-up follow-up is mechanical rather than design work. Adding `flate2 = "1"` (with `default-features = false, features = ["rust_backend"]`) to `[workspace.dependencies]` is the only new external dep; `flate2` was already a transitive dep of `tokio-util`. **(2) Subprotocol-negotiation lenient default.** The previously-shipped subprotocol negotiation from #1131 rejected a client whose `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` offer was disjoint from the server's `supported_subprotocols` allow-list with a 400 Bad Request (strict semantics). #884 flips this to lenient by default: when no client-offered token matches any server entry, the upgrade still completes, no `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` header is echoed in the response, and the session records no negotiated subprotocol. The lenient stance is the right one for TAK and similar tactical clients that probe several subprotocols and fall back to native non-subprotocol framing on no-match — a strict 400 there regressed interop. Operators running a homogeneous client fleet flip the new `WsListenerConfig::subprotocol_strict: bool` field to `true` (or pass `--ws-subprotocol-strict` / `RUSTGATE_WS_SUBPROTOCOL_STRICT=true`) so a config drift surfaces as a clean server-side 400 in logs instead of as opaque client-side protocol errors. The matching CLI flag and the TOML kebab-case key both live in `rustgate-server`; the existing `--websocket-subprotocols` / `RUSTGATE_WS_SUBPROTOCOLS` field is unchanged. **Net test delta**: +18 inline unit tests in `rustgate_websocket::compression::tests` covering the disabled-config short-circuit, no-offer pass-through, bare offer at default envelope, server-side-no-context-takeover honoured / refused, client-side-no-context-takeover required by server, both `*_max_window_bits` parameters at and below the envelope max, out-of-range / non-numeric / unknown-parameter rejection (including the four out-of-range probes 7 / 16 / 0 / 255 plus an unparseable string), comma-separated offer fall-through to the second acceptable offer, multi-header walk-in-order, RFC 7692 §7.1.1.1 flag-with-disallowed-value rejection, RFC 7230 OWS tolerance around separators, MAX_OFFERED_PARAMETERS defensive cap, deflate/inflate round-trip recovery, and the headline `deflate_compresses_repetitive_xml_payload` ratio assertion (must compress a 64 KiB CoT-shaped XML payload to under 30% of original — typical observed ratio is ~1%, a 99% reduction); +4 integration tests in `crates/rustgate-websocket/tests/ws_compression.rs` covering the handshake-level negotiation surface against a real `tokio_tungstenite` client (negotiated when both sides offer it, disabled-via-config not negotiated, repetitive payload compression ratio, operator-supplied envelope reflected in response); +4 integration tests in `crates/rustgate-websocket/tests/ws_subprotocol.rs` for the new lenient/strict semantics (`subprotocol_first_match_is_chosen`, `subprotocol_no_match_lenient_completes_without_header`, `subprotocol_no_match_strict_rejects_with_400`, `subprotocols_default_empty_preserves_existing_behavior`). **Backward compatibility**: existing clients not requesting `permessage-deflate` continue to work uncompressed (the negotiator returns `None` when no offer is present and the response header is omitted); existing clients not requesting any subprotocol continue to work because the `supported_subprotocols`-empty-default short-circuit is unchanged; the `disjoint_client_offer_is_rejected_with_400` test that pinned the old strict-only behaviour is replaced by the matched lenient/strict pair so a future regression of either branch surfaces here. References RFC 7692 (`permessage-deflate`) and RFC 6455 §1.9 (subprotocol field) for spec lookups.

- **Encrypted-archive KDF + key-expiration hygiene (refs #883, sub-item 1 of 4 — partial close)** — extends `rustgate_core::encrypted::KeyRing` along two axes that previously forced operators to derive 32-byte ChaCha20-Poly1305 keys out-of-band and paste the hex into the JSON keyfile. **(1) Argon2id KDF.** A new `Derivation::Argon2id` variant joins the existing `Derivation::HkdfSha256` under the `serde(tag = "kdf")` discriminator. Argon2id is the OWASP-recommended primitive for password-seeded keys: defaults follow the cheat sheet (`m_cost=19 MiB, t_cost=2, p_cost=1`), salt is mandatory and floor-checked at 8 bytes (RFC 9106 § 3.1), and operators may override individual `params` fields for memory-constrained hardware. The HKDF path retains its 16-byte IKM minimum because HKDF adds no work factor — Argon2 explicitly accepts shorter inputs since its memory-hard work factor is the security boundary. **(2) Pluggable IKM source.** Both `HkdfSha256` and `Argon2id` variants now accept IKM from one of three sources, exactly one of which must be set per entry: inline lowercase-hex (the legacy shape — preserved verbatim for backward compat), `ikm_from_env` (read the named environment variable at load time), or `ikm_from_file` (resolved via `rustgate_core::secrets::read_secret_file`, inheriting the workspace-wide `mode 0o077` permission gate, 16 KiB size cap, and ownership-UID check on Unix). All three paths wrap the resolved IKM in `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` for the lifetime of derivation and wipe it immediately after the KDF returns; only the derived 32-byte key persists in the `KeyRing`. **(3) Operator-facing rotation hygiene.** `KeyRing::from_bytes` now emits a `tracing::warn!` at target `rustgate_core::encrypted` when the loaded key file has no `key_expirations` entries at all — backward compat is preserved (the load still succeeds), but operators are nudged toward setting per-key `not_after` timestamps. When the active key has a `not_after` within the next 14 days, a new `audit::archive_key_rotation_due { kid, days_remaining, action: "rotate_key", result: "due" }` event fires once per `from_bytes` call so SIEM rules and dashboards see a steady reminder until the operator rotates — emitted at load rather than at first-use because encrypted archives are typically opened lazily. **(4) Hard fail-closed for expired active keys.** `EncryptedWriter::create` already refused to seal a new file when `active_key_expired_at(now)` returned true (this admission gate landed earlier on the same branch); historical data encrypted under an expired key remains readable, only new-write admission is gated. **Backward compatibility:** every previously-valid key file continues to load. The legacy raw-hex shape (`{"keys": {"id": "<64-hex>"}, "active_key_id": "id"}`) parses identically; the legacy HKDF shape (`{"key_derivations": {"id": {"kdf": "hkdf-sha256", "ikm": "<hex>", ...}}}`) also parses identically because `ikm` remains a top-level field on each variant alongside the new `ikm_from_env` / `ikm_from_file` siblings.
