- **STANAG 4586 LOI 4 emergency status request command frame (refs #1122)** — continues the LOI 4 graduation kicked off by #1170 (waypoint upload), #1174 (sensor pointing), #1176 (mission abort), #1177 (GCS handover), #1179 (route upload), and #1180 (payload control), shipping the **seventh command-side** message in the `rustgate-stanag4586` crate. Where the prior six command-side frames each direct the platform to *act* on the world — fly to a waypoint, slew the optics, terminate the mission, transfer authority to another GCS, upload a multi-leg route, start/stop/reconfigure a payload bay — `EmergencyStatusRequest` does not direct the platform to act at all: it asks the platform for an **immediate health/status snapshot** when the normal-cadence LOI 2-3 telemetry feed has gone degraded, intermittent, or absent altogether and the operator needs an out-of-band picture of what the platform thinks its own state is. **Operational scenario**: the platform's LOI 2-3 telemetry stream ([`vehicle_position`](crate::vehicle_position), [`system_state`](crate::system_state), [`sensor_status`](crate::sensor_status), [`payload_status`](crate::payload_status), [`bit_report`](crate::bit_report)) goes degraded — the operator's GCS UI shows a stale-data indicator on the panel, the heartbeat counter has stopped advancing, or the cross-frame consistency checks raised a flag (the BIT report claims green while the system state shows a Major fault, the vehicle position has not advanced for 30 seconds while ground speed reports 80 knots). Rather than wait the next 1–5 Hz telemetry cycle and hope the picture clears, the operator asks the platform to interrupt its normal cadence and emit a fresh snapshot of the requested telemetry surface right now. The GCS picks a [`RequestKind`](crate::emergency_status_request::RequestKind) selecting which surface is most diagnostically useful to refresh first ([`FullStatus`](crate::emergency_status_request::RequestKind::FullStatus) for "give me everything you have right now", [`FuelOnly`](crate::emergency_status_request::RequestKind::FuelOnly) when the concern is endurance margin, [`BatteryOnly`](crate::emergency_status_request::RequestKind::BatteryOnly) for an electric platform's pack state, [`BitOnly`](crate::emergency_status_request::RequestKind::BitOnly) for the platform's own self-test verdict, [`PositionOnly`](crate::emergency_status_request::RequestKind::PositionOnly) for the smallest-payload fastest-to-emit surface when the link is bandwidth-constrained), an [`UrgencyLevel`](crate::emergency_status_request::UrgencyLevel) biasing how the platform schedules the response against its own command-execution loop, and an operator-supplied `request_id` for correlating the eventual response. New module `crates/rustgate-stanag4586/src/emergency_status_request.rs`. Public surface: `emergency_status_request::{encode, encode_into, decode}`, the convenience `EmergencyStatusRequest::encode_to_vec`, the typed `EmergencyStatusRequest { vehicle_id, request_id, request_kind, urgency_level, response_deadline_ms, timestamp_unix_ms }`, the `RequestKind { FullStatus, FuelOnly, BatteryOnly, BitOnly, PositionOnly, Other(u8) }` request-scope enum, the `UrgencyLevel { Routine, Priority, Immediate, Flash, Other(u8) }` precedence enum, and the `EMERGENCY_STATUS_REQUEST_FRAME_LEN = 32` constant. **Wire format**: fixed 32 bytes, NATO big-endian throughout — `vehicle_id` (u32, offset 0), `request_id` (u32, offset 4, zero = unsolicited), `request_kind` (u8, offset 8), `urgency_level` (u8, offset 9), 2 reserved zero-padded bytes (offset 10), `response_deadline_ms` (u32, offset 12, zero = no deadline), 8 reserved zero-padded bytes (offset 16), `timestamp_unix_ms` (u64, offset 24, Unix epoch milliseconds). The two reserved blocks are zero-filled on encode but the decoder does NOT validate them as zero, so a future spec revision allocating the bytes (a per-subsystem request-scope mask, a command sequence number for matching against the future response message, an optional cryptographic nonce for request authentication) stays backward-compatible at the frame-length level. **Cross-frame `vehicle_id` correlation**: the `vehicle_id` field matches the `vehicle_id` carried by every prior LOI 2-3 telemetry frame and every prior LOI 4 command frame, so a GCS can correlate "which platform did I ask for an emergency status" against "which platform's telemetry feed is degraded on my UI" by direct byte comparison without an intermediate lookup table — this is the same correlation discipline the prior six LOI 4 frames already use and is the property that lets an operator under time pressure copy the bytes verbatim from a degraded telemetry frame into a follow-up emergency request and be sure the request targets the right airframe. **`urgency_level: Flash` interrupt-style semantics**: the load-bearing tier of the [`UrgencyLevel`](crate::emergency_status_request::UrgencyLevel) enum is `Flash` — the operator's "I believe something is wrong and I cannot wait" signal. A `Flash`-tier request SHOULD trigger interrupt-style status emission on the platform: rather than queue the response behind the platform's current instruction (the `Routine` and `Priority` tiers' behaviour) or wait for the next instruction boundary (the `Immediate` tier's behaviour), the platform interrupts its current instruction, emits the requested snapshot, and then resumes. This is why `Flash` is allocated to wire byte `0x03` rather than the highest byte slot — the byte table puts `Flash` at a low byte for fast wire-byte recognition by analyzer tools and fast comparator dispatch on a platform's urgency-routing path, where seeing the `Flash` tier early in a byte-by-byte scan lets the platform short-circuit subsequent decode work. The wire-byte ordering deliberately does NOT match precedence ordering — `Immediate` sits at byte `0x04` even though it is operationally a step below `Flash` — and the type-level docs spell this out so an operator reading the byte table does not infer urgency ranking from the byte value. The `0x03 = Flash` allocation is pinned by the dedicated golden-fixture test that asserts both the literal wire byte and the named-variant resolution. **Zero-as-sentinel design**: `request_id == 0` is the documented "unsolicited" sentinel — the operator declined to correlate the response (a one-shot diagnostic ping where the GCS only needs the snapshot to render once and does not care which request-response cycle it belongs to); a regression that rejected `0` would silently drop every uncorrelated request, pinned by `decode_accepts_zero_request_id_as_unsolicited`. `response_deadline_ms == 0` is the documented "no deadline" sentinel — the operator has no time bound and the platform may queue the response behind its own scheduling policy; a regression that rejected `0` would silently drop every "respond when you can" request, pinned by `decode_accepts_zero_response_deadline_as_no_deadline`. **Forward-compat enums**: both `RequestKind` and `UrgencyLevel` carry an `Other(u8)` catch-all preserving the raw wire byte so a future spec revision allocating a new request kind (a `LinkOnly` for downlink-margin diagnostics, a `PayloadOnly` for recorder/streamer state, a `MissionOnly` for active-mission progress) or a new urgency tier (a `FlashOverride` matching ACP 121's CRITIC/ECP precedence) stays decodable on a receiver running today's build — matches the same forward-compat discipline used by every sibling LOI 2-3 / LOI 4 frame's enums. **Validation**: decode applies no range checks beyond the 32-byte frame-length floor — every `u32` / `u64` field accepts any wire value; the two enum bytes always succeed (named variants for the recognised bytes, `Other(u8)` for the rest). Truncation below 32 bytes surfaces as `Stanag4586Error::FrameTooShort { actual, expected: 32 }`; trailing bytes beyond 32 are ignored so a future spec revision that appends fields keeps decoding the prefix unchanged. **Test coverage delta**: 172 → 185 tests in the `rustgate-stanag4586` crate (+13 tests). Three hand-built fixture round-trips (zero-valued, `FullStatus`/`Routine` typical, `BitOnly`/`Flash` high-priority) plus a 256-case proptest covering every `u32`/`u64` value and every `u8` enum byte. Golden-fixture decode (`decode_known_fixture_matches_expected_bytes`) pins the literal big-endian byte layout for `vehicle_id = 0x11223344`, `request_id = 0xAABBCCDD`, `request_kind = 0x01 (FullStatus)`, `urgency_level = 0x03 (Flash)`, `response_deadline_ms = 0x000007D0` (2000ms), `timestamp_unix_ms = 0xFEDCBA9876543210` so a regression that swapped to little-endian could pass round-trip + proptest but would still fail this byte-pinning check, plus a follow-up assertion that `0x03` resolves to `UrgencyLevel::Flash` (not some other named variant) so a future refactor that rebinds the byte trips the test rather than silently changing operational semantics. Truncation sweep across `[0, 1, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 31]`-byte inputs all surface as `FrameTooShort`. Trailing-bytes-tolerated case (`decode_extra_trailing_bytes_are_ignored`) appends a 32-byte garbage trailer and asserts the decoded struct is unchanged. Both enum round-trip tables (`request_kind_round_trip_preserves_named_variants_and_other_byte`, `urgency_level_round_trip_preserves_named_variants_and_other_byte`) exhaustively pin each named variant's wire byte plus an `Other(0xFF)` catch-all. **Out of scope**: the response message itself — the platform's "here is the requested status snapshot" reply — is the existing LOI 2-3 read-side telemetry surface ([`vehicle_position`](crate::vehicle_position), [`system_state`](crate::system_state), [`sensor_status`](crate::sensor_status), [`payload_status`](crate::payload_status), [`bit_report`](crate::bit_report)); the codec for those frames already exists and the response-correlation glue (a `request_id` echo field on each response frame, or a separate response-envelope frame carrying the request_id alongside one of the existing frames) is a follow-up read-side PR rather than a command-side concern, so this PR ships only the request side. The remaining LOI 4 mode-change command, the request-side acknowledgement handshake (the platform's "request accepted, snapshot will be emitted at T+50ms" or "request rejected, status surface unavailable" reply), per-subsystem request scoping beyond the named `RequestKind` variants (a future spec revision can use the reserved bytes for a per-subsystem bit-mask without breaking the existing frame-length contract), and UDP/TCP listener wiring (this module is pure encode/decode over `&[u8]`; the network glue is a separate change mirroring how `rustgate-mavlink` got a listener in a follow-up to its codec PR) are all separate follow-up PRs.
- **MAVLink HEARTBEAT audit event + per-aircraft Prometheus counter (refs #909)** — adds operational observability to the MAVLink ingress path so an operator can answer "is *this particular drone* still on the network at the wire level?" without waiting for a higher-layer protocol timeout. When the v1/v2 frame decoder in `rustgate-mavlink` recognises a `MSG_ID = 0` HEARTBEAT, it now (a) emits a structured `mavlink.heartbeat_received` audit event carrying `system_id`, `component_id`, `autopilot`, and `vehicle_type`, and (b) increments the new `rustgate_mavlink_heartbeats_total{system_id}` Prometheus counter. The four `u8` fields come from two distinct sources: `system_id` and `component_id` are pulled from the v1/v2 header (offsets 3/4 in v1 and 5/6 in v2), while `autopilot` and `vehicle_type` come from the HEARTBEAT payload itself (offsets 5 and 4 after MAVLink's field-size-descending wire reordering). A typical drone fleet emits HEARTBEATs at 1 Hz, so the counter gives a per-aircraft presence ping at the wire level — useful for correlating "aircraft fell off the network" higher-level SIEM events with low-level network partition or radio-link drop dashboard signals, and for distinguishing a genuine network outage from a payload-layer silence where the airframe still has a healthy TCP/UDP path. Surfacing `autopilot` and `vehicle_type` separately means the SIEM can also slice presence by ArduPilot vs PX4 vs Vector vs other autopilot vendors at correlation time without having to keep a dialect parser online — a forensic dimension the existing `mavlink.unsigned_rejected` and `mavlink.v1_rejected` events do not provide. Wired through a new `OnMavlinkHeartbeat` callback alias (`Arc<dyn Fn(u8, u8, u8, u8) + Send + Sync>`) installed on `MavlinkFrameCodec` via the new `with_on_heartbeat` builder; the callback only fires for HEARTBEATs whose wire-declared `LEN` byte is at least 6 (covering `custom_mode` + `vehicle_type` + `autopilot`), so a sender that v2-truncates its HEARTBEAT past the autopilot field cannot generate a fake `system_id=0, autopilot=0, type=0` presence signal that would be indistinguishable from a bench-test airframe in the SIEM. The metric uses an `IntCounterVec` with a single `system_id` label — cardinality is bounded by `u8::MAX + 1` (256 distinct values), well within the per-metric scrape-target ceiling, and the per-aircraft separation is what makes per-drone alerts ("system_id=42 has been silent for 90 seconds") possible at all. **Operationally additive**: the design preserves the existing decode hot path verbatim — the observer-on inspection runs only when an operator wires in a callback (gated on `Option::is_some()`), and a build that does not enable `--features metrics` sees zero behaviour change. The `#909` umbrella is a coverage-tracking issue for the MAVLink path; this PR is a small targeted enhancement that improves operational visibility into the framing layer ahead of the listener wiring (UDP/TCP transports) that arrives in a follow-up PR.

- **STANAG 4586 LOI 4 payload control command frame (refs #1122)** — continues the LOI 4 graduation kicked off by #1170 (waypoint upload), continued by #1174 (sensor pointing), continued by #1176 (mission abort), continued by #1177 (GCS handover), and continued by #1179 (route upload), shipping the **sixth command-side** message in the `rustgate-stanag4586` crate. Where waypoint upload, sensor pointing, mission abort, GCS handover, and route upload each direct the airframe (the flight path, the optics, the active mission, the controlling station, the multi-leg route), `PayloadControlCommand` directs an onboard payload bay — a recorder, a streamer, a sensor link — telling it to start, stop, pause, resume, or reconfigure its current operation. It is the **command-side companion to the LOI 2-3 [`payload_status`](crate::payload_status) read-side telemetry frame from #1157**: where `PayloadStatus` reports "the recorder is `Recording`, storage at 42%, link at 8 Mbps", `PayloadControlCommand` lets the operator send the corresponding `Start`, `Stop`, `Pause`, or `Configure` instruction back to that same payload — the second of the two command-side surfaces the LOI 2-3 telemetry frames imply but do not themselves provide (sensor pointing #1174 commands the optics, payload control commands the recording/streaming bay behind those optics). **Operational model**: the platform emits LOI 2-3 [`payload_status`](crate::payload_status) frames at 1–5 Hz reporting the bay's current `recording_state`, `streaming_state`, `storage_used_pct`; the operator decides to act (start a recording before crossing into the target area, pause an ongoing stream while the platform climbs through a known-noisy altitude band, reconfigure the streamer's bandwidth ceiling because the downlink is congested, stop a recording whose data is no longer mission-relevant); the GCS emits a `PayloadControlCommand` carrying the target `payload_id`, a [`ControlAction`](crate::payload_control_command::ControlAction), an optional [`QualityPreset`](crate::payload_control_command::QualityPreset), and optional `bandwidth_kbps_limit` / `record_duration_secs` configuration; the platform applies the command and the next [`payload_status`](crate::payload_status) frame reflects the new state. New module `crates/rustgate-stanag4586/src/payload_control_command.rs`. Public surface: `payload_control_command::{encode, encode_into, decode}`, the convenience `PayloadControlCommand::encode_to_vec`, the typed `PayloadControlCommand { vehicle_id, payload_id, control_action, quality_preset, bandwidth_kbps_limit, record_duration_secs, timestamp_unix_ms }`, the `ControlAction { Start, Stop, Pause, Resume, Configure, Other(u8) }` action enum, the `QualityPreset { Low, Medium, High, Maximum, Other(u8) }` quality-bias enum, and the `PAYLOAD_CONTROL_COMMAND_FRAME_LEN = 32` constant. **Wire format**: fixed 32 bytes, NATO big-endian throughout — `vehicle_id` (u32, offset 0), `payload_id` (u32, offset 4), `control_action` (u8, offset 8), `quality_preset` (u8, offset 9), 2 reserved zero-padded bytes (offset 10), `bandwidth_kbps_limit` (u32, offset 12, kilobits/sec), `record_duration_secs` (u32, offset 16, seconds), 4 reserved zero-padded bytes (offset 20), `timestamp_unix_ms` (u64, offset 24, Unix epoch milliseconds). The two reserved blocks are zero-filled on encode but the decoder does NOT validate them as zero so a future spec revision allocating the bytes (a recording-format selector, a streamer-codec hint, a command sequence number for matching against the future response message) stays backward-compatible at the frame-length level. **Cross-frame `payload_id` correlation contract**: this command's `payload_id` field MUST round-trip the same big-endian byte sequence as [`payload_status::PayloadStatus::payload_id`](crate::payload_status::PayloadStatus::payload_id) from #1157 so a GCS that observes a `PayloadStatus` telemetry frame can copy the four wire bytes verbatim into a follow-up `PayloadControlCommand` and be sure the command targets the same bay the telemetry described. The two frames place the field at different absolute offsets (0 in `PayloadStatus`, 4 in `PayloadControlCommand` — after the leading `vehicle_id`), so the pinned property is "the four-byte big-endian representation of the same logical value is byte-for-byte identical between the two frames", not "the absolute offset is the same"; the constraint is enforced by the dedicated `payload_id_field_matches_payload_status_module` test that constructs both frames with `payload_id = 42` and asserts byte-for-byte equality on the four wire bytes representing that value. Without this guarantee, an operator who copied the bytes verbatim from a status frame into a command frame could end up commanding a different payload — a silent footgun the codec is explicitly designed to prevent. **Zero-as-sentinel design**: `bandwidth_kbps_limit == 0` is the documented "no limit" sentinel — the operator declined to constrain bandwidth and the platform should use whatever the streamer's default policy chooses; a regression that rejected `0` would silently drop every "unconstrained" payload command (the most common operational case for a recorder, where bandwidth is irrelevant), pinned by `decode_accepts_zero_bandwidth_limit_as_no_limit_sentinel`. `record_duration_secs == 0` is the documented "unbounded" sentinel — the recording continues until storage fills, the operator issues a subsequent `Stop`, or the platform terminates it for some other reason; a regression that rejected `0` would silently drop every "record until told to stop" command, pinned by `decode_accepts_zero_record_duration_as_unbounded_sentinel`. **Operational note on `QualityPreset::Maximum`**: the variant is tagged as distinct from `High` rather than a synonym to pin that the operator explicitly accepted whatever bandwidth / storage cost the encoder needs at full quality — typically used only for short-duration close-up captures where archival fidelity outweighs link-budget considerations; a regression that silently downgraded `Maximum` to `High` "to save bandwidth" would defeat the operator's explicit choice. **Forward-compat enums**: both `ControlAction` and `QualityPreset` carry an `Other(u8)` catch-all preserving the raw wire byte so a future spec revision allocating a new action (a `Snapshot` for grabbing a single-frame still while a stream is running, a `Flush` for forcing a buffered streamer to drain) or a new quality preset stays decodable on a receiver running today's build — matches the same forward-compat discipline used by every sibling LOI 2-3 / LOI 4 frame's enums. **Validation**: decode applies no range checks beyond the 32-byte frame-length floor — every `u32` / `u64` field accepts any wire value; the two enum bytes always succeed (named variants for the recognised bytes, `Other(u8)` for the rest). Truncation below 32 bytes surfaces as `Stanag4586Error::FrameTooShort { actual, expected: 32 }`; trailing bytes beyond 32 are ignored so a future spec revision that appends fields keeps decoding the prefix unchanged. **Test coverage delta**: 158 → 172 tests in the `rustgate-stanag4586` crate (+14 tests). Three hand-built fixture round-trips (zero-valued, `Start`/`Maximum` typical, `Configure` with bandwidth limit) plus a 256-case proptest covering every `u32`/`u64` value and every `u8` enum byte. Golden-fixture decode (`decode_known_fixture_matches_expected_bytes`) pins the literal big-endian byte layout for `vehicle_id = 0x11223344`, `payload_id = 0xAABBCCDD`, `control_action = 0x01 (Start)`, `quality_preset = 0x04 (Maximum)`, `bandwidth_kbps_limit = 0x00100000` (1 Mbps), `record_duration_secs = 0x00000E10` (3600s = 1 hour), `timestamp_unix_ms = 0xFEDCBA9876543210` so a regression that swapped to little-endian could pass round-trip + proptest but would still fail this byte-pinning check. Truncation sweep across `[0, 1, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 31]`-byte inputs all surface as `FrameTooShort`. Trailing-bytes-tolerated case (`decode_extra_trailing_bytes_are_ignored`) appends a 32-byte garbage trailer and asserts the decoded struct is unchanged. Both enum round-trip tables (`control_action_round_trip_preserves_named_variants_and_other_byte`, `quality_preset_round_trip_preserves_named_variants_and_other_byte`) exhaustively pin each named variant's wire byte plus an `Other(0xFF)` catch-all. **Out of scope**: sensor calibration commands (gain trim, white balance, focus — a separate command-side surface from this start/stop/pause control), route-time-window updates (re-anchoring an already-uploaded route's `start_unix_ms` / `expiry_unix_ms` belongs on the [`route_upload_command`](crate::route_upload_command) surface from #1179), response/acknowledgement messages (the bidirectional command-response handshake — the platform's "recording started, session id N" or "configure rejected, bandwidth limit below minimum" reply — is a separate follow-up PR), the remaining LOI 4 mode-change command (separate follow-up PR), and UDP/TCP listener wiring (this module is pure encode/decode over `&[u8]`; the network glue is a separate change mirroring how `rustgate-mavlink` got a listener in a follow-up to its codec PR).
- **V2 federation `ServerFederateGroupsStream` + `ClientFederateGroupsStream` observation stubs (refs #864)** — graduates the two GroupSync streaming RPCs in the V2 `FederatedChannel` service from "drain + bookkeep" stubs to **observable** stubs, mirroring the operational discipline established by `SendOneEvent` (#1154), `SendOneBlob` (#1167), and the recently-shipped `ServerROLStream` / `ClientROLStream` pair (#1175): the handlers do **not** propagate group-sync state internally yet, but every received `FederateGroups` update on the client-streaming side now triggers full peer-auth (mTLS CN extraction with no IP fallback), per-update hop validation (the proto's `FederateGroups` message carries a `federate_hops` field), inbound allowlist enforcement when `with_allowed_peer_groups` is configured, a per-RPC Prometheus counter increment, a `federation.event_received` audit record, and an opt-in `OnGroupSync` callback for downstream consumers — all on top of the existing per-peer group bookkeeping (count + name-length limits, in-memory `peer_groups` map) which continues to run unchanged alongside. The stub explicitly does **not** route group-sync state — observation-first lets a deployment SEE inbound group-sync traffic on the dashboard before committing to internal incremental group-sync state machinery (which lands as a separate, larger follow-up PR alongside the bidirectional routing half). New module-level constants `RPC_SERVER_FEDERATE_GROUPS_STREAM = "server_federate_groups_stream"` and `RPC_CLIENT_FEDERATE_GROUPS_STREAM = "client_federate_groups_stream"` co-locate the canonical RPC label with the handler so a SIEM dashboard joining audit log records to the new `rustgate_federation_messages_in_by_rpc_total{rpc=server_federate_groups_stream}` and `{rpc=client_federate_groups_stream}` Prometheus labels sees a uniform vocabulary across the unary `SendOneEvent` / `SendOneBlob` paths and the streaming `ServerROLStream` / `ClientROLStream` / `ServerFederateGroupsStream` / `ClientFederateGroupsStream` paths. New public type alias `pub type OnGroupSync = Arc<dyn Fn(figpb::FederateGroups, String) + Send + Sync>` matching the shape of `OnEvent` / `OnBlob` / `OnRolEvent` (the `String` argument is the peer's mTLS-authenticated CN). New builder method `FederationService::with_on_group_sync` composes with `with_on_blob` / `with_on_rol_event` / `with_allowed_peer_groups` / `with_limits` so a deployment that only wants group-sync ingress can wire it without touching the event, blob, or ROL hot paths; the default callback (set by `FederationService::new` / `with_limits`) is a no-op closure that discards the payload, preserving the existing zero-config behaviour for callers that don't yet need group-sync ingress while keeping the hop-count + authz validation always-on for forensic completeness. New private `validate_group_sync_hop_count` helper sits next to the existing `validate_hop_count` (for `FederatedEvent`), `validate_blob_hop_count` (for `BinaryBlob`), and `validate_rol_hop_count` (for `Rol`) — same shape, different parent message — rejecting updates whose `federate_hops.current_hops` is negative or at-or-above `MAX_FEDERATION_HOPS` (8); group-sync updates without hop metadata are treated as first-hop for backward compat with peers that predate hop tracking. New private `observe_inbound_group_sync` static helper extracts the per-update observation policy (hop check + audit + metric + callback) from the `tokio::spawn` drain loop in `client_federate_groups_stream` so unit tests can drive it directly without constructing a synthetic `tonic::Streaming<FederateGroups>` (which has no public test constructor) — the streaming handler and the unit tests share one body, mirroring the `observe_inbound_rol_event` pattern from #1175 so a regression in the policy can't slip through the tests by going only through the streaming path. **Asymmetry note**: `ClientFederateGroupsStream` is client-streaming in the proto (peer pushes a stream of `FederateGroups` updates, server returns one `Subscription` after the stream closes) and `ServerFederateGroupsStream` is server-streaming (peer sends one `Subscription`, server pushes a stream of `FederateGroups` back). The observation stub for `ClientFederateGroupsStream` runs the per-update hooks on every inbound `FederateGroups`, INCLUDING the existing per-peer group bookkeeping; a hop-limit-rejected update skips both the bookkeeping AND the callback so the in-memory `peer_groups` state never reflects an event the forensic trail recorded as rejected. The observation stub for `ServerFederateGroupsStream` runs the hooks once on the subscription open (peer-auth + allowlist + audit + metric), sends the initial groups roster, then holds the stream open via a `pending::<()>()` task — the routing-side machinery for incremental group-sync updates lives in the bidirectional follow-up PR. **Pre-existing handler hardening**: the previous `server_federate_groups_stream` handler extracted the peer ID from the inbound `Subscription.identity.name` (peer-controlled, untrusted) and was open to **any** caller that could reach the gRPC port, with no allowlist or audit. This PR replaces that path with the same `peer_id_from_request` mTLS extraction the rest of the V2 surface uses (F-44 / #759) — a peer without a verified client cert now short-circuits with `Unauthenticated` BEFORE the initial groups roster is sent. The companion `tests/v2_integration.rs::server_federate_groups_stream_returns_groups` test was updated to use the existing `start_mtls_server` / `mtls_client` fixtures the rest of the integration suite already runs against — same change shape that ROL / SendOne* required when those graduated. Twelve new tests in `crates/rustgate-federation/src/v2/server.rs::tests` cover the contract: five `client_federate_groups_stream_*` tests pin (1) the success path routing the inbound `FederateGroups` update to the registered `OnGroupSync` callback, (2) the `peer_not_in_allowlist` rejection at stream open with `PermissionDenied` and a matching `federation.event_rejected` audit record, (3) the silent hop-limit drop with audit record and no callback, (4) the per-update metrics counter increment under `feature = "api"` (gated because the metrics module itself is only compiled with that feature), and (5) the `Unauthenticated` short-circuit when the request carries no mTLS client certificate (the F-44 / #759 invariant); five `server_federate_groups_stream_*` tests mirror the same shape adapted for the server-streaming proto direction — (1) subscription open succeeds for an authorized peer in open mode AND the initial groups roster reaches the client (pinning that the observable-stub graduation didn't break the existing payload contract), (2) `peer_not_in_allowlist` rejection at subscription open, (3) explicit pin that the hop-limit gate is **not applicable** here because `Subscription` has no `federate_hops` field (a regression that wired hop logic into the subscription open path would surface), (4) per-subscription metrics counter increment under `feature = "api"`, and (5) `Unauthenticated` rejection without a client cert; plus two builder/plumbing tests pinning that `with_on_group_sync` overrides the default no-op and that the default service has a working no-op callback. The peer-auth and allowlist tests reuse the `empty_streaming_request` helper introduced in #1175 (built on `http_body_util::Empty` and `tonic_prost::ProstDecoder` to construct a `tonic::Request<Streaming<T>>` that yields zero messages and immediately reports end-of-stream — the only reasonable way to drive `tonic::Streaming` from a unit test today since tonic exposes no synthetic constructor); the helper and three of the new tests carry an `#[cfg(feature = "api")]` gate (with a `// justification:` comment per F-156) because `http_body_util` is an `api`-only optional dep and the fips / post-quantum CI builds skip `api`. Crate test count: 770 → 782. **Out of scope for this PR (called out as explicit follow-ups, not silent gaps)**: (a) **internal group-sync routing** — the stub fires the `OnGroupSync` callback on every accepted update but does NOT push group-sync state into a `Router::dispatch_inbound`-equivalent path; routing-side group-sync state lands as a separate, larger PR alongside (b); (b) **bidirectional stream wiring** — the proto defines group-sync streams as a bidirectional pair (`ClientFederateGroupsStream` IN, `ServerFederateGroupsStream` OUT) and a deployment that wants to actually relay group-sync updates between federated peers needs both halves wired together with shared state; this PR ships the **observable halves** of each direction independently, and the bidirectional state machine that joins them is the follow-up; (c) **incremental group-sync state machine** — `FederateGroups` carries a `nested_groups` field and a `stream_update` ServerHealth tag that conceptually drive a state machine (subscribe, full snapshot, incremental update, server health change) but the stub does not interpret either field — the callback receives the raw `figpb::FederateGroups` and downstream consumers decide what to do with it; (d) the corresponding **per-group allowlist UX** for the streaming path — currently the audit reason vocabulary is uniform with `SendOneBlob` / `ServerROLStream`'s `peer_not_in_allowlist` token, but a deployment that wants group-sync-specific allowlist groups (separate from the event allowlist) needs a dedicated config knob — out of scope for this PR. Builds on #1175 (`ServerROLStream` / `ClientROLStream` observation stubs — exact template), #1154 (`SendOneEvent` observation stub), #1167 (`SendOneBlob` observation stub), and the existing `peer_id_from_request` mTLS-CN extraction path (F-44 / #759).
- **STANAG 4586 LOI 4 route upload command frame (refs #1122)** — continues the LOI 4 graduation kicked off by #1170 (waypoint upload), continued by #1174 (sensor pointing), continued by #1176 (mission abort), and continued by #1177 (GCS handover), shipping the **fifth command-side** message in the `rustgate-stanag4586` crate and — uniquely — the **first variable-length** LOI 4 frame. Where the prior four command-side frames each carry a fixed 32-byte payload, `RouteUploadCommand` carries a 32-byte header followed by exactly `2 * waypoint_count` bytes of u16 big-endian waypoint references that together form the active mission route. A Ground Control Station emits one `RouteUploadCommand` to load (or replace, or extend) the platform's current route in a single round trip rather than streaming the constituent waypoints one-at-a-time across N `waypoint_command` (#1170) frames. **Operational model**: routes are how a UAS expresses "fly this multi-leg mission" — a sequence of waypoint references the platform navigates in order. The GCS first uploads each constituent waypoint individually via `waypoint_command` (or via a pre-loaded mission package the platform already knows about, with each waypoint carrying a deployment-defined identifier opaque to this codec), then emits a `RouteUploadCommand` carrying the ordered list of waypoint identifiers as `waypoint_indices`. The platform looks each identifier up locally against its waypoint store and applies the route per the chosen [`RouteKind`](crate::route_upload_command::RouteKind) ([`Replace`](crate::route_upload_command::RouteKind::Replace) for "this is the active route now, discard whatever was previously there", [`Append`](crate::route_upload_command::RouteKind::Append) for "extend the existing route with these waypoints", [`Insert`](crate::route_upload_command::RouteKind::Insert) for "splice these into the existing route" — the splice-position semantics are deployment-defined and out of scope for the codec). The platform begins executing the route at `start_unix_ms` (or immediately if the field is `0`) and abandons it at `expiry_unix_ms` (or never, if that field is `0`). New module `crates/rustgate-stanag4586/src/route_upload_command.rs`. Public surface: `route_upload_command::{encode, encode_into, decode}`, the convenience `RouteUploadCommand::encode_to_vec`, the typed `RouteUploadCommand { vehicle_id, route_id, route_kind, start_unix_ms, expiry_unix_ms, waypoint_indices }`, the `RouteKind { Replace, Append, Insert, Other(u8) }` semantics enum, the `ROUTE_UPLOAD_HEADER_LEN = 32` constant, and the `MAX_ROUTE_WAYPOINTS = 256` cap constant. **Wire format**: variable length — a 32-byte header followed by exactly `2 * waypoint_count` bytes of trailer. NATO big-endian byte order throughout. Header layout: `vehicle_id` (u32, offset 0), `route_id` (u32, offset 4), `waypoint_count` (u16, offset 8), `route_kind` (u8, offset 10), 5 reserved zero-padded bytes, `start_unix_ms` (u64, offset 16, Unix epoch milliseconds), `expiry_unix_ms` (u64, offset 24, Unix epoch milliseconds). Trailer: `waypoint_count` × u16 big-endian, each value an opaque waypoint reference resolved locally by the platform. The reserved block is zero-filled on encode but the decoder does NOT validate it as zero so a future spec revision that allocates the bytes (e.g. a route-priority byte, a per-route flags word, or a command sequence number for matching against the future response message) stays backward-compatible at the frame-length level. The `RouteKind` enum carries an `Other(u8)` forward-compat catch-all preserving the raw wire byte so a future spec revision allocating a new route-load semantics (a `Prepend`, a `ReplaceAfterCurrent`, a merge-with-conflict-resolution variant) stays decodable on a receiver running today's build — matches the same discipline used by every sibling LOI 2-3 / LOI 4 frame's enums. **Cross-frame correlation contract**: `vehicle_id` matches the same opaque platform identifier carried by the LOI 2-3 telemetry frames and the `waypoint_command` (#1170) / `sensor_pointing_command` (#1174) / `mission_abort_command` (#1176) / `gcs_handover_command` (#1177) frames so a GCS can correlate "which route did I upload to which platform" against "which platform's telemetry am I currently displaying" by direct byte comparison. The `waypoint_indices` values typically reference waypoints previously uploaded via `waypoint_command` (#1170) — the cross-frame link from a single waypoint upload to the route that strings multiple waypoints together — but the codec does not enforce that relationship, since a route can equally reference waypoints from a pre-loaded mission package the platform already had in memory before the GCS connected. The platform's mission-management layer is responsible for resolving each `waypoint_index` against its local waypoint store and rejecting unknown references; the codec ships only the wire-format contract. **256-waypoint sanity cap**: `MAX_ROUTE_WAYPOINTS = 256` is a sanity bound on `waypoint_count` rather than a STANAG spec ceiling — a route with more than 256 hops is operationally implausible (a 256-waypoint route with 1 km legs is already a 256 km mission, well past the endurance of every fielded LOI 4 platform) and a client sending a larger count is overwhelmingly likely to be a misconfiguration or a wire-format mismatch (a length field that has been byte-swapped, a wrong message type, an attacker probing the decoder's allocation discipline) so failing fast is more useful than accepting a 65535-waypoint route and tying up a ~131 KiB allocation plus the platform's waypoint resolution path on every frame. Counts greater than 256 surface as `Stanag4586Error::FieldOutOfRange { field: "waypoint_count", value: <count.to_string()> }` — the error variant chosen because the field has an explicit upper bound, making the existing range-violation variant the cleanest semantic fit (over either inventing a new variant or shoehorning into `FrameTooShort` with a synthetic minimum). The cap is enforced on decode only — the encode side will saturate to `u16::MAX` if a Vec longer than 65535 is passed, and a hypothetical sender that wants to ship more than 256 waypoints can do so but its receiver will reject the frame at the `FieldOutOfRange` check. **Empty route (`waypoint_count == 0`) is the documented "clear active route" operation** — pinned by `decode_accepts_empty_route_with_zero_waypoint_count` — the platform discards its current route bookkeeping and reverts to whatever its no-route default behaviour is (typically loiter-at-present-position pending operator input). A regression that rejected count=0 as "what's the point of an empty route" would silently drop every clear-route command and leave the platform executing a stale route. **Validation on decode**: deliberately **no range checks on any other numeric field** — `vehicle_id` and `route_id` are opaque deployment-defined identifiers, the two timestamps are not range-checked because the documented sentinels (`start_unix_ms == 0` = "immediate", `expiry_unix_ms == 0` = "never expires") would trip a naive Unix-epoch range check, and the waypoint indices themselves are opaque references that the platform resolves against its local waypoint store rather than the codec. Trailing bytes beyond the declared frame length (`32 + 2 * waypoint_count`) are explicitly ignored on decode — pinned by `decode_extra_trailing_bytes_are_ignored` — so a future protocol revision that appends a per-frame trailer keeps decoding the prefix unchanged. Header truncation (input `< 32` bytes) surfaces as `Stanag4586Error::FrameTooShort { actual, expected: 32 }`; trailer truncation (input shorter than `32 + 2 * declared_count`) surfaces as `Stanag4586Error::FrameTooShort { actual, expected: 32 + 2 * declared_count }` so the caller sees both the actual buffer size and the size implied by the declared count. Fifteen new tests in `route_upload_command.rs::tests` cover the contract: round-trip via three hand-built fixtures (empty route — exercises the documented clear-route operation; single-waypoint route — minimum non-empty case; five-waypoint route — typical small route, also pins the index-ordering contract that the wire trailer round-trips in the same order the `Vec` was authored, not sorted, deduped, or reversed), a 256-case `proptest` round trip with `waypoint_count` ranging over the full legal `[0, MAX_ROUTE_WAYPOINTS]` interval and random u32/u64 fields, a hand-built golden-fixture decode (`decode_known_fixture_matches_expected_bytes`) that places every header field at its documented byte offset and pins literal hex bytes for `vehicle_id` (`0x11223344`), `route_id` (`0xAABBCCDD`), `waypoint_count` (3), `route_kind` (`0x01 = Replace`), the big-endian byte sequences for `start_unix_ms = 0x0123456789ABCDEF` and `expiry_unix_ms = 0xFEDCBA9876543210`, and the trailer `[0x0001, 0x0042, 0x0FFF]` — a regression that swapped to little-endian could pass round-trip and proptest but would still fail this byte-pinning check, the explicit `decode_accepts_empty_route_with_zero_waypoint_count` test that pins the clear-route contract, the header truncation sweep over `[0, 1, 8, 16, 24, 31]`-byte inputs (the boundary set covers each documented header offset plus the just-below-header 31-byte case) with the assertion that every below-header-length input surfaces as `expected: 32`, the body truncation test (declare `waypoint_count = 5` but ship only 32+8 bytes, assert `FrameTooShort { actual: 40, expected: 42 }`), the trailing-bytes-ignored test (declare two waypoints, supply 32+4+8 bytes, assert decode reads two indices and discards the trailing 8 bytes), the `decode_rejects_waypoint_count_above_256` test (count = 257, the just-above-cap boundary), the `decode_rejects_waypoint_count_at_u16_max` test (count = 65535, the wildly-out-of-range case that would tie up a ~131 KiB allocation if accepted), the `decode_accepts_waypoint_count_at_cap` test (count = 256 — the largest legal value, pinning the boundary the other way so a regression that used a strict `>=` comparison instead of `>` still fails on the cap-equal case), the `RouteKind` enum round-trip table (named variants 0x01–0x03 plus `Other(0x00)`/`Other(0x04)`/`Other(0x42)`/`Other(0xEE)`/`Other(0xFF)` to pin the forward-compat preservation contract), and parity tests for the `encode_to_vec` convenience wrapper and the `encode_into` additive-append contract. Crate test count: 143 → 158. **Out of scope for this PR (called out as explicit follow-ups, not silent gaps)**: (a) **other LOI 4 commands** — payload control, mode change — each is a separate follow-up PR with its own wire format and validation rules; (b) **response/acknowledgement messages** — the bidirectional command-response handshake (the platform's "route accepted, N/M waypoints resolved" or "route rejected, waypoint id 0x42 unknown" reply) is a separate follow-up PR; (c) **per-waypoint inline payloads** — a future spec revision could inline full waypoint definitions (lat/lon/alt) instead of referencing them by ID; this codec ships the reference-by-ID form only, matching the current spec's separation between "upload waypoint" and "upload route" messages; (d) **UDP/TCP listener wiring** — this module is pure encode/decode over `&[u8]`, network glue is a separate change; (e) **cross-frame waypoint-existence validation** — the platform's mission-management layer is responsible for resolving each `waypoint_index` against its local waypoint store and rejecting unknown references; the codec ships only the wire-format contract. Builds on #1170 (waypoint upload — the first LOI 4 command-side frame and the cross-frame correlation source for `waypoint_indices`), #1174 (sensor pointing — the second), #1176 (mission abort — the third), #1177 (GCS handover — the fourth), and #1147 + #1155 + #1157 + #1159 + #1165 (the LOI 2-3 read surface), and uses the same module structure, error variants, and test discipline so an operator who has reviewed the prior frames sees no surprises in the fifth command-side frame.
- **STANAG 4586 LOI 4 GCS handover command frame (refs #1122)** — continues the LOI 4 graduation kicked off by #1170 (waypoint upload), continued by #1174 (sensor pointing), and continued by #1176 (mission abort), shipping the **fourth command-side** message in the `rustgate-stanag4586` crate. Where the prior three command-side frames each direct a specific subsystem aboard a single platform — the airframe, a payload sensor, the active mission — GCS handover does not direct the platform at all: it reassigns *which Ground Control Station holds command authority over the platform*. In a multi-station deployment (a forward operating base ground detachment passing control to a recovery-airfield station before a long-leg transit, a primary GCS handing a platform off to a secondary GCS during a shift change, a training exercise where an observer station temporarily monitors what an instructor station is flying), one station emits a `GcsHandoverCommand` to the platform and the platform changes which station it accepts subsequent commands from. **Operational model**: multi-station operation is the load-bearing reason this frame exists — a single platform may, over the course of a single mission, be in command authority of two or more distinct GCS instances. The current GCS picks a [`HandoverKind`](crate::gcs_handover_command::HandoverKind) selecting the handover semantics ([`SoftHandover`](crate::gcs_handover_command::HandoverKind::SoftHandover) for an orderly transfer that waits for in-flight commands to complete first, [`HardHandover`](crate::gcs_handover_command::HandoverKind::HardHandover) for an immediate authority swap even if a command is mid-execution, [`MonitorOnly`](crate::gcs_handover_command::HandoverKind::MonitorOnly) for a non-authoritative observer that sees telemetry but cannot issue commands, [`Cancel`](crate::gcs_handover_command::HandoverKind::Cancel) for revoking a previously-scheduled but not-yet-effective handover) and an `effective_unix_ms` future-time timestamp scheduling the handover for later (`0` = "immediate" per documented semantics); the platform applies the new authority assignment at `effective_unix_ms` (or immediately if the field is `0`) and subsequent commands from the previous `current_gcs_id` are rejected at the platform's command authority gate. New module `crates/rustgate-stanag4586/src/gcs_handover_command.rs`. Public surface: `gcs_handover_command::{encode, encode_into, decode}`, the convenience `GcsHandoverCommand::encode_to_vec`, the typed `GcsHandoverCommand { vehicle_id, current_gcs_id, target_gcs_id, handover_kind, effective_unix_ms, timestamp_unix_ms }`, and the `HandoverKind { SoftHandover, HardHandover, MonitorOnly, Cancel, Other(u8) }` semantics enum. **Wire format**: fixed-length 32 bytes with NATO big-endian byte order — `vehicle_id` (u32, offset 0), `current_gcs_id` (u32, offset 4), `target_gcs_id` (u32, offset 8), `handover_kind` (u8, offset 12), 3 reserved zero-padded bytes, `effective_unix_ms` (u64, offset 16, Unix epoch milliseconds), `timestamp_unix_ms` (u64, offset 24, Unix epoch milliseconds). The reserved block is zero-filled on encode but the decoder does NOT validate it as zero so a future spec revision that allocates the bytes (e.g. a handover-reason code, or a command sequence number for matching against the future response message) stays backward-compatible at the frame-length level. The `HandoverKind` enum carries an `Other(u8)` forward-compat catch-all preserving the raw wire byte so a future spec revision allocating a new handover semantics stays decodable on a receiver running today's build — matches the same discipline used by every sibling LOI 2-3 / LOI 4 frame's enums. **Cross-frame correlation contract**: `vehicle_id` matches the same opaque platform identifier carried by the LOI 2-3 telemetry frames and the `waypoint_command` (#1170) / `sensor_pointing_command` (#1174) / `mission_abort_command` (#1176) frames so a GCS can correlate "which platform did I hand over" against "which platform's telemetry am I currently displaying" by direct byte comparison without an intermediate lookup table. The `current_gcs_id` and `target_gcs_id` fields are opaque to the codec — the wire byte is whatever the deployment's GCS-numbering scheme uses (a fielded number, an IP address fragment, an OPLAN-defined station identifier); the codec does not validate that the initiating sender's ID matches `current_gcs_id`, since that gate lives at the platform's command authority layer. **Validation on decode**: deliberately **no range checks on any numeric field** — `vehicle_id`, `current_gcs_id`, and `target_gcs_id` are opaque deployment-defined identifiers (every u32 value is potentially legitimate), and the two timestamps are not range-checked because a future-dated handover for scheduled shift-change operations is legal and a past-dated value is the platform's command-authority layer's problem rather than a codec concern. **Self-handover (`current_gcs_id == target_gcs_id`) is explicitly accepted** — pinned by `decode_accepts_same_current_and_target_gcs_id` — because the operator may use it as a no-op confirmation to retransmit a stable authority assignment after a momentary loss-of-link or as a heartbeat-style "I still hold authority" signal; a regression that rejected the equality case at the codec layer would silently drop these confirmations and leave the platform without the periodic re-affirmation it expects. **`effective_unix_ms == 0` is the documented "immediate handover" sentinel** — pinned by `decode_accepts_zero_effective_unix_ms_as_immediate` — a regression that rejected `0` as "off the Unix epoch" or required a non-zero (e.g. future-dated) value would silently drop every immediate handover, which is the most common operational case. Trailing bytes beyond the fixed length are explicitly ignored on decode — pinned by `decode_extra_trailing_bytes_are_ignored` — so a future protocol revision that appends a trailer keeps decoding the prefix unchanged. Truncation surfaces as `Stanag4586Error::FrameTooShort { actual, expected: 32 }` — pinned by a sweep over `[0, 1, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 31]`-byte inputs (the boundary set covers each documented field offset plus the just-below-frame-length 31-byte case). Twelve new tests in `gcs_handover_command.rs::tests` cover the contract: round-trip via three hand-built fixtures (zero-valued — preserves `Other(0)` catch-all, exercises both the documented self-handover acceptance path AND the immediate-handover sentinel; typical `SoftHandover` with non-zero IDs and a non-zero timestamp; and a `HardHandover` fixture with a non-zero `effective_unix_ms` to pin that the scheduling field round-trips independently of the handover kind), a 256-case `proptest` round trip across random domain samples (every field unconstrained — no range checks on the wire, and the `handover_kind` byte covers every u8 value with `Other` catching everything outside the named-variant table), a hand-built golden-fixture decode (`decode_known_fixture_matches_expected_bytes`) that places every field at its documented byte offset and pins literal hex bytes for `vehicle_id` (`0x11223344`), `current_gcs_id` (`0xAABBCCDD`), `target_gcs_id` (`0x55667788`), `handover_kind` (`0x01 = SoftHandover`), and the big-endian byte sequences for `effective_unix_ms = 0x0123456789ABCDEF` and `timestamp_unix_ms = 0xFEDCBA9876543210` — a regression that swapped to little-endian could pass round-trip and proptest but would still fail this byte-pinning check, the explicit `decode_accepts_same_current_and_target_gcs_id` test that pins the no-op-confirmation contract, the explicit `decode_accepts_zero_effective_unix_ms_as_immediate` test that pins the immediate-handover sentinel contract, the truncation sweep, the trailing-bytes-ignored test, the `HandoverKind` enum round-trip table (named variants 0x01–0x04 plus `Other(0x00)`/`Other(0x05)`/`Other(0x42)`/`Other(0xEE)`/`Other(0xFF)` to pin the forward-compat preservation contract), and parity tests for the `encode_to_vec` convenience wrapper and the `encode_into` additive-append contract. Crate test count: 131 → 143. **Out of scope for this PR (called out as explicit follow-ups, not silent gaps)**: (a) **other LOI 4 commands** — payload control, route upload (the multi-waypoint companion to #1170's single-waypoint upload), mode change — each is a separate follow-up PR with its own wire format and validation rules; (b) **response/acknowledgement messages** — the bidirectional command-response handshake (the platform's "handover accepted, authority will transfer at T+5s" or "handover rejected, target GCS not authenticated" reply) is a separate follow-up PR; (c) **GCS-to-GCS coordination protocol** — this codec is the platform-facing wire format only; the GCS-to-GCS coordination protocol that the two stations use to agree on the handover before either of them tells the platform is out of scope here and lives at the federation layer; (d) **UDP/TCP listener wiring** — this module is pure encode/decode over `&[u8]`, network glue is a separate change. Builds on #1170 (waypoint upload — the first LOI 4 command-side frame), #1174 (sensor pointing — the second), #1176 (mission abort — the third), and #1147 + #1155 + #1157 + #1159 + #1165 (the LOI 2-3 read surface), and uses the same module structure, error variants, and test discipline so an operator who has reviewed the prior frames sees no surprises in the fourth command-side frame.
- **ASTERIX CAT-048 (Monoradar Target Reports) decoder (refs #1121)** — adds a third ASTERIX category to `rustgate-asterix` alongside CAT-062 (#1149) and CAT-021 (#1166). CAT-048 carries Mode-S / SSR target reports — the surveillance observations emitted by ground-based primary and secondary surveillance radars after they interrogate an aircraft's transponder. This is the legacy "interrogated radar" feed that makes up the bulk of operational ATC surveillance data; almost every primary/secondary radar in the European air-traffic system emits CAT-048. For tactical UAS detect-and-avoid deployments the operational source is different from CAT-021 (ADS-B is *broadcast* from the aircraft, CAT-048 is *solicited* by ground radar) but the integration value is the same — every transponder-equipped aircraft in radar coverage is a potential conflict the UAS must deconflict against, and CAT-048 closes the gap for transponder-equipped aircraft that do not also emit ADS-B Extended Squitter (older airliners, GA aircraft on the Mode-S transponder mandate but not the ADS-B Out mandate, military Mode-S equipped without Mode-S Extended Squitter). New module `crates/rustgate-asterix/src/cat048.rs`. Public surface: `pub fn decode_cat048(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Cat048Report>, Cat048Error>`, the typed `Cat048Report { time_of_day_seconds, measured_position_polar, mode_3a_code, flight_level, aircraft_address, aircraft_identification, track_number }`, the polar-coordinate `PolarPosition { range_nm, bearing_deg }`, and a category-distinct `Cat048Error` enum with the same variant shape as `Cat021Error` / `Cat062Error` (kept as a separate type so a downstream router that dispatches on error type can distinguish CAT-048 from CAT-021 / CAT-062 failures without parsing the message string). Implements the wire format and Field Reference Numbers per Eurocontrol document **EUROCONTROL-SPEC-149**, *"Eurocontrol Standard Document for Surveillance Data Exchange — Part 4: Category 048 (Monoradar Target Reports)"*, **Edition 1.31**. The wire framing is identical to CAT-021 / CAT-062 (CAT byte + 16-bit big-endian LEN + per-record FSPEC + FX-chained extension bits) per Eurocontrol Part 1 §3.2 — only the per-FRN field set differs per the CAT-048 v1.31 UAP. **Decoded fields** for the issue-#1121 MVP: (1) **Time of Day** (I048/140, FRN 2) — 24-bit unsigned, LSB = 1/128 s, converted to seconds-since-midnight UTC, identical wire shape to CAT-021 I021/071 and CAT-062 I062/070; (2) **Measured Position in Polar Coordinates** (I048/040, FRN 4) — 4 bytes: RHO u16 BE (LSB = 1/256 NM, range 0..256 NM) + THETA u16 BE (LSB = 360 / 2^16 deg, full circle), surfacing the rawest signal a radar emits before any downstream Cartesian conversion or fusion (essential for operators who cross-check the radar's own measurement against fused tracks); (3) **Mode-3/A Code** (I048/070, FRN 5) — 2 bytes with the same V/G/L flag bits in the high octet and the same 12-bit octal code in the low 12 bits as CAT-062 I062/060, so the existing `Mode3aCode` type is **re-exported from `cat062`** rather than redefined locally — defining a parallel-but-distinct type would force downstream consumers that correlate transponder codes across CAT-048 (radar) and CAT-062 (system tracks) feeds to convert between them at every site; (4) **Flight Level** (I048/090, FRN 6) — 2 bytes with bit 16 = V flag, bit 15 = G flag, bits 14..1 = signed **14-bit** two's-complement FL value, LSB = 0.25 FL, decoded via the standard "shift up by 2 to put the sign bit at the i16 MSB, arithmetic-shift back down by 2" sign-extension trick (analogous to CAT-062's 15-bit shift-up-shift-down for I062/135 — same pattern, narrower bit-width because CAT-048 borrows two top bits for the V/G flags rather than one for QNH); (5) **Aircraft Address** (I048/220, FRN 9) — 24-bit ICAO Mode-S address, identical wire format to CAT-021 I021/080 (the canonical "hex code" that persists across flights and is what a downstream system uses to correlate successive radar plots from the same aircraft); (6) **Aircraft Identification** (I048/240, FRN 10) — 8 chars in ICAO Annex 10 6-bit alphabet packed MSB-first into 6 bytes, identical wire format to CAT-021 I021/170, decoded to a `String` with trailing 6-bit-space padding stripped so a 4-character callsign returns `"TEST"` not `"TEST    "`; (7) **Track Number** (I048/161, FRN 12) — unsigned 12-bit with the high nibble masked off because the spec reserves bits 16..13 of the wire field as zero (same masking discipline as CAT-062 I062/040). **All other CAT-048 v1.31 UAP entries are recognised by length and skipped** so a real-world datablock carrying any subset of the documented fields decodes cleanly without rejection — the dispatch table covers FRNs 1–28 (Data Source ID, Target Report Descriptor, Cartesian Position, Calculated Track Velocity, Track Status, Track Quality, Warning/Error Conditions, Mode-3/A Confidence, Mode-C Code & Confidence, Height Measured by 3D Radar, Radial Doppler Speed, Communications/ACAS Capability and Flight Status, ACAS Resolution Advisory, Mode-1 Code, Mode-2 Code, Mode-1 Code Confidence, Mode-2 Code Confidence, RE/SP). **Strict-not-lossy compound discipline**: compound items (I048/130 Radar Plot Characteristics and I048/250 Mode-S MB Data, FRN 7 and FRN 11 in the v1.31 UAP) currently surface a typed `TruncatedField` error rather than silently desyncing the cursor — operators see a clear "we don't decode this yet" signal that lets follow-up PRs upgrade individual compound items to real decoders without changing the dispatch table; the next datablock recovers at the LEN boundary so a feed that uses compound items today is degraded but not wedged. Same posture as CAT-021 / CAT-062. **Twelve new tests** in `cat048.rs` `mod tests` pin the contract: the FSPEC builder helper itself (`build_fspec_helper_handles_single_octet`, `build_fspec_helper_chains_extension_octets`) for self-stability of the test infrastructure, three rejection tests (`decode_rejects_short_datablock`, `decode_rejects_wrong_category`, `decode_rejects_length_mismatch`) for the framing layer, a minimal-datablock decode covering FRN 1 only (`decode_minimal_track_returns_data_source_skipped`), per-field decoders (`decode_target_address_round_trips_24bit_icao` — pins the unsigned-vs-signed handling on a 0xA1B2C3 hex code where a sign-extension bug would surface as a wraparound, `decode_position_polar_lsb_conversions` — pins the RHO LSB = 1/256 NM and THETA LSB = 360/2^16 deg conversions on a 1.0 NM / 90.0 deg fixture, `decode_time_of_day_lsb_one_over_one_twenty_eight`, `decode_flight_level_negative_sign_extends_14bit` — pins the **14-bit** two's-complement sign extension on FL−10 against an off-by-one bit-width regression that would mis-decode the V/G flag bits as value bits, `decode_aircraft_identification_strips_trailing_spaces`), a headline `decode_full_record_with_all_mvp_fields` test that exercises a single record carrying every decoded field with FSPEC bits 1+2+4+5+6+9+10+12 set in one record (catches a regression that decoded individual fields correctly but desynced the cursor when fields are interleaved), and a self-stability test (`decode_does_not_panic_on_arbitrary_bytes`) that exercises the documented "every error path returns a typed `Cat048Error`, never a panic" contract on five hand-crafted hostile inputs (empty, wrong CAT, declared-LEN-huge, FSPEC asserts but no data, FSPEC FX-chain truncated). Crate test count goes from 30 to 43. **Out of scope for this PR**: full decoding of compound items (I048/130 Radar Plot Characteristics and I048/250 Mode-S MB Data; each is a primary-bitmap-plus-per-subfield structure that would roughly double the decoder size for diminishing returns on the MVP detect-and-avoid use case); UDP listener wiring (the codec is pure encode/decode over `&[u8]` — a follow-up PR adds the multicast-UDP listener mirroring how the future CAT-062 / CAT-021 listeners will land); fuzz coverage (a follow-up extends the `asterix_cat062` / `asterix_cat021` fuzz target pattern to CAT-048 keyed on the same self-stability invariant — see how #1169 followed #1166 with `asterix_cat021`); and ROL stream / CAT-001 / CAT-150 — each is a separate decoder PR. Builds on #1149 (CAT-062 codec) and #1166 (CAT-021 codec) and uses the same module structure, framing helpers (duplicated across the three modules; a fourth ASTERIX category PR is the right time to extract a shared `framing` module — forcing the refactor with two categories was a judgement call I lost on the side of "wait until the rule of three is clearly satisfied", and three categories now means the next PR earns it without speculating), and test discipline so an operator who has reviewed the CAT-021 / CAT-062 codecs sees no surprises in CAT-048.

- **STANAG 4586 LOI 4 mission abort command frame (refs #1122)** — continues the LOI 4 graduation kicked off by #1170 (waypoint upload) and continued by #1174 (sensor pointing), shipping the **third command-side** message in the `rustgate-stanag4586` crate. Where waypoint upload directs *the platform* to navigate or hold and sensor pointing directs *a payload sensor* to slew, mission abort directs *the entire mission* to terminate: a Ground Control Station emits one `MissionAbortCommand` to instruct a UAS to abandon its current mission and execute a configurable abort behaviour (return-to-base, divert to a saved fall-back coordinate, hold at present position, land immediately, or loiter). **Operational model**: mission abort is the operator's emergency lever — the message they reach for when an ISR target is no longer worth pursuing, when airspace deconfliction requires the platform to clear, when fuel state forces a recovery, or when something safety-critical happened upstream that the GCS detected and the platform did not. The GCS picks an [`AbortBehaviour`](crate::mission_abort_command::AbortBehaviour) and a [`Priority`](crate::mission_abort_command::Priority); the platform compares the inbound `mission_id` against its currently-active mission and either actions the abort (IDs match) or treats it as a no-op (IDs differ — the platform has already transitioned to a follow-on mission and the abort is stale). The `mission_id` guard rule is the load-bearing reason that field exists on the wire — without it, a stale abort that crossed the wire after the vehicle moved on would terminate the wrong mission. New module `crates/rustgate-stanag4586/src/mission_abort_command.rs`. Public surface: `mission_abort_command::{encode, encode_into, decode}`, the convenience `MissionAbortCommand::encode_to_vec`, the typed `MissionAbortCommand { vehicle_id, mission_id, abort_behaviour, priority, divert_latitude_deg, divert_longitude_deg, timestamp_unix_ms }`, the `AbortBehaviour { ReturnToBase, Divert, Hold, LandImmediately, Loiter, Other(u8) }` verb enum, and the `Priority { Normal, Urgent, Emergency, Other(u8) }` tier enum. **Wire format**: fixed-length 32 bytes with NATO big-endian byte order — `vehicle_id` (u32, offset 0), `mission_id` (u32, offset 4), `abort_behaviour` (u8, offset 8), `priority` (u8, offset 9), 2 reserved zero-padded bytes, `divert_latitude_deg` (f64, offset 12, WGS-84), `divert_longitude_deg` (f64, offset 20, WGS-84), `timestamp_unix_ms` (u32, offset 28, Unix epoch milliseconds). The reserved block is zero-filled on encode but the decoder does NOT validate it as zero so a future spec revision that allocates the bytes (e.g. an abort-reason code, or a command sequence number for matching against the future response message) stays backward-compatible at the frame-length level. Both enums carry `Other(u8)` forward-compat catch-alls preserving the raw wire byte so a future spec revision allocating a new abort verb or priority tier stays decodable on a receiver running today's build — matches the same discipline used by every sibling LOI 2-3 / LOI 4 frame's enums. **Cross-frame correlation contract**: `vehicle_id` matches the same opaque platform identifier carried by the LOI 2-3 telemetry frames and the `waypoint_command` (#1170) / `sensor_pointing_command` (#1174) frames so a GCS can correlate "which mission did I abort on which platform" against "which platform's telemetry am I currently displaying" by direct byte comparison without an intermediate lookup table. **`Priority::Emergency` is load-bearing**: the enum tier is the wire signal that the platform MUST action the abort immediately even if it is mid-maneuver, mid-slew, or in the middle of a sensor dwell that would normally be allowed to complete first — `Normal` and `Urgent` may be queued behind a current operation, but `Emergency` overrides; downstream platform logic that interprets the byte as advisory rather than mandatory would silently degrade the contract. **Validation on decode**: `divert_latitude_deg` must be finite AND fall in `[-90, 90]` (NaN explicitly rejected — pinned by `decode_rejects_nan_divert_latitude_deg` because a naive range check silently accepts NaN, mirrors the load-bearing rule in `vehicle_position::decode` and `waypoint_command::decode`); `divert_longitude_deg` must be finite AND fall in `[-180, 180]` (NaN explicitly rejected — pinned by `decode_rejects_nan_divert_longitude_deg`); the lat/lon range checks fire **regardless of `abort_behaviour`** because the fields are structurally always present on the wire. The decoder also explicitly accepts the `(0.0, 0.0)` sentinel — pinned by `decode_accepts_zero_zero_divert_position` — because that is what senders write when the abort behaviour does not require a divert position; a regression that rejected the WGS-84 origin or required non-zero coordinates would silently drop every non-Divert abort. `timestamp_unix_ms` is not range-checked (zero is legal — represents an unset/unknown timestamp). Trailing bytes beyond the fixed length are explicitly ignored on decode — pinned by `decode_extra_trailing_bytes_are_ignored` — so a future protocol revision that appends a trailer keeps decoding the prefix unchanged. Truncation surfaces as `Stanag4586Error::FrameTooShort { actual, expected: 32 }` — pinned by a sweep over `[0, 1, 4, 8, 12, 20, 28, 31]`-byte inputs. Sixteen new tests in `mission_abort_command.rs::tests` cover the contract: round-trip via three hand-built fixtures (zero-valued — preserves `Other(0)` catch-all on both enums and exercises the documented `(0.0, 0.0)` divert sentinel; typical `ReturnToBase` with an `Urgent` priority and zero divert lat/lon to pin the non-Divert path; and a `Divert` fixture with `Emergency` priority, lat=37.7749, lon=-122.4194 to exercise the divert-coordinate path independently), a 256-case `proptest` round trip across random domain samples (constrained to the WGS-84 lat/lon range so the rejection-path tests own those edges; both enum bytes range freely so `Other` is also exercised), a hand-built golden-fixture decode (`decode_known_fixture_matches_expected_bytes`) that places every field at its documented byte offset and pins literal hex bytes for `vehicle_id` (`0x11223344`), `mission_id` (`0xAABBCCDD`), `abort_behaviour` (`0x01 = ReturnToBase`), `priority` (`0x02 = Urgent`), `timestamp_unix_ms` (`0x600F1234` — a reasonable 2021-era Unix-millis value), and the IEEE-754 big-endian byte sequences for `divert_latitude=37.7749` (`0x4042E32FEC56D5D0`) and `divert_longitude=-122.4194` (`0xC05E9AD77318FC50`) — a regression that swapped to little-endian could pass round-trip and proptest but would still fail this byte-pinning check, the explicit `decode_accepts_zero_zero_divert_position` test that pins the sentinel-value contract, two NaN-rejection tests (one per float field), two range-rejection tests (latitude at ±91.0, longitude at ±181.0), the truncation sweep, the trailing-bytes-ignored test, the `AbortBehaviour` enum round-trip table (named variants 0x01–0x05 plus `Other(0x00)`/`Other(0x06)`/`Other(0x42)`/`Other(0xEE)`/`Other(0xFF)` to pin the forward-compat preservation contract), the symmetric `Priority` enum round-trip table (named variants 0x01–0x03 plus `Other(0x00)`/`Other(0x04)`/`Other(0x42)`/`Other(0xEE)`/`Other(0xFF)`), and parity tests for the `encode_to_vec` convenience wrapper and the `encode_into` additive-append contract. Crate test count: 115 → 131. **Out of scope for this PR (called out as explicit follow-ups, not silent gaps)**: (a) **other LOI 4 commands** — GCS handover, payload control, route upload (the multi-waypoint companion to #1170's single-waypoint upload), mode change — each is a separate follow-up PR with its own wire format and validation rules; (b) **response/acknowledgement messages** — the bidirectional command-response handshake (the platform's "abort accepted, executing return-to-base" or "abort rejected, mission already complete" reply) is a separate follow-up PR; (c) **UDP/TCP listener wiring** — this module is pure encode/decode over `&[u8]`, network glue is a separate change. Builds on #1170 (waypoint upload — the first LOI 4 command-side frame), #1174 (sensor pointing — the second LOI 4 command-side frame), and #1147 + #1155 + #1157 + #1159 + #1165 (the LOI 2-3 read surface), and uses the same module structure, error variants, and test discipline so an operator who has reviewed the prior frames sees no surprises in the third command-side frame.
- **V2 federation `ServerROLStream` + `ClientROLStream` observation stubs (refs #864)** — graduates the two ROL (Region of Interest) streaming RPCs in the V2 `FederatedChannel` service from "drain and discard" stubs to **observable** stubs, mirroring the operational discipline established by `SendOneEvent` (#1154) and `SendOneBlob` (#1167): the handlers do **not** propagate ROL state internally yet, but every received ROL event now triggers full peer-auth (mTLS CN extraction with no IP fallback), per-event hop validation (where the proto carries `federate_hops` — `ServerROLStream` does, `ClientROLStream`'s `Subscription` does not), inbound allowlist enforcement when `with_allowed_peer_groups` is configured, a per-RPC Prometheus counter increment, a `federation.event_received` audit record, and an opt-in `OnRolEvent` callback for downstream consumers. The stub explicitly does **not** route ROL state — observation-first lets a deployment SEE inbound ROL traffic on the dashboard before committing to an internal ROL state machine and routing-side wiring (which lands as a separate, larger follow-up PR alongside the bidirectional stream half). New module-level constants `RPC_SERVER_ROL_STREAM = "server_rol_stream"` and `RPC_CLIENT_ROL_STREAM = "client_rol_stream"` co-locate the canonical RPC label with the handler so a SIEM dashboard joining audit log records to the new `rustgate_federation_messages_in_by_rpc_total{rpc=server_rol_stream}` and `{rpc=client_rol_stream}` Prometheus labels sees a uniform vocabulary across the unary `SendOneEvent` / `SendOneBlob` paths and the streaming `ServerROLStream` / `ClientROLStream` paths. New public type alias `pub type OnRolEvent = Arc<dyn Fn(figpb::Rol, String) + Send + Sync>` matching the shape of `OnEvent` and `OnBlob` (the `String` argument is the peer's mTLS-authenticated CN). New builder method `FederationService::with_on_rol_event` composes with `with_on_blob` / `with_allowed_peer_groups` / `with_limits` so a deployment that only wants ROL ingress can wire it without touching the event or blob hot paths; the default callback (set by `FederationService::new` / `with_limits`) is a no-op closure that discards the payload, preserving the existing zero-config behaviour for callers that don't yet need ROL ingress while keeping the hop-count + authz validation always-on for forensic completeness. New private `validate_rol_hop_count` helper sits next to the existing `validate_hop_count` (for `FederatedEvent`) and `validate_blob_hop_count` (for `BinaryBlob`) — same shape, different parent message — rejecting events whose `federate_hops.current_hops` is negative or at-or-above `MAX_FEDERATION_HOPS` (8); ROL events without hop metadata are treated as first-hop for backward compat with peers that predate hop tracking. New private `observe_inbound_rol_event` static helper extracts the per-event observation policy (hop check + audit + metric + callback) from the `tokio::spawn` drain loop in `server_rol_stream` so unit tests can drive it directly without constructing a synthetic `tonic::Streaming<Rol>` (which has no public test constructor) — the streaming handler and the unit tests share one body, so a regression in the policy can't slip through the tests by going only through the streaming path. **Asymmetry note**: `ServerROLStream` is client-streaming in the proto (peer pushes a stream of `ROL` messages, server returns one `Subscription` after the stream closes) and `ClientROLStream` is server-streaming (peer sends one `Subscription`, server pushes a stream of `ROL` messages back). The observation stub for `ServerROLStream` runs the per-event hooks on every inbound `ROL`; the observation stub for `ClientROLStream` runs the hooks once on the subscription open (peer-auth + allowlist + audit + metric) and then returns an empty stream that stays open via a `pending::<()>()` task — the routing-side machinery for actually pushing ROL events out lives in the bidirectional follow-up PR. Twelve new tests in `crates/rustgate-federation/src/v2/server.rs::tests` cover the contract: five `server_rol_stream_*` tests pin (1) the success path routing the ROL event to the registered `OnRolEvent` callback, (2) the `peer_not_in_allowlist` rejection at stream open with `PermissionDenied` and a matching `federation.event_rejected` audit record, (3) the silent hop-limit drop with audit record and no callback, (4) the per-event metrics counter increment under `feature = "api"` (gated because the metrics module itself is only compiled with that feature), and (5) the `Unauthenticated` short-circuit when the request carries no mTLS client certificate (the F-44 / #759 invariant); five `client_rol_stream_*` tests mirror the same shape adapted for the server-streaming proto direction — (1) subscription open succeeds for an authorized peer in open mode, (2) `peer_not_in_allowlist` rejection at subscription open, (3) explicit pin that the hop-limit gate is **not applicable** here because `Subscription` has no `federate_hops` field (a regression that wired hop logic into the subscription open path would surface), (4) per-subscription metrics counter increment under `feature = "api"`, and (5) `Unauthenticated` rejection without a client cert; plus two builder/plumbing tests pinning that `with_on_rol_event` overrides the default no-op and that the default service has a working no-op callback. The peer-auth and allowlist tests use a tiny `empty_streaming_request` helper built on `http_body_util::Empty` and `tonic_prost::ProstDecoder` to construct a `tonic::Request<Streaming<Rol>>` that yields zero messages and immediately reports end-of-stream — the only reasonable way to drive `tonic::Streaming` from a unit test today since tonic exposes no synthetic constructor. Crate test count: 779 → 791. **Out of scope for this PR (called out as explicit follow-ups, not silent gaps)**: (a) **internal ROL routing** — the stub fires the `OnRolEvent` callback on every accepted ROL but does NOT call any `Router::dispatch_inbound`-equivalent path; routing-side ROL state lands as a separate, larger PR alongside (b); (b) **bidirectional stream wiring** — the proto defines ROL streams as a bidirectional pair (`ServerROLStream` IN, `ClientROLStream` OUT) and a deployment that wants to actually relay ROL events between federated peers needs both halves wired together with shared state; this PR ships the **observable halves** of each direction independently, and the bidirectional state machine that joins them is the follow-up; (c) **per-RPC ROL state machine** — ROL events carry a `program` field that conceptually drives a state machine (subscribe to a region, update, unsubscribe) but the stub does not interpret `program` — the callback receives the raw `figpb::Rol` and downstream consumers decide what to do with it; (d) the corresponding **`peer_not_in_allowlist` allowlist UX** for the streaming path — currently the audit reason vocabulary is uniform with `SendOneBlob`'s `peer_not_in_allowlist` token, but a deployment that wants ROL-specific allowlist groups (separate from the event allowlist) needs a dedicated config knob — out of scope for this PR. Builds on #1154 (`SendOneEvent` observation stub), #1167 (`SendOneBlob` observation stub), and the existing `peer_id_from_request` mTLS-CN extraction path (F-44 / #759).
- **STANAG 4586 LOI 4 sensor pointing command frame (refs #1122)** — continues the LOI 4 graduation kicked off by #1170 (waypoint upload), shipping the **second command-side** message in the `rustgate-stanag4586` crate.
