Twenty-one new tests in `system_state.rs::tests` cover the contract: round-trip via three hand-built fixtures (zero-valued, max-valued, mid-range), a `proptest` round trip across 256 random domain samples (constrained to finite floats and the `[0.0, 100.0]` ranges so the rejection-path tests own those edges), a hand-built golden-fixture decode (`decode_known_fixture_matches_expected_bytes`) that places every field at its documented byte offset and pins the IEEE-754 big-endian byte sequences for `75.0_f32` (`0x42960000`), `50.0_f32` (`0x42480000`), and `90.0_f32` (`0x42B40000`) plus the literal hex bytes for `vehicle_id`, `bit_status_flags`, and `timestamp_unix_ms` (a regression that swapped to little-endian could pass round-trip and proptest but would still fail this golden-fixture check), seven rejection tests (negative + above-100 + NaN combinations across the three percentage fields), a truncation sweep over `[0, 1, 7, 16, 23, 31]`-byte inputs pinning the `FrameTooShort` variant, two enum round-trip tests apiece for `OperatingMode` and `MissionPhase` (named-variant table + `Other(byte)` preservation contract), `bit_status_flags_named_constants_are_disjoint_powers_of_two` (pins each named constant is a single bit AND no two constants alias the same bit, defending against a typo refactor that would silently merge two subsystems' fault reporting), `bit_status_flags_round_trip_preserves_unknown_bits` (pins the forward-compat property for the wire format's reserved bit space), and `bit_status_flags_helpers_return_expected_values`. Crate test count goes from 51 to 72. **Out of scope for this PR**: BIT report messages (the longer-form per-subsystem health detail beyond the 16-bit summary in `system_state`), LOI 4+ command messages (waypoint upload, sensor pointing, GCS handover, payload control), and UDP/TCP listener wiring — each of those is a separate follow-up PR. Builds on #1147 + #1155 + #1157 and uses the same module structure, error variants, and test discipline so an operator who has reviewed the first three frames' codecs sees no surprises in the fourth.
- **Fuzz coverage for STANAG 4586 vehicle-position and ASTERIX CAT-062 decoders (refs #1121, #1122)** — adds two new fuzz targets to `fuzz/fuzz_targets/` plus three hand-curated corpus seeds each. Both decoders sit on the boundary between an untrusted multicast/UDP socket and the routing layer, so making them robust against hostile input is the load-bearing security property — the unit-test suites cover the documented happy and rejection paths, but fuzzing exercises *random* byte sequences that no test author would write. **`stanag4586_vehicle_position`** calls `vehicle_position::decode(data)` and, on `Ok`, asserts a self-stability invariant: `decode(encode(decode(x))) == decode(x)` byte-for-byte. The comparison is done field-by-field via `f64::to_be_bytes` / `f32::to_be_bytes` so the round-trip is **NaN-tolerant** — by design the decoder validates `latitude_deg`/`longitude_deg` as finite (NaN is rejected upfront for those two coordinate fields) but accepts NaN for `altitude_msl_m`, `ground_speed_mps`, and `heading_deg` because senders may transmit signed or unwrapped values during turn integration; a direct `assert_eq!` comparison would fail on NaN per IEEE-754 even though the wire bytes round-trip cleanly. The bit-pattern comparison preserves the actually-load-bearing property (encode and decode agree on every byte) while accommodating the documented field semantics. Three hand-curated corpus seeds give the fuzzer a head start: `seed-minimal-valid` (lat=37.5/lon=-122.0, mid-range valid frame), `seed-all-zero` (48 zero bytes — the all-corners-zero edge case which is a valid frame and exercises the all-zero IEEE-754 representation), and `seed-edge-90-180` (lat=90/lon=180, the upper bound of the WGS-84 range that the decoder accepts as valid). **`asterix_cat062`** calls `decode_cat062(data)` with arbitrary bytes and only asserts the decoder does not panic — the documented contract is that every error path returns a typed `Cat062Error`, never a panic. Three hand-curated seeds: `seed-minimal-empty` (`CAT=62, LEN=4, FSPEC=0x40` — a record with only the FRN 2 spare bit set, the smallest valid datablock), `seed-frn12-track` (a 7-byte datablock with FRN 12 / I062/040 track number = 0x42, the most common useful field), and `seed-truncated` (a 1-byte buffer that exercises the `TruncatedDatablock` early-return path). Both fuzz targets shake out real bytes-level invariants: a 30-second `cargo +nightly fuzz run stanag4586_vehicle_position` cycle executed 18.7M iterations with no crashes after the NaN-tolerance fix; a similar `asterix_cat062` cycle executed 11M iterations with no crashes. The fuzz targets are added to `fuzz/Cargo.toml` `[[bin]]` table with new path-deps on `rustgate-stanag4586` and `rustgate-asterix`. The Weekly Extended Fuzz workflow picks up new targets automatically by globbing `fuzz/fuzz_targets/*.rs`, so both decoders are now exercised on every weekly run alongside `cot_mask_strip_coordinates`, `mavlink_v2_frame`, `tak_frame_codec`, and the rest of the existing fleet.
- **STANAG 4586 LOI 2-3 payload-status telemetry message (refs #1122)** — adds the third (and final read-side) LOI 2-3 telemetry frame to `rustgate-stanag4586`, completing the LOI 2 receive surface called out in #1122 alongside the previously-shipped `vehicle_position` (#1147) and `sensor_status` (#1155). The three frames are emitted from the same Vehicle Specific Module at different rates and carry orthogonal state — `vehicle_position` at 10–50 Hz so a moving-map can render the platform smoothly, `sensor_status` at 1–5 Hz because the sensor's pointing state changes far less frequently than the platform's position, and `payload_status` at 0.5–2 Hz because storage / link / streaming state changes on the order of seconds (a recorder filling up, a streamer pausing, a downlink dropping); together they give a LOI 2 deployment everything it needs to display, log, and relay the inbound vehicle, sensor, and payload state. New public surface: `pub fn payload_status::encode(&PayloadStatus) -> Vec<u8>`, `payload_status::encode_into(&PayloadStatus, &mut BytesMut)` for the zero-extra-allocation hot path, `payload_status::decode(&[u8]) -> Result<PayloadStatus, Stanag4586Error>`, the convenience `PayloadStatus::encode_to_vec`, plus the typed `PayloadStatus { payload_id, payload_kind, recording_state, streaming_state, storage_used_pct, link_bandwidth_kbps, link_latency_ms, timestamp_unix_ms }`, the `PayloadKind { Recorder, Streamer, Combined, Relay, Other(u8) }` modality enum, the `RecordingState { Idle, Recording, Paused, Full, Failed, Other(u8) }` storage-state enum, and the `StreamingState { Idle, Streaming, Buffering, LinkLost, Failed, Other(u8) }` link-state enum. Wire format is fixed-length 32 bytes with NATO big-endian byte order: `payload_id` (u32, offset 0), `payload_kind` (u8, offset 4), `recording_state` (u8, offset 5), `streaming_state` (u8, offset 6), 1 reserved zero-padded byte, `storage_used_pct` (f32, offset 8), `link_bandwidth_kbps` (f32, offset 12), `link_latency_ms` (f32, offset 16), 4 reserved zero-padded bytes, `timestamp_unix_ms` (u64, offset 24). The two reserved blocks are zero-filled on encode but the decoder does NOT validate them as zero so a future spec revision that allocates them stays backward-compatible at the frame-length level. All three categorical enums carry an `Other(u8)` forward-compat catch-all preserving the raw wire byte so a firmware revision that introduces a new payload kind, recording state, or streaming state stays decodable rather than being rejected at the framing layer — the decoder is in the read path where forward-compat matters more than strict rejection, matching the same discipline `vehicle_position::FlightState`, `sensor_status::SensorType`, and `sensor_status::OperationalState` already use, and the proptest round-trip pins that any byte (including those that fall into `Other`) survives encode + decode bit-identical. Validation on decode is deliberately narrow: `storage_used_pct` must be finite AND fall in `[0.0, 100.0]` (NaN explicitly rejected because a naive range check silently accepts NaN — pinned by `decode_rejects_nan_storage_used_pct`); `link_bandwidth_kbps` and `link_latency_ms` must be finite AND non-negative (NaN explicitly rejected for both — pinned by `decode_rejects_nan_link_bandwidth_kbps` and `decode_rejects_nan_link_latency_ms`). Trailing bytes beyond the fixed length are explicitly ignored on decode — pinned by `decode_extra_trailing_bytes_are_ignored` — so a future protocol revision that appends a trailer keeps decoding the prefix unchanged. Nineteen new tests in `payload_status.rs::tests` cover the contract: round-trip via four hand-built fixtures (zero-valued, max-valued, mid-range, edge cases), a `proptest` round trip across 256 random domain samples (constrained to finite floats and the documented field ranges so the rejection-path tests own those edges), a hand-built golden-fixture decode (`decode_known_fixture_matches_expected_bytes`) that places every field at its documented byte offset and pins the IEEE-754 big-endian byte sequences for `50.0_f32` (`0x42480000`), `1024.0_f32` (`0x44800000`), and `10.0_f32` (`0x41200000`) plus the literal hex bytes for `payload_id` and `timestamp_unix_ms` (a regression that swapped to little-endian could pass round-trip and proptest but would still fail this golden-fixture check), six rejection tests (`decode_rejects_negative_storage_used_pct`, `decode_rejects_storage_used_pct_above_100`, `decode_rejects_nan_storage_used_pct`, `decode_rejects_negative_link_bandwidth_kbps`, `decode_rejects_nan_link_bandwidth_kbps`, `decode_rejects_negative_link_latency_ms`, `decode_rejects_nan_link_latency_ms`), a truncation sweep over `[0, 1, 7, 16, 23, 31]`-byte inputs pinning the `FrameTooShort` variant, three categorical-enum round-trip tests (one per enum: a named-variant table plus `Other(byte)` preservation contract). Crate test count goes from 32 to 51. **Out of scope for this PR**: `system_state`, `BIT reports` (which round out the LOI 2-3 telemetry surface beyond the three primary read-side frames), LOI 4+ command messages (waypoint upload, sensor pointing, GCS handover, payload control), and UDP/TCP listener wiring — each of those is a separate follow-up PR. Builds on #1147 (vehicle_position) and #1155 (sensor_status) and uses the same module structure, error variants, and test discipline so an operator who has reviewed the first two frames' codecs sees no surprises in the third.
- **STANAG 4586 LOI 2-3 sensor-status telemetry message (refs #1122)** — adds the second LOI 2-3 telemetry frame to the `rustgate-stanag4586` crate (the first, `vehicle_position`, shipped with #1147). The two messages are emitted from the same Vehicle Specific Module at different rates: vehicle-position streams at 10–50 Hz so a moving-map can render the platform smoothly, while sensor-status streams at 1–5 Hz because the sensor's pointing state changes far less frequently than the platform's position; together they give a LOI 2 deployment everything it needs to display, log, and relay the inbound vehicle and sensor state. New public surface: `pub fn sensor_status::encode(&SensorStatus) -> Vec<u8>`, `sensor_status::encode_into(&SensorStatus, &mut BytesMut)` for the zero-extra-allocation path, `sensor_status::decode(&[u8]) -> Result<SensorStatus, Stanag4586Error>`, the convenience `SensorStatus::encode_to_vec`, plus the typed `SensorStatus { sensor_id, sensor_type, operational_state, azimuth_deg, elevation_deg, field_of_view_deg, timestamp_unix_ms }`, the `SensorType { ElectroOptical, Infrared, SyntheticApertureRadar, Lidar, SignalsIntelligence, Other(u8) }` modality enum, and the `OperationalState { Off, Standby, Operational, Calibrating, Failed, Other(u8) }` health enum. Wire format is fixed-length 32 bytes with NATO big-endian byte order: `sensor_id` (u32, offset 0), `sensor_type` (u8, offset 4), `operational_state` (u8, offset 5), 2 reserved zero-padded bytes, `azimuth_deg` (f32, offset 8), `elevation_deg` (f32, offset 12), `field_of_view_deg` (f32, offset 16), 4 reserved zero-padded bytes, `timestamp_unix_ms` (u64, offset 24). The two reserved blocks are zero-filled on encode but the decoder does NOT validate them as zero so a future spec revision that allocates them stays backward-compatible at the frame-length level. Both sensor-modality and operational-state enums carry an `Other(u8)` forward-compat catch-all preserving the raw wire byte so a firmware revision that introduces a new sensor type or state stays decodable rather than being rejected at the framing layer — the decoder is in the read path where forward-compat matters more than strict rejection, and the proptest round-trip pins that any byte (including those that fall into `Other`) survives encode + decode bit-identical. Validation on decode is deliberately narrow: `field_of_view_deg` must be strictly positive AND finite (NaN is explicitly rejected because a naive `<= 0` comparison silently accepts NaN — pinned by `decode_rejects_nan_field_of_view`); azimuth and elevation are NOT range-checked because senders use signed or unwrapped values during slew integration and downstream consumers normalise as needed. Trailing bytes beyond the fixed length are explicitly ignored on decode — pinned by `decode_extra_trailing_bytes_are_ignored` — so a future protocol revision that appends a trailer keeps decoding the prefix unchanged. Fourteen new tests in `sensor_status.rs::tests` cover the contract: round-trip via four hand-built fixtures (zero-valued, max-valued, mid-range, edge cases), a `proptest` round trip across 256 random domain samples (constrained to finite floats and a `f32::MIN_POSITIVE..1_000_000.0` FOV range so the rejection-path tests own those edges), a hand-built golden-fixture decode (`decode_known_fixture_matches_expected_bytes`) that places every field at its documented byte offset and pins the IEEE-754 big-endian byte sequences for `1.0_f32`/`2.0_f32`/`3.0_f32` plus the literal hex bytes for `sensor_id` and `timestamp_unix_ms` (a regression that swapped to little-endian could pass round-trip and proptest but would still fail this golden-fixture check), three rejection tests (`decode_rejects_zero_field_of_view`, `decode_rejects_negative_field_of_view`, `decode_rejects_nan_field_of_view`), a truncation sweep over `[0, 1, 7, 24, 31]`-byte inputs pinning the `FrameTooShort` variant, two `SensorType` round-trip tests (named-variant table + `Other(byte)` preservation contract), and the matching pair for `OperationalState`. Crate test count goes from 18 to 32. **Out of scope for this PR**: `payload_status` (the third LOI 2-3 telemetry frame called out in #1122), `system_state`, `BIT reports`, LOI 4+ command messages (waypoint upload, sensor pointing, GCS handover, payload control), and UDP/TCP listener wiring — each of those is a separate follow-up PR. Builds on #1147 (vehicle_position) and uses the same module structure, error variants, and test discipline so an operator who has reviewed the first frame's codec sees no surprises in the second.
- **MQTT will-publish audit event + Prometheus counter (refs #880)** — adds operational observability to the will-publish path landed with #1150. New `rustgate_core::audit::mqtt_will_published(cn, topic, group, retain)` audit event under tag `mqtt.will_published` (event level: `info`, target: `audit`) records the broker's decision to fire a will whenever a session ends ungracefully (TLS error, keep-alive timeout, write-loop early exit, abrupt TCP close — any path that is NOT a clean DISCONNECT). New `rustgate_mqtt_will_published_total` Prometheus counter increments once per published will. Wiring follows the existing metrics-agnostic-callback pattern: a new `OnMqttWillPublished` type alias on `MqttSessionHooks`, fired from a new `fire_will_published(hooks)` helper in `session.rs` after the will payload has been routed via `Router::route_for_egress`. Both the audit event and the metric fire AFTER the route call so the SIEM trail and the dashboard tally only the wills the broker actually committed to firing — no risk of double-counting on clean DISCONNECT (the publish_will gate at the session-end branch already filters that out) or on a session that exited before will validation completed. The audit event takes the disconnecting client's CN already-hashed via `hash_cn` and the topic / group already-sanitised via `sanitize_for_log`, matching the call-site PII and log-injection defenses used by the rest of the MQTT session crate. Operational signal: a spike in `mqtt_will_published_total` typically correlates with a partition or a fleet of clients hitting their keep-alive timeout — the dashboard shape is "presence-loss is happening at scale, look at the network", distinct from `mqtt_publishes_total` which captures regular publish traffic. The audit event lets a SIEM correlate ungraceful disconnects with the will-publish that followed them, useful when a will carries presence-loss semantics that downstream subscribers act on (a tactical client dropping off the network triggers a will, the SIEM trail records exactly when the broker took that action and on which group, regardless of who eventually saw the message). Server-side wiring in `crates/rustgate-server/src/setup.rs` adds the `Arc::new(|| metrics::mqtt_will_published().inc())` callback to the `MqttSessionHooks` literal under `#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]`; the existing in-file metrics test that pins the hook-construction shape against an upstream type rename gains an assertion on the new field so a future refactor that drops the hook from `MqttSessionHooks` without dropping it from the wiring fails to compile rather than silently zeroing the counter. Test coverage: `audit::tests::test_mqtt_will_published` exercises every realistic call shape (hashed CN with a typical fleet topic, an unprefixed group name, both retain bit positions, plus the empty-string defensive corner) and the existing `MqttSessionHooks` Debug-impl test gains a `on_will_published: "Some(<cb>)"` assertion. Operationally additive: clients that never set the will flag see no behaviour change, the wire format is unchanged, and the existing `mqtt_publishes_total` / `mqtt_subscribes_total` counters keep their semantics. Builds on #1150 (will-publish implementation) and complements #1146 / #1153 (the retain-store hooks the will path also feeds via the same dispatch helper).

### Fixed

- **Cross-path replay-detection key for non-CoT messages binds to (cn, time, payload-hash) (closes #882)** — the `DedupCache` in `crates/rustgate-transport/src/dedup.rs` is the router's single source of truth for "has this message already been delivered via another ingress path". For CoT XML payloads the key was correctly composed of `(tenant, uid, payload)`, but for non-CoT payloads (protobuf, MAVLink frames, NATS-bridged JSON, raw binary) the cache fell through to `(tenant, "", payload)` — no sender identity, no time component, just the tenant and the payload bytes. Two failure modes followed. **First**, two different senders within the same tenant emitting byte-identical bytes at the same instant (e.g. a fleet of MAVLink HEARTBEATs from N drones, two protobuf telemetry frames whose serialisation happens to match) were collapsed into a single delivery and N-1 of the messages were silently dropped without a `dropped_total` increment, only a `dedup_hits_total` tick — the dashboard showed "dedup is working" while real traffic was being lost. **Second**, the cache had no time component for non-CoT, so a legitimate retransmission within the LRU's residency window (in practice many minutes for a lightly-loaded cache far from `--dedup-cache-size`) was silently suppressed by an entry from much earlier — clients that legitimately re-sent a status frame after a network hiccup saw their second send disappear. **Third**, a non-CoT payload that happened to share bytes with a CoT XML payload could collide across the protocol boundary: the CoT path stored its key under the same SHA-256 preimage shape as the non-CoT path with a zero `time_le` slot, and an attacker who could observe whether their candidate non-CoT bytes were dedup-suppressed could probe for the existence of CoT messages from another sender. The fix introduces two domain-separated key preimages so the two paths cannot collide: CoT keys are `SHA-256(b"cot" || 0x00 || tenant || 0x00 || uid || 0x00 || payload)`; non-CoT keys are `SHA-256(b"non-cot" || 0x00 || tenant || 0x00 || cn || 0x00 || millis_window_le || 0x00 || sha256(payload))`. The leading domain tag (`b"cot"` / `b"non-cot"`) defeats cross-protocol probing — a non-CoT payload whose body bytes equal a CoT payload's body bytes still produces a different SHA-256 because the prefix differs. The `cn` slot is sourced from `RoutableMessage.source.cn` (the per-sender `Arc<str>` already routed through every dispatch decision) so two different senders no longer collide; intra-sender resends still suppress correctly because the same CN produces the same key. The `millis_window_le` slot is `received_at` floored to the dedup window in unix-millis (`(unix_ms / window_ms) * window_ms`), so a retransmission inside the same window correctly hits the cache (the bucket value matches) but a retransmission that crosses the window boundary lands in a fresh bucket and is admitted. The payload is hashed first and the SHA-256 digest is folded in (rather than the raw bytes) so the preimage stays bounded under the surrounding mutex on the hot path. The router's dispatch site (`route_inner` in `crates/rustgate-transport/src/router.rs`) switches from `dedup.check_payload(tenant, &msg.payload)` to `dedup.check_message(&msg)`, which inspects the payload for an extractable `uid=` attribute and routes through the CoT or non-CoT key path accordingly — XML messages whose `uid` is missing or whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 fall through to the non-CoT path so they still get the (cn, time, payload-hash) binding rather than the legacy `""` uid slot. Tenant isolation from #722 is preserved unchanged: the tenant slot is folded into both paths and the `with_cross_tenant(true)` opt-in still forces it empty. The legacy `check_and_insert(tenant, uid, payload)` and `check_payload(tenant, payload)` entry points stay in place but now compose the `b"cot"` prefix so the key shape is consistent across the two surface-level APIs — internal callers and tests that drive `check_and_insert` directly continue to work, just with a stronger key. Eight new unit tests in `dedup.rs::tests` pin the contract: `check_message_two_cns_same_non_cot_payload_pass_independently` (the load-bearing one — two MAVLink-style payloads from different CNs at the same instant are NOT collapsed, which would have been silently dropped pre-fix), `check_message_same_cn_same_non_cot_payload_within_window_is_deduped` (intra-sender dedup still works — the whole point of the cache), `check_message_same_cn_same_non_cot_payload_outside_window_passes` (a retransmission that crosses the dedup window is admitted, with a 100 ms window driven across the boundary so both the time-bucket binding and the LRU TTL backstop are exercised), `check_message_cot_and_non_cot_byte_collision_do_not_dedupe` (cross-protocol domain separation — a non-CoT payload sharing bytes with a CoT XML message cannot suppress it; pinned both at the dispatch level via `check_message` and at the key-builder level via direct `assert_ne!(build_cot_key(...), build_non_cot_key(...))`), `build_cot_key_domain_prefix_is_pinned` and `build_non_cot_key_domain_prefix_is_pinned` (manual SHA-256 reconstruction of the preimage so a future refactor that reorders fields or drops the domain tag fails locally without standing up a router), `window_truncated_millis_floors_to_window_boundary` (sweep test pinning that two timestamps inside the same 5 s window share a bucket and a third one in the next window does not), `window_truncated_millis_zero_window_returns_raw_millis` (no division-by-zero footgun with `Duration::ZERO`), and `window_truncated_millis_pre_unix_epoch_returns_zero` (clock-skew tolerance — a `received_at` before UNIX_EPOCH must not panic the hot path). Operationally additive: the wire format is unchanged, the `--dedup-window-secs` / `--dedup-cache-size` CLI flags keep their meaning, the `rustgate_dedup_hits_total` and `rustgate_dedup_cache_size` Prometheus metrics keep their semantics, and operators with dedup disabled (the default, `--dedup-window-secs=0`) see no change. The cache's hit rate may legitimately drop for non-CoT-heavy fleets where the pre-fix key was over-aggressive — that is the correct outcome, those "duplicates" were never duplicates. Closes the "shared NATS KV / cross-node replay state" half of section 19.9 is explicitly NOT addressed here and remains open as a separate future issue. Two complementary items from #882 already shipped: section 19.7 (obligation chaining) via #1236 and section 19.8 (point masking detail leakage) via #1234. Closes #882.
- **TLS `root_hint_subjects` rebuilt on CA rotation + `BackpressureGate` setter misordering surfaces as `Result` (closes #814, refs IMPROVEMENT-ANALYSIS.md F-50, F-51)** — two transport-layer correctness items that previously failed silently. **F-50 (post-rotation regression risk):** `DynamicCertVerifier` cached the initial `root_hint_subjects` slice at construction. After a SIGHUP-triggered trust-store reload added or rotated a CA, the inner `WebPkiClientVerifier` was rebuilt — but the hint slice the rustls handshake reads via `ClientCertVerifier::root_hint_subjects()` was not. Operators would observe "the new CA is loaded and chains under it validate, but RFC-strict and older rustls clients still won't present a chain anchored on it" because their `CertificateRequest` advertised the stale CA list and they had no signal that the new CA was acceptable. The fix replaces the cached `Vec<DistinguishedName>` with an `ArcSwap<&'static [DistinguishedName]>` that is rebuilt alongside the inner verifier on every trust-store generation advance; on rebuild failure the old hints stay in place so handshakes never advertise CAs whose keys we can no longer validate against. **F-51 (new error-returning signature):** `BackpressureGate::with_resume_dwell`, `set_on_deferred`, and `set_on_bytes_changed` previously used `Arc::get_mut` + `debug_assert!` + silent no-op. In release builds the `debug_assert!` is stripped, so calling any of the three setters after the gate had been cloned into the router and the accept loop dropped the configuration on the floor with no log, no panic, no error — the `admission_deferred_total` / `queued_bytes` gauges would freeze at zero while the gate was actively throttling, and an operator reading the dashboard would see "backpressure healthy" while connections were being refused. All three setters now return `Result<(), BackpressureConfigError::AlreadyShared { setter }>` naming the offending setter; callers handle the error explicitly (most are at startup before any clone and `expect("register before clone")` / propagate). Three new integration tests in `crates/rustgate-transport/tests/cert_rotation.rs` pin both contracts through the public re-export surface: `root_hint_subjects_rebuilds_after_ca_rotation` adds a second CA at runtime and asserts the hint count grows from one to two through the `Arc<dyn ClientCertVerifier>` boundary the listener actually consumes; `set_on_deferred_returns_err_after_clone` clones the gate first and asserts the setter returns an error whose `Display` names the offending setter so operators can grep their logs to the misordered call site; `set_on_deferred_succeeds_before_clone` pins the canonical startup ordering (wire callbacks first, then clone). The unit suites inside `verifier.rs` and `backpressure.rs` already covered the inline mechanics (`ArcSwap` swap discipline, `Arc::get_mut` setter semantics); the new integration tests pin the boundary so a refactor that broke the public re-export surface fails outside the modules it touches.
- **Federation store-forward persists post-hop-increment envelope (closes #763)** — the federation replay buffer in `crates/rustgate-federation/src/replay_buffer.rs` previously persisted each buffered message **before** the hop counter was incremented for re-emission, and the V2 reconnect-replay drain at `crates/rustgate-federation/src/v2/client.rs` constructed a fresh `FederationMetadata` from the raw on-disk payload at drain time. The result was an off-by-one inconsistency at the hop-limit boundary: a message admitted with `current_hops = max_hops - 1` (one short of the receive-side rejection boundary) was incorrectly allowed through on drain because the hop hadn't been bumped yet, even though a live emit at the same instant would have hit the boundary on the next hop. This PR moves the increment **before** persistence so the on-disk envelope reflects "what we will emit", and the drain hot-path evaluates the post-increment value uniformly with live emission. The on-disk value codec gains a wire-format change (`crates/rustgate-federation/src/replay_persist.rs`): a new v2 layout prefixes every record with the magic bytes `0xFF 0xFE` followed by a one-byte version tag and the post-increment `current_hops` `u32`. The two-byte magic cannot collide with a v1 (legacy) record because v1 starts with a Unix-millisecond timestamp encoded big-endian, whose high two bytes are always `0x00 0x00` for any plausible wall-clock value. On read, a v1 record (no magic) is surfaced through `RestoredEntry { is_legacy_pre_increment: true, current_hops: 0, .. }` and the V2 drain hot-path applies `+1` lazily before the limit check — existing on-disk records persisted by an older binary continue to be replayed, just with the boundary check applied as a post-#763 live emit would have applied it. The drain hot-path is split out as a testable `drain_decision_for(&BufferedMessage, max_hops) -> DrainDecision { Emit { effective_hops } | Drop { effective_hops } }` helper so the policy is unit-testable without standing up a full gRPC session — `tonic::Streaming` has no synthetic constructor and the drain's correctness is purely a function of the buffered envelope and the configured `max_hops`. Drop emits a structured `federation.event_rejected` audit record with `rpc=v2.replay_drain` / `reason=hop_limit`, mirroring the live `SendOneEvent` rejection path so the forensic trail captures both ingress hits and replay-time hits in the same shape. New unit tests pin the contract: `replay_persist::tests::store_forward_persists_post_increment_hops` (round-trip a `put(..., current_hops=3)` and assert `RestoredEntry::current_hops == 3` with the post-increment flag set), `replay_persist::tests::legacy_envelope_without_version_field_is_treated_as_pre_increment` (hand-build a v1 record by writing the legacy byte layout directly to redb and assert it surfaces as legacy on read), `replay_persist::tests::v2_round_trip_preserves_hop_count` (sweep the hop space `[0, 1, 5, 9, u32::MAX]`), `replay_persist::tests::value_magic_v2_is_pinned_to_ff_fe` (locks down the magic prefix so a future codec rev cannot silently invalidate every operator's on-disk record), `replay_persist::tests::decode_rejects_unknown_v2_version_byte` (refuses to parse future versions rather than silent mis-parse), `v2::client::tests::drain_rejects_message_at_hop_limit` (`current_hops = max_hops` is dropped, mirroring the live `>=` boundary), `v2::client::tests::drain_accepts_message_at_one_below_limit_inclusive` (`current_hops = max_hops - 1` is the last value that survives), `v2::client::tests::drain_accepts_message_below_hop_limit` (one step below the boundary is forwarded verbatim), `v2::client::tests::drain_legacy_envelope_applies_plus_one_lazily` (legacy `current_hops = max_hops - 1` lifts to `max_hops` and is dropped; legacy `current_hops = max_hops - 2` lifts to `max_hops - 1` and is emitted), `v2::client::tests::audit_emits_hop_limit_on_drain_drop` (uses a tracing-subscriber writer to capture the audit-target output and assert `federation.event_rejected` with `rpc=v2.replay_drain` and `reason=hop_limit` lands on the drop path), and `v2::client::tests::store_forward_persists_post_increment_hops` (buffer-layer view: `push_with_hops(..., 3)` produces an in-memory `BufferedMessage` and an on-disk record both at hops=3, no legacy flag). The fix is operationally additive — operators with persistent replay enabled continue to drain on reconnect; the change is invisible to the wire format between federation peers (the V2 protobuf hops field is unchanged) and only alters the on-disk codec, with full backward compatibility for records persisted by pre-#763 binaries. Closes #763.
- **MQTT SUBSCRIBE QoS 2 fall-through no longer aborts the broker (closes #751)** — the post-authorize match arm in `handle_subscribe_v5` (`crates/rustgate-mqtt/src/session.rs`) terminated the `QoS::ExactlyOnce` branch with `unreachable!()`. Although an upstream guard at the top of the per-filter loop already short-circuits QoS 2 SUBSCRIBEs with `SubscribeReasonCode::ImplementationSpecific` and a `continue`, the `unreachable!()` was fragile against any refactor that touched the guard — and `clippy::panic = "deny"` notwithstanding, an `unreachable!()` reached at runtime is a process abort in release profile, the worst possible outcome on a security-sensitive ingress path. Replaces the panic-source with a graceful fall-through that logs at `tracing::debug!` (sanitized CN + filter for forensics) and returns `SubscribeReasonCode::Unspecified` (MQTT 5.0 §3.9.3 reason 0x80 — "the subscription is not accepted and the Server either does not wish to reveal the reason or none of the other Reason Codes apply"), the spec-defined catch-all that keeps the broker running and the SUBSCRIBE rejected if the upstream guard ever moved. New regression test `subscribe_with_qos_exactly_once_returns_implementation_specific` in `crates/rustgate-mqtt/tests/mqtt_integration.rs` pins the spec-correct SUBACK reason code so a future refactor that silently downgrades QoS 2 to QoS 1, or drops the upstream guard, fails the assertion rather than the broker process. No wire-format change; QoS 2 SUBSCRIBEs were already rejected and continue to be rejected with the same reason code on the wire.
- **`rustgate_cot::mask::strip_coordinates` self-stability under hostile XML attribute values** — the weekly extended-fuzz job (`cot_mask_strip_coordinates`) found an input on `main` where `strip_coordinates(input)` returned `Ok(bytes)` whose own next parse attempt failed with quick_xml `error while parsing attribute: position 102: attribute key must be directly followed by '=' or space`. Root cause: quick_xml's reader is permissive about attribute values that contain the byte that is **not** the wrapping quote (e.g. a value wrapped in `'...'` may freely contain a literal `"` byte), but its writer always emits attribute values wrapped in `"..."` and does **not** escape inner `"` characters. The result is that one read followed by one write of an attribute whose `'`-quoted value contained `"` characters produces a byte sequence whose next read fails — exactly the case the fuzz target's "second pass must succeed" invariant was designed to catch. The fix is a **defensive output-validation pass** appended to `strip_coordinates`: after the writer finishes, the function re-parses its own output via `quick_xml::Reader` AND iterates `.attributes()` on every `Start`/`Empty` event so attribute syntax errors surface in pass 1 rather than crashing the next consumer's pass 2 (the lazy attribute-parsing model means a top-level `read_event_into` walk alone is insufficient — the original `mask_point_attrs` hot path triggers the error only when it iterates the attribute list, so the validator must do the same). Any failure in the verification walk surfaces as `MaskError::Xml(_)`, which the per-recipient delivery path already documents as fail-closed: the caller drops the payload rather than forwarding bytes that might leak coordinates back to a receiver whose parser disagrees with ours. This matches the function's pre-existing contract: "a sender that emits `<event><point …/>` and then truncates … must NOT leak coordinates via pass-through recovery". Cost is one extra single-pass quick_xml walk over the masker's output — microseconds for a typical CoT event (≤2 KiB) and absent for the fast-path "non-XML payload, return verbatim" branch which never enters the writer at all. The original crash artifact is committed as a fuzz corpus seed at `fuzz/corpus/cot_mask_strip_coordinates/seed-weekly-fuzz-crash-27a80e9c` so the same input is replayed every fuzz cycle. Two new unit tests pin the contract: `weekly_fuzz_crash_27a80e9c_fails_closed_on_unwriteable_attribute_value` (feeds the exact 232-byte crash input as a literal byte vector and asserts the masker either returns `Err(MaskError::Xml(_))` OR produces output that itself re-parses cleanly — the test allows either outcome so a hypothetical future quick_xml fix that emits round-trippable bytes does not cause a regression on this test, while what is NOT acceptable — bytes the masker itself cannot read back — is rejected), and `output_is_always_re_acceptable` (sweep test asserting that for every input, either pass 1 fails OR pass 1 succeeds AND pass 2 succeeds — pinning self-stability as a unit-level invariant so a regression fails locally without the fuzzer in the loop). Discovered by [run #24922732689](https://github.com/rchiofalo/rustgate/actions/runs/24922732689) at 04:38 UTC against `main` `8e52e877`.

### Added

- **MQTT packet-ID wrap-around regression coverage (refs #880)** — pins the broker's pkid echo path against u16 boundary regressions. MQTT 5.0 §1.5.4 / 3.1.1 §2.3.1 reserves Packet Identifier 0 as "no packet identifier" and uses the full 16-bit space `[1, 65535]` for any control packet that carries one. The broker echoes inbound pkids in the matching ack (`PUBACK` for QoS 1 PUBLISH, `SUBACK` for SUBSCRIBE, `UNSUBACK` for UNSUBSCRIBE) without transforming them — a correct implementation, but one that is invisible to existing tests (the prior single QoS 1 test used `pkid=42` and never exercised the boundaries). Five new integration tests in `tests/mqtt_integration.rs` close that gap: `publish_qos1_pkid_max_u16_round_trips_in_puback` (the upper edge — pkid = `u16::MAX = 65535`, exactly where a naive `+1` increment would wrap to `0` instead of staying at `65535`), `publish_qos1_pkid_one_round_trips_in_puback` (the lower edge — pkid = 1, the smallest legal pkid), `publish_qos1_round_trips_pkids_across_wraparound_boundary` (sequence test stepping `[65534, 65535, 1, 2]` to simulate a high-throughput client whose own pkid counter wraps mid-stream — every PUBACK must echo the exact pkid sent so a regression that stored pkids in a `u8`, an `i16`, or applied `wrapping_add` somewhere in the dispatch path fails loudly), `subscribe_pkid_max_u16_round_trips_in_suback` (SUBSCRIBE → SUBACK echo at the upper edge), and `unsubscribe_pkid_max_u16_round_trips_in_unsuback` (UNSUBSCRIBE → UNSUBACK echo at the upper edge). The three packet-type echo paths are covered symmetrically so a regression in any single dispatch arm — not just the PUBLISH path — fails as well. No production code change in this PR: the audit confirmed the existing echo paths in `handle_publish_v5` (`session.rs:1065-1077`), `handle_publish_v4` (`session.rs:1169-1180`), `handle_subscribe_v5/v4`, and `handle_unsubscribe_v5/v4` are already correct (they pass `publish.pkid` / `sub.pkid` / `unsub.pkid` straight through without arithmetic), but the broker now has executable proof of correctness across the full 16-bit boundary set so a future refactor that introduces a wrap-around bug cannot land silently. Closes the "Packet ID Wrap-Around" audit item from #880; QoS 2 (PUBREC/PUBREL/PUBCOMP) and full session-persistence work continue in follow-ups.
- **MQTT retain-store Prometheus metrics (refs #880)** — three new counters that surface the operational shape of the broker's last-known-value cache wired up in #1146: `rustgate_mqtt_retain_stored_total` increments on every PUBLISH that inserted or overwrote a retained entry (retain=1, non-empty payload), `rustgate_mqtt_retain_cleared_total` on every spec-mandated zero-byte clear (retain=1, zero-length payload, MQTT 5.0 §3.3.1.3), and `rustgate_mqtt_retain_replayed_total` per delivered retained PUBLISH on a fresh subscriber's matching SUBSCRIBE filter (incremented *per delivered message*, not per SUBSCRIBE — a wildcard subscribe expanding to N retained topics produces N increments). Wiring follows the existing metrics-agnostic-callback pattern that the MQTT crate already uses for its publish/subscribe accept/reject counters: three new `OnMqttRetainStored`/`OnMqttRetainCleared`/`OnMqttRetainReplayed` type aliases (`Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>`) on `MqttSessionHooks`, fired from new `fire_retain_outcome(hooks, RetainOutcome)` and `fire_retain_replayed(hooks)` helpers in `session.rs`. The retain-outcome dispatch is centralised in one helper so all three publish call sites (the live `handle_publish_v5` and `handle_publish_v4` paths, plus the `publish_will_message` retained-will path landed with #1150) share one branch matrix — a regression that wired the wrong outcome variant to the wrong counter would surface in only one place rather than three. The replay hook fires inside the per-subscriber retained-PUBLISH loop in both `handle_subscribe_v5` and `handle_subscribe_v4` so a single SUBSCRIBE that matches three retained topics produces three increments, mirroring the existing `rustgate_mqtt_subscribes_total` per-filter semantics. The authorisation re-check in `collect_retained_for_filter` (the security gate landed with #1146) runs BEFORE the replay counter fires, so the metric only ever counts deliveries the subscriber was actually allowed to receive; an attacker who tries to inflate the counter via a wildcard subscribe across topics they have no group membership for cannot register an increment. Server-side wiring in `crates/rustgate-server/src/setup.rs` adds three `Arc::new(|| metrics::mqtt_retain_*().inc())` callbacks to the `MqttSessionHooks` literal under `#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]`; the existing in-file metrics test that pins the hook-construction shape against an upstream type rename gains assertions on the three new fields so a future refactor that drops a hook from `MqttSessionHooks` without dropping it from the wiring fails to compile rather than silently zeroing a counter. Five new unit tests in `session.rs::tests` pin the firing contract: `fire_retain_outcome_dispatches_stored_only_on_stored`, `fire_retain_outcome_dispatches_cleared_only_on_cleared`, `fire_retain_outcome_is_noop_on_passthrough` (the load-bearing one — a regression that fired stored/cleared on every PUBLISH would inflate the counter by 100x in typical traffic where most messages are not retained), `fire_retain_replayed_fires_only_its_own_callback`, and `fire_retain_helpers_nop_when_individual_callback_is_none` (defends partial population — operators can wire only stored/cleared and not replay, the replay helper must not spill onto the others). Operationally additive: clients that never use retain see no behaviour change, the wire format is unchanged, and the existing `rustgate_mqtt_publishes_total` / `rustgate_mqtt_subscribes_total` counters keep their semantics. Operators dividing `mqtt_retain_stored_total / mqtt_publishes_total` get a "fraction of traffic that is retain=1" gauge useful for capacity planning; a flat `mqtt_retain_cleared_total` while `mqtt_retain_stored_total` climbs is the operational signal that the retain store will keep growing for the listener's lifetime; and a `mqtt_retain_replayed_total` spike correlates with an operator opening a wide wildcard subscribe across the retain set. Builds on #1146 (retain-store implementation) and complements #1150 (will messages) — the will-publish retain path also feeds these counters via the same dispatch helper.
- **Federation V2 `SendOneEvent` audit + per-RPC ingress metric (refs #864)** —
  hardens the existing `FederatedChannel.SendOneEvent` unary handler in
  `crates/rustgate-federation/src/v2/server.rs` so every accepted or
  rejected event leaves a structured forensic trail and a counter
  increment, closing the observability gap that made the V2 unary
  ingress path effectively invisible to operators. The proto/.proto
  definition (`crates/rustgate-federation/proto/figpb/fig.proto`) and
  the wire handler were already in place from earlier V2 work; this PR
  finishes the operational wiring that was missing for production
  rollout: (1) a new `crate::metrics::messages_in_by_rpc` labelled
  counter (`rustgate_federation_messages_in_by_rpc_total{rpc}`) that
  splits ingress out per RPC method so dashboards can attribute load
  to `send_one_event` versus the streaming variants once those are
  wired (the existing unlabelled `rustgate_federation_messages_in_total`
  is also incremented for backward-compatible aggregate queries —
  pre-this-PR, *neither* counter had ever been incremented in
  production code), (2) two new `rustgate_core::audit` functions —
  `federation_event_received(rpc, peer_cn)` for the success path and
  `federation_event_rejected(rpc, peer_cn, reason)` for post-auth
  policy rejections — emitting structured records on the standard
  `target = "audit"` channel with `event_type` of
  `federation.event_received` and `federation.event_rejected`
  respectively. The audit emission ordering is load-bearing: the
  success record is written *before* the `on_event` callback fires so
  the forensic trail captures ingress even if downstream routing
  panics or drops the event mid-dispatch. Rejection records carry one
  of three stable `reason` tokens — `"hop_limit"` (event arrived with
  `current_hops >= MAX_FEDERATION_HOPS` or a negative count, returned
  as `Ok(Empty)` per V2 protocol semantics — the protocol cannot
  signal hop drops to the sender so the audit is the only forensic
  vantage point), `"unauthorized_group"` (peer is in the allowlist but
  the event claims a group the peer is not authorized for), or
  `"peer_not_in_allowlist"` (peer absent from the allowlist entirely)
  — so downstream alerting can split misconfiguration from Byzantine
  behaviour. mTLS-layer rejections are still captured by
  `federation_peer_rejected` (no double-audit on the unauthenticated
  path). The metric increment lives behind `#[cfg(feature = "api")]`
  because the federation crate's `metrics` module is itself only
  compiled under the `api` feature (the workspace-level `federation`
  feature implies both `v2` and `api`, so production builds always
  see the increments). Four new tests in
  `v2::server::tests::send_one_event_*` pin the contract:
  `send_one_event_routes_to_router_on_success` guarantees an
  authorized event reaches the registered `OnEvent` callback (which
  production wires through `manager::create_v2_event_handler` into
  the `Router::dispatch_inbound` pipeline as a synthetic
  `RoutableMessage` with `source_protocol = "federation"`),
  `send_one_event_emits_audit_on_failure` attaches a capturing
  tracing subscriber filtered to `target = "audit"` and asserts the
  rejected event produces a record containing
  `federation.event_rejected`, `send_one_event`, and
  `unauthorized_group`, `send_one_event_increments_metrics_counter`
  (gated on `feature = "api"`) reads the labelled counter
  pre-and-post and asserts a strict advance, and
  `send_one_event_rejects_unauthenticated` constructs a `tonic::Request`
  without the test-only `TestPeerCn` extension so the production
  `peer_id_from_request` path runs and refuses with `Unauthenticated`
  before any group/hop evaluation — this is the F-44 / #759 invariant
  that the previous IP-fallback behaviour silently violated. The
  metric advance assertion uses `>` rather than `==` because parallel
  tests share the global Prometheus registry. A new pub(crate)
  constant `RPC_SEND_ONE_EVENT = "send_one_event"` is the canonical
  label value so audit records and metric labels stay in lockstep
  with no string drift. **First in a series of PRs for issue #864**:
  the remaining V2 federation RPCs documented as "Missing" in the
  upstream protocol survey — `BinaryMessageStream`, `SendOneBlob`,
  `ClientROLStream`, `ServerROLStream`, `ClientFederateGroupsStream`
  and `ServerFederateGroupsStream` (full ROL / mission integration),
  `GetAuthTokenByX509`, and `Getx509Identity` — ship as follow-up PRs
  in the same series; the present PR establishes the audit + metric
  conventions those follow-ups will mirror so the four
  `send_one_event_*` tests serve as the template for each future
  handler's verification suite. Operationally additive: clients that
  do not call `SendOneEvent` see zero behaviour change, the
  `messages_in_by_rpc` counter starts at zero on first read for any
  unseen `rpc` label, and existing dashboards keyed on
  `rustgate_federation_messages_in_total` continue to work and now
  finally reflect actual ingress volume.
- **MQTT will messages (refs #880)** — implements the MQTT 3.1.1 §3.1.2.5 / 5.0 §3.1.2.5–3.1.3 last-will-and-testament semantics that `rustgate-mqtt` previously rejected at CONNECT. A client that sets the will flag in its CONNECT packet now has the configured payload published by the broker on its behalf when the connection ends **ungracefully** — TLS error, keep-alive timeout, write-loop early exit, or any other path that is NOT a clean DISCONNECT. The will publishes through `Router::route_for_egress` with the disconnecting client's `Identity` as the source, so it lands on every subscriber of the target group exactly as a live `PUBLISH` from that identity would, including the egress fan-out (NATS / federation / HTTP) wired through `MqttForwardingHooks` — operators do not need to plumb a parallel "will egress" path. The will is **NOT** published when the client sends a clean DISCONNECT: in MQTT 3.1.1 any `DISCONNECT` is graceful (§3.14), and in MQTT 5.0 a `DISCONNECT` with `NormalDisconnection` reason code (0x00) suppresses the will (§3.14.4); the dedicated `DisconnectWithWillMessage` reason code (0x04) is honoured per §4.13 — a v5 client that wants to flag an unexpected shutdown but still notify the broker can request a will publish on a graceful disconnect by using that reason code. **Authorization is enforced at CONNECT time** via the same `topic::validate_publish_topic` + `topic_to_group` + `Identity::is_member_of` chain as a live PUBLISH: a will targeting a group the client is not a member of rejects the CONNECT with `NotAuthorized` (v5: `ConnectReturnCode::NotAuthorized`; v4: same code, since 3.1.1 has no dedicated reason for this), a will whose topic contains MQTT wildcards or is otherwise malformed rejects with `TopicNameInvalid` (v5; v4 collapses to `NotAuthorized` since the v3.1.1 CONNACK code set has no syntax-error variant), and a will requesting QoS 2 is rejected via `TopicNameInvalid` because the broker still does not implement the four-step PUBREC/PUBREL/PUBCOMP handshake. The validated `Will { topic, group, payload, retain }` is captured at the end of the handshake and threaded through the session lifetime; the topic-to-group resolution is cached on the struct so the publish path at session end does not re-resolve. Will retain semantics are honoured per §3.1.2.7 / §3.1.3.5: a will with `retain=true` updates the shared `RetainStore` before routing, so a client subscribing **after** the disconnect receives the will payload via the retain replay path — the security-critical authorization re-check on the retain replay (introduced with the retained-messages PR earlier in this series) still applies, so a stored will can never leak to a subscriber outside the original group. The clean-disconnect detection required a small codec workaround: `mqttbytes 0.6.0` incorrectly returns `Error::PayloadRequired` for the standard MQTT 5.0 `0xE0 0x00` wire form of a `NormalDisconnection`-with-no-properties DISCONNECT (the v5 read function omits `Disconnect` from its zero-remaining-length whitelist while v4 includes it correctly), which would otherwise have mis-classified every conformant v5 clean disconnect as a malformed packet and fired the will spuriously; `try_parse` now pre-detects the literal two-byte sequence and synthesises the matching `Disconnect::new()` packet so the read loop sees `ReadLoopOutcome::CleanDisconnect` and the will-suppression branch fires correctly. The session loop's outcome dispatch was refactored to a small `enum SessionEnd { Read(_), Write(_) }` over the two `tokio::select!` arms so the publish-vs-suppress decision can be made on a single match against the disconnect cause; the prior `Result<(), MqttError>` shape could not distinguish "read loop returned cleanly" from "write loop ended early" — both ungraceful sources of session end that must trigger the will if one is configured. Out of scope for this PR (deferred to follow-ups in the #880 series): the QoS 2 four-step handshake (PUBREC/PUBREL/PUBCOMP), MQTT 5.0 session expiry interval (§3.1.2.11) — clean-session is still required for now — and packet-ID wrap-around audit. Four new integration tests in `tests/mqtt_integration.rs` pin the on-the-wire behaviour against a real TLS listener with mTLS: `will_published_on_ungraceful_disconnect` (Alice connects with a will targeting `alpha`, abruptly drops her TLS stream without DISCONNECT, Bob — subscribed to `alpha` — must receive the will payload within 2s), `will_not_published_on_clean_disconnect` (Alice connects with a will, sends `Disconnect { reason_code: NormalDisconnection }` cleanly, then closes; Bob must NOT receive the will within a 400ms grace window — pins the v5 clean-disconnect codec workaround end-to-end), `will_validation_rejects_unauthorized_topic` (Alice — member of `alpha` only — sends CONNECT with a will targeting `bravo`; the broker must respond with `ConnAck { code: NotAuthorized }` so the will cannot be used to bypass per-group authz), and `will_with_retain_flag_persists_to_retain_store` (Alice connects with `will_retain=true`, abruptly drops; Bob subscribes after Alice is gone and receives the will via the retain replay path with `retain=true` set on the wire — pins both the will publish and the retain-store wiring at session end). Operationally additive for clients that never set the will flag: the existing 186-test MQTT suite still passes, the wire format is unchanged for non-will sessions, and the only observable change for existing deployments is that a CONNECT with a will is now accepted and processed instead of being rejected with the long-deprecated `WillUnsupported` error — which has been replaced by `WillRejected(String)` carrying the validation reason for operators who want to grep audit logs for the precise rejection cause. Second of the MQTT 5.0 production-completeness PRs for #880 (after retained messages); QoS 2 and session expiry follow.
- **STANAG 4586 LOI 2-3 vehicle position telemetry codec (refs #1122)** — new workspace member `rustgate-stanag4586` providing the encode/decode pair for the LOI 2-3 vehicle position frame, the inbound vehicle-state stream that any LOI 2 deployment needs to display, log, and relay. Targets the publicly documented STANAG 4586 vehicle-state structure (latitude/longitude in WGS-84 decimal degrees, altitude MSL in metres, ground speed in m/s, true heading in degrees, plus a discrete flight-state enum, a 32-bit GCS-assigned `vehicle_id`, and a 64-bit Unix-millis platform timestamp); the wire format is fixed-length at 48 bytes with NATO big-endian byte order and two reserved zero-padded regions (3 bytes between flight state and the lat/lon block to keep the f64 fields 8-byte aligned, 4 bytes between the heading f32 and the timestamp u64) so a future protocol revision can allocate them without breaking length-based framing. Public surface is two free functions and one method-style wrapper: `vehicle_position::encode(&VehiclePosition) -> Vec<u8>`, `vehicle_position::encode_into(&VehiclePosition, &mut BytesMut)` for the zero-extra-allocation path when the encoded frame is the body of a larger packet, `vehicle_position::decode(&[u8]) -> Result<VehiclePosition, Stanag4586Error>`, and the convenience `VehiclePosition::encode_to_vec`. The `FlightState` enum carries five named variants (`LaunchPreparation`, `Loiter`, `Transit`, `ReturnToBase`, `Landed`) plus a forward-compat `Other(u8)` catch-all so a firmware revision that introduces a new state byte stays decodable rather than being rejected at the framing layer — the decoder is in the read path where forward-compat matters more than strict rejection, and the round-trip property test pins that any byte (including ones that fall into `Other`) survives encode + decode bit-identical. Validation on decode is deliberately narrow: lat ∈ [-90, 90] and lon ∈ [-180, 180] are checked (NaN explicitly rejected because a naive range check would silently accept it), altitude allows negative values (Death Valley, water-borne platforms), heading is not range-checked because senders may transmit signed or unwrapped values during turn integration, and unrecognised flight-state bytes are accepted into `Other(byte)` rather than producing an error. Truncation surfaces as `Stanag4586Error::FrameTooShort { actual, expected }` with the byte counts so log readers can correlate without guessing. Trailing bytes beyond the fixed length are explicitly ignored on decode — pinned by `decode_extra_trailing_bytes_are_ignored` — so a future protocol revision that appends a trailer keeps decoding the prefix unchanged. Eighteen tests cover the contract: a per-case round trip across four hand-built fixtures (zero-valued, max-valued, mid-range with unknown flight state byte, signed-altitude edge case), a `proptest` round trip across the full random domain (constrained to the WGS-84 lat/lon range plus finite floats, since out-of-range and NaN rejection is exercised by their own dedicated tests), a hand-built golden fixture (`decode_known_fixture_matches_expected_fields`) that places every field at its documented byte offset and asserts the field-by-field decode result so a regression that swapped to little-endian or reordered fields fails loudly rather than relying on the round-trip self-consistency, three rejection tests (`decode_rejects_latitude_above_90`, `decode_rejects_longitude_below_neg180`, `decode_rejects_nan_latitude`), a truncation test that sweeps `[0, 1, 7, 24, 47]`-byte inputs and pins the dedicated error variant, two `FlightState` round-trip tests (`flight_state_to_byte_round_trips_for_known_variants` for the named-variant table, `flight_state_other_round_trips_arbitrary_byte` for the `Other(byte)` preservation contract), `flight_state_unknown_byte_falls_back_to_other` sweeping `[0x00, 0x06, 0x10, 0x42, 0xFF]` to pin the forward-compat behaviour, the load-bearing `encode_produces_documented_byte_layout` that asserts the exact byte values at every documented offset (a regression that secretly swapped to little-endian could pass the round-trip property and the golden fixture but would still fail this test because it pins the IEEE-754 big-endian byte sequences for lat=1.0, lon=2.0, alt=3.0, gs=4.0, hdg=5.0 and the literal `[0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44]` for the `vehicle_id` and `[0xDE, 0xAD, 0xBE, 0xEF, 0xCA, 0xFE, 0x00, 0x42]` for the `timestamp_unix_ms`), `encode_into_appends_without_clearing_destination` (the BytesMut-additive contract), and `encode_to_vec_method_matches_free_encode_function` (struct-method ↔ free-function output equality). Wired into the workspace via `[workspace.members]` and `[workspace.dependencies]` only — NO `stanag4586` feature gate is added to `rustgate-server` in this PR because no server-side code yet imports the codec, and `cargo-machete` would (correctly) flag the unused optional dependency. The server-side feature gate and the network listener that consumes the codec land together in the follow-up integration PR. **Spec accessibility note**: the full STANAG 4586 specification is NATO-restricted and not publicly distributable; the field set, ordering, value range, and byte-order conventions used here mirror the publicly documented vehicle-state structure as cited in NATO UCS interoperability technical references and open-source vendor implementations, with NATO's standard big-endian byte order. Specific byte offsets are documented inline in `vehicle_position.rs` so a deployment that has access to the controlled spec can verify each field against their authoritative copy; vendor-confirmed offsets vs spec-derived offsets are not separately marked because the publicly available material describes the message at the field-set level rather than the byte-offset level — operators with access to the controlled document should treat this codec as a starting reference and run their own conformance testing against the message types they need. **Out of scope for this PR**: LOI 4+ command messages (waypoint upload, sensor pointing, GCS handover, payload control), other LOI 2-3 telemetry message types beyond vehicle position (sensor status, payload status, system state, BIT reports), UDP/TCP listener wiring, and MAVLink wrapping for platforms that encapsulate STANAG 4586 over MAVLink rather than running native — each of those is a separate follow-up PR. First in the STANAG 4586 series; the receive side has to be exercised against real traffic before the LOI 4+ command surface ships.
- **ASTERIX CAT-062 binary surveillance-track codec (refs #1121)** — new workspace crate `rustgate-asterix` (under `crates/rustgate-asterix/`) implementing a decode-only parser for ASTERIX CAT-062 ("SDPS Track Messages"), the Eurocontrol surveillance data exchange standard for system-track updates emitted by Surveillance Data Processing Systems and counter-UAS radar trackers. The crate is wire-format only — no UDP listener, no `RoutableMessage`/Entity mapping (deliberately deferred to follow-up integration work tracked by #847), no encoder direction (production rustgate ingests ASTERIX, it does not synthesise it; receive-only halves the surface area and removes interop bugs). New public surface: `pub fn decode_cat062(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Cat062Track>, Cat062Error>`, plus the typed result types `Cat062Track`, `WgsPosition`, `CartesianVelocity`, `Mode3aCode`, `ModeCCode`, `TrackStatus`, and a `thiserror`-derived `Cat062Error` with six precise variants (`TruncatedDatablock`, `WrongCategory`, `LengthMismatch`, `DeclaredLengthTooSmall`, `TruncatedFspec`, `TruncatedField` — each carrying enough context that the future UDP listener can route truncations to a recoverable resync path and reject only the offending datablock rather than tearing down the multicast subscription). **Spec version**: implements the wire format and Field Reference Numbers (FRNs) defined by Eurocontrol document **SUR.ET1.ST05.2000-STD-12-01**, *"Eurocontrol Standard Document for Surveillance Data Exchange — Part 9: Category 062 (System Track Data)"*, **Edition 1.20** (March 2017). The generic datablock framing (CAT byte, 16-bit big-endian length, per-record FSPEC) is from Part 1 ("Generic ASTERIX Concept", SUR.ET1.ST05.2000-STD-01) §3.2 — the framing code is straightforward to lift if a later PR adds CAT-021 (ADS-B), CAT-048 (Mode-S radar), or CAT-150 (mil tracks). **Decoded fields** (the issue-#1121 minimum-viable subset): I062/070 Time of Track Information (FRN 4, fixed 3 bytes, LSB 1/128 s, decoded into `time_of_day_seconds: f64` UTC seconds-since-midnight), I062/105 Calculated Track Position in WGS-84 Coordinates (FRN 5, fixed 8 bytes — lat i32 BE + lon i32 BE — LSB `180 / 2^25` deg ≈ 5.36 × 10⁻⁶ deg ≈ 60 cm at the equator, decoded into `position_wgs84: WgsPosition { latitude_deg, longitude_deg }` in decimal degrees with the documented LSB conversion), I062/185 Calculated Track Velocity in Cartesian Coordinates (FRN 7, fixed 4 bytes — vx i16 BE + vy i16 BE — LSB 0.25 m/s, decoded into `velocity_cartesian: CartesianVelocity { vx_mps, vy_mps }` in metres/second; components are local Cartesian in the SDPS reference frame, vx eastward, vy northward), I062/060 Track Mode 3/A Code (FRN 9, fixed 2 bytes, decoded into `mode_3a_code: Mode3aCode { raw: u16, validation_failed, garbled, from_local_track }` — the V/G/L flag bits from the high octet plus the 12-bit transponder code from the low 12 bits, with `as_octal()` rendering the canonical 4-digit zero-padded octal form so emergency squawks like `7700`/`7600`/`7500` round-trip correctly), I062/040 Track Number (FRN 12, fixed 2 bytes, decoded into `track_number: u16` with the high nibble masked off because the spec reserves bits 16..13 of the wire field as zero), I062/080 Track Status (FRN 13, extended-length octet chain — first octet's MON/SPI/MRH/SRC/CNF flags decoded into `track_status: TrackStatus`, FX-chained extension octets recognised and skipped — the typed surface only exposes the leading-octet flags today; extension semantics land when a downstream consumer needs them), and I062/135 Calculated Track Barometric Altitude (FRN 19, fixed 2 bytes — bit 16 = QNH-applied flag, bits 15..1 = signed 15-bit two's-complement altitude, LSB 25 ft — decoded via the standard "shift-up-shift-down" sign-extension trick into `mode_c_altitude: ModeCCode { raw_25ft_units: i16 }` with `altitude_feet()` and `flight_level()` accessors so callers do not redo the LSB arithmetic at every site). **Skipped fields** (recognised by length, cursor advanced, no output): I062/010 (data source ID, 2), I062/015 (service ID, 1), I062/100 (Cartesian position, 6), I062/210 (acceleration, 4), I062/245 (target ID, 7), I062/200 (mode of movement, 1), I062/136 (measured FL, 2), I062/130 (geometric altitude, 2), I062/220 (climb/descent rate, 2), I062/270 (extended target size, FX-chain), I062/300 (vehicle fleet ID, 1), I062/120 (Mode 2 code, 2), I062/510 (composed track number, FX-chain ≥ 3), and the I062/RE / I062/SP length-prefixed wrappers. Compound items (I062/380, I062/290, I062/295, I062/390, I062/110, I062/500, I062/340) currently surface a typed `TruncatedField { item, .. }` error rather than silently desyncing the cursor — the parser is strict not lossy, and operators see a clear "we don't decode this yet" signal that lets follow-up PRs upgrade individual compound items to real decoders without changing the dispatch table; the next datablock recovers at the LEN boundary so a feed that uses compound items today is degraded but not wedged. **Forward compatibility**: FSPEC bits in the spare slots of the v1.20 UAP (FRN 2 in the first octet and FRN 29-32 in the fourth octet) are treated as no-ops and consume zero bytes — pinned by `decode_unknown_fspec_bit_skips_unsupported_field`, which sets the FRN 30 spare bit alongside FRN 12 and asserts the track number still decodes correctly. FRNs beyond the v1.20 UAP (FRN > 34) are likewise no-ops at the dispatch layer — pinned by `decode_unknown_fspec_bit_beyond_uap_does_not_panic`. A future spec edition that allocates one of those bits to a real field will mis-decode here, but **so will every other parser in the wild** — there is no way to recover field length from the FSPEC alone, and producing a typed error here would force every operator to update on every spec bump. **Endianness**: ASTERIX is big-endian end-to-end; every multi-byte integer (datablock length, signed coordinates, velocities, track number) is decoded with `from_be_bytes`. **Multi-record datablocks**: a single ASTERIX datablock can carry N records of the same category (Eurocontrol Part 1 §3.2). The parser walks records sequentially using the datablock LEN as the outer terminator, returning a `Vec<Cat062Track>` — pinned by `decode_multi_record_datablock_returns_all_records`, which builds three records each carrying just FRN 12 and asserts every track number round-trips. **Sixteen unit tests** in `cat062.rs` `mod tests` pin the contract: `decode_minimal_track_returns_track_number` (FRN 12 alone — minimum-viable decode), `decode_minimal_track_masks_high_nibble_of_track_number` (defends the spec-reserved high-nibble mask against a producer bug that stuffs values into bits 16..13), `decode_full_track_returns_position_and_velocity` (every FRN in the issue-#1121 subset present in one record — round-trip lat/lon/vx/vy/mode-3A/track-number/status/altitude with explicit LSB conversions and tolerances), `decode_multi_record_datablock_returns_all_records` (3-record datablock — pin the outer-loop record-walking), `decode_truncated_frame_returns_error` (declared LEN exceeds buffer — `LengthMismatch`), `decode_short_buffer_below_minimum_returns_truncated_datablock` (buffer < 4 bytes — `TruncatedDatablock`), `decode_wrong_category_returns_error` (CAT byte ≠ 62 — `WrongCategory`), `decode_declared_length_below_minimum_returns_error` (LEN < 4 — `DeclaredLengthTooSmall`), `decode_field_truncation_inside_record_returns_error` (FSPEC says FRN 5 present but body too short — `TruncatedField { item: 105, need: 8, .. }`), `decode_unknown_fspec_bit_skips_unsupported_field` and `decode_unknown_fspec_bit_beyond_uap_does_not_panic` (forward-compat — spare and out-of-UAP bits no-op), `decode_mode_c_negative_altitude_sign_extends` (15-bit two's-complement sign-extension for FL−10 — pin the shift-up-shift-down trick against an off-by-one bit-width regression), `mode_3a_formats_as_zero_padded_octal` (4-digit padded display string for low-value codes), `mode_3a_emergency_codes_decode_correctly` (the universal 7700 emergency squawk round-trips — operationally critical for ATC/counter-UAS displays), `fspec_parser_handles_chained_octets` (multi-octet FX-chain with mid-chain bits set), and `fspec_parser_rejects_truncated_chain` (FX bit set with no following octet — `TruncatedFspec`). Tests use a `fspec_with_frns(frns: &[usize])` helper that mechanically computes the canonical FSPEC bit layout from a list of FRN numbers, so every fixture is authored from the spec and not by hand-encoding bits — a regression in the helper's encoding maths fails loudly on the asserted equality of the helper output against the manually-computed expected FSPEC. **Workspace wiring**: the new crate is added to `[workspace.members]` and `[workspace.dependencies]` in the root `Cargo.toml` so other crates can later depend on `rustgate-asterix` via workspace inheritance. NO feature flag is added to `rustgate-transport` or `rustgate-server` in this PR because no code in those crates yet uses the codec — `cargo-machete` would (correctly) flag the unused dependency. The transport-side feature gate and the UDP listener that consumes it land together in the follow-up integration PR. The crate ships only `thiserror` as a runtime dependency — no `rustgate-core`, no `tokio`, no `bytes`, no `tracing` — matching the "pure decode library, no I/O" scope and keeping the dependency footprint minimal so downstream crates pulling in CAT-062 do not pay for transport plumbing they will never use. Operationally additive: no behaviour change for any existing build; the codec is dormant until a follow-up PR (#1122 or similar) wires up the UDP multicast listener and the `Cat062Track → Entity` mapping. First of an expected series of ASTERIX category PRs covering counter-UAS surveillance integration; CAT-021 (ADS-B), CAT-048 (Mode-S radar), and CAT-150 (mil track) become sibling modules behind the same `decode_*` entry-point shape when operationally needed.
- **MQTT retained messages (refs #880)** — implements the MQTT 3.1.1 §3.3.1 / 5.0 §3.3.1.3 retain semantics that `rustgate-mqtt` previously dropped on the floor. A `PUBLISH` packet with `retain=1` now causes the broker to store the payload (keyed by topic) in a process-local `RetainStore` (`crates/rustgate-mqtt/src/retain.rs`); a subsequent `SUBSCRIBE` with a matching topic filter receives the stored payload as a `PUBLISH` packet immediately after the `SUBACK`, with the wire-level `retain` flag set per spec so the client can distinguish a retained replay from a fresh publication. The store is single-instance, shared across every accepted session for the lifetime of the listener (mirrors the existing `ClientIdRegistry` pattern); it is created inside `MqttServer::run` and threaded through `handle_mqtt_session` → `ReadLoopParams` into both `handle_publish_{v5,v4}` and `handle_subscribe_{v5,v4}`. **Spec-compliant clear-on-empty-payload**: a `PUBLISH` with `retain=1` AND a zero-byte payload removes any existing entry for that topic (`RetainOutcome::Cleared`) — pinned by `publish_with_retain_and_empty_payload_clears_existing` and the integration test `retain_with_empty_payload_clears_existing`, both of which exercise the round-trip via two clients. **Spec-compliant QoS downgrade**: retained replays are sent at `min(publisher_qos, subscriber_qos)` per MQTT 5.0 §3.8.4, with a local `min_qos(a, b)` helper because `mqttbytes::QoS` does not implement `Ord` (the spec distinguishes 0/1/2 by behaviour, not by ordering). **Authorization is enforced on the replay path**: `collect_retained_for_filter` re-runs `topic_to_group` + `Identity::is_member_of` against every retained topic that matches a subscribe filter so a stale entry whose group the new subscriber is NOT a member of stays hidden — the security-critical `retain_does_not_leak_across_group_boundaries` integration test pins this by retaining a payload from an `alpha`-only client, then subscribing from an `bravo`-only client and asserting the retained payload does not appear within a 400ms grace window. Storage is a `parking_lot::Mutex<HashMap<String, RetainedMessage>>` where `RetainedMessage { payload: Bytes, qos: QoS }` — `Bytes` keeps clones cheap (atomic refcount bump, no copy) so the per-subscriber retained-PUBLISH fan-out does not duplicate the underlying buffer. The mutex is released BEFORE the per-subscriber send loop so the `parking_lot::Mutex`-across-`.await` deadlock footgun the workspace already lints against does not fire (`RetainStore::matching` collects an owned `Vec` and drops the lock before returning). **Persistence is process-local only**: restarts lose the cache; this matches what the MQTT spec requires (no durability mandate for retain) and the typical operational pattern where publishers re-send retained "last-known-value" on connect — the broader broker-wide session-persistence work for #880 (QoS 2 handshake, will messages, packet ID wrap-around) ships in follow-up PRs. **QoS 1 retained replay** uses pkid 0 — the spec allows this when the broker has not allocated a packet id, which is our case since we do not track per-subscriber retained-PUBLISH acks; full QoS 1 retained-replay round-trip ack tracking lands with the session-persistence work tracked under #880. **Ordering**: SUBACK is sent FIRST, then retained PUBLISHes, matching Mosquitto / HiveMQ behaviour — MQTT 5.0 §3.8.4 leaves the order implementation-defined, and putting SUBACK first ensures the client's subscription state is updated before the retained payloads land. Twelve new unit tests in `retain.rs` cover the store directly: `publish_with_retain_false_is_passthrough`, `publish_with_retain_and_payload_stores`, `publish_with_retain_and_empty_payload_clears_existing`, `publish_with_retain_and_empty_payload_on_unknown_topic_is_clear` (defensive — a clear on a nonexistent topic must not panic), `publish_overwrites_previous_entry` (newer overwrites older — only last-value semantics), `matching_returns_exact_topic_match`, `matching_supports_single_level_wildcard` (`+` expansion), `matching_supports_multi_level_wildcard` (`#` expansion), `matching_strips_topic_prefix_consistently` (broker-prefix coordinate-space alignment), `matching_with_filter_outside_prefix_returns_empty` (defensive — filter outside the broker prefix cannot match anything), `matching_returns_empty_on_no_matches`, and `matching_preserves_qos_in_retained_message`. Five new integration tests in `tests/mqtt_integration.rs` pin the on-the-wire behaviour against a real TLS listener with mTLS: `retained_publish_delivered_to_late_subscriber` (Alice retains then disconnects → Bob subscribes after and receives the payload with `retain=true` on the wire — the load-bearing semantic of the retain flag), `retain_with_empty_payload_clears_existing` (store, clear, subscribe — must yield no PUBLISH within a 500ms grace window), `retain_delivered_independently_to_multiple_subscribers` (two distinct subscribers both receive their own copy of the retained PUBLISH — pin against a regression that consumed entries on read), `non_retained_publish_does_not_persist` (PUBLISH with retain=0 must not enter the store — defends against an inverted-bit regression), and `retain_does_not_leak_across_group_boundaries` (cross-tenant authorization regression guard — Alice retains on `alpha`, Eve subscribes on her own `bravo` filter, must NOT see Alice's payload). The `RetainStore::publish` return value is a typed `RetainOutcome { Stored, Cleared, Passthrough }` so future audit/metrics call sites can branch on the outcome without re-reading the publish header. Operationally additive: clients that never set the retain bit observe zero behaviour change, the wire format is unchanged, and existing topic/filter validation, ACL membership checks, and authz PEPs all run on the retain path before the store is touched. First in a series of MQTT 5.0 production-completeness PRs for #880; QoS 2 (PUBREC/PUBREL/PUBCOMP), Will messages, session expiry, and packet-ID wrap-around hardening follow.
- **HTTP DLQ admin replay endpoint `POST /api/dlq/{target}/replay` (refs #881)** — operators can now trigger a manual DLQ drain for a specific HTTP egress target via the management REST API without waiting for the circuit breaker's `HalfOpen → Closed` recovery edge to fire automatically. Useful when (a) the circuit has been Closed for a while but a sealed segment is still on disk because the recovery happened before #1144 landed, (b) an operator has fixed a downstream issue out-of-band and wants to flush the backlog immediately rather than wait for the next failure-driven recovery cycle, or (c) they are validating a freshly deployed receiver against captured traffic. New public surface on `rustgate_http`: `HttpPublisher::trigger_drain(&self, target_name: &str) -> Result<(), TriggerDrainError>`, `HttpPublisher::target_names(&self) -> Vec<String>`, and the `pub enum TriggerDrainError { DlqNotConfigured, UnknownTarget, ChannelFull, ChannelClosed }` (with stable `Display` strings — pinned by `trigger_drain_error_display_strings_are_stable`). The trigger is a fire-and-forget signal on the same `mpsc::Sender<String>` channel the auto-recovery observer feeds, so manual and automatic drains share the same worker, the same audit trail, and the same metrics — no parallel path that could drift in behaviour. The `HttpPublisher` struct gains a top-level `drain_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<String>>` field populated only when DLQ is configured (the per-target circuit observers continue to clone their own senders on top), and the `mpsc::Receiver` is dropped synchronously when DLQ is absent so any clone of the per-target sender immediately observes `Err(Closed)` and falls through to the existing audit-log degradation. The `target_names` accessor lets the management API enumerate which `{target}` segments are routable for diagnostics or future autocomplete tooling. Inside `trigger_drain` the validation order is load-bearing: (1) `drain_tx.is_none()` → `DlqNotConfigured`, (2) `target_names` linear scan → `UnknownTarget` if no match, (3) `try_send` → `ChannelFull`/`ChannelClosed`/`Ok`.
