Alias bounds: `last_pong_is_send_sync_clone_static` uses `fn assert_bounds<T: Send + Sync + Clone + 'static>()` to pin the `LastPong = Arc<Mutex<Instant>>` alias's cross-task shareability — a regression to `Rc<RefCell<_>>` or a runtime-only mutex (`std::sync::Mutex<Instant>` is fine; `tokio::sync::Mutex` would break the across-`.await` lock rule) fails here at test-compile rather than at the first `tokio::spawn(async move { last_pong.clone() … })` site inside the read loop. Suite grows from 7 to 17 tests; zero changes to any production API — every new test drives only existing constructors and methods through their documented contracts. `cargo nextest run -p rustgate-websocket -E 'test(health)'` reports 16/16 passing (the new boundary test replaces the implicit coverage the existing "within window" test provided at the 14s-inside-15s case, so net visible growth is +9 in the module output); full-workspace clippy with the canonical feature-set from CLAUDE.md is clean. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-nats::subscriber` — `DEFAULT_LAG_POLL_INTERVAL` constant, `LagSnapshot` type-surface (Copy/Clone/Debug/Eq bounds, per-field equality, Debug field enumeration), callback alias Send+Sync+Clone bounds, `handle_lag_poll_result` latency-before-lag ordering + error-path asymmetry + None-latency branch + duration pass-through, `LagPollerGuard` abort-on-drop via `DropProbe`, `extract_group` edge cases (deep-subject first-segment-only, prefix-equal fallback, prefix-plus-trailing-dot, multi-segment-prefix round-trip, segment-anchoring byte-prefix defence), and `build_consumer_config` ack/deliver policy + durable-name agreement + multi-segment filter-subject + idempotence** — `crates/rustgate-nats/src/subscriber.rs` is the JetStream pull-consumer surface every rustgate NATS deployment flows through: it owns consumer configuration (`build_consumer_config`), subject→group extraction (`extract_group_from_subject`), the lag-monitoring poll loop (`handle_lag_poll_result`), the background-poller guard (`LagPollerGuard`), and the observable snapshot types (`LagSnapshot`, `LagCallback`, `LatencyCallback`) that operators reach for to wire Grafana dashboards against consumer-lag gauges. Before this PR the inline suite (12 tests) covered the happy-path lag-callback invocation, the `extract_group` standard / anon / no-prefix-match / custom-default / two-segment / empty-segment branches, three `build_consumer_config` max-deliver tests, and the `handle_lag_poll_result_error_then_ok_keeps_going` continuation case — but it left a significant amount of load-bearing contract surface unpinned, each branch a silent regression candidate. Twenty new inline tests close those gaps. Coverage layout: `default_lag_poll_interval_is_five_seconds` pins `DEFAULT_LAG_POLL_INTERVAL == Duration::from_secs(5)` so an accidental edit to the top-of-file constant fails here rather than silently shifting every production consumer's poll cadence — doubling would halve the observability resolution, halving would double the overhead on every JetStream API call; `lag_snapshot_has_copy_clone_debug_eq_bounds` uses a `fn assert_bounds<T: Copy + Clone + Debug + Eq + PartialEq>()` compile-time helper parameterised on `LagSnapshot` so a future refactor that added a non-Copy field (like a boxed error or a String description) fails at test-compile time rather than at the first call site in `rustgate-server::setup` that passes the snapshot by value through the lag callback; `lag_snapshot_equality_distinguishes_every_field` is the mutation-resistance test — it builds a base `LagSnapshot { num_pending: 10, num_redelivered: 5, ack_floor_stream_seq: 100 }` and constructs three mutants each flipping exactly one field (+1 on each), asserting all three are `!=` the base, so a refactor that accidentally narrowed the `PartialEq` derive (e.g. `#[derive(Eq, PartialEq)]` replaced with a manual impl that compared only two of the three fields) fails here rather than silently muting the Grafana alert that keys on `ack_floor_stream_seq` stalls; `lag_snapshot_debug_exposes_all_three_field_values` formats the snapshot via `{:?}` and asserts the output contains all three field names (`num_pending`, `num_redelivered`, `ack_floor_stream_seq`) and all three numeric values — operators grep `tracing::debug!(?snapshot, …)` for these tokens during triage, so the derive must stay `#[derive(Debug)]` (a manual impl that only exposed `num_pending` would look fine in the usual case but hide the redelivery count during an actual lag incident); `callback_aliases_are_send_sync_clone` compile-time-asserts `Send + Sync + Clone` on both `LagCallback` and `LatencyCallback` via a parameterised bound helper — the router stores these as `Arc<dyn Fn(...) + Send + Sync>` and clones them on every session spawn, so any future narrowing would break the transitive call chain at its leaves rather than at this helper; five `handle_lag_poll_result_*` tests pin the factored-out branch helper's contract: `handle_lag_poll_result_invokes_latency_before_lag_on_success` drives a success path with both callbacks wired to a shared `Vec<&'static str>` and asserts the post-call state is exactly `vec!["latency", "lag"]` (ordering matters because downstream Prometheus scrapers see latency and lag as separate metrics — a swap would invert the observed correlation between API round-trip time and consumer backlog, which is the canonical "is this slow because upstream is slow or because we are overwhelmed" triage question), `handle_lag_poll_result_error_fires_latency_but_not_lag` pins the error-path asymmetry (latency still measures the failed round-trip so ops can see "all API calls taking 30s" but lag cannot be inferred from a failed response, hence no lag-callback fire), `handle_lag_poll_result_without_latency_callback_still_invokes_lag` pins the `None`-latency-callback branch (deployments that only care about lag, not latency, must not crash and must still see their lag callback fire), and `handle_lag_poll_result_passes_elapsed_duration_verbatim` pins the `Duration` pass-through contract by sending a specific `Duration::from_millis(42)` and asserting the captured value is exactly that (a regression that rounded to whole milliseconds or added drift would fail here and manifest as Grafana quantiles that always rounded to nice numbers); `lag_poller_guard_aborts_wrapped_task_on_drop` is a `#[tokio::test]` using the `DropProbe(Arc<AtomicBool>)` pattern — it wraps a task that holds a `DropProbe` and loops forever on a `tokio::time::sleep`, constructs a `LagPollerGuard` around the `JoinHandle`, drops the guard, yields the runtime a handful of times for the abort propagation to complete, and asserts the `AtomicBool` was flipped to `true` by the probe's `Drop` impl (proving the aborted task's future was dropped, not merely "marked as cancelled") — this is the canonical guard-on-drop contract that every long-lived `LagPollerGuard` callsite in the server binary relies on to avoid orphaning background NATS polling tasks across a SIGHUP reload; five `extract_group_*` tests pin the subject→group extraction's defensive surface: `extract_group_deep_subject_returns_first_segment_only` feeds `"points.CYAN.position.update.v2"` and asserts the result is `"CYAN"` (first segment after the configured prefix, not the last or a concatenation — a regression that returned the full remainder would break every multicast routing table that keys on group-id), `extract_group_subject_equal_to_prefix_returns_default` feeds a subject equal to the prefix (`"points"`) and asserts the `__ANON__` fallback (no group can be extracted from a prefix-only subject), `extract_group_subject_is_prefix_plus_trailing_dot_returns_default` feeds `"points."` and asserts fallback (the empty segment after the dot is not a valid group), `extract_group_handles_multi_segment_prefix` pins the multi-segment-prefix round-trip (`"cot.live.BRAVO.update"` with prefix `"cot.live"` → `"BRAVO"`), and `extract_group_rejects_byte_prefix_that_is_not_a_segment` is the security-critical test — it feeds `"pointsx.GROUP.action"` with prefix `"points"` and asserts the result is the default fallback, not `"GROUP"`, pinning the segment-anchoring guard that exists specifically to prevent a naive `starts_with("points")` from confusing `pointsx` for `points` and silently routing an attacker-controlled subject into the wrong group's ACL scope (the same SPIFFE-prefix footgun the authz compiler normalises against); five `build_consumer_config_*` tests pin the consumer-config factory's derived contracts: `build_consumer_config_sets_ack_policy_explicit` pins `matches!(pull_config.ack_policy, AckPolicy::Explicit)` so a regression that silently flipped to `AckPolicy::None` would result in messages being acked on delivery rather than on processing completion (and silently losing data on downstream failure), `build_consumer_config_sets_deliver_policy_new` pins `matches!(deliver_policy, DeliverPolicy::New)` so a regression to `All` would cause every fresh consumer to replay the entire stream history on startup (and overwhelm downstream session state), `build_consumer_config_durable_name_matches_returned_consumer_name` asserts the `(name, pull_config.durable_name)` tuple returned by the factory agrees on both sides (a regression that derived the durable name from a different field would silently orphan JetStream consumer-state records on every reload), `build_consumer_config_filter_subject_handles_multi_segment_prefix` pins the embedded-dot prefix round-trip through the filter-subject field so a multi-segment operator-supplied prefix survives factory transformation, and `build_consumer_config_is_idempotent_across_repeated_calls` asserts the same input produces the same `(name, pull_config)` output across two successive calls (pinning the "no hidden state" contract the factory relies on to be safely callable from the reconnection path). Suite grows from 12 to 32 tests; zero changes to any production API — every new test drives only existing constructors, methods, and free functions through their documented contracts. `cargo nextest run -p rustgate-nats subscriber::tests::` reports 32/32 passing; full-workspace clippy with the canonical feature-set from CLAUDE.md is clean. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-websocket::server` — `DEFAULT_MAX_WRITE_BUFFER_BYTES` relationship with `MAX_FRAME_SIZE` + sanity band, per-callback-alias end-to-end invocation round-trips, deepened `WsServerConfig` Debug redaction (no Arc / closure / omitted-field leak), `WsSessionHooks` Default-vs-literal equivalence + asymmetric Debug rendering + Send+Sync+Clone+Default bounds, shutdown resilience under zero-permit connection limit + repeated notify + enabled health-check config, `tick_or_never` microsecond-interval Some branch, and `WriteAction::Ping` unit-variant shape** — `crates/rustgate-websocket/src/server.rs` owns the WebSocket accept loop, session handler, and per-session read/write loops that bridge authenticated WebSocket clients into the message `Router`; it is the counterpart to the TLS listener's accept-loop and is the only path between a browser-shaped WS client and the router's session registry. Before this PR the inline suite (19 tests) covered the `WebSocketServer` Debug derive, the four callback-alias Send+Sync bounds, `WsSessionHooks` Default/Clone/Debug-for-None-and-Some-branches, the `DEFAULT_MAX_WRITE_BUFFER_BYTES` exact-value pin, `tick_or_never` never-resolving + resolving branches, and three `WebSocketServer::run` shutdown-responsiveness scenarios (pre-notify, post-spawn notify, external Arc clone notify, and observers-do-not-fire-on-clean-shutdown). Fifteen new inline tests close a set of load-bearing gaps. Coverage layout: `default_max_write_buffer_bytes_is_less_than_core_max_frame_size` pins the strict-inequality relationship between the per-session slow-consumer cap (4 MiB) and the workspace-wide `rustgate_core::constants::MAX_FRAME_SIZE` (16 MiB) — the write-loop arithmetic is `pending_bytes.saturating_add(frame_len) > max_write_buffer_bytes`, so a refactor that bumped the cap beyond the frame-size ceiling would defeat the slow-consumer defence (the guard could never fire on a single max-size frame) and a refactor that dropped the cap to sub-frame sizes would auto-disconnect on every max-size payload — pinning the `<` inequality locks both failure modes out; `default_max_write_buffer_bytes_is_inside_sanity_band` asserts the `[1 MiB, 32 MiB]` band so a typo that dropped a MiB multiplier (landing at 4 KiB, which would refuse every real payload) or added an extra zero (40 MiB, pinning ~40 MiB of per-session buffer on top of tenant quota accounting) fails a focused test rather than manifesting at the operator's desk; five per-callback-alias end-to-end invocation round-trips (`on_nats_publish_callback_round_trips_message_through_arc_invocation`, `on_federation_forward_callback_receives_all_three_args_verbatim`, `on_http_forward_callback_round_trips_message_through_arc_invocation`, `on_ws_accept_callback_round_trips_through_arc_invocation`, `on_ws_reject_callback_round_trips_through_arc_invocation`) deepen the existing compile-time Send+Sync pins with actual invocation tests — each constructs a real `Arc<dyn Fn>` through the alias, captures arguments via `Arc<Mutex<_>>` (to keep compatibility with the `Fn` not `FnMut` bound), clones the Arc, and asserts the captured argument matches the supplied input — the federation-forward test is the strongest of the five because it carries three arguments (`Bytes`, `Vec<String>`, `Metadata`) and an argument-order swap in the closure body would silently misroute every federated send without tripping a compile error (the test pins payload, groups, and source_protocol individually against their supplied values so a positional swap fails rather than passes with the types alone agreeing); `session_hooks_default_equals_explicit_all_none_literal_init` pins the `#[derive(Default)]`'s field-by-field agreement with an explicit `None/None` literal — a manual refactor that added a "noop callback" default (intending to avoid branching on `None`) would silently break the documented "None disables dispatch with no runtime cost" contract; `session_hooks_debug_asymmetric_when_only_one_callback_installed` pins the asymmetric `true`/`false` rendering when only the accept hook is installed — a regression that collapsed the two fields into a shared flag (saving one line in the manual Debug impl but silently misreporting the actual configuration to operators) fails here; `config_debug_does_not_leak_closure_or_arc_internals` is the defensive Debug-redaction pin — the manual `WsServerConfig::Debug` impl only renders `listener`, the `<Router>` redaction token, and the codec's `protocol_id()`, so a regression that swapped back to `#[derive(Debug)]` (which would splatter every `Arc<dyn Fn>` into the rendered output) must trip by virtue of the assertions on the absence of `Router {` / `dyn Fn` / `nats_publish` / `session_hooks` tokens in the rendered string — pinning both positive (what should be shown) and negative (what must never leak) sides closes the redaction contract; three `run_exits_*` resilience tests pin the accept-loop's shutdown responsiveness under hostile configurations — `run_exits_on_shutdown_even_with_zero_permit_connection_limit` drives a `Semaphore::new(0)` so no client could ever be admitted and asserts shutdown still wins (a regression that gated the shutdown branch of the select on the permit path would deadlock defensive-lockdown deployments on SIGTERM), `run_exits_cleanly_after_repeated_shutdown_notify_calls` fires `notify_one` three times in succession before any spawn and asserts clean exit (pinning `Notify`'s documented "extra notifications are no-ops" semantic so flaky operator TTY re-fires don't stall the loop), `run_exits_cleanly_when_health_check_is_enabled_but_no_clients_connect` installs a real 30s/10s `HealthCheckConfig` and pins that an enabled health-check does not leak into the accept-loop select and delay shutdown until the first ping tick (this was a live regression risk during the health-check feature rollout — a refactor that accidentally hoisted the ping ticker into the accept-loop scope would stall shutdown for up to 30 seconds, which the test forbids by timing out at 5 seconds); `tick_or_never_with_some_resolves_under_microsecond_interval` pins the Some-branch at the smallest practically-usable cadence (`Duration::from_micros(1)`, since `tokio::time::interval` panics on `Duration::ZERO`) — a regression that added a lower-bound clamp inside the helper would trip here rather than at a surprised operator driving the health-check at 100 µs cadence; `session_hooks_is_send_sync_clone_default` compile-time-asserts the `Send + Sync + Clone + Default` bound set via a parameterised `fn assert_bounds<T: Send + Sync + Clone + Default>()` helper so any future refactor that narrowed any of the four bounds fails at this file rather than at a transitive call site in `rustgate-server::setup`; `write_action_ping_variant_is_constructible_and_parkable` pins the `WriteAction::Ping` unit-variant shape — the write loop's match exhaustiveness check relies on `Ping` being a zero-payload unit variant, so a refactor that widened it to `Ping(Bytes)` or `Ping { serial: u64 }` would cascade across the write-loop match arms and the test pins the current shape as the stable contract. Suite grows from 19 to 34 tests; zero changes to any production API — every new test drives only existing constructors, methods, free functions, and alias types through their documented contracts. `cargo nextest run -p rustgate-websocket server::tests` reports 35/35 passing (35 includes a pre-existing `config_debug_redacts_router_and_renders_codec_id` test that previously lived outside the counted 19 `#[test]` set); full-workspace clippy with the canonical feature-set from CLAUDE.md is clean. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-authz::compile` — `SpiffePrefix::matches` segment-anchoring semantics, `resource_kind_tag` variant-to-tag mapping + pairwise distinctness, `NatsSubject` compile-time validation (six rejection arms + one success), `normalize_spiffe_prefix` rejection branches + trailing-slash canonicalisation, `compute_policy_id` determinism + change-sensitivity, `compile` epoch monotonicity, #621 + #622 warning emission/suppression, `CompiledResourcePred::matches` per-variant dispatch + kind-mismatch fallthrough, and `attr_matches` AttrValue scalar / `SubsetOfSet` / type-mismatch dispatch** — `crates/rustgate-authz/src/compile.rs` is the one-way funnel every authored policy flows through before it reaches the hot-path decision engine: `RuleSet::compile()` validates the input, assigns a fresh monotonic `epoch`, computes a SHA-256 `policy_id`, and lowers every matcher into a `CompiledResourcePred` + `CompiledSubjectPred` pair bucketed by `(action, resource_kind)` for constant-time lookup. Before this PR the inline suite (6 tests) covered only the `CompiledSubjectPred::is_match_all` per-field diagnostic used by the #622 warning, leaving the security-critical SPIFFE segment-anchoring, the six NATS-subject compile-time guards, the `normalize_spiffe_prefix` rejection surface, the compile-warning (#621 + #622) emission contract, the epoch monotonicity story, the `compute_policy_id` determinism contract, the full `CompiledResourcePred` dispatch table, and the `attr_matches` AttrValue type-coercion table entirely uncovered at unit level. Twenty-nine new inline tests close those gaps. The test module adds two small helpers (`empty_ruleset()` returns a `RuleSet` at the currently-supported `POLICY_SCHEMA_VERSION` with `default_effect = Deny` and no rules; `rule(id, effect, resource)` builds an allow/deny rule with `Action::Send` and an empty subject matcher) so each test body stays focused on the single invariant it pins. Coverage layout: `spiffe_prefix_matches_exact_trust_domain_or_path`, `spiffe_prefix_matches_segment_anchored_subpath`, and `spiffe_prefix_rejects_byte_prefix_segment_impostor` pin the three legs of the documented "exact OR segment-extension" contract — the third test is the security-critical one, asserting that `SpiffePrefix { exact: "spiffe://td/ops", with_slash: "spiffe://td/ops/" }` rejects `spiffe://td/operator-evil` and `spiffe://td/ops-readonly` (a regression that dropped the `with_slash` branch and reverted to raw `starts_with` would silently grant every `operator-evil` subject every permission the rule intended for `ops`, which is the exact SPIFFE-spec footgun the normalisation layer exists to prevent); `resource_kind_tag_maps_every_variant_distinctly` asserts both the literal tag values `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, u8::MAX]` for `[Direct, Group, Broadcast, Federation, NatsSubject, Any]` (operators grep source for these numbers) AND pairwise distinctness via a `BTreeSet<u8>` size check so a refactor that accidentally collapsed two tags (which would cross-fire rules between resource kinds) fails at the assert rather than at a live authz outage; six NATS-subject compile tests — `compile_nats_subject_rejects_empty_pattern` (empty-string ambiguity), `compile_nats_subject_rejects_bare_star_pattern` (`"*"` would `starts_with("")` → match-all), `compile_nats_subject_rejects_greater_than_wildcard` (`">"` not supported, must error loudly rather than silently match the literal char), `compile_nats_subject_trailing_star_produces_prefix_predicate` (the one supported wildcard — pins both the success compile shape `NatsPrefix("cot.")` AND the runtime `.matches(Resource::NatsSubject { subject: "cot.position.broadcast" })` behaviour), `compile_nats_subject_rejects_interior_star_without_trailing_wildcard` (`"cot.*.broadcast"` would silently compile to a dead literal match), `compile_nats_subject_rejects_multi_star_pattern` (`"cot.*.*"` strips suffix to `"cot.*."` which the engine cannot process) — pin every operator footgun the compile-time guard was built to catch; four `normalize_spiffe_prefix` tests cover the rejection surface + canonicalisation: `normalize_spiffe_prefix_rejects_missing_scheme` feeds `"example.org/ops"` and asserts the error names the expected `spiffe://` scheme (so an operator who typo'd the URL-without-scheme sees a usable message), `normalize_spiffe_prefix_rejects_empty_trust_domain` feeds `"spiffe://"` and asserts the error calls out the missing authority (so a rule that would match every SPIFFE ID in existence fails to compile), `normalize_spiffe_prefix_trims_trailing_slash_for_exact_match` drives both forms (`"spiffe://td/ops/"` and `"spiffe://td/ops"`) and asserts they produce observably-identical match state (the two forms must match the same set of SPIFFE IDs regardless of whether the operator wrote the trailing slash), `normalize_spiffe_prefix_trust_domain_only_matches_td_and_subpaths` pins the trust-domain-only case (`"spiffe://td"`) — must match `spiffe://td`, `spiffe://td/foo`, `spiffe://td/foo/bar` and must reject `spiffe://other` and `spiffe://td-evil`; `compute_policy_id_is_deterministic_across_calls` pins the determinism contract (same input → same 64-char SHA-256 hex) so caches keyed on `policy_id` dedupe across restarts, and `compute_policy_id_differs_when_default_effect_changes` pins change-sensitivity so a policy reload that only flipped the default posture from Deny to Allow still produces a different digest (a regression that ignored `default_effect` in the serialisation would silently leave cached decisions in the old epoch); `compile_yields_monotonic_epoch_across_successive_compiles` pins that two successive compiles of logically-identical rule sets still produce strictly-greater epochs (the epoch is a process-global monotonic counter, not a function of policy content — a regression that tied the epoch to `policy_id` would defeat the decision-cache invalidation story); four warning-emission tests — `compile_emits_warning_for_allow_rule_with_any_resource` (#621: allow + `resource: any` warns with the offending rule id), `compile_does_not_warn_for_deny_rule_with_any_resource` (deny + `any` is a valid blanket-deny fallback, must NOT warn), `compile_emits_warning_for_allow_rule_with_empty_subject_matcher` (#622: allow + empty subject matcher warns, naming both the rule id and the subject-matcher fault token), `compile_emits_both_warnings_when_rule_hits_621_and_622` (an allow rule with BOTH hazards must emit exactly two warnings — pins that the second branch does not short-circuit out of the first) — pin both emission and non-emission so a regression that dropped either guardrail (or started warning on deny rules) is caught; `compiled_resource_pred_any_matches_every_resource_kind` pins the `CompiledResourcePred::Any` special case over all five `Resource` variants, and `compiled_resource_pred_kind_mismatch_returns_false` walks the catch-all `_ => false` arm of the dispatch table by driving `DirectAny`, `Broadcast`, and `NatsExact` each against every wrong-kind `Resource` variant to confirm kind-mismatch consistently returns `false` (a regression that removed the fallthrough would produce a match explosion across resource kinds); `attr_matches_scalar_variants_use_equality` pins every `(CompiledAttrValue, AttrValue)` scalar pair (Str/Int/Bool) on both the equal-pass and the unequal-reject cases; `attr_matches_subset_of_set_requires_every_needle` pins the empty-needles vacuous true, the full-subset pass, and — the critical one — the "any missing needle" reject case that asserts the `all` semantic over `any` (a regression from `all(needles).any(haystack)` to `any(needles).any(haystack)` would silently widen every set-membership allow rule); `attr_matches_type_mismatch_returns_false` drives every cross-type combination the dispatch table enumerates (Str want vs Int have, Int want vs Bool have, Bool want vs Str have, SubsetOfSet want vs Str have) and asserts all four reject rather than panic — the catch-all is the trait-object-less fallback the compile step relies on; three `compile_subject` JSON-value rejection tests — `compile_subject_rejects_non_integer_number_attribute` feeds `1.5` for the `clearance` attribute and asserts the error names both the attribute and the integer constraint, `compile_subject_rejects_non_string_in_array_attribute` feeds a mixed-type array `["ops", 7]` for `roles` and asserts the error names both the attribute and the string-only constraint, `compile_subject_rejects_unsupported_json_type` feeds both an object (`{}`) and a null for two different attribute keys and asserts each rejection names the offending key — the compiler refuses to invent type coercion silently, so an operator-authored policy that typo'd a JSON type fails at compile with a usable error rather than silently dropping the constraint (which would invert the rule's semantics). Suite grows from 6 to 35 tests; zero changes to any production API — every test drives the module's public and crate-private surface through its existing constructors and methods. `cargo nextest run -p rustgate-authz compile::tests` reports 35/35 passing; full-workspace clippy with the canonical feature-set from CLAUDE.md is clean. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-transport::cert_reloader` — `CertReloader` trait bounds, Debug redaction, empty-chain rejection, `update_from_der` change-detection idempotence, accessor/handshake agreement, missing-file diagnostics, memory-backed watcher inertia, SHA-256 boundary pins, and `extract_serial` fallback sentinels** — `crates/rustgate-transport/src/cert_reloader.rs` is the `ResolvesServerCert` implementation every mTLS listener in the workspace relies on for zero-downtime certificate rotation; it is shared between the file-backed polling path (TLS listener, enrollment server, metrics server) and the in-memory SPIFFE path (Workload API SVID refresh). Before this PR the inline suite (6 tests) covered the happy-path file load, SHA-256 determinism on fixed input bytes, the pre-rotation `reload()` no-op branch, reload detection on changed content, and the `ConfigError::PemParse` rejection for a corrupted cert file — but it left a material set of contract surfaces unpinned that a refactor could silently break without tripping any integration test. Twenty-six new inline tests close the gap: `cert_reloader_is_send_sync_debug_and_resolves_server_cert` and `arc_cert_reloader_is_send_sync` compile-time-assert the `Send + Sync + fmt::Debug + ResolvesServerCert` bound set on `CertReloader` (and `Send + Sync` on `Arc<CertReloader>`) via `fn assert_bounds<T: ... + ?Sized>()` helpers so a future refactor that narrows any of the bounds fails at test-compile time rather than at the first transitive call site in `rustgate-server::setup`; `debug_includes_file_paths_when_file_backed`, `debug_shows_none_paths_when_memory_backed`, and `debug_does_not_leak_key_material` pin the custom `impl Debug` — operators grep `tracing::warn!(?reloader, …)` for the cert path when a reload fails, so `cert.pem` / `key.pem` must appear in the file-backed render, `None` must appear for the SPIFFE-style memory-backed render (no ghost-path leak), and neither variant may contain a `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` / `BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY` / `BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY` marker (regression guard against a refactor that accidentally started inlining the cert chain or key bytes in Debug output); `from_der_rejects_empty_cert_chain` and `update_from_der_rejects_empty_cert_chain_when_bytes_differ` pin that both constructor-and-mutator paths refuse an empty chain with a typed error (`ConfigError::EmptyPem { kind: "certificates" }`) rather than panicking or silently installing a zero-leaf `CertifiedKey` that would cause every subsequent TLS handshake to fail with an opaque rustls error — the `update_from_der` test is careful to seed the reloader with real TestCa-issued material first so the hash-equality short-circuit does NOT fire, driving the call through the `certs.is_empty()` guard; `update_from_der_returns_false_on_identical_bytes` and `update_from_der_idempotent_across_repeated_calls` pin the change-detection contract that SPIFFE's SVID refresh loop relies on — identical bytes must return `Ok(false)` (no rebuild, no `CertifiedKey` churn) and must stay idempotent across five repeated identical calls, so a regression that always rebuilt would thrash the crypto provider's `load_private_key` path and invalidate every external cache (OCSP stapler, session resumption ticketer) keyed on the `Arc<CertifiedKey>` identity; `certified_key_accessor_agrees_with_resolve` pins that two consecutive `certified_key()` reads return the same `Arc` handle via `Arc::ptr_eq` (the handshake path uses `resolve()` and the OCSP seed path uses `certified_key()` — both read through the same `RwLock`-guarded slot, so they must agree, otherwise the stapler would serve a response bound to a stale cert); `certified_key_returns_some_after_initialization` and `certified_key_returns_some_for_memory_backed` cover both constructor paths; `certified_key_refreshes_after_rotation` pins the negation — after a successful `update_from_der`, `certified_key()` must return a new `Arc` (not `ptr_eq` to the pre-rotation handle); `new_missing_key_file_mentions_key_path` and `new_missing_cert_file_mentions_cert_path` pin the two-file read sequence's diagnostic contract — each missing file must produce an error that names the path, which is the only signal operators have when debugging misconfigured volume mounts in Kubernetes secrets or systemd credential directories; `spawn_watcher_is_noop_on_memory_backed` (a `#[tokio::test]`) arms a 1-ms poll interval, yields the runtime ten times to let any erroneously-spawned watcher tick, and asserts the `certified_key()` `Arc` identity is unchanged — the SPIFFE path drives rotation via `update_from_der` on its own schedule, so any file polling would at best waste CPU and at worst race against the SVID refresh task; `reload_is_noop_on_memory_backed` pins the direct-call variant that returns `Ok(false)` without rebuilding; `compute_hash_detects_cert_only_change` and `compute_hash_detects_key_only_change` pin that the SHA-256 feed is sensitive to edits on *either* side of the cert/key pair — a regression that hashed only one would miss the "same cert, rotated key" rekey case or the "same key, reissued cert" RFC 7469 SPKI-pinning scenario (issue #948); `compute_hash_distinguishes_cert_key_boundary` documents and pins the subtle fact that because `Sha256::update` is associative over concatenation, `hash(a+b, "")`, `hash(a, b)`, and `hash(ab, "")` produce identical digests — the test asserts `assert_eq!` on three split configurations to pin "single canonical hash independent of boundary" as the actual (non-obvious) invariant, so a refactor that added a delimiter between the cert and key halves would trip here rather than silently change the digest of every existing cert/key pair on the next reload tick; `compute_hash_output_is_sha256_sized` pins the 32-byte output; `compute_hash_stable_across_empty_inputs` asserts two empty-input calls return identical bytes and additionally pins the digest against the hex-literal SHA-256 of empty input (`e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`) so a silent swap to a different hash function (e.g. a refactor that misrouted the call through `Sha3_256` or `Blake2`) fails here rather than producing a new cert-file-unchanged-but-hash-differs cascade on every deployed reloader; `extract_serial_on_invalid_pem_returns_unknown`, `extract_serial_on_non_utf8_returns_unknown`, and `extract_serial_on_empty_returns_unknown` pin all three fallback branches of the best-effort audit-metadata helper to the literal string `"unknown"` so SIEM tooling that keys on the sentinel stays stable; `extract_serial_on_valid_cert_returns_hex_string` pins the happy-path output to ASCII-hex characters only (the helper uses `serial.to_str_radix(16)`, so any unit-test assertion against a specific serial value would be fragile — `TestCa` assigns random serials per issuance — but asserting every character is `is_ascii_hexdigit()` is a stable invariant). Suite grows from 6 to 32 tests; zero changes to any production API — every new test drives only existing constructors and methods through their documented contracts. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-authz::model` `DecisionOutcome` helpers, `Resource::kind_tag` mapping, `Action`/`Obligation` serde snake_case contract, `CacheStats` derives, and `Subject` borrow adapters** — `crates/rustgate-authz/src/model.rs` had seven `subject_hash_tests` pinning the 128-bit subject-fingerprint hashing defence, but the surrounding decision-model surface was largely unpinned: the `DecisionOutcome::{allow,deny,is_allow}` shorthand helpers (used throughout the engine to build default outcomes and short-circuit on allow checks), the `Resource::kind_tag` discriminant mapping (Direct=0, Group=1, Broadcast=2, Federation=3, NatsSubject=4 — load-bearing for the compiled-rule bucketing in `crate::compile`), the `Action` and `Obligation` serde `rename_all = "snake_case"` wire contract (stored policy JSON files use exact strings like `"send"`, `"mask_point"`, `"audit_extended"`), the `#[non_exhaustive]` unknown-tag rejection path on deserialize, the `Copy + Hash + Eq` bound set on the hot-path enums that keeps them HashMap-keyable without clone cost, the `CacheStats` `Default`/`Copy`/`Eq` plumbing used across crate boundaries, and the `Subject::{from_identity, with_hash, compute_hash}` borrow adapters that every hot-path evaluator funnels through. Seventeen new inline tests in a new `model_tests` sibling module close that gap: `decision_outcome_allow_is_allow_with_no_rule_no_obligations` and `decision_outcome_deny_is_deny_with_no_rule_no_obligations` pin both shorthand constructors to their empty-state defaults and verify the `is_allow()` predicate agrees; `decision_outcome_is_allow_ignores_rule_id_and_obligations` is the strongest of the three — it constructs an `Allow` with a populated `rule_id` and two obligations (`MaskPoint`, `AuditExtended`) and asserts `is_allow()` still returns `true`, preventing a regression where the helper also required empty obligations (which would silently flip allow-with-masking semantics to deny at every call site); `resource_kind_tag_matches_documented_wire_values` pins all five variant-to-tag mappings; `resource_kind_tags_are_all_distinct` asserts pairwise distinctness via a `BTreeSet<u8>` size check so a refactor that duplicated a tag (and caused rules for one kind to fire on another's traffic) trips; `resource_kind_tag_is_independent_of_inner_fields` verifies the tag keys only on the enum discriminant — `Direct { target_cn: "alice" }` and `Direct { target_cn: "bob" }` must share a tag; `action_serde_round_trips_via_snake_case_wire_names` and `obligation_serde_round_trips_via_snake_case_wire_names` drive every variant through `serde_json::to_string` and `serde_json::from_str` and assert the exact wire format for all five actions and all four obligations; `action_rejects_unknown_wire_tag` and `obligation_rejects_unknown_wire_tag` pin that unknown tags fail deserialization rather than silently coercing to a default — `#[non_exhaustive]` growth stays a visible change; `action_and_obligation_are_copy_and_hash` compile-time-asserts `Copy + Hash + Eq` on `Action`, `Obligation`, and `Decision` via a generic no-op function so a future variant holding a non-Copy field trips here; `cache_stats_default_is_zeros_and_copy_and_eq` pins the `Default` zero-init, the `Copy` moveability, and the `Eq` derive semantics across three cheap assertions; `subject_from_identity_borrows_every_field_verbatim` uses `std::ptr::eq` to verify the `Subject` struct points at the source `Identity`'s bytes for CN, groups, attributes, and fingerprint (a regression that added `.to_string()` would allocate on every call and break that invariant); `subject_with_hash_uses_provided_hash_verbatim` installs a sentinel `SubjectHash { primary: 0xDEAD_BEEF, secondary: 0xCAFE_F00D }` and asserts it round-trips — a silent recompute would reintroduce per-evaluation hashing cost on the hot path; `subject_compute_hash_matches_subject_hash_compute` asserts the compatibility wrapper delegates rather than reimplements, so benches stay representative of production; `subject_fingerprint_is_empty_for_plaintext_identity` pairs with `plaintext.rs::session_identity_fingerprint_is_empty_string_for_plaintext` to pin the plaintext symmetry point from the Subject side; `subject_hash_is_copy_and_eq_for_cache_keying` compile-asserts the `Copy + Eq + Hash` bound set used by the cache key. Twenty-four tests total (seven existing `subject_hash_tests` + seventeen new `model_tests`), zero changes to any production API. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-federation::api::handlers` connection/federate/certificate/stats/status REST handler contracts** — `crates/rustgate-federation/src/api/handlers.rs` hosts twelve feature-gated (`api`) HTTP handlers that every operator-driven federation management call flows through: `handle_list_connections` / `handle_get_connection` (peer state readout), `handle_list_federates` / `handle_create_federate` / `handle_get_federate` / `handle_update_federate` / `handle_delete_federate` / `handle_enable_federate` / `handle_set_routing_mode` (federate CRUD), `handle_list_certificates` / `handle_add_certificate` / `handle_get_certificate` / `handle_delete_certificate` (trust-store CRUD), and the `handle_stats` / `handle_status` readouts. Before this PR the module had zero inline tests — every wire contract (`SuccessResponse { data }` envelope shape, `ErrorResponse { error }` shape, `201 Created` on insert vs `200 OK` on update, `400 Bad Request` body-framing and message contents, `404 Not Found` path, side-effects on the `FileStore` / `TrustStore` pair, JSON round-trip through `RoutingMode` / `CreateFederateRequest` / `UpdateFederateRequest` / `SetRoutingModeRequest`) was only exercised by the tokio-listener integration harness in `tests/api_integration.rs`, which cannot target individual branches (malformed JSON, empty-field validation, invalid enum variants) without a full HTTP round-trip. A silent regression where the `handle_create_federate` validator stopped rejecting an empty `address`, where `handle_delete_federate` started returning `200 OK` with a stale snapshot instead of the canonical `{"deleted": id}` payload on the second call, where `handle_set_routing_mode` silently accepted an unknown enum variant because the JSON deserializer was swapped out for one without `deny_unknown_fields`, where `handle_add_certificate` accidentally persisted a malformed PEM into the `TrustStore` (turning a parse error into a silent trust-store poison), where `handle_stats` stopped aggregating `messages_sent` / `messages_received` across peers (leaving operators staring at zero gauges during real incidents), or where the status-fn callback was invoked more than once per request (doubling every federation RPC under the metrics dashboard) could all ship green. Twenty-two new inline tests close the gap. The test module constructs a reusable in-memory `ApiState<FileStore>` via `make_default_state()` — each call builds a fresh `FileStore::new(None)` wrapped in `Arc<RwLock<_>>`, a fresh `TrustStore::new(None)`, a constant `status_fn` that returns a three-peer `FederationStatus` snapshot (connected `peer-1`, connecting `peer-2`, disconnected `peer-3` with populated counters and a half-open circuit breaker), and a constant `peer_status_fn` that returns `Some(peer)` for `peer-1` and `None` otherwise. `body_bytes` and `body_json` use `BodyExt::collect().await.to_bytes()` to decode the `Response<Full<Bytes>>` return type into assertions. `prime_federate(state, id)` calls `store.upsert(FederateInfo::new(id, …))` to seed CRUD handlers whose 404 or round-trip branches need a pre-existing entry. Coverage layout: `handle_list_connections_surfaces_status_fn_peers_in_data_envelope` asserts the `data` key is an array of the three peers produced by the status-fn with every field preserved; `handle_get_connection_returns_404_envelope_when_peer_status_fn_returns_none` pins the `ErrorResponse { error }` shape and the 404 status on an unknown id; `handle_get_connection_returns_peer_inside_data_envelope_when_found` pins the positive path and all field preservation; `handle_create_federate_rejects_malformed_json_with_400` feeds `b"{not-json"` and asserts the 400 status + `error` envelope (not the `data` key); `handle_create_federate_rejects_empty_id_with_specific_message` / `handle_create_federate_rejects_empty_address_with_specific_message` pin the exact validator error tokens (`"id is required"`, `"address is required"`) that operators triage from CLI output; `handle_create_federate_returns_201_and_persists_to_store` asserts both the `201 Created` status and that `store.get(id).await.unwrap().is_some()` after the call — a regression that returned 201 without persisting (or persisted without returning 201) would fail here but pass a pure-wire test that only checked one side; `handle_get_federate_returns_404_envelope_for_unknown_id` closes the negative path; `handle_update_federate_rejects_malformed_json_with_400` mirrors the create-path malformed-body branch through the update handler; `handle_update_federate_returns_404_when_id_does_not_exist` pins the "update does not double as upsert" contract (a regression that started inserting on update would silently break operator expectation that `PUT /federates/:id` rejects unknown ids); `handle_delete_federate_returns_deleted_payload_then_404_on_second_call` drives a two-call sequence — first call asserts both the `200 OK` + `{"deleted": id}` payload + `store.get(id).is_none()` side-effect, second call asserts the 404 response, pinning idempotence in both directions; `handle_enable_federate_returns_404_for_unknown_id` pins the enable-path negative case; `handle_set_routing_mode_round_trips_matrix_to_broadcast` drives the Matrix→Broadcast transition end-to-end (pre-seeded federate with `RoutingMode::Matrix`, `handle_set_routing_mode` with `{"mode":"broadcast"}` body, assert 200 OK + `store.get(id).routing_mode == RoutingMode::Broadcast`) — pins both the JSON tag deserializer (`#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]`) and the persistent state update; `handle_set_routing_mode_rejects_unknown_enum_variant_with_400` feeds `{"mode":"triangle"}` and asserts 400 + unchanged store state, pinning that unknown enum variants do not silently fall through to a default and do not mutate store state; `handle_add_certificate_rejects_empty_body_with_400` pins the empty-body branch (and asserts the trust store count stays at 0 after the call, ruling out any silent side-effect); `handle_add_certificate_rejects_malformed_pem_with_400` pins the parse-error branch against `b"-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nnot-valid-pem\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n"` (same no-side-effect assertion); `handle_get_certificate_returns_404_for_unknown_cn` / `handle_delete_certificate_returns_404_for_unknown_cn` pin the certificate-readout and deletion negative paths through `TrustStore::new(None)`; `handle_stats_aggregates_messages_across_peers_and_exposes_trust_store_count` uses the three-peer status-fn fixture (sent counts 10, 20, 30 and recv counts 15, 25, 35) and asserts `total_messages_sent == 60`, `total_messages_received == 75`, `trust_store_certificate_count == 0`, and `total_connections == 3` — aggregating arithmetic regressions in `fold` / `sum` (silently switching `+` to `max`, or dropping one peer via an off-by-one `take`) fail here rather than at a Grafana outage; `handle_status_returns_status_fn_snapshot_verbatim` pins that the status-fn output is passed through verbatim without mutation (so a regression that accidentally cloned a stale cache or filtered the peer list would fail); `handle_list_federates_returns_empty_array_on_fresh_store` / `handle_list_certificates_returns_empty_array_on_fresh_trust_store` pin that a fresh-store list returns `{"data": []}` rather than a `null` or a missing `data` key — both are failure modes clients parse differently, and the `serde_json::to_string(&SuccessResponse { data: vec![] })` path must produce an empty array literal. The `handle_federate_peer` handler is deliberately not covered at unit level because it takes `Request<hyper::body::Incoming>` which is not constructable in a unit-test context (same limitation `handlers::revoke::handle_revoke` and `handlers::api::handle_device_profile` carry). All twenty-two tests pass under `cargo nextest run -p rustgate-federation --features api api::handlers::tests::`; focused clippy with `--features api,v2 --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the full-workspace clippy with the canonical feature-set from CLAUDE.md both report clean. Zero changes to any production code path. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-enrollment::handlers::revoke` CRL and list endpoints** — `crates/rustgate-enrollment/src/handlers/revoke.rs` previously had zero inline tests; the three public handlers (`handle_revoke`, `handle_crl`, `handle_list_revoked`) and the `RevokeRequest` DTO were only covered indirectly via `tests/server_integration.rs`. A silent regression in the `handle_crl` `Content-Type` header (`application/x-pem-file`), the PEM begin/end framing of the CRL body, the revoked-serial round-trip through the CRL DER, the JSON shape of `handle_list_revoked` (entries, their `serial`/`reason`/`revoked_by`/`revoked_at` fields, or the "empty array when no revocations" shape), or the `RevokeRequest` deserializer's `reason` default could all land without tripping a wire-level test. Seven new inline tests close that gap by spinning up a fresh `TestCa` + `RevocationStore` per test and asserting handler outputs at the `Response<Full<Bytes>>` boundary: `handle_crl_returns_pem_with_correct_content_type` pins the content-type header and the `-----BEGIN/END X509 CRL-----` markers; `handle_crl_reflects_newly_revoked_serial` routes a revoke through the store and decodes the handler's PEM body back to DER via `rustgate_core::b64::decode` + `x509_parser::parse_x509_crl`, asserting the revoked serial is present in `iter_revoked_certificates()` (matches on raw PEM bytes would be unsafe since base64 output is not stable across re-encodings); `handle_list_revoked_returns_empty_array_when_no_revocations` pins the empty-slice JSON shape; `handle_list_revoked_returns_entries_with_expected_fields` revokes two serials and asserts the full `serial`/`reason`/`revoked_by`/`revoked_at` field set (mapping by serial so the test does not depend on HashMap iteration order); `revoke_request_uses_default_reason_when_absent` and `revoke_request_honours_explicit_reason` pin the `#[serde(default)]` behaviour of the DTO; `default_reason_is_unspecified` pins the literal. Tests stay scoped to the `handle_crl` / `handle_list_revoked` surface because `handle_revoke` takes `Request<hyper::body::Incoming>` which is not constructable in a unit-test context (the same limitation `handlers::api` documents at the `device_profile_response_format` test) — integration-level `handle_revoke` coverage lives in `tests/server_integration.rs`. Closes the `handlers/revoke.rs` line item on #909. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-core::tasks` panic-safety and subsystem-lifecycle contract** — `crates/rustgate-core/src/tasks.rs` is the workspace-wide helper module for fire-and-forget background work (`spawn_background`) and drainable subsystems (`SubsystemHandle` + `stop_subsystem`); every long-lived task across 16 crates flows through one of these two entry points. Before this PR the module had three inline tests: a `spawn_background` smoke test, a `stop_subsystem` sunny-path test, and a `stop_subsystem` timeout test. That left four contract branches untested: (a) `spawn_background`'s outer watcher task that catches panics and logs `error!` rather than bringing down the runtime, (b) the `Ok(Err(e))` arm of `stop_subsystem` that fires when the task panics after receiving shutdown notification, (c) the sunny-path case where the task has already exited before `stop_subsystem` is called (notify becomes a buffered permit that no one consumes), and (d) the `#[derive(Debug)]` on `SubsystemHandle` that every caller logging a handle via `tracing::debug!(?handle, …)` relies on. Five new inline tests close those gaps: `spawn_background_panic_does_not_crash_runtime` spawns a panicking task, waits for it to reach the panic point (via an `AtomicBool` set immediately before `panic!`), then spawns a healthy task and asserts it runs to completion — proving the outer watcher catches the `JoinError` and the runtime is not poisoned (a regression that replaced the two-task wrapper with a bare `drop(tokio::spawn(...))` would still pass the happy-path test but would bring down the runtime on the first panic in production); `stop_subsystem_returns_cleanly_when_task_panics_after_shutdown` wires a task that awaits the notify and then panics, calls `stop_subsystem`, and asserts the function returns rather than propagating the panic — pinning the `Ok(Err(_))` arm that would otherwise fail only under real production panics; `stop_subsystem_succeeds_when_task_already_exited_before_notify` has the task return straight away, sleeps briefly so the task completes before `stop_subsystem` is called, and proves the notify-one-to-nobody case does not deadlock; `subsystem_handle_implements_debug` compile-time-asserts the `Debug` bound via `fn assert_debug<T: std::fmt::Debug>(_: &T)` and checks the `Debug` rendering mentions the type name (the exact tokio `JoinHandle` formatting is deliberately not pinned — it changes between tokio versions and is not part of rustgate's stable surface); `subsystem_handle_shutdown_is_externally_cloneable_before_construction` pins the `Arc<Notify>` pattern every listener subsystem (WebSocket, MQTT, plaintext TCP, UDP, enrollment) relies on — external callers clone the shutdown notifier before moving it into the task body, and firing through the external clone must wake the task inside the subsystem. All eight tests pass under `cargo nextest run -p rustgate-core tasks::` and `cargo clippy -p rustgate-core --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` is clean. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-federation::v2::convert` `ConvertError` surface and XML helper contract** — `crates/rustgate-federation/src/v2/convert/mod.rs` previously had three XML-escape tests but zero coverage for the `ConvertError` error-type hierarchy (`Xml`, `MissingField`, `InvalidField`, `InvalidTimestamp` variants), zero coverage for the `std::error::Error` trait impl, zero coverage for the `From<rustgate_proto::ProtoError>` conversion (which maps `MissingField` 1:1, `InvalidTimestamp` 1:1, and routes every other variant through `Xml(other.to_string())`), and zero coverage for the `write_attr` XML-attribute helper. Eleven new inline tests close that gap: `xml_escape_into_empty_is_no_op` and `xml_escape_into_preserves_non_ascii_bytes_unchanged` pin the low-level byte writer's boundary behaviour and the "only escape the five entities, never lossily transform UTF-8 continuation bytes" contract (a regression here would produce subtly-malformed XML that downstream parsers accept but misinterpret); `xml_escape_string_helper_escapes_all_five_entities` mirrors the existing `xml_escape_special_characters` test through the `String`-based helper so a future refactor that accidentally dropped `&apos;` / `&quot;` from only one code path fails on the first build; `write_attr_emits_name_equals_quoted_value_with_leading_space` pins the exact output format (` name="value"` with a leading space so `build_tag()` can chain attributes without explicit separators); `write_attr_escapes_value_but_not_name` pins that the name is written raw (it is always an internal static) while the value is escaped — a regression that started escaping the name would produce malformed XML that quick-xml's strict validator would reject at the peer; four `convert_error_*_display_renders_*` tests pin the `Display` output for every `ConvertError` variant so log-grep and SIEM ingest rules that key off the prefix tokens ("xml parse error:", "missing required field:", "invalid field:", "invalid timestamp:") stay stable; `convert_error_implements_std_error_trait` compile-time-asserts the `std::error::Error` bound via `fn assert_error<T: Error>(_: &T) {}` so a caller wrapping a `ConvertError` in `anyhow::Error` or `Box<dyn Error>` stays compilable, and pins that `source()` returns `None` on leaf errors (the impl is default-derived); three `proto_error_*_converts_to_*` tests pin the `From<ProtoError>` shape end-to-end — `MissingField("event")` preserves the `&'static str` through the conversion, `InvalidTimestamp("missing T separator")` preserves the owned `String`, and `FrameTooLarge { size: 1 << 24, max: 1 << 20 }` (a representative non-MissingField, non-InvalidTimestamp variant) falls through to `ConvertError::Xml(other.to_string())` with the `Display` rendering preserved. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-authz::cache` — `DecisionCache` sizing, counters, Debug, Clone semantics, dedup invariants, shard formula, and cross-key hash disambiguation** — `crates/rustgate-authz/src/cache.rs` previously had three inline tests (`hit_miss_basic`, `epoch_change_invalidates`, `fifo_evicts_oldest`) covering the sunny-path contracts of the sharded authz decision cache but leaving a significant amount of load-bearing behaviour unpinned: the power-of-two shard rounding in `DecisionCache::new` (which `shard_mask = shards - 1` silently relies on — break the rounding and `shard_idx` stops covering the full shard array), the `Default` sizing constants (`16 × 4096`) that every engine without an explicit cache-size configuration inherits, the custom `Debug` impl that operators rely on for metrics dumps and triage, the `Clone` impl's documented "fresh empty cache with same sizing, counters reset" contract (which exists specifically so cloning an authz engine doesn't smuggle the original's steady-state decisions into the clone), the `insert` early-return on duplicate keys (which must neither overwrite the existing outcome *nor* bump the FIFO position — a silent overwrite would let a later caller flip a cached decision, and a silent FIFO touch would degrade the LRU-ish approximation into something stranger), the `CachedOutcome` round-trip of `rule_id` and `obligations` through the private wire type between `insert` and `get`, the `DecisionKey` Eq/Hash derive's inclusion of the full 128-bit `SubjectHash` (drop `secondary` from the derive and the adversarial-resistance claim in the module docs evaporates silently), the per-key independence of `action` and `resource_hash` in the key identity (fold either out and a Send decision silently satisfies a Receive check — authz escape hatch), the independence of the `hits`/`misses` atomic counters (a regression that bumped the wrong one would only show up as nonsense ratios in prod Grafana), and the `shard_idx` formula's consumption of `secondary` (if the mix dropped `secondary`, an adversary who pins `primary = 0` and `resource_hash = 0` funnels every cache entry into shard 0). Ten new inline tests close those gaps: `new_rounds_shard_count_up_to_next_power_of_two` drives a six-case table (3→4, 5→8, 7→8, 9→16, 16→16, 1→1, 0→1) and asserts both `shards.len()` and `shard_mask == shards - 1`; `default_cache_is_sized_16_by_4096_with_zero_counters` pins the exact Default constants; `debug_output_exposes_shape_and_live_counters` primes the cache with one miss + one hit and asserts the Debug string starts with `DecisionCache` and contains `shards: 4`, `capacity_per_shard: 8`, `hits: 1`, `misses: 1`; `clone_returns_empty_cache_with_same_sizing_and_zero_counters` exercises the source (miss+insert+hit → hits=1, misses=1), clones, and asserts the clone has no carried entry, hits=0 (but misses=1 from the lookup-that-proved-the-entry-was-gone), and the same shard count / per-shard capacity; `insert_dedup_does_not_overwrite_or_bump_fifo_position` is the strongest test — fills a 1-shard 2-cap cache with A then B, performs a dedup insert of A with a DIFFERENT outcome (Deny instead of Allow) to prove the existing Allow is not overwritten, then inserts C and asserts A was the one evicted (if the dedup had refreshed FIFO position, B would have been evicted instead); `cached_outcome_round_trip_preserves_rule_id_and_obligations` inserts a non-default outcome (`rule_id = Some("rule-42")`, `obligations = [MaskPoint, AuditExtended]`) and asserts every field survives the `CachedOutcome` round-trip including obligation ordering; `decision_key_distinct_secondary_hashes_do_not_collide` builds two keys with identical `primary`/`resource_hash`/`action`/`policy_epoch` but different `secondary` and asserts both `assert_ne!` equality AND cache-lookup miss-on-second — this is the 128-bit collision-resistance security claim made concrete; `decision_key_action_and_resource_are_part_of_identity` inserts a base key and performs cache lookups with the exact same subject but varied `action` (Send→Receive) and varied `resource_hash` (known→999), asserting both miss; `hits_and_misses_counters_track_independently` issues 2 misses followed by 3 hits and asserts `cache.hits() == 3 && cache.misses() == 2`; `shard_formula_consumes_secondary_hash_for_adversarial_resistance` pins the adversarial-resistance claim by building four keys that differ *only* in `secondary` (using `1u64 << {47, 48, 49, 50}` so `rotate_left(17)` places a non-zero low nibble) and asserting the resulting `shard_idx` set has more than one distinct element — if the formula ever drops `secondary`, every crafted key funnels into shard 0 and the assertion trips. Thirteen tests total (three existing + ten new), zero changes to any production API. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-nats::jetstream` `Checkpoint` load/save defensive branches and `JetStreamReplay` constructor field-preservation contract** — `crates/rustgate-nats/src/jetstream.rs` hosts two types that together own the situational-awareness bootstrap path every rustgate NATS consumer depends on: `Checkpoint` persists the last-processed JetStream stream sequence number to disk via `tokio::fs::read_to_string` / `write`, and `JetStreamReplay` drains the `TRACKS_HISTORY` stream on startup and populates `Router`'s `PositionCache` so newly connected TAK clients receive a full SA picture even when live publish traffic has not yet arrived. Before this PR the inline suite (3 tests: happy-path round-trip, invalid-content → `None`, missing-file → `None`) left every defensive branch of `Checkpoint::load` / `save` unpinned — a silent regression where `"42\n".parse::<u64>()` stopped accepting trailing whitespace (the file would otherwise be written by `echo 42 > checkpoint` during incident-response), where an empty/torn-write sentinel byte produced `Some(0)` instead of `None` (replaying the entire stream on every restart), where a pathological overflow value silently wrapped to `0`, where `-1` silently parsed instead of rejecting cleanly, where `save()` failed to create missing parent directories recursively (the checkpoint path is operator-supplied and often points into a fresh state directory), where `save()` on a bare filename with no parent panicked on the `Option::unwrap` hidden inside `Path::parent`, where `save()` appended rather than atomically overwrote (accumulating stale sequences forever and defeating the whole point of checkpointing), or where `u64::MAX` failed to round-trip could all ship green. Twelve new inline tests close the gap: `checkpoint_load_trims_whitespace_and_newlines_from_seq_string` pins the `.trim().parse::<u64>()` chain that the hand-edit workflow depends on; `checkpoint_load_empty_file_returns_none` pins the "empty file must parse as None, not Some(0)" invariant; `checkpoint_load_overflow_seq_returns_none` writes a 29-digit value and asserts the `.ok()` on the parse result routes cleanly to `None`; `checkpoint_load_negative_value_returns_none` pins that `u64::from_str` rejects leading `-` so a config migration that writes a signed `i64` representation by mistake fails loudly at load; `checkpoint_save_creates_parent_dirs_recursively` builds a four-level nested path (`a/b/c/d/checkpoint`) underneath a `tempdir` and asserts both the `save().await.unwrap()` call succeeds and the resulting `load().await` returns the written value, pinning the `tokio::fs::create_dir_all` branch every operator-supplied path relies on; `checkpoint_save_at_bare_filename_does_not_panic_on_none_parent` points `Checkpoint::new` at a bare filename inside `tempdir`-cwd (no directory component in the path), drives `save()` through the `Path::parent() == Some("")` branch that the naive `create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap())` spelling would panic on, and asserts both success and round-trip — the test relies on `tempfile::tempdir`'s automatic cleanup + `std::env::set_current_dir` restoration via the `Drop` on the guard so parallel tests stay isolated; `checkpoint_save_is_atomic_overwrite_not_append` writes `42` then `7` and asserts the final file contents are exactly `"7"` (not `"427"` and not `"42\n7"`), pinning the `write()`-is-truncate contract that every subsequent `load()` relies on; `checkpoint_save_and_load_round_trips_u64_max` pins the `u64::MAX = 18_446_744_073_709_551_615` boundary so a future refactor that accidentally narrowed the on-disk encoding to `i64` (flipping the MSB and producing `-1` on reload) fails here rather than at a live operator incident; `checkpoint_debug_impl_renders_path_field` pins the `#[derive(Debug)]` output contains the `path: "..."` field so `tracing::debug!(?checkpoint, …)` lines stay human-readable and operators can grep for the configured checkpoint location at startup; `jetstream_replay_and_checkpoint_compile_time_debug_bounds` uses `fn assert_debug<T: std::fmt::Debug + ?Sized>()` parameterised on `Checkpoint` and `JetStreamReplay` to pin the `missing_debug_implementations = "warn"` workspace-lint compliance at test-compile time — a refactor that removed the derive would fail here rather than at a downstream `tracing::debug!` call site; `jetstream_replay_new_preserves_none_checkpoint_path` and `jetstream_replay_new_preserves_some_checkpoint_path` are the two `require_nats!`-gated tests that exercise `JetStreamReplay::new(client, NatsConfig::default(), checkpoint_path)` with both `None` and `Some(PathBuf)` arguments, format the result with `{replay:?}`, and assert the `checkpoint_path: None` / `checkpoint_path: Some("...")` field survives constructor verbatim — a silent regression where `new()` dropped the checkpoint argument on the floor would otherwise only surface after a restart fails to resume from the persisted sequence. Both `require_nats!`-gated tests skip cleanly when nats-server is absent from PATH (same `rustgate-test-utils::require_nats!` macro used by every other NATS-touching integration test in the workspace). Total suite grows from 3 to 15 tests; zero changes to any production API — every test drives the module's public/crate-private surface through its existing constructors and methods. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-federation::discovery::consul` catalog URL, serde contract, peer defaults, Debug redaction, and timeout constant** — `crates/rustgate-federation/src/discovery/consul.rs` is the Consul catalog backend for dynamic federation peer discovery (`/v1/catalog/service/<name>` HTTP polling → `Vec<PeerConfig>`, gated on the `peer-discovery-consul` feature). Before this PR the inline suite pinned four behaviours — trailing-slash stripping in `catalog_url`, `ServiceAddress` preferred over node `Address`, empty-string `ServiceAddress` falling back to node `Address`, and IPv6 bracketing — but left seven contract-shaped invariants unpinned, each of which could silently regress without tripping a live-Consul integration test. Nine new inline tests close the gaps: `catalog_url_without_trailing_slash_uses_single_separator` pins the no-trailing-slash branch of `trim_end_matches` so a regression that always appended `/` would produce `http://consul:8500//v1/...` and fail here (the doc-comment explicitly advertises "without a trailing slash" as the canonical form); `catalog_entry_deserializes_pascal_case_wire_fields` deserializes a real-shaped JSON payload with `ServiceID`, `ServiceAddress`, `ServicePort`, `Address` and asserts all four fields round-trip correctly — pins both `#[serde(rename_all = "PascalCase")]` and the explicit `#[serde(rename = "ServiceID")]` override (Consul emits the id field in all-caps specifically, and a dropped rename would still round-trip internally but fail on real Consul output); `catalog_entry_service_address_is_optional` omits the `ServiceAddress` key entirely from the JSON payload to pin the `Option<String>` tolerance — Consul omits this field when a service registered without an explicit address (common with Consul Connect / sidecar registrations) and an accidental narrowing to `String` would reject every such node; `entry_to_peer_applies_documented_defaults` drives a single entry through the mapper and asserts all twelve output fields against the hardcoded constants — `groups = ["__ANON__"]`, `inbound_groups = None`, `outbound_groups = None`, `enabled = true`, `is_outbound = true`, `trust_cert_cn = None`, `routing_mode = RoutingMode::default()`, `protocol_version = 2`, `jwt_token = None`, `region = None`, `zone = None`, `priority = 100` — so a silent flip (e.g. `enabled = false` during a "disable peers by default until review" refactor or a bump of `protocol_version` to 3 that breaks mixed-version fleets) fails a focused test rather than surfacing as a production federation outage; `entry_to_peer_already_bracketed_ipv6_is_not_double_bracketed` pins the `!host.starts_with('[')` guard so a `[2001:db8::1]` service address (the form the Consul HTTP API sometimes returns when a node registered with an explicit literal) does not become `[[2001:db8::1]]:9000` and fail every downstream `SocketAddr::parse`; `backend_name_is_stable_consul_token` resolves the `PeerDiscovery` trait's `backend_name()` through `&dyn PeerDiscovery` and asserts the `&'static str` return is exactly `"consul"` — operators grep for this token in reconciler log lines and a rename would break every deployed alerting rule; `debug_impl_redacts_http_client_and_renders_key_fields` pins the manual `Debug` impl's contract — `base_url` and `service` are visible for operators (a `tracing::debug!(?backend, …)` line should let the on-call identify which backend errored) but the `reqwest::Client` is elided via `finish_non_exhaustive()` and the rendered output must contain `..` (the sentinel) and must not contain `Client {` (which would indicate a silent swap to `#[derive(Debug)]` that would leak connector pool state into logs); `default_http_timeout_is_ten_seconds` pins both `DEFAULT_HTTP_TIMEOUT == 10s` and the critical arithmetic `DEFAULT_HTTP_TIMEOUT < 30s` (the reconciler's default interval) so a future bump past the reconciler tick would fail here instead of silently starving the discovery loop on every slow Consul response; `new_accepts_owned_string_and_str_slice` drives both `&str` and `String` call shapes through `ConsulDiscovery::new` to pin `impl Into<String>` compiles for both forms so a future narrowing to `&str` (which would break every owned-`String` caller in the server bin) fails at test-compile time rather than at the call site. Coverage grows from 4 to 13 tests; zero changes to production code. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-core::net` tactical-socket helpers (constants, SO_KEEPALIVE observability, idempotence, AsFd bound width)** — `crates/rustgate-core/src/net.rs` hosts the socket-hardening primitives (`configure_tcp_keepalive`, `configure_tcp_nodelay`, `configure_tactical_socket`) that every accepted TCP stream in the workspace flows through: TLS listener, plaintext TCP, WebSocket, MQTT, enrollment server, metrics server, federation connector, and the client dial side. Before this PR the inline suite (3 tests) only asserted `TCP_NODELAY` is observable after `configure_tcp_nodelay` and that the combined helper does not error, leaving five contract-shaped invariants unpinned. Six new tests close the gap: `keepalive_idle_and_interval_constants_pin_rustgate_defaults` pins `TCP_KEEPALIVE_IDLE = 30s` and `TCP_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL = 10s` so an accidental edit to the top-of-file durations fails here rather than silently shifting every production listener's dead-connection detection curve — doubling the idle would push dead-peer cleanup past the `FEDERATION_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT` budget; `tcp_nodelay_starts_disabled_so_configure_is_not_a_no_op` is the defensive vacuity-guard — if a future OS ever ships sockets with Nagle already disabled, every nodelay assertion in this file would become vacuously true, so this test fails loudly in that case and forces a redesign of the positive-path tests rather than letting them pass silently; `configure_tcp_keepalive_enables_so_keepalive_flag` uses `SockRef::keepalive()` (cross-platform accessor) to pin that SO_KEEPALIVE is actually set — closing the "the call didn't error" gap the existing `keepalive_does_not_fail_on_tcp_listener` test leaves; `tactical_socket_enables_both_so_keepalive_and_tcp_nodelay_observably` is the end-to-end pin on the combined helper — the F-151 / #745 regression was that listeners set keepalive but forgot `TCP_NODELAY`, paying a ~40ms Nagle+DELACK penalty per tactical message, and `configure_tactical_socket` exists precisely to make the "keepalive + nodelay" pair atomic at every call site, so both observables must be asserted after a single call; `tactical_socket_is_idempotent_on_repeated_calls` pins the contract that the helpers are safe to call multiple times against the same live socket — shared code paths (session spawns, cert reloads, reconnection loops) can plausibly run more than once without a "has it been configured" gate, so toggling-on-second-call would be a regression; `tactical_socket_accepts_both_tcp_listener_and_tcp_stream_via_as_fd_bound` is the load-bearing compile-time + runtime self-check that the `impl AsFd` generic bound stays wide enough for every call site in the workspace — if a future refactor narrowed the bound to `&TcpStream`, the callers that pass a `TcpListener` (`server/metrics.rs`, `enrollment/server.rs`) would fail to compile, but not via this module's own suite. Suite grows from 3 to 9 tests; no behavioural change to the module under test. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-enrollment::contacts` Marti API provider (serde rename contract, Debug redaction, factory wrapper, zero-TTL edge case, double-check concurrency)** — `crates/rustgate-enrollment/src/contacts.rs` hosts the Marti-compatible `/Marti/api/contacts/all` and `/Marti/api/clientEndPoints` provider stack (`ContactInfo` struct, `ContactsProvider` callback alias, `CachedContactsProvider` with TTL cache, and the `cached_contacts_provider` free-function wrapper). Before this PR the inline suite only covered the happy-path cache TTL behaviour (three tests: within-ttl cache hit, post-ttl refresh, and post-ttl updated-data round-trip), leaving five contract-shaped invariants unpinned that a refactor could silently break without tripping the integration layer. Six new inline tests close that gap: `contact_info_serializes_with_marti_compatible_last_status_field` asserts the `#[serde(rename = "lastStatus")]` attribute is load-bearing for iTAK/ATAK wire-compat (a regression that dropped the rename would still round-trip between rustgate binaries but break every Marti consumer — the test pins both `obj.contains_key("lastStatus")` **and** `!obj.contains_key("last_status")` so the absence of the snake_case key is part of the contract); `contact_info_clone_and_partial_eq_round_trip` pins the `#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]` derives that the cache relies on (`contacts.clone()` on every cache hit) so a future narrowing fails here rather than at transitive callers; `cached_contacts_provider_debug_shows_ttl_but_not_inner` pins the custom `Debug` impl's `finish_non_exhaustive()` call — the `..` marker in the rendered output is the contract that keeps the `Arc<dyn Fn>` callback pointer out of `tracing::debug!(?c, …)` lines while still exposing the `ttl` field operators want to see, and the test asserts both the presence of `ttl` + `..` and the absence of `inner` / `cache` tokens; `cached_contacts_provider_factory_function_wraps_with_ttl` drives the `cached_contacts_provider(inner, ttl) -> ContactsProvider` free-function wrapper that the server binary actually uses (the existing suite only exercised `CachedContactsProvider::new` directly, so a regression in the wrapper closure that accidentally skipped the cache and always called the inner would slip through) and asserts `call_count == 1` across two `wrapped().await` calls within the TTL; `zero_ttl_always_invokes_inner_provider` pins the ttl=0 edge case where `elapsed() < Duration::ZERO` is mathematically never true and both the read-lock fast path and the write-lock double-check must therefore fall through to inner on every call (operators who want "cache disabled" semantics rely on this — a regression that treated 0 as a sentinel for "no expiry" would silently pin the first snapshot forever); `concurrent_gets_on_fresh_cache_invoke_inner_exactly_once` uses `tokio::join!` with a 20ms sleep inside the inner callback to deliberately force the second caller onto the write-lock double-check branch and pins `call_count == 1` as the contract the fast path depends on to avoid a thundering-herd fan-out into the router's session state under a spike of concurrent Marti requests. Total suite grows from 3 to 9 tests; no behavioural change to the module under test. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for `rustgate-client::connect` dial-path defensive branches and plaintext `Stream::Plain` I/O** — `crates/rustgate-client/src/connect.rs` is the sole dial helper every integration test (and every downstream consumer of the lightweight client library) reaches through, and its existing inline suite covered seven sunny-path and TLS-configuration-error cases but left three defensive branches of `build_tls_config` / `dial_inner` unpinned and the entire `Stream::Plain` `AsyncRead`/`AsyncWrite`/`poll_shutdown` impl untouched by the unit-test layer. A silent refactor that (a) swallowed a `std::fs::read_to_string` error on the key path into a non-`Io` variant, (b) did the same on the CA path, (c) narrowed the `dial_inner` `MissingField("tls")` guard to only match on a public-API caller (so direct `ClientConfig` construction with `plaintext=false, tls=None` silently produced a `Stream::Plain` rather than the explicit error the field name promises), or (d) regressed any of the four `AsyncRead`/`AsyncWrite` forwarders on `Stream::Plain` (the two `poll_read`/`poll_write` vtable entries, `poll_flush`, `poll_shutdown`) could all ship green. Four new inline tests close those gaps: `build_tls_config_missing_key_file_returns_io_error` issues a real cert via `TestCa` but points the `key` field at a nonexistent path and asserts `Err(ClientError::Io(e))` with `e.kind() == ErrorKind::NotFound`, mirroring the existing cert-path test; `build_tls_config_missing_ca_file_returns_io_error` repeats the pattern on the CA path (the `ca` field is the last PEM the helper reads, and the matching error arm was previously uncovered); `dial_without_tls_on_non_plaintext_config_returns_missing_field` direct-constructs a `ClientConfig` with `plaintext=false, tls=None` (bypassing the `ClientConfigBuilder` which enforces invariants, to pin the defensive branch that exists specifically for callers who assemble `ClientConfig` by hand), spawns a throwaway `TcpListener` on `127.0.0.1:0` so `TcpStream::connect` succeeds and the test reaches the TLS-vs-plaintext switch in `dial_inner`, and asserts `ClientError::MissingField("tls")` — split into `Err(MissingField(field))` / `Err(other)` / `Ok(_)` arms because `Stream` does not derive `Debug` and the usual `{other:?}` panic formatter will not compile; `dial_plaintext_connects_and_stream_round_trips_bytes` spawns a local TCP echo, dials with `plaintext=true`, round-trips `b"ping"` to exercise `Stream::Plain`'s `poll_read`/`poll_write`/`poll_flush` vtable entries, then calls `stream.shutdown().await.unwrap()` to exercise `poll_shutdown` — the four delegations to the inner `TcpStream` are now covered by a single end-to-end test rather than relying on an integration-test side-effect. `cargo nextest run -p rustgate-client` reports 38/38 passing. (Refs #909)
- **Unit-test coverage for the `rustgate-core::codec::Codec` trait contract** — `crates/rustgate-core/src/codec.rs` defines the `Codec` trait that every transport-layer codec (`TakXmlCodec`, `RawLineCodec`, `RawLengthPrefixedCodec`, `TakFrameCodec`, `MavlinkCodec`, `NoopCodec`) implements; the trait is the seam the router reaches for to go from wire bytes to a `RoutableMessage` and back. Before this PR the file had zero inline tests — the individual codec impls were covered by their own modules but the trait itself, its super-trait bounds (`Send + Sync + std::fmt::Debug`), its object-safety, and its method signatures had no direct test that would fail if a future refactor silently tightened one of the bounds to `Send + Sync` without `Debug` (breaking `tracing::debug!(?codec, …)` at every call site) or narrowed `decode_payload` from `BytesMut` to `&[u8]` (breaking the zero-copy `frame.freeze()` contract every passthrough codec relies on).
